```rustix/docs/roadmap/README.md
   172	## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI
   173	
   174	Userspace begins only after page tables, exception handling, scheduling, and controlled memory allocation are trustworthy. The syscall ABI is a product interface and must not emerge accidentally from internal functions. Milestone 3's single-vCPU IRQ-safe locking and timer-preemption gate is locally validated; this enables scheduler progress but does not by itself make user code isolated or safe. SMP remains outside this milestone.
   175	
   176	### Planned work
   177	
   178	- [x] Decide and document the initial x86_64 user-entry/syscall mechanism, register convention, selector/MSR setup, per-CPU state requirements, and safe return path. The design uses a DPL-3 `int $0x80` gate and validated `IRETQ`, with no syscall MSRs or `SWAPGS`. Vector `0x80` is excluded from the device allocator; the GDT installs asserted Ring 3 selectors, and the gate saves GPR/x87/SSE state and sanitizes return flags. The opt-in process probe exercises entry/return and mapping-aware return checks; it uses the static bootstrap entry stack and is not general process scheduling. Revisit the entry model if per-process stacks or SMP requirements change.
   179	- [x] Define per-process address-space construction without deep-cloning the entire kernel page-table tree for every process. The design shares validated supervisor-only upper-half subtrees, keeps lower-half tables and user frames process-owned, and specifies kernel-owner lifetime, teardown, permission, and local TLB rules. Implementation and validation remain pending.
   180	- [x] Complete the initial user/kernel page-permission and process-owned address-space path, including teardown and local TLB invalidation rules. The implementation shares validated supervisor-only kernel entries, maps/unmaps private lower-half user frames, retains executable/writable metadata, validates the initial entry and writable NX stack, and destroys the root only after switching away. Host tests cover ownership and rollback; `just verify` validates one activation/return/teardown cycle and frame-count restoration in QEMU. General concurrent process management, per-process kernel stacks, curated kernel mappings, and broader isolation guarantees remain pending.
   181	- [x] Complete copy-in/copy-out semantics for the initial implemented syscall set. Frame-token-based helpers preflight ranges and permissions; bounded `write` and ready-child `wait` use them. Host tests cover cross-page copies, permissions, partial writes, and descriptor errors; `just process-smoke` verifies invalid write/status pointers return `-EFAULT` without kernel corruption or consuming the exited child, and returns `-ENOTSUP` for a running child. QEMU fault smokes verify CPL3 termination and fatal CPL0 separation for #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE. Blocking wait and memory-transfer semantics for future syscalls remain pending.
   182	- [x] Specify v1 version discovery, initial syscall numbers/argument meanings, fixed-width layouts, negative error encoding, bounded partial-write/copy behavior, wait semantics, no-restart policy, and append-only compatibility before exposing calls. The contract is documented in `docs/architecture/syscall-abi.md`; host-tested decoding and the dedicated gate/stub are implemented. The diagnostic path exercises ABI-version, descriptor-authorized write, close/dup, wait for an exited child, one-page mmap/munmap, and exit; a running child returns `ENOTSUP` until blocking wait is integrated. Future read/open, general file-object semantics, signals, and clocks need implementation/specification.
   183	- [ ] Complete process lifecycle and descriptor-table semantics: create/load, exit, wait, close, duplication/inheritance, and cleanup. The diagnostic path binds exit/reap to the process root and implements userspace wait for already-exited children with status copyout-before-reap; QEMU uses kernel-seeded exited/running child fixtures to verify invalid status pointers leave a zombie waitable and running-child wait returns `ENOTSUP`. The fixed-capacity table now inherits console stream handles on spawn, supports close/dup with lowest-free descriptor allocation, clears handles on exit, and returns `EMFILE` on exhaustion; host tests cover defaults, inheritance, duplicate independence, invalid/closed entries, slot reuse, capacity, and exit cleanup, while `just process-smoke` exercises dup/write/close from Ring 3. Child creation tied to executable roots, blocking scheduler waits, per-process kernel stacks, and general file-object/process ownership are still unimplemented.
   184	- [ ] Integrate a general-purpose static ELF64 process loader and execution path. The bounded allocation-free parser validates `PT_LOAD` bounds, alignment, permissions, lower-half ranges, overlaps, file bounds, and executable entry points. The diagnostic build loads the bundled static `rustix-init`, maps its stack, enters Ring 3, and tears down after exit; malformed-load paths are host-tested, but this remains a single opt-in boot probe rather than a reusable exec service. Use `.bin` for command-line programs and `.app` for GUI applications as role-based suffixes for the same underlying format. `.app` is a Rustix single-file application suffix, not an Apple/macOS app bundle; initially require application resources to be embedded or absent.
   185	- [x] Complete and validate the initial user-mode exception policy. The diagnostic runtime terminates noncritical CPL3 faults with status `128 + vector`, while kernel-origin faults and NMI/#DF/#MC remain fatal. QEMU exercises #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE from CPL3 and #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE from CPL0; this does not provide recovery for arbitrary kernel accesses or all architectural vectors.
   186	- [ ] Define user virtual-memory regions, stack bounds/guard behavior, and a minimal anonymous allocation interface such as `mmap`/`munmap` (or a documented equivalent) before running general user programs. The diagnostic init reserves its ELF segments, one-page stack, and unmapped guard in a host-tested fixed-capacity `UserRegionTable`; anonymous reservations are first-fit within a bounded lower-half window and reject overlap, overflow, invalid ranges, and capacity exhaustion. The opt-in ABI now maps one zero-filled RW/NX page per `mmap` call (requested length 1–4096) and only unmaps an exact tracked anonymous page; QEMU verifies zeroing, user write/read, stale-address `EFAULT`, and process-root teardown/frame restoration. This is a limited page-granular service, not general multi-page allocation or stack growth. Failure-injection during PTE edits, broader exhaustion/lifecycle coverage, and reusable address-space integration remain outstanding, so the item is not complete.
   187	- [ ] Complete a small, `no_std`-friendly shared userspace runtime crate for process entry, syscall wrappers, panic handling, common I/O/formatting, and a user allocator backed by the anonymous mapping interface. The `crates/rustix-user` workspace crate now supplies typed ABI-version/write/wait/exit/close/dup and one-page mmap/munmap wrappers, stable error decoding, short-write-safe output, allocation-free formatting, and best-effort panic reporting; bundled `rustix-init` uses these wrappers. Process entry support, a process heap/anonymous-map-backed allocator, and independent application-crate integration remain outstanding.

Reusable-exec failure cases and general file-object descriptor semantics remain pending alongside those features.

   192	
   193	A small controlled `init` process should start from a reproducible image, write through a descriptor, exit with a status, and be waited on by a kernel test harness. Do not claim userspace or process isolation from ring-0 tasks that merely use process-shaped structs.
   194
```

```rustix/docs/roadmap/README.md
   367	## Cross-cutting acceptance gates
   368	
   369	Every milestone should include the relevant subset of these gates:
   370	
   371	1. **Design:** documented ownership, invariants, resource limits, error semantics, and unsupported cases.
   372	2. **Tests:** host tests for pure policy and malformed/boundary input; integration tests for hardware-facing behavior.
   373	3. **Safety:** review unsafe blocks, pointer provenance/access, integer overflow, privilege boundaries, concurrency, and cleanup/rollback paths.
   374	4. **Build:** format, host tests, target check, and final ELF link as appropriate.
   375	5. **Boot/integration:** QEMU tests for changes to boot, paging, descriptors, interrupts, drivers, processes, or persistence.
   376	6. **Documentation/status:** update architecture and roadmap docs; never check off a criterion without evidence.
   377	7. **Compatibility:** claim Unix/POSIX behavior only for the exact documented subset with conformance-style tests.
   378	8. **Privilege boundaries:** test user/kernel fault separation, file ownership and special permission bits, credential confidentiality, trusted `sudo` command lookup, and recovery assumptions.
   379	9. **Resource readiness:** do not begin process, VFS-cache, or driver workloads that require dynamic allocation, active mappings, DMA, wall-clock time, or secure randomness until the corresponding service and failure behavior are validated.
   380	
   381	## Working rule
   382	
   383	Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable scaffolding. A source file, interface, or architecture document is not proof that the corresponding subsystem is operational. When a check cannot run, record the exact environment blocker and leave that acceptance gate pending.

```

```
kernel_target := "x86_64-unknown-none"

# List the common development tasks.
help:
    @just --list

# Format all Rust sources and fail if formatting changes are needed.
fmt:
    cargo fmt --all -- --check

# Check the freestanding kernel for the target architecture.
check:
    cargo check --target {{kernel_target}}

# Build the optimized kernel ELF for the target architecture.
build:
    cargo build --release --target {{kernel_target}}

# Build the optimized kernel ELF with full debug symbols for CodeLLDB.
debug-build:
    cargo build --release --target {{kernel_target}} --config profile.release.debug=true

# Create a debug-symbol-enabled Limine ISO.
debug-image: debug-build
    python3 scripts/boot.py image

# Run QEMU paused with a loopback-only GDB stub for Zed/CodeLLDB.
debug-run: debug-image
    python3 scripts/boot.py debug

# Build a pinned Limine BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO. Requires Python 3 and xorriso.
image: build
    python3 scripts/boot.py image

# Boot the ISO in QEMU's default BIOS mode and verify Crabshell's prompt.
smoke: image
    python3 scripts/boot.py smoke

# Boot the ISO with OVMF and verify ACPI MADT, CR3 transition, and prompt.
uefi-smoke: image
    python3 scripts/boot.py uefi-smoke

# Probe active owned-page mappings and TLB invalidation in QEMU, then restore the default image.
active-map-smoke:
    python3 scripts/boot.py active-map-smoke

# Probe checked HHDM access, inherited mappings, and an inactive candidate root in QEMU.
frame-smoke:
    python3 scripts/boot.py frame-smoke

# Run bundled init in Ring 3 and verify syscalls, wait status, and root teardown in QEMU.
process-smoke:
    python3 scripts/boot.py process-smoke

# Terminate Ring 3 processes on #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and verify wait/reap plus teardown in QEMU.
user-fault-smoke:
    python3 scripts/boot.py user-fault-smoke

# Exercise IRQ-safe locking, cooperative waits, timer preemption, and FPU state in OVMF.
thread-smoke:
    python3 scripts/boot.py thread-smoke

# Exercise UART and PS/2 IRQ input waking the cooperative shell in OVMF.
input-smoke: image
    python3 scripts/boot.py input-smoke

# Inject controlled exceptions in QEMU, then restore the default release image.
fault-smoke:
    python3 scripts/boot.py fault-smoke

# Run Crabshell interactively over the host terminal's serial connection.
run: image
    python3 scripts/boot.py run

# Run host-side unit tests for architecture-independent kernel and shell code.
test:
    cargo test --workspace --lib

# Run formatting, host tests, target checks, and the boot, scheduler, input, and process QEMU smokes.
verify: fmt test check smoke uefi-smoke active-map-smoke thread-smoke input-smoke fault-smoke process-smoke user-fault-smoke
```

<thinking>
I've settled on building the user runtime slice: a process entry point and an allocator backed by mmap'd pages, which should finish the remaining parts of the shared userspace runtime item. I'm also planning to move rustix-init onto that entry point and a heap-backed Vec/format, checking it with process-smoke. The main risk is that an allocator built on one-page mmap calls will be slow, so I'm starting to sketch the `UserHeap` design in rustix-user.

I'm working out the allocator's internals now: size-class slabs from 16 to 2048 bytes, with larger requests returning null. Freed blocks go onto a per-class intrusive free list, and I'm weighing a simple atomic spinlock for `GlobalAlloc` against an `unsafe impl Sync`, since the project prefers avoiding the latter.

I'm weighing how the entry point should look: either a `_start` macro or a plain `start(main)` function that exits with main's return value. I'm also considering whether the global allocator should be declared in the application crate rather than forced on everyone who links rustix-user, so I'm leaning toward the app declaring a `UserHeap` static backed by mmap pages.

I'm checking how the runtime-side expectations and the build setup for rustix-init fit together, starting with what process-smoke asserts in boot.py and how rustix-init's linker script is wired in.

I'm also noting the kernel's anonymous mmap is first-fit and munmap releases pages, so the heap pages can stay mapped for now. The rustix-init side will use the `alloc` crate via `extern crate alloc`, since no_std crates can use it once a global allocator exists. Next I want to check what process-smoke expects in boot.py and how rustix-init's build is wired.

The user-side pieces are small enough to finish cleanly: a process entry helper and an mmap-backed allocator in `rustix-user`, exercised by `rustix-init` under the existing QEMU smoke. [package]
```
name = "rustix-user"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
publish = false
license = "Apache-2.0"
description = "no_std Rustix userspace syscall wrappers"

[lib]
path = "src/lib.rs"
OUTPUT_FORMAT(elf64-x86-64)
OUTPUT_ARCH(i386:x86-64)
ENTRY(_start)

PHDRS
{
    text PT_LOAD FLAGS(5);
}

SECTIONS
{
    . = 0x40000000;

    .text ALIGN(4K) :
    {
        *(.text .text.*)
    } :text

    .rodata ALIGN(4K) :
    {
        *(.rodata .rodata.*)
    } :text

    /DISCARD/ :
    {
        *(.eh_frame .eh_frame.*)
        *(.note .note.*)
        *(.comment .comment.*)
    }
}
```

```
        asm!("ud2", options(noreturn));

            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            guard = const USER_STACK_GUARD_ADDRESS,
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack, readonly)
        );
    }

    #[cfg(rustix_user_fault_gp)]
    // SAFETY: DPL 0 vector 0x20 is intentionally invoked from Ring 3 to trigger
    // #GP before the interrupt handler can run.
    unsafe {
        asm!("int 0x20", options(nomem, nostack));
    }

    #[cfg(rustix_user_fault_de)]
    // SAFETY: The zero divisor deliberately produces user-mode #DE in QEMU.
    unsafe {
        asm!(

            "xor eax, eax",
            "xor ecx, ecx",
            "div ecx",
            out("eax") _,
            out("edx") _,
            out("ecx") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }

    loop {
        core::hint::spin_loop();
    }
```

```
#![no_std]

//! Small `no_std` wrappers for the stable Rustix syscall ABI v1.
//!
//! The raw syscall entry accepts register-sized values and never dereferences
//! them in Rust; the kernel validates all user pointers before access. Prefer
//! the typed wrappers when they match the operation being performed.

use core::arch::asm;

#[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
compile_error!("rustix-user currently supports x86_64 only");

pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = 0x0001_0000;
pub const SYS_ABI_VERSION: u64 = 0;
pub const SYS_EXIT: u64 = 1;
pub const SYS_WRITE: u64 = 2;
pub const SYS_WAIT: u64 = 3;
pub const SYS_MMAP: u64 = 4;
pub const SYS_MUNMAP: u64 = 5;
pub const SYS_CLOSE: u64 = 6;
pub const SYS_DUP: u64 = 7;
pub const USER_PAGE_SIZE: usize = 4096;

pub const STDOUT: u64 = 1;
pub const STDERR: u64 = 2;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallError {
    InvalidArgument,
    BadFileDescriptor,
    Fault,
    OutOfMemory,
    NoChild,
    Interrupted,
    Io,
    NotImplemented,
    ArgumentListTooLong,
    Overflow,
    NotSupported,
    TooManyOpenFiles,
    ResultOutOfRange,
    Unknown(i64),
}

/// Invoke one v1 syscall using the documented x86_64 register convention.
///
/// This low-level entry is safe because pointer values are passed opaquely to
/// the kernel, which validates ranges and permissions before dereferencing.
/// Prefer [`write`], [`wait`], and [`exit`] when possible.
#[inline]
pub fn syscall(number: u64, arguments: [u64; 6]) -> i64 {
    let [first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth] = arguments;
    let result: u64;
    // SAFETY: The v1 ABI assigns RAX and the six argument registers exactly as
    // declared here. Rustix's DPL-3 gate and entry stub preserve Rust's memory
    // validity invariants by treating user pointers as integers in the kernel.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "int 0x80",
            inlateout("rax") number => result,
            in("rdi") first,
            in("rsi") second,
            in("rdx") third,
            in("r10") fourth,
            in("r8") fifth,
            in("r9") sixth,
            lateout("rcx") _,
            lateout("r11") _,
        );
    }
    result as i64
}

pub fn abi_version() -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    decode_result(syscall(SYS_ABI_VERSION, [0; 6]))
}

/// Write one buffer to a v1 file descriptor. A successful short write is valid.
pub fn write(file_descriptor: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError> {
    let result = decode_result(syscall(
        SYS_WRITE,
        [
            file_descriptor,
            bytes.as_ptr() as u64,
            bytes.len() as u64,
            0,
            0,
            0,
        ],
    ))?;
    usize::try_from(result).map_err(|_| SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange)
}

/// Close a process-local descriptor.
pub fn close(file_descriptor: u64) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    match decode_result(syscall(SYS_CLOSE, [file_descriptor, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]))? {
        0 => Ok(()),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange),
    }
}

/// Duplicate a descriptor into the lowest available descriptor slot.
pub fn dup(file_descriptor: u64) -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    decode_result(syscall(SYS_DUP, [file_descriptor, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]))
}

/// A single page returned by the anonymous mapping syscall.
///
/// The pointer is raw: callers must not dereference it unless they uphold the
/// normal pointer validity and aliasing requirements. `munmap` consumes the
/// handle so safe code cannot accidentally release the same mapping twice.
pub struct MappedRegion {
    address: u64,
}

impl MappedRegion {
    pub const fn address(&self) -> u64 {
        self.address
    }

    pub const fn length(&self) -> usize {
        USER_PAGE_SIZE
    }

    pub const fn as_mut_ptr(&self) -> *mut u8 {
        self.address as *mut u8
    }
}

/// Map one zero-filled read/write, non-executable anonymous user page.
///
/// `requested_length` must be in `1..=USER_PAGE_SIZE`; the kernel maps one page
/// and returns a `MappedRegion` whose length is exactly one page.
pub fn mmap(requested_length: usize) -> Result<MappedRegion, SyscallError> {
    let address = decode_result(syscall(SYS_MMAP, [requested_length as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]))?;
    Ok(MappedRegion { address })
}

/// Unmap one page previously returned by [`mmap`].
pub fn munmap(region: MappedRegion) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    match decode_result(syscall(
        SYS_MUNMAP,
        [region.address, USER_PAGE_SIZE as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    ))? {
        0 => Ok(()),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange),
    }
}

/// Write all bytes, retrying successful short writes.
///
/// A zero-length write before the buffer is complete is reported as [`SyscallError::Io`]
/// to avoid an infinite loop.
pub fn write_all(file_descriptor: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    write_all_with(bytes, |remaining| write(file_descriptor, remaining))
}

/// Format directly to a file descriptor without allocating.
///
/// Formatting stops at the first write failure and returns its syscall error.
pub fn write_fmt(
    file_descriptor: u64,
    arguments: core::fmt::Arguments<'_>,
) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    write_fmt_with(arguments, |bytes| write(file_descriptor, bytes))
}

/// Best-effort panic reporting to stderr followed by process exit status 127.
pub fn panic_exit(info: &core::panic::PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    let _ = write_fmt(STDERR, format_args!("rustix: panic: {info}\n"));
    exit(127)
}

fn write_all_with<W>(mut remaining: &[u8], mut write: W) -> Result<(), SyscallError>
where
    W: FnMut(&[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>,
{
    while !remaining.is_empty() {
        let written = write(remaining)?;
        if written == 0 {
            return Err(SyscallError::Io);
        }
        if written > remaining.len() {
            return Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange);
        }
        remaining = &remaining[written..];
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn write_fmt_with<W>(arguments: core::fmt::Arguments<'_>, write: W) -> Result<(), SyscallError>
where
    W: FnMut(&[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>,
{
    let mut output = SyscallFormatter { write, error: None };
    match core::fmt::write(&mut output, arguments) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(_) => Err(output.error.unwrap_or(SyscallError::Io)),
    }
}

struct SyscallFormatter<W> {
    write: W,
    error: Option<SyscallError>,
}

impl<W> core::fmt::Write for SyscallFormatter<W>
where
    W: FnMut(&[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>,
{
    fn write_str(&mut self, text: &str) -> core::fmt::Result {
        match write_all_with(text.as_bytes(), |remaining| (self.write)(remaining)) {
            Ok(()) => Ok(()),
            Err(error) => {
                self.error = Some(error);
                Err(core::fmt::Error)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Wait for a child and optionally copy its signed 32-bit status to `status`.
///
/// The current kernel probe supports already-exited children; a running child
/// returns [`SyscallError::NotSupported`] until blocking process scheduling is
/// integrated.
pub fn wait(child_pid: u64, status: Option<&mut i32>) -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    let status_address = status.map_or(0, |status| status as *mut i32 as u64);
    decode_result(syscall(SYS_WAIT, [child_pid, status_address, 0, 0, 0, 0]))
}

/// Exit the current process. The kernel ABI does not return from a successful exit.
pub fn exit(status: i32) -> ! {
    let _ = syscall(SYS_EXIT, [status as u32 as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
    loop {
        core::hint::spin_loop();
    }
}

fn decode_result(result: i64) -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    if result >= 0 {
        return Ok(result as u64);
    }
    match result.checked_neg() {
        Some(1) => Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument),
        Some(2) => Err(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor),
        Some(3) => Err(SyscallError::Fault),
        Some(4) => Err(SyscallError::OutOfMemory),
        Some(5) => Err(SyscallError::NoChild),
        Some(6) => Err(SyscallError::Interrupted),
        Some(7) => Err(SyscallError::Io),
        Some(8) => Err(SyscallError::NotImplemented),
        Some(9) => Err(SyscallError::ArgumentListTooLong),
        Some(10) => Err(SyscallError::Overflow),
        Some(11) => Err(SyscallError::NotSupported),
        Some(12) => Err(SyscallError::TooManyOpenFiles),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::Unknown(result)),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{decode_result, write_all_with, write_fmt_with, SyscallError, ABI_VERSION};

    #[test]
    fn decodes_nonnegative_results_and_stable_v1_errors() {
        assert_eq!(decode_result(ABI_VERSION as i64), Ok(ABI_VERSION));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(0), Ok(0));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-3), Err(SyscallError::Fault));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-5), Err(SyscallError::NoChild));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-11), Err(SyscallError::NotSupported));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-12), Err(SyscallError::TooManyOpenFiles));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-13), Err(SyscallError::Unknown(-13)));
        assert_eq!(
            decode_result(i64::MIN),
            Err(SyscallError::Unknown(i64::MIN))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_all_retries_short_writes_until_complete() {
        let mut output = [0; 5];
        let mut output_length = 0;
        let result = write_all_with(b"hello", |remaining| {
            let count = remaining.len().min(2);
            output[output_length..output_length + count].copy_from_slice(&remaining[..count]);
            output_length += count;
            Ok(count)
        });
        assert_eq!(result, Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(&output[..output_length], b"hello");
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_all_rejects_zero_and_impossible_write_counts() {
        assert_eq!(write_all_with(b"x", |_| Ok(0)), Err(SyscallError::Io));
        assert_eq!(
            write_all_with(b"x", |_| Ok(2)),
            Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            write_all_with(b"x", |_| Err(SyscallError::Fault)),
            Err(SyscallError::Fault)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn formatting_is_allocation_free_and_preserves_write_errors() {
        let mut output = [0; 8];
        let mut output_length = 0;
        let result = write_fmt_with(format_args!("value={}", 42), |remaining| {
            let count = remaining.len().min(3);
            output[output_length..output_length + count].copy_from_slice(&remaining[..count]);
            output_length += count;
            Ok(count)
        });
        assert_eq!(result, Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(&output[..output_length], b"value=42");

        assert_eq!(
            write_fmt_with(format_args!("failure"), |_| Err(SyscallError::Fault)),
            Err(SyscallError::Fault)
        );
    }
}

fn main() {

    let runtime_source = root.join("crates/rustix-user/src/lib.rs");
    let runtime_manifest = root.join("crates/rustix-user/Cargo.toml");
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", source.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", linker_script.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", runtime_source.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", runtime_manifest.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=RUSTC");

    if env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").as_deref() != Ok("none") {
        return;
    }

    let runtime = out_dir.join("librustix_user.rlib");

        .current_dir(&root)
        .arg("--crate-name")
        .arg("rustix_user")
        .arg("--edition=2021")
        .arg("--crate-type=rlib")
        .arg("--target=x86_64-unknown-none")
        .arg("-Cpanic=abort")
        .arg("-Copt-level=2")
        .arg("-Ccode-model=small")
        .arg("-Crelocation-model=static")
        .arg("-Ctarget-feature=-avx,-avx2,-avx512f")
        .arg(&runtime_source)
        .arg("--out-dir")
        .arg(&out_dir)
        .status()
        .expect("failed to invoke rustc for the rustix-user runtime");
    assert!(
        runtime_status.success(),
        "failed to build rustix-user runtime"
    );

    let output = out_dir.join("rustix-init.elf");
    let linker_arg = format!("-T{}", linker_script.display());
    let mut command = Command::new(rustc);
    command
        .current_dir(&root)
        .arg("--crate-name")
        .arg("rustix_init")
        .arg("--edition=2021")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_fault_probe)")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_user_fault_ud)")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_user_fault_page)")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_user_fault_gp)")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_user_fault_de)")
        .arg("--crate-type=bin")
        .arg("--target=x86_64-unknown-none")
        .arg("-Cpanic=abort")
        .arg("-Copt-level=2")
        .arg("-Ccode-model=small")
        .arg("-Crelocation-model=static")
        .arg("-Ctarget-feature=-avx,-avx2,-avx512f")
        .arg(format!("-Clink-arg={linker_arg}"))
        .arg("-Clink-arg=--build-id=none")
        .arg("--extern")
        .arg(format!("rustix_user={}", runtime.display()))
        .arg(&source)
        .arg("-o")
        .arg(&output);
    let fault_modes = [
        ("CARGO_FEATURE_PROBE_USER_FAULT", "rustix_user_fault_ud"),
        (
            "CARGO_FEATURE_PROBE_USER_PAGE_FAULT",
            "rustix_user_fault_page",
        ),
        (
            "CARGO_FEATURE_PROBE_USER_GENERAL_PROTECTION",
            "rustix_user_fault_gp",
        ),
        (
            "CARGO_FEATURE_PROBE_USER_DIVIDE_ERROR",
            "rustix_user_fault_de",
        ),
    ];
    let enabled_fault_modes: Vec<_> = fault_modes
        .iter()
        .filter(|(feature, _)| env::var_os(feature).is_some())
        .collect();
    assert!(
        enabled_fault_modes.len() <= 1,
        "only one user-fault probe feature may be enabled"
    );
    if let Some((_, mode)) = enabled_fault_modes.first() {
        command
            .arg("--cfg=rustix_fault_probe")
            .arg(format!("--cfg={mode}"));
    }
    let status = command
        .status()
        .expect("failed to invoke rustc for the init payload");
    assert!(
        status.success(),
        "failed to build the rustix-init ELF payload"
    );
}
```

```
def process_smoke_workflow(timeout: int) -> None:
    failure: BuildError | OSError | subprocess.SubprocessError | None = None
    try:
        build_kernel(("probe-user-process",))
        build_image()
        smoke_test(timeout)
        serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
        output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
        markers = (
            "bundled init ELF validated:",
            "rustix-init: hello from ring 3",
            "rustix-init: invalid user buffer returned EFAULT",
            "rustix-init: wait copied child status 7 after EFAULT retry",
            "rustix-init: wait returned ENOTSUP for a running child",
            "init process exited with status 42 and was reaped by kernel wait",
            "Ring 3 init passed: write/EFAULT/ready-child wait/running-child ENOTSUP/exit syscalls, kernel wait, and process-root teardown",
        )
        missing = [marker for marker in markers if marker not in output]
        if missing:
            raise BuildError(
                "QEMU did not report successful process-root validation; missing serial markers: "
                + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
                + f"\nSerial output:\n{output}"
            )
        print("QEMU Ring 3 init write/EFAULT/ready-child wait/running-child ENOTSUP/exit, kernel wait, and process-root teardown passed.")
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        failure = error

    try:
        build_kernel()
        build_image()
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as restore_error:
        if failure is not None:
            raise BuildError(
                f"process-root workflow failed ({failure}); restoring the default image "
                f"also failed ({restore_error})"
            ) from restore_error
        raise

    if failure is not None:
        raise BuildError(
            f"process-root workflow failed; the default release image was restored: {failure}"
        ) from failure
    print("Restored the default release kernel and ISO after the Ring 3 init test.")
```

```
#![no_std]

//! Small `no_std` wrappers for the stable Rustix syscall ABI v1.
//!
//! The raw syscall entry accepts register-sized values and never dereferences
//! them in Rust; the kernel validates all user pointers before access. Prefer
//! the typed wrappers when they match the operation being performed.

use core::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout};
use core::arch::asm;
use core::cell::UnsafeCell;
use core::ptr::{null_mut, NonNull};
use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

#[cfg(not(target_arch = "x86_64"))]
compile_error!("rustix-user currently supports x86_64 only");

pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = 0x0001_0000;
pub const SYS_ABI_VERSION: u64 = 0;
pub const SYS_EXIT: u64 = 1;
pub const SYS_WRITE: u64 = 2;
pub const SYS_WAIT: u64 = 3;
pub const SYS_MMAP: u64 = 4;
pub const SYS_MUNMAP: u64 = 5;
pub const SYS_CLOSE: u64 = 6;
pub const SYS_DUP: u64 = 7;
pub const USER_PAGE_SIZE: usize = 4096;

pub const STDOUT: u64 = 1;
pub const STDERR: u64 = 2;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallError {
    InvalidArgument,
    BadFileDescriptor,
    Fault,
    OutOfMemory,
    NoChild,
    Interrupted,
    Io,
    NotImplemented,
    ArgumentListTooLong,
    Overflow,
    NotSupported,
    TooManyOpenFiles,
    ResultOutOfRange,
    Unknown(i64),
}

/// Invoke one v1 syscall using the documented x86_64 register convention.
///
/// This low-level entry is safe because pointer values are passed opaquely to
/// the kernel, which validates ranges and permissions before dereferencing.
/// Prefer [`write`], [`wait`], and [`exit`] when possible.
#[inline]
pub fn syscall(number: u64, arguments: [u64; 6]) -> i64 {
    let [first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth] = arguments;
    let result: u64;
    // SAFETY: The v1 ABI assigns RAX and the six argument registers exactly as
    // declared here. Rustix's DPL-3 gate and entry stub preserve Rust's memory
    // validity invariants by treating user pointers as integers in the kernel.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "int 0x80",
            inlateout("rax") number => result,
            in("rdi") first,
            in("rsi") second,
            in("rdx") third,
            in("r10") fourth,
            in("r8") fifth,
            in("r9") sixth,
            lateout("rcx") _,
            lateout("r11") _,
        );
    }
    result as i64
}

pub fn abi_version() -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    decode_result(syscall(SYS_ABI_VERSION, [0; 6]))
}

/// Write one buffer to a v1 file descriptor. A successful short write is valid.
pub fn write(file_descriptor: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError> {
    let result = decode_result(syscall(
        SYS_WRITE,
        [
            file_descriptor,
            bytes.as_ptr() as u64,
            bytes.len() as u64,
            0,
            0,
            0,
        ],
    ))?;
    usize::try_from(result).map_err(|_| SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange)
}

/// Close a process-local descriptor.
pub fn close(file_descriptor: u64) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    match decode_result(syscall(SYS_CLOSE, [file_descriptor, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]))? {
        0 => Ok(()),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange),
    }
}

/// Duplicate a descriptor into the lowest available descriptor slot.
pub fn dup(file_descriptor: u64) -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    decode_result(syscall(SYS_DUP, [file_descriptor, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]))
}

/// A single page returned by the anonymous mapping syscall.
///
/// The pointer is raw: callers must not dereference it unless they uphold the
/// normal pointer validity and aliasing requirements. `munmap` consumes the
/// handle so safe code cannot accidentally release the same mapping twice.
pub struct MappedRegion {
    address: u64,
}

impl MappedRegion {
    pub const fn address(&self) -> u64 {
        self.address
    }

    pub const fn length(&self) -> usize {
        USER_PAGE_SIZE
    }

    pub const fn as_mut_ptr(&self) -> *mut u8 {
        self.address as *mut u8
    }
}

/// Map one zero-filled read/write, non-executable anonymous user page.
///
/// `requested_length` must be in `1..=USER_PAGE_SIZE`; the kernel maps one page
/// and returns a `MappedRegion` whose length is exactly one page.
pub fn mmap(requested_length: usize) -> Result<MappedRegion, SyscallError> {
    let address = decode_result(syscall(SYS_MMAP, [requested_length as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]))?;
    Ok(MappedRegion { address })
}

/// Unmap one page previously returned by [`mmap`].
pub fn munmap(region: MappedRegion) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    match decode_result(syscall(
        SYS_MUNMAP,
        [region.address, USER_PAGE_SIZE as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    ))? {
        0 => Ok(()),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange),
    }
}

/// Write all bytes, retrying successful short writes.
///
/// A zero-length write before the buffer is complete is reported as [`SyscallError::Io`]
/// to avoid an infinite loop.
pub fn write_all(file_descriptor: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    write_all_with(bytes, |remaining| write(file_descriptor, remaining))
}

/// Format directly to a file descriptor without allocating.
///
/// Formatting stops at the first write failure and returns its syscall error.
pub fn write_fmt(
    file_descriptor: u64,
    arguments: core::fmt::Arguments<'_>,
) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    write_fmt_with(arguments, |bytes| write(file_descriptor, bytes))
}

/// Best-effort panic reporting to stderr followed by process exit status 127.
pub fn panic_exit(info: &core::panic::PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    let _ = write_fmt(STDERR, format_args!("rustix: panic: {info}\n"));
    exit(127)
}

fn write_all_with<W>(mut remaining: &[u8], mut write: W) -> Result<(), SyscallError>
where
    W: FnMut(&[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>,
{
    while !remaining.is_empty() {
        let written = write(remaining)?;
        if written == 0 {
            return Err(SyscallError::Io);
        }
        if written > remaining.len() {
            return Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange);
        }
        remaining = &remaining[written..];
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn write_fmt_with<W>(arguments: core::fmt::Arguments<'_>, write: W) -> Result<(), SyscallError>
where
    W: FnMut(&[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>,
{
    let mut output = SyscallFormatter { write, error: None };
    match core::fmt::write(&mut output, arguments) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(_) => Err(output.error.unwrap_or(SyscallError::Io)),
    }
}

struct SyscallFormatter<W> {
    write: W,
    error: Option<SyscallError>,
}

impl<W> core::fmt::Write for SyscallFormatter<W>
where
    W: FnMut(&[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>,
{
    fn write_str(&mut self, text: &str) -> core::fmt::Result {
        match write_all_with(text.as_bytes(), |remaining| (self.write)(remaining)) {
            Ok(()) => Ok(()),
            Err(error) => {
                self.error = Some(error);
                Err(core::fmt::Error)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Wait for a child and optionally copy its signed 32-bit status to `status`.
///
/// The current kernel probe supports already-exited children; a running child
/// returns [`SyscallError::NotSupported`] until blocking process scheduling is
/// integrated.
pub fn wait(child_pid: u64, status: Option<&mut i32>) -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    let status_address = status.map_or(0, |status| status as *mut i32 as u64);
    decode_result(syscall(SYS_WAIT, [child_pid, status_address, 0, 0, 0, 0]))
}

/// Exit the current process. The kernel ABI does not return from a successful exit.
pub fn exit(status: i32) -> ! {
    let _ = syscall(SYS_EXIT, [status as u32 as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
    loop {
        core::hint::spin_loop();
    }
}

/// Run a process `main` and exit with its status.
///
/// Applications define `_start` as a call to this helper so `main` can return
/// normally instead of managing the exit syscall itself.
pub fn run_main(main: fn() -> i32) -> ! {
    exit(main())
}

pub const HEAP_PAGE_SIZE: usize = USER_PAGE_SIZE;
const HEAP_MIN_BLOCK: usize = 16;
const HEAP_MAX_BLOCK: usize = 2048;
const HEAP_CLASS_COUNT: usize = 8;

/// Source of page-sized, page-aligned, zeroed read/write memory for the heap.
pub trait PageSource {
    fn allocate_page(&mut self) -> Option<NonNull<u8>>;
}

/// Page source backed by one `mmap` syscall per page. Pages are never returned.
pub struct MmapPages;

impl PageSource for MmapPages {
    fn allocate_page(&mut self) -> Option<NonNull<u8>> {
        let region = mmap(1).ok()?;
        if region.address() % HEAP_PAGE_SIZE as u64 != 0 {
            return None;
        }
        NonNull::new(region.as_mut_ptr())
    }
}

/// Power-of-two size-class allocator for requests up to 2048 bytes.
///
/// Each class keeps an intrusive free list. Blocks are carved from whole pages,
/// so a block whose size is at least its alignment is naturally aligned. Freed
/// blocks are reused by their class; pages are never returned to the kernel.
/// Requests larger than 2048 bytes or aligned above 4096 bytes return null.
pub struct SizeClassHeap<P> {
    pages: P,
    free: [Option<NonNull<FreeBlock>>; HEAP_CLASS_COUNT],
}

struct FreeBlock {
    next: Option<NonNull<FreeBlock>>,
}

impl<P: PageSource> SizeClassHeap<P> {
    pub const fn new(pages: P) -> Self {
        Self {
            pages,
            free: [None; HEAP_CLASS_COUNT],
        }
    }

    /// Return a block satisfying `layout`, or null when the request is out of
    /// range or no page can be obtained.
    pub fn allocate(&mut self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        let Some(class) = size_class(layout) else {
            return null_mut();
        };
        if self.free[class].is_none() && !self.refill(class) {
            return null_mut();
        }
        let Some(block) = self.free[class] else {
            return null_mut();
        };
        // SAFETY: Every node on a free list was written by `refill` or
        // `deallocate` as an unused, exclusively owned block of this heap.
        self.free[class] = unsafe { block.as_ref().next };
        block.cast::<u8>().as_ptr()
    }

    /// Return a block to its size class.
    ///
    /// `pointer` must come from [`SizeClassHeap::allocate`] on this heap with the
    /// same `layout`, and must not be used afterward.
    pub fn deallocate(&mut self, pointer: NonNull<u8>, layout: Layout) {
        let Some(class) = size_class(layout) else {
            return;
        };
        let node = pointer.cast::<FreeBlock>();
        // SAFETY: The caller returns a block previously handed out for this
        // class, so it is at least `HEAP_MIN_BLOCK` bytes, suitably aligned,
        // and no longer in use.
        unsafe {
            node.as_ptr().write(FreeBlock {
                next: self.free[class],
            });
        }
        self.free[class] = Some(node);
    }

    fn refill(&mut self, class: usize) -> bool {
        let Some(page) = self.pages.allocate_page() else {
            return false;
        };
        let block_size = HEAP_MIN_BLOCK << class;
        for index in (0..HEAP_PAGE_SIZE / block_size).rev() {
            // SAFETY: `page` is an owned, page-sized mapping and `index` keeps
            // `offset + block_size` within it. Page alignment and the power-of-two
            // block size make the node aligned for `FreeBlock`.
            let node = unsafe { page.as_ptr().add(index * block_size) }.cast::<FreeBlock>();
            // SAFETY: `node` is inside the page and is not yet visible to any user.
            unsafe {
                node.write(FreeBlock {
                    next: self.free[class],
                });
            }
            self.free[class] = NonNull::new(node);
        }
        true
    }
}

fn size_class(layout: Layout) -> Option<usize> {
    if layout.align() > HEAP_PAGE_SIZE {
        return None;
    }
    let block = layout
        .size()
        .max(layout.align())
        .max(HEAP_MIN_BLOCK)
        .checked_next_power_of_two()?;
    if block > HEAP_MAX_BLOCK {
        return None;
    }
    Some((block / HEAP_MIN_BLOCK).trailing_zeros() as usize)
}

/// Global allocator for Rustix user processes.
///
/// Declare one with `#[global_allocator]` in an application that uses `alloc`.
/// Access is serialized by a spin lock, so the type may be shared safely.
pub struct UserAllocator {
    locked: AtomicBool,
    heap: UnsafeCell<SizeClassHeap<MmapPages>>,
}

// SAFETY: `heap` is only accessed inside `with_heap`, which holds `locked` for the
// full duration of the access, so there is never more than one live `&mut` to it.
unsafe impl Sync for UserAllocator {}

impl UserAllocator {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            locked: AtomicBool::new(false),
            heap: UnsafeCell::new(SizeClassHeap::new(MmapPages)),
        }
    }

    fn with_heap<R>(&self, operation: impl FnOnce(&mut SizeClassHeap<MmapPages>) -> R) -> R {
        while self
            .locked
            .compare_exchange_weak(false, true, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Relaxed)
            .is_err()
        {
            core::hint::spin_loop();
        }
        // SAFETY: The acquired `locked` flag grants exclusive access until the
        // release store below, and the reference does not escape `operation`.
        let result = operation(unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() });
        self.locked.store(false, Ordering::Release);
        result
    }
}

// SAFETY: Allocation and deallocation follow the `GlobalAlloc` contract: blocks
// returned by `alloc` satisfy `layout`, and `dealloc` is only given blocks from
// the same size class.
unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for UserAllocator {
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        self.with_heap(|heap| heap.allocate(layout))
    }

    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
        if let Some(pointer) = NonNull::new(pointer) {
            self.with_heap(|heap| heap.deallocate(pointer, layout));
        }
    }
}

fn decode_result(result: i64) -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    if result >= 0 {
        return Ok(result as u64);
    }
    match result.checked_neg() {
        Some(1) => Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument),
        Some(2) => Err(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor),
        Some(3) => Err(SyscallError::Fault),
        Some(4) => Err(SyscallError::OutOfMemory),
        Some(5) => Err(SyscallError::NoChild),
        Some(6) => Err(SyscallError::Interrupted),
        Some(7) => Err(SyscallError::Io),
        Some(8) => Err(SyscallError::NotImplemented),
        Some(9) => Err(SyscallError::ArgumentListTooLong),
        Some(10) => Err(SyscallError::Overflow),
        Some(11) => Err(SyscallError::NotSupported),
        Some(12) => Err(SyscallError::TooManyOpenFiles),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::Unknown(result)),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod heap_tests {
    use super::{PageSource, SizeClassHeap, HEAP_PAGE_SIZE};
    use core::alloc::Layout;
    use core::ptr::NonNull;

    #[repr(align(4096))]
    struct Page([u8; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]);

    struct Arena<'a> {
        pages: &'a mut [Page],
        next: usize,
    }

    impl PageSource for Arena<'_> {
        fn allocate_page(&mut self) -> Option<NonNull<u8>> {
            let page = self.pages.get_mut(self.next)?;
            self.next += 1;
            NonNull::new(page.0.as_mut_ptr())
        }
    }

    fn arena(pages: &mut [Page]) -> SizeClassHeap<Arena<'_>> {
        SizeClassHeap::new(Arena { pages, next: 0 })
    }

    #[test]
    fn rounds_to_aligned_blocks_and_reuses_freed_blocks() {
        let mut storage: [Page; 2] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(40, 8).unwrap();
        let first = heap.allocate(layout);
        assert!(!first.is_null());
        assert_eq!(first as usize % 64, 0);
        heap.deallocate(NonNull::new(first).unwrap(), layout);
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), first);
    }

    #[test]
    fn honors_large_alignment_within_a_page() {
        let mut storage: [Page; 1] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(16, 1024).unwrap();
        let block = heap.allocate(layout);
        assert!(!block.is_null());
        assert_eq!(block as usize % 1024, 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_oversized_overaligned_and_exhausted_requests() {
        let mut storage: [Page; 1] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
        assert!(heap
            .allocate(Layout::from_size_align(2049, 8).unwrap())
            .is_null());
        assert!(heap
            .allocate(Layout::from_size_align(8, 8192).unwrap())
            .is_null());
        // One page holds two 2048-byte blocks; the third needs a page the arena lacks.
        let max = Layout::from_size_align(2048, 8).unwrap();
        assert!(!heap.allocate(max).is_null());
        assert!(!heap.allocate(max).is_null());
        assert!(heap.allocate(max).is_null());
    }

    #[test]
    fn keeps_size_classes_separate() {
        let mut storage: [Page; 2] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
        let small = Layout::from_size_align(16, 16).unwrap();
        let large = Layout::from_size_align(512, 16).unwrap();
        let small_block = heap.allocate(small);
        heap.deallocate(NonNull::new(small_block).unwrap(), small);
        let large_block = heap.allocate(large);
        assert_ne!(large_block, small_block);
        assert!(!large_block.is_null());
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{decode_result, write_all_with, write_fmt_with, SyscallError, ABI_VERSION};

    #[test]
    fn decodes_nonnegative_results_and_stable_v1_errors() {
        assert_eq!(decode_result(ABI_VERSION as i64), Ok(ABI_VERSION));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(0), Ok(0));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-3), Err(SyscallError::Fault));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-5), Err(SyscallError::NoChild));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-11), Err(SyscallError::NotSupported));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-12), Err(SyscallError::TooManyOpenFiles));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-13), Err(SyscallError::Unknown(-13)));
        assert_eq!(
            decode_result(i64::MIN),
            Err(SyscallError::Unknown(i64::MIN))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_all_retries_short_writes_until_complete() {
        let mut output = [0; 5];
        let mut output_length = 0;
        let result = write_all_with(b"hello", |remaining| {
            let count = remaining.len().min(2);
            output[output_length..output_length + count].copy_from_slice(&remaining[..count]);
            output_length += count;
            Ok(count)
        });
        assert_eq!(result, Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(&output[..output_length], b"hello");
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_all_rejects_zero_and_impossible_write_counts() {
        assert_eq!(write_all_with(b"x", |_| Ok(0)), Err(SyscallError::Io));
        assert_eq!(
            write_all_with(b"x", |_| Ok(2)),
            Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            write_all_with(b"x", |_| Err(SyscallError::Fault)),
            Err(SyscallError::Fault)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn formatting_is_allocation_free_and_preserves_write_errors() {
        let mut output = [0; 8];
        let mut output_length = 0;
        let result = write_fmt_with(format_args!("value={}", 42), |remaining| {
            let count = remaining.len().min(3);
            output[output_length..output_length + count].copy_from_slice(&remaining[..count]);
            output_length += count;
            Ok(count)
        });
        assert_eq!(result, Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(&output[..output_length], b"value=42");

        assert_eq!(
            write_fmt_with(format_args!("failure"), |_| Err(SyscallError::Fault)),
            Err(SyscallError::Fault)
        );
    }
}
```

```
#[cfg(rustix_fault_probe)]
fn trigger_user_fault() -> ! {
    #[cfg(rustix_user_fault_ud)]
    // SAFETY: This payload variant deliberately raises user-mode #UD in QEMU.
    unsafe {
        asm!("ud2", options(noreturn));
    }

    #[cfg(rustix_user_fault_page)]
    // SAFETY: The diagnostic process maps one stack page at USER_STACK_BASE;
    // this reads the immediately preceding unmapped guard page from Ring 3.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "mov rax, {guard}",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            guard = const USER_STACK_GUARD_ADDRESS,
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack, readonly)
        );
    }

    #[cfg(rustix_user_fault_gp)]
    // SAFETY: DPL 0 vector 0x20 is intentionally invoked from Ring 3 to trigger
    // #GP before the interrupt handler can run.
    unsafe {
        asm!("int 0x20", options(nomem, nostack));
    }

    #[cfg(rustix_user_fault_de)]
    // SAFETY: The zero divisor deliberately produces user-mode #DE in QEMU.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "xor edx, edx",
            "xor eax, eax",
            "xor ecx, ecx",
            "div ecx",
            out("eax") _,
            out("edx") _,
            out("ecx") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }

    loop {
        core::hint::spin_loop();
    }
}

#[inline]
fn exit(status: i32) -> ! {
    rustix_user::exit(status)
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    rustix_user::panic_exit(info)
}
```

```
## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI

Userspace begins only after page tables, exception handling, scheduling, and controlled memory allocation are trustworthy. The syscall ABI is a product interface and must not emerge accidentally from internal functions. Milestone 3's single-vCPU IRQ-safe locking and timer-preemption gate is locally validated; this enables scheduler progress but does not by itself make user code isolated or safe. SMP remains outside this milestone.

### Planned work

- [x] Decide and document the initial x86_64 user-entry/syscall mechanism, register convention, selector/MSR setup, per-CPU state requirements, and safe return path. The design uses a DPL-3 `int $0x80` gate and validated `IRETQ`, with no syscall MSRs or `SWAPGS`. Vector `0x80` is excluded from the device allocator; the GDT installs asserted Ring 3 selectors, and the gate saves GPR/x87/SSE state and sanitizes return flags. The opt-in process probe exercises entry/return and mapping-aware return checks; it uses the static bootstrap entry stack and is not general process scheduling. Revisit the entry model if per-process stacks or SMP requirements change.
- [x] Define per-process address-space construction without deep-cloning the entire kernel page-table tree for every process. The design shares validated supervisor-only upper-half subtrees, keeps lower-half tables and user frames process-owned, and specifies kernel-owner lifetime, teardown, permission, and local TLB rules. Implementation and validation remain pending.
- [x] Complete the initial user/kernel page-permission and process-owned address-space path, including teardown and local TLB invalidation rules. The implementation shares validated supervisor-only kernel entries, maps/unmaps private lower-half user frames, retains executable/writable metadata, validates the initial entry and writable NX stack, and destroys the root only after switching away. Host tests cover ownership and rollback; `just verify` validates one activation/return/teardown cycle and frame-count restoration in QEMU. General concurrent process management, per-process kernel stacks, curated kernel mappings, and broader isolation guarantees remain pending.
- [x] Complete copy-in/copy-out semantics for the initial implemented syscall set. Frame-token-based helpers preflight ranges and permissions; bounded `write` and ready-child `wait` use them. Host tests cover cross-page copies, permissions, partial writes, and descriptor errors; `just process-smoke` verifies invalid write/status pointers return `-EFAULT` without kernel corruption or consuming the exited child, and returns `-ENOTSUP` for a running child. QEMU fault smokes verify CPL3 termination and fatal CPL0 separation for #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE. Blocking wait and memory-transfer semantics for future syscalls remain pending.
- [x] Specify v1 version discovery, initial syscall numbers/argument meanings, fixed-width layouts, negative error encoding, bounded partial-write/copy behavior, wait semantics, no-restart policy, and append-only compatibility before exposing calls. The contract is documented in `docs/architecture/syscall-abi.md`; host-tested decoding and the dedicated gate/stub are implemented. The diagnostic path exercises ABI-version, descriptor-authorized write, close/dup, wait for an exited child, one-page mmap/munmap, and exit; a running child returns `ENOTSUP` until blocking wait is integrated. Future read/open, general file-object semantics, signals, and clocks need implementation/specification.
- [ ] Complete process lifecycle and descriptor-table semantics: create/load, exit, wait, close, duplication/inheritance, and cleanup. The diagnostic path binds exit/reap to the process root and implements userspace wait for already-exited children with status copyout-before-reap; QEMU uses kernel-seeded exited/running child fixtures to verify invalid status pointers leave a zombie waitable and running-child wait returns `ENOTSUP`. The fixed-capacity table now inherits console stream handles on spawn, supports close/dup with lowest-free descriptor allocation, clears handles on exit, and returns `EMFILE` on exhaustion; host tests cover defaults, inheritance, duplicate independence, invalid/closed entries, slot reuse, capacity, and exit cleanup, while `just process-smoke` exercises dup/write/close from Ring 3. Child creation tied to executable roots, blocking scheduler waits, per-process kernel stacks, and general file-object/process ownership are still unimplemented.
- [ ] Integrate a general-purpose static ELF64 process loader and execution path. The bounded allocation-free parser validates `PT_LOAD` bounds, alignment, permissions, lower-half ranges, overlaps, file bounds, and executable entry points. The diagnostic build loads the bundled static `rustix-init`, maps its stack, enters Ring 3, and tears down after exit; malformed-load paths are host-tested, but this remains a single opt-in boot probe rather than a reusable exec service. Use `.bin` for command-line programs and `.app` for GUI applications as role-based suffixes for the same underlying format. `.app` is a Rustix single-file application suffix, not an Apple/macOS app bundle; initially require application resources to be embedded or absent.
- [x] Complete and validate the initial user-mode exception policy. The diagnostic runtime terminates noncritical CPL3 faults with status `128 + vector`, while kernel-origin faults and NMI/#DF/#MC remain fatal. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.
```

```docs/architecture/syscall-abi.md
    57	The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.

    61	### Static ELF64 image validation and page initialization (partial)
    62	
    63	`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It bounds the program-header count, load-segment count, and total mapped pages; checks file and virtual arithmetic, page alignment and `p_align` congruence, lower-half canonical ranges, non-overlapping page spans, readable segment flags, W^X, and that the entry point lies in a non-writable executable `PT_LOAD`. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` allocates, populates, cache-selects, and maps every load page into an inactive process root.     64	
    65	## ABI decisions still pending beyond v1
    66	
    67	The initial v1 versioning, error encoding, syscall numbers, register-level request decoding, and assembly-matched syscall context layout are implemented in `src/syscall.rs`. The diagnostic `int 0x80` path sanitizes return frames and serves ABI-version, bounded descriptor-authorized write, close/dup, wait-for-exited-child, one-page mmap/munmap, and exit calls; invalid unmapped write/status buffers return `EFAULT` without corrupting the process or consuming a waitable child. `src/process.rs` provides fixed-capacity identity/exit-state policy, and the diagnostic kernel harness performs a nonblocking kernel-side wait/reap after the user-entry trampoline returns. The userspace `wait` call can reap an already-exited child; it returns `ENOTSUP` for a running child because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. Status copyout is frame-token-based and happens before reaping, while child creation and scheduler integration are not implemented. The fixed-capacity process table now tracks stdout/stderr console handles, child inheritance, duplicate slots, close, exit cleanup, and bounded-table exhaustion; these are not general file objects, and there is no read/open support. User faults are process-terminating only while the opt-in callback is installed; QEMU covers CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and kernel-fatal coverage for the same four vectors. This does not make arbitrary kernel accesses recoverable. Still to be specified before broader process operations are process-creation/exec and file-action semantics, general descriptor-object sharing and close-on-exec behavior, read/open support, blocking wait interruption, signal-like asynchronous delivery, clocks, and any additional structure layouts.
    68	
    69	## Suggested first user-visible slice
    70	
    71	The first controlled `no_std` init process now runs only in the opt-in QEMU probe and exercises ABI-version discovery, descriptor duplication/write/close, EFAULT, ready-child wait/status-copyout, exit, kernel-side wait/reap, and teardown. Its exited and running wait fixtures are kernel-seeded; they do not establish child execution or scheduling. The `rustix-user` crate provides typed wrappers, short-write handling, allocation-free formatting, and a best-effort panic-exit helper, but remains an early support library rather than a general runtime. The next work is to make process execution reusable, implement blocking userspace wait and a real child lifecycle, define per-process kernel stacks and scheduler interaction, and expand user-fault/VM tests before considering a normal-boot userspace service. Read/write/open/close and descriptor-lifetime semantics need their own complete implementation and adversarial tests before any Unix-compatibility claim.
```

```
            if allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).is_err() {
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error)
        }
    }
}
```
