## Milestone 7 — ARM64 (AArch64) platform support (long-term)

The current implementation targets x86_64. Add ARM64 as a separate platform backend without weakening the existing x86_64 path or implying feature parity. Start with one documented emulator configuration and expand only when its boot, memory, interrupt, and device contracts are validated.

### Planned work

- [ ] Select and document the initial AArch64 execution environment, firmware/boot protocol, Rust target, linker layout, entry state, and supported CPU/platform assumptions. Use QEMU `virt` as the first repeatable emulator target.
- [ ] Add an isolated AArch64 architecture backend and target-specific build/boot configuration; preserve the working x86_64 target and share code only where the architecture-independent contract is clear.
- [ ] Establish a minimal boot path with bounded serial diagnostics and validated boot metadata, kernel-image bounds, stack state, and usable-memory ownership. Reject unsupported or malformed handoff state visibly.
- [ ] Implement the architecture-specific exception/vector setup, translation-table and cache-maintenance operations, timer, and interrupt-controller path required by the kernel's supported runtime. Keep privileged instructions and raw MMIO access narrow and documented.
- [ ] Adapt the existing kernel services incrementally to explicit architecture interfaces. Keep features unavailable on AArch64 disabled rather than silently approximating their behavior.
- [ ] Add host tests for architecture-independent policy and repeatable AArch64 QEMU tests for boot, diagnostics, memory setup, and configured interrupt/timer behavior. Track physical-hardware validation separately.

**Exit criteria:** the documented AArch64 QEMU target boots the Rustix kernel through a validated platform initialization path, runs the explicitly supported kernel services with integration evidence, and leaves the existing x86_64 validation path passing. This milestone does not claim userspace or full feature parity across architectures.

---

## Milestone 8 — graphical console and GUI (long-term)

A GUI is intentionally downstream of stable memory management, interrupts/input, process isolation, drivers, and userspace. Keep Crabshell's parser independent so a graphical terminal frontend can reuse it.

### Planned work

- [ ] Add validated framebuffer discovery and memory ownership; implement a minimal text/graphics console without compromising serial panic diagnostics.
- [ ] Establish an input subsystem that separates raw device events from key mapping and terminal policy. Plan PS/2 and USB HID support separately; do not treat the current raw scancode poller as a keyboard driver stack.
- [ ] Define a graphics buffer ownership/presentation API, clipping rules, pixel format, and bounds/overflow checks.
- [ ] Implement a minimal compositor/windowing policy only after process isolation and input routing are ready.
- [ ] Define and launch single-file `.app` GUI applications using the documented static ELF64 format and shared userspace runtime; specify how any required resources are embedded.
- [ ] Support drag-and-drop installation of a `.app` file into `~/Apps/`; global installation into `/usr/Apps/` requires root. Reject malformed apps and never silently overwrite an existing file.
- [ ] Run Crabshell as a terminal application in a GUI window using the same parser and userspace services as the serial/TTY path, backed by the TTY/PTY interface rather than direct device access.
- [ ] Preserve serial as a headless recovery/debug console and add repeatable QEMU display/input tests.

**Exit criteria:** a documented GUI session starts from userspace, renders a terminal, accepts tested input, and does not require direct kernel-private VFS access.

---

## Milestone 9 — networking (long-term, after drivers and process isolation)

Networking is not implied by the current device drivers. The initial target should be a tightly scoped virtual-device path with clear ownership and bounded buffers.

### Planned work

- [ ] Build on the PCI discovery and DMA ownership/mapping foundations established in Milestone 5; add only networking-specific device and buffer policy here.
- [ ] Implement one virtual NIC driver with bounded queues and timeouts; test against QEMU user networking.
- [ ] Choose and document a minimal link/network protocol scope before implementation. Keep packet parsing length-checked and fuzzable on the host.
- [ ] Add interface configuration, routing, socket/descriptor ownership, and per-process access policy.
- [ ] Add adversarial packet tests and integration tests for link loss, malformed packets, queue exhaustion, and device reset.
- [ ] Add higher-level transports/services only when the required protocol semantics, tested CSPRNG/entropy-source behavior, and security model are designed.

**Exit criteria:** documented user processes can communicate through a tested virtual NIC/network stack, with malformed input and resource exhaustion handled safely. Do not claim internet, TLS, or POSIX sockets merely from a packet driver.

---

## Milestone 10 — installation, updates, and physical security (long-term)

This milestone depends on persistent storage. Local installation and update workflows can precede networking; remote update-server integration additionally depends on the networking and GUI milestones. Recovery media by itself is not protection against physical attackers.

### Planned work

- [ ] Define a reproducible installer for placing Rustix on a target disk, including partition/boot setup, first-boot account creation, failure handling, and recovery. Preserve a supported local/offline install path.
- [ ] Define system upgrade transactions with integrity checks, safe interruption behavior, and rollback or recovery after a failed upgrade. Do not report success until changes are durable.
- [ ] Add a package manager for both `.app` GUI applications and `.bin` command-line tools. Support per-user and system-wide installation/removal; system-wide changes require root. Keep package/dependency metadata and file ownership consistent with the filesystem policy.
- [ ] Require signed update metadata and packages, verified before installation. Trust Rustix's official signing keys for system updates; require explicit user trust for third-party user-app publishers or repositories. In-app updaters must use the same verification policy.
- [ ] Route system-application updates through Rustix system updates and the package manager. Allow user-installed applications to update through either a verified in-app updater or the package manager.
- [ ] Once networking and the GUI are available, let the GUI check an update server and fetch eligible system and application updates. Keep the local/offline update path available.
- [ ] Design secure boot, disk encryption, and key recovery as long-term physical-security goals. Specify the threat model and recovery-key policy before claiming protection against physical attackers.

**Exit criteria:** a documented local installation and upgrade path recovers safely from interrupted or invalid updates; package signatures and repository trust are enforced; and physical-security claims match the implemented boot and key-protection mechanisms.

---

## Cross-cutting acceptance gates

Every milestone should include the relevant subset of these gates:

1. **Design:** documented ownership, invariants, resource limits, error semantics, and unsupported cases.
2. **Tests:** host tests for pure policy and malformed/boundary input; integration tests for hardware-facing behavior.
3. **Safety:** review unsafe blocks, pointer provenance/access, integer overflow, privilege boundaries, concurrency, and cleanup/rollback paths.
4. **Build:** format, host tests, target check, and final ELF link as appropriate.
5. **Boot/integration:** QEMU tests for changes to boot, paging, descriptors, interrupts, drivers, processes, or persistence.
6. **Documentation/status:** update architecture and roadmap docs; never check off a criterion without evidence.
7. **Compatibility:** claim Unix/POSIX behavior only for the exact documented subset with conformance-style tests.
8. **Privilege boundaries:** test user/kernel fault separation, file ownership and special permission bits, credential confidentiality, trusted `sudo` command lookup, and recovery assumptions.
9. **Resource readiness:** do not begin process, VFS-cache, or driver workloads that require dynamic allocation, active mappings, DMA, wall-clock time, or secure randomness until the corresponding service and failure behavior are validated.

## Working rule

Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable scaffolding. A source file, interface, or architecture document is not proof that the corresponding subsystem is operational. When a check cannot run, record the exact environment blocker and leave that acceptance gate pending.

+/// Access is serialized by a spin lock, so the type may be shared safely.
+pub struct UserAllocator {
+    locked: AtomicBool,
+    heap: UnsafeCell<SizeClassHeap<MmapPages>>,
+}
+
+// SAFETY: `heap` is only accessed inside `with_heap`, which holds `locked` for the
+// full duration of the access, so there is never more than one live `&mut` to it.
+unsafe impl Sync for UserAllocator {}
+
+impl UserAllocator {
+    pub const fn new() -> Self {
+        Self {
+            locked: AtomicBool::new(false),
+            heap: UnsafeCell::new(SizeClassHeap::new(MmapPages)),
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn with_heap<R>(&self, operation: impl FnOnce(&mut SizeClassHeap<MmapPages>) -> R) -> R {
+        while self
+            .locked
+            .compare_exchange_weak(false, true, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Relaxed)
+            .is_err()
+        {
+            core::hint::spin_loop();
+        }
+        // SAFETY: The acquired `locked` flag grants exclusive access until the
+        // release store below, and the reference does not escape `operation`.
+        let result = operation(unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() });
+        self.locked.store(false, Ordering::Release);
+        result
+    }
+}
+
+// SAFETY: Allocation and deallocation follow the `GlobalAlloc` contract: blocks
+// returned by `alloc` satisfy `layout`, and `dealloc` is only given blocks from
+// the same size class.
+unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for UserAllocator {
+    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
+        self.with_heap(|heap| heap.allocate(layout))
+    }
+
+    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
+        if let Some(pointer) = NonNull::new(pointer) {
+            self.with_heap(|heap| heap.deallocate(pointer, layout));
+        }
+    }
+}

+#[cfg(test)]
+mod heap_tests {
+    use super::{PageSource, SizeClassHeap, HEAP_PAGE_SIZE};
+    use core::alloc::Layout;
+    use core::ptr::NonNull;
+
+    #[repr(align(4096))]
+    struct Page([u8; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]);
+
+    struct Arena<'a> {
+        pages: &'a mut [Page],
+        next: usize,
+    }
+
+    impl PageSource for Arena<'_> {
+        fn allocate_page(&mut self) -> Option<NonNull<u8>> {
+            let page = self.pages.get_mut(self.next)?;
+            self.next += 1;
+            NonNull::new(page.0.as_mut_ptr())
+        }
+    }
+
+    fn arena(pages: &mut [Page]) -> SizeClassHeap<Arena<'_>> {
+        SizeClassHeap::new(Arena { pages, next: 0 })
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn rounds_to_aligned_blocks_and_reuses_freed_blocks() {
+        let mut storage: [Page; 2] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
+        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
+        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(40, 8).unwrap();
+        let first = heap.allocate(layout);
+        assert!(!first.is_null());
+        assert_eq!(first as usize % 64, 0);
+        heap.deallocate(NonNull::new(first).unwrap(), layout);
+        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), first);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn honors_large_alignment_within_a_page() {
+        let mut storage: [Page; 1] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
+        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
+        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(16, 1024).unwrap();
+        let block = heap.allocate(layout);
+        assert!(!block.is_null());
+        assert_eq!(block as usize % 1024, 0);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn rejects_oversized_overaligned_and_exhausted_requests() {
+        let mut storage: [Page; 1] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
+        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
+        assert!(heap
+            .allocate(Layout::from_size_align(2049, 8).unwrap())
+            .is_null());
+        assert!(heap
+            .allocate(Layout::from_size_align(8, 8192).unwrap())
+            .is_null());
+        // One page holds two 2048-byte blocks; the third needs a page the arena lacks.
+        let max = Layout::from_size_align(2048, 8).unwrap();
+        assert!(!heap.allocate(max).is_null());
+        assert!(!heap.allocate(max).is_null());
+        assert!(heap.allocate(max).is_null());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn keeps_size_classes_separate() {
+        let mut storage: [Page; 2] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
+        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
+        let small = Layout::from_size_align(16, 16).unwrap();
+        let large = Layout::from_size_align(512, 16).unwrap();
+        let small_block = heap.allocate(small);
+        heap.deallocate(NonNull::new(small_block).unwrap(), small);
+        let large_block = heap.allocate(large);
+        assert_ne!(large_block, small_block);
+        assert!(!large_block.is_null());
+    }
+}

-ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts, addresses, and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and bounded write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. The workspace crate `crates/rustix-user` provides typed `no_std` wrappers for ABI version, write, wait, exit, close, descriptor duplication, and one-page anonymous mappings plus a raw register-level call for low-level tests; its error decoding, short-write handling, formatting, and region wrapper are host-tested. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub. -The opt-in single-vCPU process probe enters Ring 3 with a validated five-word `IRETQ` frame and enters the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated DPL-3 IDT gate. +The opt-in single-vCPU process probe enters Ring 3 with a validated five-word `IRETQ` frame and enters the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated DPL-3 IDT gate. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in this first slice. The register and error contract below is the versioned v1 ABI, but the syscall surface and runtime are not general-purpose or enabled in the default boot path. # Unix-like process and syscall direction

**Status: Milestone 4 is in progress. The opt-in single-vCPU QEMU diagnostic path creates a lower-half process root sharing the validated supervisor kernel half, loads and runs a bundled static ELF in Ring 3, serves ABI-version/write/close/dup/ready-child-wait/exit and one-page anonymous-map syscalls, terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE with status `128 + vector`, and restores/reaps the root. The normal kernel does not launch userspace. Descriptors are bounded console-stream handles with inheritance, duplication, close, and exit cleanup; the diagnostic `wait` path reaps already-exited children, preserves a zombie when status copyout fails, and returns `ENOTSUP` for a running child. Blocking for that child, general process scheduling/kernel stacks, reusable ELF execution, multi-page virtual-memory allocation, and a complete userspace runtime remain unimplemented.**

Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.

## Proposed compatibility principles

- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::copy_from_user` and `copy_to_user` preflight the complete lower-half mapped range, check writable metadata for kernel-to-user copies, and operate only on owned frame tokens through `UserFrameMemory`; they never form a Rust reference from a user virtual address. Backend copy faults report the completed prefix. The diagnostic user-exception path terminates a process on supported CPL3 faults; it does not make arbitrary kernel memory accesses recoverable.
- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.

## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)

ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts, addresses, and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and bounded write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. The workspace crate `crates/rustix-user` provides typed `no_std` wrappers for ABI version, write, wait, exit, close, descriptor duplication, and one-page anonymous mappings plus a raw register-level call for low-level tests; it also provides a `run_main` entry helper and an optional mmap-backed `GlobalAlloc` implementation. Error decoding, short-write handling, formatting, region handling, and the size-class heap core are host-tested. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub. The opt-in diagnostic process runtime dispatches ABI-version, bounded descriptor-authorized write, close, duplication, one-page anonymous map/unmap, exit, and wait for already-exited children; a wait on a running child returns `ENOTSUP` because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. QEMU init checks the anonymous page is zeroed, writable, and no longer readable by the kernel copy path after unmap; it also uses kernel-seeded exited/running child fixtures to verify status copyout, invalid-pointer `EFAULT` without reaping, and `ENOTSUP` for a running child. The wait fixtures test syscall mechanics, not concurrent child execution or scheduler integration. A separate kernel-side test harness waits for the synchronous process after its exit trampoline returns.

| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | ABI contract: blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. Current diagnostic support is nonblocking: it reaps an already-exited child, returns `-ENOTSUP` for a running child, and returns `-EFAULT` without reaping if status copyout fails. |
| 4 | `mmap` | `RDI`: requested byte length, `1..=4096` | Maps one zero-filled, read/write, non-executable anonymous page and returns its user address. Lengths above one page return `-E2BIG`; the first-fit address comes from the bounded anonymous region window; exhaustion returns `-ENOMEM`. |
| 5 | `munmap` | `RDI`: page-aligned anonymous base, `RSI`: exactly `4096` | Removes one exact page previously allocated by `mmap`; invalid addresses, lengths, or non-anonymous regions return `-EINVAL`. |
| 6 | `close` | `RDI`: descriptor | Closes one process-local descriptor; invalid or already-closed descriptors return `-EBADF`. |
| 7 | `dup` | `RDI`: source descriptor | Duplicates the stream into the lowest free descriptor slot at or above 3; invalid descriptors return `-EBADF`, and the fixed table limit returns `-EMFILE`. |

Numbers above 7 are unassigned and return `-ENOSYS`; assigning a number later is an additive extension, never a reinterpretation. `mmap`, `munmap`, `close`, and `dup` are available only in the opt-in diagnostic process runtime today. Descriptor 0 is reserved for input but v1 has no `read` or `open` call. Descriptors 1 and 2 start as stdout/stderr; child process records inherit the parent's current console-descriptor table, duplication creates an independent handle to the same stream, and process exit clears its descriptor table. The initial process is created by the kernel loader, not a syscall.

Stable v1 error numbers (returned negated in `RAX`) are: `1 EINVAL`, `2 EBADF`, `3 EFAULT`, `4 ENOMEM`, `5 ECHILD`, `6 EINTR`, `7 EIO`, `8 ENOSYS`, `9 E2BIG`, `10 EOVERFLOW`, and `11 ENOTSUP`, and `12 EMFILE`. Unknown syscall numbers return `-ENOSYS`. Pointer-plus-length ranges use checked arithmetic and must lie wholly in a mapped lower-half user range. `write` preflights the whole input range before output; a later endpoint failure may return a short count, and an error before progress returns `-EIO`. A copy fault after progress returns the completed prefix. An unmapped diagnostic `write` buffer returns `-EFAULT` before the syscall returns to userspace. `mmap` rounds any positive length up to one page, zeroes its frame before publication, and grants RW/NX access; this first ABI slice deliberately supports one page per call. `munmap` is restricted to exact anonymous-page reservations, and the kernel switches to its supervisor root, removes the PTE, and only releases the frame after the page table no longer references it. For `wait`, the optional status is copied before the matching exited child is reaped; failed copyout returns `-EFAULT` and leaves the child waitable. The current diagnostic dispatcher implements that ready-child case only and returns `-ENOTSUP` for a running child; blocking and interruption behavior remain future work. V1 has no signals, asynchronous interruption, or automatic syscall restart.

All ABI integers are fixed-width little-endian x86_64 values. The wait status is one signed 32-bit integer with no implicit padding or extra fields. No other user-visible structs exist in v1.

## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; diagnostic path integrated)

The opt-in single-vCPU process probe enters Ring 3 with a validated five-word `IRETQ` frame and enters the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated DPL-3 IDT gate. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in this first slice. The register and error contract below is the versioned v1 ABI, but the syscall surface and runtime are not general-purpose or enabled in the default boot path. The `rustix-user` crate includes typed wrappers, the `run_main` process-entry helper, complete-write and allocation-free formatting helpers, best-effort panic reporting, and an optional mmap-backed global allocator. The allocator obtains one zeroed page per `mmap` call, serves power-of-two classes from 16 through 2048 bytes, rejects larger or over-aligned requests, and retains pages until process teardown; applications opt in by declaring `UserAllocator` as their global allocator. `rustix-init` exercises the entry helper and heap with `Vec` and `Box`, but the crate remains an early runtime and is not a general application or process-scheduling environment.

- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` lies inside the device-vector range (`0x20..=0xef`) and is reserved by `InterruptVectorAllocator`; generic IRQ allocation/release cannot claim it. The IDT installs a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. Its assembly entry rejects CPL0 invocation, saves all GPRs and x87/SSE state, clears the direction flag, and calls a normalized Rust dispatcher with IF clear. The opt-in process probe implements ABI-version discovery, write, exit, and wait for an already-exited child; it does not block or create children.
- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Ring-3 data and 64-bit code descriptors are appended at GDT indexes 5 and 6, with compile-time selector assertions for user data `0x2b` and user code `0x33` (RPL 3); the process probe uses these selectors in its validated entry frame.
- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`. The current synchronous QEMU probe uses the bootstrap static ring-0 stack, mapped in both the kernel and process roots; it does not allocate per-process kernel stacks or schedule among user processes. `interrupts::set_kernel_entry_stack` validates canonical upper-half address shape and alignment before updating `RSP0`, but no general process scheduler calls it. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
- **Entry frame and state:** the dedicated assembly stub saves all GPRs in the `SyscallContext` layout, passes the five-word privilege frame separately from the exception frame, and saves/restores x87/SSE state around the Rust dispatcher; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Kernel code runs with the direction flag clear. The process probe validates saved RIP/RSP against the active process mappings and accesses user buffers only through owned frame tokens. It does not block or schedule in a syscall.
- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This convention and its initial numbers/errors are versioned as ABI v1. Implemented operations remain a subset of the documented contract.
- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Initial entry uses a host-tested frame sanitizer that requires exact ring-3 selectors, a canonical lower-half instruction pointer, a lower-half stack range, 16-byte initial stack alignment, and safe flags. Syscall resume uses a separate sanitizer that keeps exact selectors, canonical lower-half address shape, and privileged-flag checks but does not impose 16-byte alignment on an in-function RSP; it replaces user flags with `0x2` (IF remains clear). Once a process is active, the dispatcher also validates the saved instruction pointer against an executable mapping and the saved stack pointer against a writable NX mapping. A malformed frame is converted into process exit rather than returned to CPL3.
- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. NMI, double fault, and machine check remain fatal even when their saved CS indicates CPL3. Other user-origin exceptions terminate the process with status `128 + vector` in the diagnostic runtime; QEMU exercises CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE. Kernel-origin #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE are separately tested as fatal. Ordinary maskable IRQs stay disabled throughout the synchronous process run.

This path depends on each process root sharing supervisor-only upper-half mappings that cover syscall/exception code, the IDT, GDT, TSS, and active kernel stack. The bundled process root and syscall/exception transitions are exercised by opt-in QEMU smokes, but the shared Limine-derived kernel mapping is not a curated kernel map or a general isolation policy. Do not enable normal boot-time Ring 3 execution until process scheduling, per-process kernel stacks, blocking wait semantics, and the remaining Milestone 4 fault/teardown criteria are implemented and validated.

### Process address spaces (design; root construction partially implemented)

Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.

Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any effectively user-accessible leaf. U/S permission is the conjunction of every entry on a path, so a U/S bit on one non-leaf alone does not grant user access. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.

The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the shared kernel owner alive. PCID-aware invalidation and SMP shootdown remain unsupported and need a separate design.

The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned tables as owned, and holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend; it is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. `SharedKernelHalf` validates and snapshots the sanitized upper root entries while borrowing the kernel owner. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` uses one exclusive backend borrow for multiple private roots, maps allocator-owned user 4 KiB leaves only in inactive lower halves, retains writable/executable permission metadata, validates the initial executable entry and writable NX stack, provides range-preflighted copy-in/copy-out through a separate `UserFrameMemory` backend, and destroys private leaf/table/root frames without freeing shared subtrees. Host tests cover four-/five-level sharing, U/S sanitization, independent mappings, permission checks, cross-page copies, unmap ownership, active-root release rejection, and rollback. The opt-in `probe-user-process` target additionally constructs and activates one root, loads the bundled ELF, serves write and ready-child wait-status copyout/exit calls using token-based copies, and restores CR3 before kernel wait/reap and teardown. The bootstrap static kernel-entry stack and Limine-derived shared kernel subtree are used; this is not a general multi-process or curated kernel-map policy. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.

### Static ELF64 image validation and page initialization (partial)

`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It bounds the program-header count, load-segment count, and total mapped pages; checks file and virtual arithmetic, page alignment and `p_align` congruence, lower-half canonical ranges, non-overlapping page spans, readable segment flags, W^X, and that the entry point lies in a non-writable executable `PT_LOAD`. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` allocates, populates, cache-selects, and maps every load page into an inactive process root. The diagnostic build reproducibly compiles `crates/rustix-init` as a static ELF64 payload; `just process-smoke` loads and runs the normal image, and `just user-fault-smoke` builds a `ud2` entry variant and validates process termination/reaping/teardown.

## ABI decisions still pending beyond v1

The initial v1 versioning, error encoding, syscall numbers, register-level request decoding, and assembly-matched syscall context layout are implemented in `src/syscall.rs`. The diagnostic `int 0x80` path sanitizes return frames and serves ABI-version, bounded descriptor-authorized write, close/dup, wait-for-exited-child, one-page mmap/munmap, and exit calls; invalid unmapped write/status buffers return `EFAULT` without corrupting the process or consuming a waitable child. `src/process.rs` provides fixed-capacity identity/exit-state policy, and the diagnostic kernel harness performs a nonblocking kernel-side wait/reap after the user-entry trampoline returns. The userspace `wait` call can reap an already-exited child; it returns `ENOTSUP` for a running child because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. Status copyout is frame-token-based and happens before reaping, while child creation and scheduler integration are not implemented. The fixed-capacity process table now tracks stdout/stderr console handles, child inheritance, duplicate slots, close, exit cleanup, and bounded-table exhaustion; these are not general file objects, and there is no read/open support. User faults are process-terminating only while the opt-in callback is installed; QEMU covers CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and kernel-fatal coverage for the same four vectors. This does not make arbitrary kernel accesses recoverable. Still to be specified before broader process operations are process-creation/exec and file-action semantics, general descriptor-object sharing and close-on-exec behavior, read/open support, blocking wait interruption, signal-like asynchronous delivery, clocks, and any additional structure layouts.

## Suggested first user-visible slice

The first controlled `no_std` init process now runs only in the opt-in QEMU probe and exercises ABI-version discovery, descriptor duplication/write/close, EFAULT, ready-child wait/status-copyout, one-page mmap/munmap, `Vec`/`Box` heap allocation, exit, kernel-side wait/reap, and teardown. Its exited and running wait fixtures are kernel-seeded; they do not establish child execution or scheduling. The `rustix-user` crate provides typed wrappers, a process-entry helper, short-write handling, allocation-free formatting, panic exit, and an optional size-class allocator backed by the one-page anonymous-map syscall. It remains an early runtime rather than a general process execution environment. The next work is to make process execution reusable, implement blocking userspace wait and a real child lifecycle, define per-process kernel stacks and scheduler interaction, and expand user-fault/VM tests before considering a normal-boot userspace service. Read/write/open/close and descriptor-lifetime semantics need their own complete implementation and adversarial tests before any Unix-compatibility claim.

**Milestone 4 is still in progress**, but this slice adds and validates a reusable userspace runtime foundation.

- `crates/rustix-user/src/lib.rs` now provides `run_main` and an optional mmap-backed size-class allocator. It supports allocations up to 2048 bytes, with alignment up to 2048; mapped pages are retained until process teardown.

fn switch_process_to_kernel_root<M: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    state: &ActiveUserProcessSyscallContext,
    roots: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
) {
    // SAFETY: Syscall entry has IF clear and runs on a stack mapped in both roots.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(state.kernel_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != state.kernel_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The kernel root is active and no other CPU can use this process root.
    if unsafe { roots.mark_inactive(state.process) }.is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

pub(crate) fn timer_interrupt() {
... 1 line elided
    if runtime_pointer.is_null() {
        return;
    }

    // The interrupt gate has cleared IF. Every ordinary scheduler mutation also
    // disables IF before borrowing this runtime, so the single CPU cannot observe
    // a partially updated scheduler state here.
    let switch = unsafe {
        let runtime = &mut *runtime_pointer;
        runtime.wake_ready_events();
        let Some(current) = runtime.policy.current() else {
            return;
        };
        let old_context = runtime.current_context;
        if old_context != current.slot_index() + 1 {
            halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure();
        }
        let next = runtime
            .policy
            .preempt_current()
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        let next_context = next.slot_index() + 1;
        runtime.current_context = next_context;
        if next == current {
            None
        } else {
            Some((
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.saved_rsp[old_context]),
                runtime.saved_rsp[next_context],
                core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(runtime.fx_state[next_context]),
            ))
        }
    };
    if let Some((old_rsp, new_rsp, new_fx_state)) = switch {
        // SAFETY: The interrupted context's FXSAVE image was written by the IRQ
        // stub before Rust ran. This suspends the handler stack and restores the
        // selected context; the interrupted thread later resumes through IRETQ.
        unsafe {
            rustix_arch_context_switch_from_irq(old_rsp, new_rsp as *mut usize, new_fx_state)
        };
    }
}

    pub fn create_initial(&mut self) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        if self
            .records
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .any(|record| record.parent == KERNEL_PROCESS_ID)
        {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::InitialProcessAlreadyExists);
        }
        self.insert(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, initial_console_descriptors())
    }

    /// Register a child of a currently running process.
    pub fn spawn(&mut self, parent: ProcessId) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        let parent_record = self
            .record(parent)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)?;
        if parent_record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited);
        }
        self.insert(parent, parent_record.descriptors)
    }

pub fn zero_user_frame<U: UserFrameMemory>(
    frame: &Frame,
    user_memory: &mut U,
) -> Result<(), U::Error> {
    const ZERO_CHUNK: [u8; 128] = [0; 128];

    for offset in (0..PAGE_SIZE as usize).step_by(ZERO_CHUNK.len()) {
        user_memory.copy_to_frame(frame, offset, &ZERO_CHUNK)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

     1	//! Fixed-capacity policy state for single-vCPU kernel threads.
     2	//!
     3	//! This module does not own stacks, switch CPU contexts, or access hardware.
     4	//! Its caller must serialize every call, including against timer IRQs (the
     5	//! runtime does so by disabling local interrupts around policy mutations). A
     6	//! thread is either ready, the sole running thread, blocked on exactly
     7	//! one live wait queue, or exited. Exited slots remain occupied until `reap`.
     8	//! Dispatch scans slots in deterministic round-robin order; waiters are woken
     9	//! in FIFO order. All storage is inline and bounded by the const capacities.

    24	/// Build the fresh stack frame consumed by the x86_64 cooperative switch.
    25	///
    26	/// The saved-register order is R15, R14, R13, R12, RBP, RBX, followed by the
    27	/// trampoline return address. The returned address is 16-byte aligned; after
    28	/// six pops and `ret`, the trampoline observes the SysV entry alignment
    29	/// (`RSP % 16 == 8`). This helper only prepares bounded inline stack storage.
    30	pub fn initialize_thread_context_stack(
    31	    stack: &mut [usize],
    32	    saved_registers: [usize; 6],
    33	    trampoline: usize,
    34	) -> Option<usize> {
    35	    const REGISTER_SLOTS: usize = 6;
    36	    const FRAME_SLOTS: usize = REGISTER_SLOTS + 1;
    37	    let word_size = core::mem::size_of::<usize>();
    38	    let frame_bytes = FRAME_SLOTS.checked_mul(word_size)?;
    39	    let stack_bytes = stack.len().checked_mul(word_size)?;
    40	    let stack_start = stack.as_mut_ptr() as usize;
    41	    let stack_end = stack_start.checked_add(stack_bytes)?;
    42	    let frame_start = stack_end.checked_sub(frame_bytes)? & !15usize;
    43	    let frame_offset = frame_start.checked_sub(stack_start)?;
    44	    if frame_offset % word_size != 0 {
    45	        return None;
    46	    }
    47	    let first_slot = frame_offset / word_size;
    48	    let frame_end = first_slot.checked_add(FRAME_SLOTS)?;
    49	    if frame_end > stack.len() || frame_start & 15 != 0 {
    50	        return None;
    51	    }
    52	
    53	    stack[first_slot..first_slot + REGISTER_SLOTS].copy_from_slice(&saved_registers);
    54	    stack[first_slot + REGISTER_SLOTS] = trampoline;
    55	    Some(frame_start)
    56	}

pub fn initialize_thread_context_stack(
    stack: &mut [usize],
    saved_registers: [usize; 6],
    trampoline: usize,
) -> Option<usize> {
    const REGISTER_SLOTS: usize = 6;
    const FRAME_SLOTS: usize = REGISTER_SLOTS + 1;
    let word_size = core::mem::size_of::<usize>();
    let frame_bytes = FRAME_SLOTS.checked_mul(word_size)?;
    let stack_bytes = stack.len().checked_mul(word_size)?;
    let stack_start = stack.as_mut_ptr() as usize;
    let stack_end = stack_start.checked_add(stack_bytes)?;
    let frame_start = stack_end.checked_sub(frame_bytes)? & !15usize;
    let frame_offset = frame_start.checked_sub(stack_start)?;
    if frame_offset % word_size != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let first_slot = frame_offset / word_size;
    let frame_end = first_slot.checked_add(FRAME_SLOTS)?;
    if frame_end > stack.len() || frame_start & 15 != 0 {
        return None;
    }

    stack[first_slot..first_slot + REGISTER_SLOTS].copy_from_slice(&saved_registers);
    stack[first_slot + REGISTER_SLOTS] = trampoline;

fn unmap_anonymous_user_page<M, U>(
    state: &mut ActiveUserProcessSyscallContext,
    roots: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    virtual_address: u64,
) -> Result<(), rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallError>
where
    M: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory,
{
    use rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    use rustix_kernel::process::UserRegionKind;
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallError;

    let Some(regions) = (unsafe { state.user_regions.as_mut() }) else {
        halt_forever();
    };
    let is_anonymous = regions.regions().any(|region| {
        region.start() == virtual_address
            && region.length() == PAGE_SIZE
            && region.kind() == UserRegionKind::Anonymous
    });
    if !is_anonymous {
        return Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument);
    }

    let mut probe = [0u8; 1];
    // SAFETY: This kernel-stack byte is disjoint from all allocator-owned user
    // frames; copy_from_user validates and accesses the user frame by token.
    if let Err(failure) =
        unsafe { roots.copy_from_user(state.process, virtual_address, &mut probe, user_memory) }
    {
        return Err(match failure.cause {
            rustix_kernel::paging::ProcessUserCopyError::Memory(_) => SyscallError::Io,
            _ => SyscallError::Fault,
        });
    }

    switch_process_to_kernel_root(state, roots);
    let Some(allocator) = (unsafe { state.allocator.as_mut() }) else {
        halt_forever();
    };
    let frame = match roots.unmap_user_page(state.process, virtual_address) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(_) => {
            switch_kernel_to_process_root(state, roots);
            return Err(SyscallError::Io);
        }
    };
    if let Err(failure) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        let frame = failure.frame;
        let (mapping, cache_attributes) =
            match user_mapping_attributes(state, virtual_address, &frame) {
                Ok(attributes) => attributes,
                Err(_) => halt_forever(),
            };
        if let Err(failure) =
            roots.map_user_page(allocator, state.process, frame, mapping, cache_attributes)
        {
            let _owned_frame = failure.frame;
            halt_forever();
        }
        switch_kernel_to_process_root(state, roots);
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }
    let Some(regions) = (unsafe { state.user_regions.as_mut() }) else {
        halt_forever();
    };
    if regions
        .release_anonymous(virtual_address, PAGE_SIZE)
        .is_err()
    {
        halt_forever();
    }
    switch_kernel_to_process_root(state, roots);
    Ok(())
}

   357	/// Decode a v1 syscall number and its register arguments without touching user memory.
   358	///
   359	/// The exit status uses the low 32 bits of RDI, interpreted as a signed value.
   360	/// A zero-length write preserves the supplied pointer without validating it; the
   361	/// eventual syscall implementation must return zero before inspecting that pointer.
   362	pub const fn decode_syscall(
   363	    syscall_number: u64,
   364	    arguments: SyscallArguments,
   365	) -> Result<SyscallRequest, SyscallError> {
   366	    match syscall_number {
   367	        number::ABI_VERSION => Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion),
   368	        number::EXIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit {
   369	            status: arguments.rdi as u32 as i32,
   370	        }),
   371	        number::WRITE => {
   372	            if arguments.rdx > MAX_WRITE_BYTES {
   373	                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
   374	            }
   375	            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
   376	                fd: arguments.rdi,
   377	                user_buffer: arguments.rsi,
   378	                length: arguments.rdx as usize,
   379	            })
   380	        }
   381	        number::WAIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
   382	            child_pid: arguments.rdi,

   409	        }

   411	        number::DUP => Ok(SyscallRequest::Duplicate { fd: arguments.rdi }),

   413	    }

//! Stable, host-testable decoding for the initial Rustix syscall ABI.
//!
//! This module defines ABI values, validates register-level request shape,
//! sanitizes user return frames, and provides a host-testable bounded write
//! service. It does not install an entry gate or dispatch requests from hardware.

pub const ABI_MAJOR: u16 = 1;
pub const ABI_MINOR: u16 = 0;
pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = (ABI_MAJOR as u64) << 16 | ABI_MINOR as u64;
pub const MAX_WRITE_BYTES: u64 = 4096;
pub const USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES: u64 = crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
pub const MAX_USER_ANONYMOUS_REGION_BYTES: u64 = 1 << 20;
pub const USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR: u8 = 0x80;
pub const USER_DATA_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x2b;
pub const USER_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x33;
pub const SAFE_USER_RFLAGS: u64 = 1 << 1;

const RFLAGS_IOPL: u64 = 3 << 12;
const RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK: u64 = 1 << 14;
const RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086: u64 = 1 << 17;

pub mod number {
    pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = 0;
    pub const EXIT: u64 = 1;
    pub const WRITE: u64 = 2;
    pub const WAIT: u64 = 3;
    pub const MMAP: u64 = 4;
    pub const MUNMAP: u64 = 5;
    pub const CLOSE: u64 = 6;
    pub const DUP: u64 = 7;
    pub const MMAP_REGION: u64 = 8;
    pub const MUNMAP_REGION: u64 = 9;
}

/// Stable v1 error numbers. Syscall returns encode these as negative `i64`s.
#[repr(i64)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallError {
    InvalidArgument = 1,
    BadFileDescriptor = 2,
    Fault = 3,
    OutOfMemory = 4,
    NoChild = 5,
    Interrupted = 6,
    Io = 7,
    NoSys = 8,
    TooBig = 9,
    Overflow = 10,
    NotSupported = 11,
    TooManyOpenFiles = 12,
}

impl SyscallError {
    pub const fn return_value(self) -> i64 {
        -(self as i64)
    }
}

/// The six argument registers reserved by the x86_64 v1 calling convention.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct SyscallArguments {
    pub rdi: u64,
    pub rsi: u64,
    pub rdx: u64,
    pub r10: u64,
    pub r8: u64,
    pub r9: u64,
}

/// Register and privilege frame saved by the dedicated `int 0x80` entry stub.
///
/// The field order matches the assembly push sequence, followed by the five-word
/// hardware frame created by a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt transition.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct SyscallContext {
    pub r15: u64,
    pub r14: u64,
    pub r13: u64,
    pub r12: u64,
    pub r11: u64,
    pub r10: u64,
    pub r9: u64,
    pub r8: u64,
    pub rbp: u64,
    pub rdi: u64,
    pub rsi: u64,
    pub rdx: u64,
    pub rcx: u64,
    pub rbx: u64,
    pub rax: u64,
    pub instruction_pointer: u64,
    pub code_selector: u64,
    pub flags: u64,
    pub stack_pointer: u64,
    pub stack_selector: u64,
}

const _: [(); 160] = [(); core::mem::size_of::<SyscallContext>()];
const _: [(); 0] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, r15)];
const _: [(); 112] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, rax)];
const _: [(); 120] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, instruction_pointer)];
const _: [(); 128] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, code_selector)];
const _: [(); 136] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, flags)];
const _: [(); 144] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, stack_pointer)];
const _: [(); 152] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, stack_selector)];

/// The five-word privilege-return frame consumed by `IRETQ` in long mode.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct UserIretFrame {
    pub instruction_pointer: u64,
    pub code_selector: u64,
    pub flags: u64,
    pub stack_pointer: u64,
    pub stack_selector: u64,
}

/// A user return frame with validated selectors/addresses and kernel-chosen flags.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame);

impl ValidatedUserIretFrame {
    pub const fn into_raw(self) -> UserIretFrame {
        self.0
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserIretFrameError {
    InvalidAddressWidth,
    InvalidSelectors,
    InvalidFlags,
    InvalidInstructionPointer,
    InvalidStackPointer,
}

/// Validate the initial privilege-return frame, including the required 16-byte
/// stack alignment, and replace user flags with a conservative kernel value.
///
/// The safe flags deliberately leave IF clear until a process-aware interrupt
/// scheduler is installed. The caller must separately verify that RIP names an
/// executable process mapping and RSP names a writable stack mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_iret_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    sanitize_user_frame(frame, virtual_address_bits, true)
}

/// Sanitize a syscall's saved user return frame without imposing a new stack
/// alignment on an in-function RSP. SysV permits transient stack alignment while
/// executing a function; the active process root must still validate its mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    sanitize_user_frame(frame, virtual_address_bits, false)
}

fn sanitize_user_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    require_aligned_stack: bool,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth);
    }
    if frame.code_selector != u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR)
        || frame.stack_selector != u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR)
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors);
    }
    if frame.flags & (1 << 1) == 0
        || frame.flags & (RFLAGS_IOPL | RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK | RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086) != 0
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags);
    }

    let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
    if frame.instruction_pointer >= lower_half_end
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(
            frame.instruction_pointer,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer);
    }
    let stack_last = frame
        .stack_pointer
        .checked_sub(1)
        .filter(|address| *address < lower_half_end)
        .filter(|address| {
            crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(*address, virtual_address_bits)
        });
    if stack_last.is_none() || (require_aligned_stack && frame.stack_pointer & 0xf != 0) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer);
    }

    Ok(ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: frame.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
        flags: SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer: frame.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
    }))
}

/// A syscall whose number and register-level arguments have been decoded.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallRequest {
    AbiVersion,
    Exit {
        status: i32,
    },
    Write {
        fd: u64,
        user_buffer: u64,
        length: usize,
    },
    Wait {
        child_pid: u64,
        status_address: Option<u64>,
    },
    Mmap {
        length: u64,
    },
    Munmap {
        address: u64,
    },
    MmapRegion {
        length: u64,
    },
    MunmapRegion {
        address: u64,
        length: u64,
    },
    Close {
        fd: u64,
    },
    Duplicate {
        fd: u64,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ConsoleStream {
    Stdout,
    Stderr,
}

/// The kernel-side sink for the v1 console descriptors.
pub trait ConsoleOutput {
    type Error;

    fn write(&mut self, stream: ConsoleStream, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, Self::Error>;
}

/// Copy and write one bounded v1 user buffer through a process root.
///
/// The complete user range is preflighted by `copy_from_user` before output.
/// If the frame backend faults after copying a prefix, that prefix is still
/// offered to the console and a positive short write is returned when accepted.
///
/// # Safety
/// The current kernel stack, including this function's fixed scratch buffer,
/// must not be mapped as a user frame in `process`. The boot allocator enforces
/// this by excluding the kernel image and bootstrap-stack spans from usable
/// frame allocation; future kernel stacks must preserve the same invariant.
pub unsafe fn write_user_buffer<M, U, O>(
    roots: &crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    fd: u64,
    user_buffer: u64,
    length: usize,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    output: &mut O,
) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>
where
    M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
    O: ConsoleOutput,
{
    let stream = match fd {
        1 => ConsoleStream::Stdout,
        2 => ConsoleStream::Stderr,
        _ => return Err(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor),
    };
    // SAFETY: The caller's stack/user-frame disjointness contract applies to the
    // shared stream-based copy-and-write implementation below.
    unsafe {
        write_user_buffer_to_stream(
            roots,
            process,
            stream,
            user_buffer,
            length,
            user_memory,
            output,
        )
    }
}

/// Copy and write one bounded user buffer to an already-authorized console stream.
///
/// # Safety
/// The current kernel stack, including the fixed scratch buffer, must not be
/// mapped as a user frame in `process`. The caller must authorize `stream` for
/// this process before calling; this function does not validate descriptor state.
pub unsafe fn write_user_buffer_to_stream<M, U, O>(
    roots: &crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    stream: ConsoleStream,
    user_buffer: u64,
    length: usize,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    output: &mut O,
) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>
where
    M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
    O: ConsoleOutput,
{
    use crate::paging::{ProcessUserCopyError, MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES};

    if length > MAX_WRITE_BYTES as usize {
        return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
    }
    if length == 0 {
        return Ok(0);
    }

    let mut scratch = [0; MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES];
    let copied = match unsafe {
        roots.copy_from_user(process, user_buffer, &mut scratch[..length], user_memory)
    } {
        Ok(copied) if copied <= length => copied,
        Ok(_) => return Err(SyscallError::Fault),
        Err(failure) if failure.transferred > 0 && failure.transferred <= length => {
            failure.transferred
        }
        Err(failure) => {
            return Err(match failure.cause {
                ProcessUserCopyError::LengthTooLarge => SyscallError::TooBig,
                ProcessUserCopyError::Memory(_) => SyscallError::Io,
                ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidHandle
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Releasing
                | ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidRange
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Unmapped
                | ProcessUserCopyError::PermissionDenied => SyscallError::Fault,
            });
        }
    };
    if copied == 0 {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }

    let written = output
        .write(stream, &scratch[..copied])
        .map_err(|_| SyscallError::Io)?;
    if written == 0 || written > copied {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }
    Ok(written)
}

/// Decode a v1 syscall number and its register arguments without touching user memory.
///
/// The exit status uses the low 32 bits of RDI, interpreted as a signed value.
/// A zero-length write preserves the supplied pointer without validating it; the
/// eventual syscall implementation must return zero before inspecting that pointer.
pub const fn decode_syscall(
    syscall_number: u64,
    arguments: SyscallArguments,
) -> Result<SyscallRequest, SyscallError> {
    match syscall_number {
        number::ABI_VERSION => Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion),
        number::EXIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit {
            status: arguments.rdi as u32 as i32,
        }),
        number::WRITE => {
            if arguments.rdx > MAX_WRITE_BYTES {
                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: arguments.rdi,
                user_buffer: arguments.rsi,
                length: arguments.rdx as usize,
            })
        }
        number::WAIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
            child_pid: arguments.rdi,
            status_address: if arguments.rsi == 0 {
                None
            } else {
                Some(arguments.rsi)
            },
        }),
        number::MMAP => {
            if arguments.rdi == 0 {
                return Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument);
            }
            if arguments.rdi > USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES {
                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Mmap {
                length: arguments.rdi,
            })
        }
        number::MUNMAP => {
            if arguments.rsi != USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES
                || arguments.rdi & (crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
            {
                return Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Munmap {
                address: arguments.rdi,
            })
        }
        number::MMAP_REGION => {
            if arguments.rdi == 0 {
                return Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument);
            }
            if arguments.rdi > MAX_USER_ANONYMOUS_REGION_BYTES {
                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::MmapRegion {
                length: arguments.rdi,
            })
        }
        number::MUNMAP_REGION => {
            if arguments.rsi == 0
                || arguments.rsi > MAX_USER_ANONYMOUS_REGION_BYTES
                || arguments.rdi & (crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
                || arguments.rsi & (crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
            {
                return Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::MunmapRegion {
                address: arguments.rdi,
                length: arguments.rsi,
            })
        }
        number::CLOSE => Ok(SyscallRequest::Close { fd: arguments.rdi }),
        number::DUP => Ok(SyscallRequest::Duplicate { fd: arguments.rdi }),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::NoSys),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        decode_syscall, number, sanitize_user_iret_frame, sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame,
        SyscallArguments, SyscallError, SyscallRequest, UserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError,
        ABI_VERSION, MAX_WRITE_BYTES, SAFE_USER_RFLAGS, USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES,
        USER_CODE_SELECTOR, USER_DATA_SELECTOR,
    };

    const EMPTY_ARGUMENTS: SyscallArguments = SyscallArguments {
        rdi: 0,
        rsi: 0,
        rdx: 0,
        r10: 0,
        r8: 0,
        r9: 0,
    };

    fn valid_iret_frame() -> UserIretFrame {
        UserIretFrame {
            instruction_pointer: 0x4000_0000,
            code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
            flags: 0x202,
            stack_pointer: 0x7fff_fff0,
            stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn abi_version_and_syscall_numbers_are_stable() {
        assert_eq!(ABI_VERSION, 0x0001_0000);
        assert_eq!(number::ABI_VERSION, 0);
        assert_eq!(number::EXIT, 1);
        assert_eq!(number::WRITE, 2);
        assert_eq!(number::WAIT, 3);
        assert_eq!(number::MMAP, 4);
        assert_eq!(number::MUNMAP, 5);
        assert_eq!(number::CLOSE, 6);
        assert_eq!(number::DUP, 7);
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::ABI_VERSION, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn error_numbers_encode_as_negative_i64_results() {
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::InvalidArgument.return_value(), -1);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor.return_value(), -2);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Fault.return_value(), -3);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::OutOfMemory.return_value(), -4);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NoChild.return_value(), -5);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Interrupted.return_value(), -6);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Io.return_value(), -7);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NoSys.return_value(), -8);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::TooBig.return_value(), -9);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Overflow.return_value(), -10);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(), -11);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::TooManyOpenFiles.return_value(), -12);
    }

    #[test]
    fn close_and_duplicate_decode_the_descriptor_argument() {
        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 3,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::CLOSE, arguments),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Close { fd: 3 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::DUP, arguments),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Duplicate { fd: 3 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn exit_status_is_the_signed_low_32_bits_of_rdi() {
        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 0xfeed_beef_ffff_fffe,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::EXIT, arguments),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit { status: -2 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_decoding_accepts_zero_and_maximum_lengths_without_pointer_access() {
        let zero_length = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 1,
            rsi: u64::MAX,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WRITE, zero_length),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: 1,
                user_buffer: u64::MAX,
                length: 0,
            })
        );

        let maximum = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 2,
            rsi: 0x4000,
            rdx: MAX_WRITE_BYTES,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WRITE, maximum),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: 2,
                user_buffer: 0x4000,
                length: MAX_WRITE_BYTES as usize,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_larger_than_the_v1_limit_is_rejected() {
        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdx: MAX_WRITE_BYTES + 1,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WRITE, arguments),
            Err(SyscallError::TooBig)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn wait_decoding_distinguishes_optional_status_pointer() {
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WAIT, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
                child_pid: 0,
                status_address: None,
            })
        );

        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 42,
            rsi: 0x7000,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::WAIT, arguments),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
                child_pid: 42,
                status_address: Some(0x7000),
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn anonymous_mapping_requests_are_page_bounded_and_unmap_is_exactly_one_page() {
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(
                number::MMAP,
                SyscallArguments {
                    rdi: 1,
                    ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
                }
            ),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Mmap { length: 1 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(
                number::MMAP,
                SyscallArguments {
                    rdi: USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES,
                    ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
                }
            ),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Mmap {
                length: USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::MMAP, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS),
            Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(
                number::MMAP,
                SyscallArguments {
                    rdi: USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES + 1,
                    ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
                }
            ),
            Err(SyscallError::TooBig)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(
                number::MUNMAP,
                SyscallArguments {
                    rdi: 0x4000,
                    rsi: USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES,
                    ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
                }
            ),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Munmap { address: 0x4000 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(
                number::MUNMAP,
                SyscallArguments {
                    rdi: 0x4001,
                    rsi: USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES,
                    ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
                }
            ),
            Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(
                number::MUNMAP,
                SyscallArguments {
                    rdi: 0x4000,
                    rsi: USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES * 2,
                    ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
                }
            ),
            Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_iret_frame_checks_selectors_addresses_alignment_and_sanitizes_flags() {
        let mut frame = valid_iret_frame();
        let sanitized = sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48).unwrap().into_raw();
        assert_eq!(sanitized.instruction_pointer, frame.instruction_pointer);
        assert_eq!(sanitized.code_selector, u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR));
        assert_eq!(sanitized.stack_selector, u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR));
        assert_eq!(sanitized.flags, SAFE_USER_RFLAGS);
        assert_eq!(sanitized.stack_pointer, frame.stack_pointer);

        frame.code_selector = 0x08;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.stack_selector = 0x10;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn syscall_return_frame_preserves_valid_in_function_stack_alignment() {
        let mut frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.stack_pointer = 0x7fff_fff8;
        let sanitized = sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(frame, 48)
            .unwrap()
            .into_raw();
        assert_eq!(sanitized.stack_pointer, 0x7fff_fff8);
        assert_eq!(sanitized.flags, SAFE_USER_RFLAGS);
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_iret_frame_rejects_bad_flags_and_non_user_addresses() {
        let mut frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.flags |= 3 << 12;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.flags &= !(1 << 1);
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.instruction_pointer = 1 << 47;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.stack_pointer = 0x7fff_fff8;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer)
        );
        frame = valid_iret_frame();
        frame.stack_pointer = 0x0000_8000_0000_0000;
        assert!(sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48).is_ok());
        frame.stack_pointer += 16;
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(frame, 48),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            sanitize_user_iret_frame(valid_iret_frame(), 52),
            Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn unassigned_numbers_return_enosys() {
        assert_eq!(decode_syscall(8, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS), Err(SyscallError::NoSys));
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(u64::MAX, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS),
            Err(SyscallError::NoSys)
        );
    }
}

const IO_APIC_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS: u64 = LOCAL_APIC_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS + rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
const KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE: u64 = 0xffff_c200_0000_0000;
const KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES: usize = 256;

macro_rules! kprintln {
    () => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
    ($($argument:tt)*) => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!($($argument)*));
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
}

pub(crate) use kprintln;

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {
        // SAFETY: Active mapping callers provide the current virtual page and run
        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
enum LimineUserFrameMemoryError {
    OutOfBounds,
    Address(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError),
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
struct LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
impl LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    fn frame_slice_address(
        &self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        length: usize,
    ) -> Result<*mut u8, LimineUserFrameMemoryError> {
        if offset
            .checked_add(length)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE as usize)
        {
            return Err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::OutOfBounds);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Ok(core::ptr::null_mut());
        }

        let base = frame
            .hhdm_address(
                self.memory_map,
                self.hhdm_offset,
                self.physical_address_bits,
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address)?;
        let address =
            base.checked_add(offset as u64)
                .ok_or(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address(
                    rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow,
                ))?;
        Ok(address as *mut u8)
    }
}
