//! Stable, host-testable decoding for the initial Rustix syscall ABI.
//!
//! This module defines ABI values, validates register-level request shape,
//! sanitizes user return frames, and provides a host-testable bounded write
//! service. It does not install an entry gate or dispatch requests from hardware.

pub const ABI_MAJOR: u16 = 1;
pub const ABI_MINOR: u16 = 0;
pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = (ABI_MAJOR as u64) << 16 | ABI_MINOR as u64;
pub const MAX_WRITE_BYTES: u64 = 4096;
pub const USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES: u64 = crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
pub const MAX_USER_ANONYMOUS_REGION_BYTES: u64 = 1 << 20;
pub const USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR: u8 = 0x80;
pub const USER_DATA_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x2b;
pub const USER_CODE_SELECTOR: u16 = 0x33;
pub const SAFE_USER_RFLAGS: u64 = 1 << 1;

const RFLAGS_IOPL: u64 = 3 << 12;
const RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK: u64 = 1 << 14;
const RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086: u64 = 1 << 17;

pub mod number {
    pub const ABI_VERSION: u64 = 0;
    pub const EXIT: u64 = 1;
    pub const WRITE: u64 = 2;
    pub const WAIT: u64 = 3;
    pub const MMAP: u64 = 4;
    pub const MUNMAP: u64 = 5;
    pub const CLOSE: u64 = 6;
    pub const DUP: u64 = 7;
    pub const MMAP_REGION: u64 = 8;
    pub const MUNMAP_REGION: u64 = 9;
}

/// Stable v1 error numbers. Syscall returns encode these as negative `i64`s.
#[repr(i64)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallError {
    InvalidArgument = 1,
    BadFileDescriptor = 2,
    Fault = 3,
    OutOfMemory = 4,
    NoChild = 5,
    Interrupted = 6,
    Io = 7,
    NoSys = 8,
    TooBig = 9,
    Overflow = 10,
    NotSupported = 11,
    TooManyOpenFiles = 12,
}

impl SyscallError {
    pub const fn return_value(self) -> i64 {
        -(self as i64)
    }
}

/// The six argument registers reserved by the x86_64 v1 calling convention.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct SyscallArguments {
    pub rdi: u64,
    pub rsi: u64,
    pub rdx: u64,
    pub r10: u64,
    pub r8: u64,
    pub r9: u64,
}

/// Register and privilege frame saved by the dedicated `int 0x80` entry stub.
///
/// The field order matches the assembly push sequence, followed by the five-word
/// hardware frame created by a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt transition.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct SyscallContext {
    pub r15: u64,
    pub r14: u64,
    pub r13: u64,
    pub r12: u64,
    pub r11: u64,
    pub r10: u64,
    pub r9: u64,
    pub r8: u64,
    pub rbp: u64,
    pub rdi: u64,
    pub rsi: u64,
    pub rdx: u64,
    pub rcx: u64,
    pub rbx: u64,
    pub rax: u64,
    pub instruction_pointer: u64,
    pub code_selector: u64,
    pub flags: u64,
    pub stack_pointer: u64,
    pub stack_selector: u64,
}

const _: [(); 160] = [(); core::mem::size_of::<SyscallContext>()];
const _: [(); 0] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, r15)];
const _: [(); 112] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, rax)];
const _: [(); 120] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, instruction_pointer)];
const _: [(); 128] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, code_selector)];
const _: [(); 136] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, flags)];
const _: [(); 144] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, stack_pointer)];
const _: [(); 152] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(SyscallContext, stack_selector)];

/// The five-word privilege-return frame consumed by `IRETQ` in long mode.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct UserIretFrame {
    pub instruction_pointer: u64,
    pub code_selector: u64,
    pub flags: u64,
    pub stack_pointer: u64,
    pub stack_selector: u64,
}

/// A user return frame with validated selectors/addresses and kernel-chosen flags.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame);

impl ValidatedUserIretFrame {
    pub const fn into_raw(self) -> UserIretFrame {
        self.0
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserIretFrameError {
    InvalidAddressWidth,
    InvalidSelectors,
    InvalidFlags,
    InvalidInstructionPointer,
    InvalidStackPointer,
}

/// Validate the initial privilege-return frame, including the required 16-byte
/// stack alignment, and replace user flags with a conservative kernel value.
///
/// The safe flags deliberately leave IF clear until a process-aware interrupt
/// scheduler is installed. The caller must separately verify that RIP names an
/// executable process mapping and RSP names a writable stack mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_iret_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    sanitize_user_frame(frame, virtual_address_bits, true)
}

/// Sanitize a syscall's saved user return frame without imposing a new stack
/// alignment on an in-function RSP. SysV permits transient stack alignment while
/// executing a function; the active process root must still validate its mapping.
pub fn sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    sanitize_user_frame(frame, virtual_address_bits, false)
}

fn sanitize_user_frame(
    frame: UserIretFrame,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    require_aligned_stack: bool,
) -> Result<ValidatedUserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidAddressWidth);
    }
    if frame.code_selector != u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR)
        || frame.stack_selector != u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR)
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidSelectors);
    }
    if frame.flags & (1 << 1) == 0
        || frame.flags & (RFLAGS_IOPL | RFLAGS_NESTED_TASK | RFLAGS_VIRTUAL_8086) != 0
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidFlags);
    }

    let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
    if frame.instruction_pointer >= lower_half_end
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(
            frame.instruction_pointer,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidInstructionPointer);
    }
    let stack_last = frame
        .stack_pointer
        .checked_sub(1)
        .filter(|address| *address < lower_half_end)
        .filter(|address| {
            crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(*address, virtual_address_bits)
        });
    if stack_last.is_none() || (require_aligned_stack && frame.stack_pointer & 0xf != 0) {
        return Err(UserIretFrameError::InvalidStackPointer);
    }

    Ok(ValidatedUserIretFrame(UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: frame.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
        flags: SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer: frame.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
    }))
}

/// A syscall whose number and register-level arguments have been decoded.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum SyscallRequest {
    AbiVersion,
    Exit {
        status: i32,
    },
    Write {
        fd: u64,
        user_buffer: u64,
        length: usize,
    },
    Wait {
        child_pid: u64,
        status_address: Option<u64>,
    },
    Mmap {
        length: u64,
    },
    Munmap {
        address: u64,
    },
    MmapRegion {
        length: u64,
    },
    MunmapRegion {
        address: u64,
        length: u64,
    },
    Close {
        fd: u64,
    },
    Duplicate {
        fd: u64,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ConsoleStream {
    Stdout,
    Stderr,
}

/// The kernel-side sink for the v1 console descriptors.
pub trait ConsoleOutput {
    type Error;

    fn write(&mut self, stream: ConsoleStream, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, Self::Error>;
}

/// Copy and write one bounded v1 user buffer through a process root.
///
/// The complete user range is preflighted by `copy_from_user` before output.
/// If the frame backend faults after copying a prefix, that prefix is still
/// offered to the console and a positive short write is returned when accepted.
///
/// # Safety
/// The current kernel stack, including this function's fixed scratch buffer,
/// must not be mapped as a user frame in `process`. The boot allocator enforces
/// this by excluding the kernel image and bootstrap-stack spans from usable
/// frame allocation; future kernel stacks must preserve the same invariant.
pub unsafe fn write_user_buffer<M, U, O>(
    roots: &crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    fd: u64,
    user_buffer: u64,
    length: usize,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    output: &mut O,
) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>
where
    M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
    O: ConsoleOutput,
{
    let stream = match fd {
        1 => ConsoleStream::Stdout,
        2 => ConsoleStream::Stderr,
        _ => return Err(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor),
    };
    // SAFETY: The caller's stack/user-frame disjointness contract applies to the
    // shared stream-based copy-and-write implementation below.
    unsafe {
        write_user_buffer_to_stream(
            roots,
            process,
            stream,
            user_buffer,
            length,
            user_memory,
            output,
        )
    }
}

/// Copy and write one bounded user buffer to an already-authorized console stream.
///
/// # Safety
/// The current kernel stack, including the fixed scratch buffer, must not be
/// mapped as a user frame in `process`. The caller must authorize `stream` for
/// this process before calling; this function does not validate descriptor state.
pub unsafe fn write_user_buffer_to_stream<M, U, O>(
    roots: &crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    stream: ConsoleStream,
    user_buffer: u64,
    length: usize,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    output: &mut O,
) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>
where
    M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
    O: ConsoleOutput,
{
    use crate::paging::{ProcessUserCopyError, MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES};

    if length > MAX_WRITE_BYTES as usize {
        return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
    }
    if length == 0 {
        return Ok(0);
    }

    let mut scratch = [0; MAX_PROCESS_USER_COPY_BYTES];
    let copied = match unsafe {
        roots.copy_from_user(process, user_buffer, &mut scratch[..length], user_memory)
    } {
        Ok(copied) if copied <= length => copied,
        Ok(_) => return Err(SyscallError::Fault),
        Err(failure) if failure.transferred > 0 && failure.transferred <= length => {
            failure.transferred
        }
        Err(failure) => {
            return Err(match failure.cause {
                ProcessUserCopyError::LengthTooLarge => SyscallError::TooBig,
                ProcessUserCopyError::Memory(_) => SyscallError::Io,
                ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidHandle
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Releasing
                | ProcessUserCopyError::InvalidRange
                | ProcessUserCopyError::Unmapped
                | ProcessUserCopyError::PermissionDenied => SyscallError::Fault,
            });
        }
    };
    if copied == 0 {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }

    let written = output
        .write(stream, &scratch[..copied])
        .map_err(|_| SyscallError::Io)?;
    if written == 0 || written > copied {
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }
    Ok(written)
}

/// Decode a v1 syscall number and its register arguments without touching user memory.
///
/// The exit status uses the low 32 bits of RDI, interpreted as a signed value.
/// A zero-length write preserves the supplied pointer without validating it; the
/// eventual syscall implementation must return zero before inspecting that pointer.
pub const fn decode_syscall(
    syscall_number: u64,
    arguments: SyscallArguments,
) -> Result<SyscallRequest, SyscallError> {
    match syscall_number {
        number::ABI_VERSION => Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion),
        number::EXIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit {
            status: arguments.rdi as u32 as i32,
        }),
        number::WRITE => {
            if arguments.rdx > MAX_WRITE_BYTES {
                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Write {
                fd: arguments.rdi,
                user_buffer: arguments.rsi,
                length: arguments.rdx as usize,
            })
        }
        number::WAIT => Ok(SyscallRequest::Wait {
            child_pid: arguments.rdi,
            status_address: if arguments.rsi == 0 {
                None
            } else {
                Some(arguments.rsi)
            },
        }),
        number::MMAP => {
            if arguments.rdi == 0 {
                return Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument);
            }
            if arguments.rdi > USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES {
                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Mmap {
                length: arguments.rdi,
            })
        }
        number::MUNMAP => {
            if arguments.rsi != USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES
                || arguments.rdi & (crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
            {
                return Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Munmap {
                address: arguments.rdi,
            })
        }
        number::MMAP_REGION => {
            if arguments.rdi == 0 {
                return Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument);
            }
            if arguments.rdi > MAX_USER_ANONYMOUS_REGION_BYTES {
                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::MmapRegion {
                length: arguments.rdi,
            })
        }
        number::MUNMAP_REGION => {
            if arguments.rsi > MAX_USER_ANONYMOUS_REGION_BYTES {
                return Err(SyscallError::TooBig);
            }
            if arguments.rsi == 0
                || arguments.rdi & (crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
                || arguments.rsi & (crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
            {
                return Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument);
            }
            Ok(SyscallRequest::MunmapRegion {
                address: arguments.rdi,
                length: arguments.rsi,
            })
        }
        number::CLOSE => Ok(SyscallRequest::Close { fd: arguments.rdi }),
        number::DUP => Ok(SyscallRequest::Duplicate { fd: arguments.rdi }),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::NoSys),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]

        SyscallArguments, SyscallError, SyscallRequest, UserIretFrame, UserIretFrameError,
        ABI_VERSION, MAX_USER_ANONYMOUS_REGION_BYTES, MAX_WRITE_BYTES, SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        USER_ANONYMOUS_PAGE_BYTES, USER_CODE_SELECTOR, USER_DATA_SELECTOR,
    };

    const EMPTY_ARGUMENTS: SyscallArguments = SyscallArguments {

        rsi: 0,
        rdx: 0,
        r10: 0,
        r8: 0,
        r9: 0,
    };

    fn valid_iret_frame() -> UserIretFrame {
        UserIretFrame {
            instruction_pointer: 0x4000_0000,
            code_selector: u64::from(USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
            flags: 0x202,
            stack_pointer: 0x7fff_fff0,
            stack_selector: u64::from(USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn abi_version_and_syscall_numbers_are_stable() {
        assert_eq!(ABI_VERSION, 0x0001_0000);
        assert_eq!(number::ABI_VERSION, 0);
        assert_eq!(number::EXIT, 1);
        assert_eq!(number::WRITE, 2);
        assert_eq!(number::WAIT, 3);
        assert_eq!(number::MMAP, 4);
        assert_eq!(number::MUNMAP, 5);
        assert_eq!(number::CLOSE, 6);
        assert_eq!(number::DUP, 7);
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::ABI_VERSION, EMPTY_ARGUMENTS),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn error_numbers_encode_as_negative_i64_results() {
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::InvalidArgument.return_value(), -1);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor.return_value(), -2);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Fault.return_value(), -3);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::OutOfMemory.return_value(), -4);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NoChild.return_value(), -5);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Interrupted.return_value(), -6);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Io.return_value(), -7);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NoSys.return_value(), -8);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::TooBig.return_value(), -9);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::Overflow.return_value(), -10);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(), -11);
        assert_eq!(SyscallError::TooManyOpenFiles.return_value(), -12);
    }

    #[test]
    fn close_and_duplicate_decode_the_descriptor_argument() {
        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 3,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::CLOSE, arguments),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Close { fd: 3 })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::DUP, arguments),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Duplicate { fd: 3 })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn exit_status_is_the_signed_low_32_bits_of_rdi() {
        let arguments = SyscallArguments {
            rdi: 0xfeed_beef_ffff_fffe,
            ..EMPTY_ARGUMENTS
        };
        assert_eq!(
            decode_syscall(number::EXIT, arguments),
            Ok(SyscallRequest::Exit { status: -2 })
        );
    }

    #[test]

        let zero_length = SyscallArguments {

//! Small `no_std` wrappers for the stable Rustix syscall ABI v1.
//!
//! The raw syscall entry accepts register-sized values and never dereferences

pub const STDERR: u64 = 2;

pub enum SyscallError {

    NoChild,
    Interrupted,

/// Invoke one v1 syscall using the documented x86_64 register convention.
///
/// This low-level entry is safe because pointer values are passed opaquely to
/// the kernel, which validates ranges and permissions before dereferencing.
/// Prefer [`write`], [`wait`], and [`exit`] when possible.
#[inline]
pub fn syscall(number: u64, arguments: [u64; 6]) -> i64 {
    let [first, second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth] = arguments;
    let result: u64;
    // SAFETY: The v1 ABI assigns RAX and the six argument registers exactly as
    // declared here. Rustix's DPL-3 gate and entry stub preserve Rust's memory
    // validity invariants by treating user pointers as integers in the kernel.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "int 0x80",
            inlateout("rax") number => result,
            in("rdi") first,
            in("rsi") second,
            in("rdx") third,
            in("r10") fourth,
            in("r8") fifth,
            in("r9") sixth,
            lateout("rcx") _,
            lateout("r11") _,
        );
    }
    result as i64
}

pub fn abi_version() -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    decode_result(syscall(SYS_ABI_VERSION, [0; 6]))
}

/// Write one buffer to a v1 file descriptor. A successful short write is valid.
pub fn write(file_descriptor: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError> {
    let result = decode_result(syscall(
        SYS_WRITE,
        [
            file_descriptor,
            bytes.as_ptr() as u64,
            bytes.len() as u64,
            0,
            0,
            0,
        ],
    ))?;
    usize::try_from(result).map_err(|_| SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange)
}

/// Close a process-local descriptor.
pub fn close(file_descriptor: u64) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    match decode_result(syscall(SYS_CLOSE, [file_descriptor, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]))? {
        0 => Ok(()),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange),
    }
}

/// Duplicate a descriptor into the lowest available descriptor slot.
pub fn dup(file_descriptor: u64) -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    decode_result(syscall(SYS_DUP, [file_descriptor, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]))
}

/// A single page returned by the anonymous mapping syscall.
///
/// The pointer is raw: callers must not dereference it unless they uphold the

/// handle so safe code cannot accidentally release the same mapping twice.
pub struct MappedRegion {
    address: u64,
}

impl MappedRegion {

        self.address
    }

///

/// and returns a `MappedRegion` whose length is exactly one page.
pub fn mmap(requested_length: usize) -> Result<MappedRegion, SyscallError> {
    let address = decode_result(syscall(SYS_MMAP, [requested_length as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]))?;
    Ok(MappedRegion { address })

pub fn munmap(region: MappedRegion) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {

        SYS_MUNMAP,
        [region.address, USER_PAGE_SIZE as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    ))? {
        0 => Ok(()),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange),
    }

    address: u64,
    length: usize,
}

impl MappedPages {

        self.address
    }

    }

/// Map a zero-filled read/write, non-executable anonymous region.
///
/// The requested size is rounded up to a 4096-byte page. The current bounded
/// ABI supports regions up to [`MAX_MAPPED_REGION_SIZE`] bytes.
pub fn mmap_region(requested_length: usize) -> Result<MappedPages, SyscallError> {
    let address = decode_result(syscall(
        SYS_MMAP_REGION,
        [requested_length as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    ))?;
    let rounded_length = requested_length
        .checked_add(USER_PAGE_SIZE - 1)
        .ok_or(SyscallError::Overflow)?
        & !(USER_PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    Ok(MappedPages {
        address,
        length: rounded_length,
    })
}

/// Unmap an exact region returned by [`mmap_region`].
pub fn munmap_region(region: MappedPages) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    match decode_result(syscall(
        SYS_MUNMAP_REGION,
        [region.address, region.length as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0],
    ))? {
        0 => Ok(()),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange),
    }
}

/// Write all bytes, retrying successful short writes.
///
/// A zero-length write before the buffer is complete is reported as [`SyscallError::Io`]
/// to avoid an infinite loop.
pub fn write_all(file_descriptor: u64, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    write_all_with(bytes, |remaining| write(file_descriptor, remaining))
}

/// Format directly to a file descriptor without allocating.
///
/// Formatting stops at the first write failure and returns its syscall error.
pub fn write_fmt(
    file_descriptor: u64,
    arguments: core::fmt::Arguments<'_>,
) -> Result<(), SyscallError> {
    write_fmt_with(arguments, |bytes| write(file_descriptor, bytes))
}

/// Best-effort panic reporting to stderr followed by process exit status 127.
pub fn panic_exit(info: &core::panic::PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    let _ = write_fmt(STDERR, format_args!("rustix: panic: {info}\n"));
    exit(127)
}

fn write_all_with<W>(mut remaining: &[u8], mut write: W) -> Result<(), SyscallError>
where
    W: FnMut(&[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>,
{
    while !remaining.is_empty() {
        let written = write(remaining)?;
        if written == 0 {
            return Err(SyscallError::Io);
        }
        if written > remaining.len() {
            return Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange);
        }
        remaining = &remaining[written..];
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn write_fmt_with<W>(arguments: core::fmt::Arguments<'_>, write: W) -> Result<(), SyscallError>
where
    W: FnMut(&[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>,
{
    let mut output = SyscallFormatter { write, error: None };
    match core::fmt::write(&mut output, arguments) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(_) => Err(output.error.unwrap_or(SyscallError::Io)),
    }
}

struct SyscallFormatter<W> {
    write: W,
    error: Option<SyscallError>,
}

impl<W> core::fmt::Write for SyscallFormatter<W>
where
    W: FnMut(&[u8]) -> Result<usize, SyscallError>,
{
    fn write_str(&mut self, text: &str) -> core::fmt::Result {
        match write_all_with(text.as_bytes(), |remaining| (self.write)(remaining)) {
            Ok(()) => Ok(()),
            Err(error) => {
                self.error = Some(error);
                Err(core::fmt::Error)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Wait for a child and optionally copy its signed 32-bit status to `status`.
///
/// The current kernel probe supports already-exited children; a running child
/// returns [`SyscallError::NotSupported`] until blocking process scheduling is
/// integrated.
pub fn wait(child_pid: u64, status: Option<&mut i32>) -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    let status_address = status.map_or(0, |status| status as *mut i32 as u64);
    decode_result(syscall(SYS_WAIT, [child_pid, status_address, 0, 0, 0, 0]))
}

/// Exit the current process. The kernel ABI does not return from a successful exit.
pub fn exit(status: i32) -> ! {
    let _ = syscall(SYS_EXIT, [status as u32 as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
    loop {
        core::hint::spin_loop();
    }
}

/// Run a process `main` and exit with its status.
///
/// Applications define `_start` as a call to this helper so `main` can return
/// normally instead of managing the exit syscall itself.
pub fn run_main(main: fn() -> i32) -> ! {
    exit(main())
}

pub const HEAP_PAGE_SIZE: usize = USER_PAGE_SIZE;
const HEAP_MIN_BLOCK: usize = 16;
const HEAP_MAX_BLOCK: usize = 2048;
const HEAP_CLASS_COUNT: usize = 8;

/// Source of page-sized, page-aligned, zeroed read/write memory for the heap.
pub trait PageSource {
    fn allocate_page(&mut self) -> Option<NonNull<u8>>;
}

/// Page source backed by one `mmap` syscall per page. Pages are never returned.
pub struct MmapPages;

impl PageSource for MmapPages {
    fn allocate_page(&mut self) -> Option<NonNull<u8>> {
        let region = mmap(1).ok()?;
        if region.address() % HEAP_PAGE_SIZE as u64 != 0 {
            let _ = munmap(region);
            return None;
        }
        NonNull::new(region.as_mut_ptr())
    }
}

/// Power-of-two size-class allocator for requests up to 2048 bytes.
///
/// Each class keeps an intrusive free list. Blocks are carved from whole pages,
/// so a block whose size is at least its alignment is naturally aligned. Freed
/// blocks are reused by their class; pages are never returned to the kernel.
/// Requests larger than 2048 bytes or requiring alignment above 2048 bytes return null.
pub struct SizeClassHeap<P> {
    pages: P,
    free: [Option<NonNull<FreeBlock>>; HEAP_CLASS_COUNT],
}

struct FreeBlock {
    next: Option<NonNull<FreeBlock>>,
}

impl<P: PageSource> SizeClassHeap<P> {
    pub const fn new(pages: P) -> Self {
        Self {
            pages,
            free: [None; HEAP_CLASS_COUNT],
        }
    }

    /// Return a block satisfying `layout`, or null when the request is out of
    /// range or no page can be obtained.
    pub fn allocate(&mut self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        let Some(class) = size_class(layout) else {
            return null_mut();
        };
        if self.free[class].is_none() && !self.refill(class) {
            return null_mut();
        }
        let Some(block) = self.free[class] else {
            return null_mut();
        };
        // SAFETY: Every node on a free list was written by `refill` or
        // `deallocate` as an unused, exclusively owned block of this heap.
        self.free[class] = unsafe { block.as_ref().next };
        block.cast::<u8>().as_ptr()
    }

    /// Return a block to its size class.
    ///
    /// `pointer` must come from [`SizeClassHeap::allocate`] on this heap with the
    /// same `layout`, and must not be used afterward.
    pub fn deallocate(&mut self, pointer: NonNull<u8>, layout: Layout) {
        let Some(class) = size_class(layout) else {
            return;
        };
        let node = pointer.cast::<FreeBlock>();
        // SAFETY: The caller returns a block previously handed out for this
        // class, so it is at least `HEAP_MIN_BLOCK` bytes, suitably aligned,
        // and no longer in use.
        unsafe {
            node.as_ptr().write(FreeBlock {
                next: self.free[class],
            });
        }
        self.free[class] = Some(node);
    }

    fn refill(&mut self, class: usize) -> bool {
        let Some(page) = self.pages.allocate_page() else {
            return false;
        };
        let block_size = HEAP_MIN_BLOCK << class;
        for index in (0..HEAP_PAGE_SIZE / block_size).rev() {
            // SAFETY: `page` is an owned, page-sized mapping and `index` keeps
            // `offset + block_size` within it. Page alignment and the power-of-two
            // block size make the node aligned for `FreeBlock`.
            let node = unsafe { page.as_ptr().add(index * block_size) }.cast::<FreeBlock>();
            // SAFETY: `node` is inside the page and is not yet visible to any user.
            unsafe {
                node.write(FreeBlock {
                    next: self.free[class],
                });
            }
            self.free[class] = NonNull::new(node);
        }
        true
    }
}

fn size_class(layout: Layout) -> Option<usize> {
    if layout.align() > HEAP_PAGE_SIZE {
        return None;
    }
    let block = layout
        .size()
        .max(layout.align())
        .max(HEAP_MIN_BLOCK)
        .checked_next_power_of_two()?;
    if block > HEAP_MAX_BLOCK {
        return None;
    }
    Some((block / HEAP_MIN_BLOCK).trailing_zeros() as usize)
}

/// Global allocator for Rustix user processes.
///
/// Declare one with `#[global_allocator]` in an application that uses `alloc`.
/// Access is serialized by a spin lock, so the type may be shared safely.
pub struct UserAllocator {
    locked: AtomicBool,
    heap: UnsafeCell<SizeClassHeap<MmapPages>>,
}

// SAFETY: `heap` is only accessed inside `with_heap`, which holds `locked` for the
// full duration of the access, so there is never more than one live `&mut` to it.
unsafe impl Sync for UserAllocator {}

impl UserAllocator {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            locked: AtomicBool::new(false),
            heap: UnsafeCell::new(SizeClassHeap::new(MmapPages)),
        }
    }

    fn with_heap<R>(&self, operation: impl FnOnce(&mut SizeClassHeap<MmapPages>) -> R) -> R {
        while self
            .locked
            .compare_exchange_weak(false, true, Ordering::Acquire, Ordering::Relaxed)
            .is_err()
        {
            core::hint::spin_loop();
        }
        // SAFETY: The acquired `locked` flag grants exclusive access until the
        // release store below, and the reference does not escape `operation`.
        let result = operation(unsafe { &mut *self.heap.get() });
        self.locked.store(false, Ordering::Release);
        result
    }
}

// SAFETY: Allocation and deallocation follow the `GlobalAlloc` contract: blocks
// returned by `alloc` satisfy `layout`, and `dealloc` is only given blocks from
// the same size class.
unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for UserAllocator {
    unsafe fn alloc(&self, layout: Layout) -> *mut u8 {
        self.with_heap(|heap| heap.allocate(layout))
    }

    unsafe fn dealloc(&self, pointer: *mut u8, layout: Layout) {
        if let Some(pointer) = NonNull::new(pointer) {
            self.with_heap(|heap| heap.deallocate(pointer, layout));
        }
    }
}

fn decode_result(result: i64) -> Result<u64, SyscallError> {
    if result >= 0 {
        return Ok(result as u64);
    }
    match result.checked_neg() {
        Some(1) => Err(SyscallError::InvalidArgument),
        Some(2) => Err(SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor),
        Some(3) => Err(SyscallError::Fault),
        Some(4) => Err(SyscallError::OutOfMemory),
        Some(5) => Err(SyscallError::NoChild),
        Some(6) => Err(SyscallError::Interrupted),
        Some(7) => Err(SyscallError::Io),
        Some(8) => Err(SyscallError::NotImplemented),
        Some(9) => Err(SyscallError::ArgumentListTooLong),
        Some(10) => Err(SyscallError::Overflow),
        Some(11) => Err(SyscallError::NotSupported),
        Some(12) => Err(SyscallError::TooManyOpenFiles),
        _ => Err(SyscallError::Unknown(result)),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod heap_tests {
    use super::{PageSource, SizeClassHeap, HEAP_PAGE_SIZE};
    use core::alloc::Layout;
    use core::ptr::NonNull;

    #[repr(align(4096))]
    struct Page([u8; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]);

    struct Arena<'a> {
        pages: &'a mut [Page],
        next: usize,
    }

    impl PageSource for Arena<'_> {
        fn allocate_page(&mut self) -> Option<NonNull<u8>> {
            let page = self.pages.get_mut(self.next)?;
            self.next += 1;
            NonNull::new(page.0.as_mut_ptr())
        }
    }

    fn arena(pages: &mut [Page]) -> SizeClassHeap<Arena<'_>> {
        SizeClassHeap::new(Arena { pages, next: 0 })
    }

    #[test]
    fn rounds_to_aligned_blocks_and_reuses_freed_blocks() {
        let mut storage: [Page; 2] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(40, 8).unwrap();
        let first = heap.allocate(layout);
        assert!(!first.is_null());
        assert_eq!(first as usize % 64, 0);
        heap.deallocate(NonNull::new(first).unwrap(), layout);
        assert_eq!(heap.allocate(layout), first);
    }

    #[test]
    fn honors_large_alignment_within_a_page() {
        let mut storage: [Page; 1] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
        let layout = Layout::from_size_align(16, 1024).unwrap();
        let block = heap.allocate(layout);
        assert!(!block.is_null());
        assert_eq!(block as usize % 1024, 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn rejects_oversized_overaligned_and_exhausted_requests() {
        let mut storage: [Page; 1] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
        assert!(heap
            .allocate(Layout::from_size_align(2049, 8).unwrap())
            .is_null());
        assert!(heap
            .allocate(Layout::from_size_align(8, 8192).unwrap())
            .is_null());
        // One page holds two 2048-byte blocks; the third needs a page the arena lacks.
        let max = Layout::from_size_align(2048, 8).unwrap();
        assert!(!heap.allocate(max).is_null());
        assert!(!heap.allocate(max).is_null());
        assert!(heap.allocate(max).is_null());
    }

    #[test]
    fn keeps_size_classes_separate() {
        let mut storage: [Page; 2] = core::array::from_fn(|_| Page([0; HEAP_PAGE_SIZE]));
        let mut heap = arena(&mut storage);
        let small = Layout::from_size_align(16, 16).unwrap();
        let large = Layout::from_size_align(512, 16).unwrap();
        let small_block = heap.allocate(small);
        heap.deallocate(NonNull::new(small_block).unwrap(), small);
        let large_block = heap.allocate(large);
        assert_ne!(large_block, small_block);
        assert!(!large_block.is_null());
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{decode_result, write_all_with, write_fmt_with, SyscallError, ABI_VERSION};

    #[test]
    fn decodes_nonnegative_results_and_stable_v1_errors() {
        assert_eq!(decode_result(ABI_VERSION as i64), Ok(ABI_VERSION));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(0), Ok(0));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-3), Err(SyscallError::Fault));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-5), Err(SyscallError::NoChild));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-11), Err(SyscallError::NotSupported));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-12), Err(SyscallError::TooManyOpenFiles));
        assert_eq!(decode_result(-13), Err(SyscallError::Unknown(-13)));
        assert_eq!(
            decode_result(i64::MIN),
            Err(SyscallError::Unknown(i64::MIN))
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_all_retries_short_writes_until_complete() {
        let mut output = [0; 5];
        let mut output_length = 0;
        let result = write_all_with(b"hello", |remaining| {
            let count = remaining.len().min(2);
            output[output_length..output_length + count].copy_from_slice(&remaining[..count]);
            output_length += count;
            Ok(count)
        });
        assert_eq!(result, Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(&output[..output_length], b"hello");
    }

    #[test]
    fn write_all_rejects_zero_and_impossible_write_counts() {
        assert_eq!(write_all_with(b"x", |_| Ok(0)), Err(SyscallError::Io));
        assert_eq!(
            write_all_with(b"x", |_| Ok(2)),
            Err(SyscallError::ResultOutOfRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            write_all_with(b"x", |_| Err(SyscallError::Fault)),
            Err(SyscallError::Fault)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn formatting_is_allocation_free_and_preserves_write_errors() {
        let mut output = [0; 8];
        let mut output_length = 0;
        let result = write_fmt_with(format_args!("value={}", 42), |remaining| {
            let count = remaining.len().min(3);
            output[output_length..output_length + count].copy_from_slice(&remaining[..count]);
            output_length += count;
            Ok(count)
        });
        assert_eq!(result, Ok(()));
        assert_eq!(&output[..output_length], b"value=42");

        assert_eq!(
            write_fmt_with(format_args!("failure"), |_| Err(SyscallError::Fault)),
            Err(SyscallError::Fault)
        );
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build a pinned Limine hybrid ISO and smoke-test it in QEMU.

Only Python's standard library is required. The Limine binary archive is kept
under target/ and checked against the SHA-256 published for the pinned release.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import select
import shutil
import socket
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.request
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TARGET_DIR = ROOT / "target"
LIMINE_VERSION = "12.9.3"
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME = "limine-binary.zip"
# Provenance: SHA-256 of limine-binary.zip v12.9.3 as published for the
# upstream v12.9.3 release (cross-checked against the GitHub release API
# digest at pin time; the release is marked immutable upstream). The archive is
# re-hashed on every run and mismatch is fatal. The upstream PGP signature
# (limine-binary.zip.sig) is NOT verified by this script; verify it out-of-band
# whenever the pin is bumped.
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256 = "1bdbbcda650c5dba9b1eca5833d598137bf11bd6289bc89b6bcc4f8f112fa676"
LIMINE_ARCHIVE_URL = (
    "https://github.com/Limine-Bootloader/Limine/releases/download/"
    f"v{LIMINE_VERSION}/{LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME}"
)
KERNEL = TARGET_DIR / "x86_64-unknown-none" / "release" / "rustix"
ISO_ROOT = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-iso-root"
ISO_PATH = TARGET_DIR / "rustix.iso"

REQUIRED_LIMINE_FILES = (
    "limine-bios.sys",
    "limine-bios-cd.bin",
    "limine-uefi-cd.bin",
    "BOOTX64.EFI",
)


class BuildError(RuntimeError):
    """An actionable error while preparing or testing the boot image."""


def require_tool(name: str) -> str:
    path = shutil.which(name)
    if path is None:
        raise BuildError(f"required tool '{name}' was not found on PATH")
    return path


def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as source:
        for block in iter(lambda: source.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            digest.update(block)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def safe_extract(archive: zipfile.ZipFile, destination: Path) -> None:
    root = destination.resolve()
    for member in archive.infolist():
        name = PurePosixPath(member.filename)
        mode = member.external_attr >> 16
        if not name.parts or name.is_absolute() or ".." in name.parts or ":" in name.parts[0]:
            raise BuildError(f"unsafe path in Limine archive: {member.filename}")
        if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
            raise BuildError(f"symlink in Limine archive is not allowed: {member.filename}")
        output = (destination / Path(*name.parts)).resolve()
        if output != root and root not in output.parents:
            raise BuildError(f"archive member escapes extraction directory: {member.filename}")
    archive.extractall(destination)


def ensure_limine() -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    cache = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / f"limine-{LIMINE_VERSION}"
    archive_path = TARGET_DIR / "tools" / LIMINE_ARCHIVE_NAME
    extracted = cache / "archive"
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    extracted.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if not archive_path.exists():
        print(f"Downloading Limine {LIMINE_VERSION} binary release...")
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            LIMINE_ARCHIVE_URL,
            headers={"User-Agent": "Rustix-OS-build/0.1"},
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response, archive_path.open(
                "wb"
            ) as output:
                shutil.copyfileobj(response, output)
        except Exception as error:
            archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            raise BuildError(f"could not download pinned Limine release: {error}") from error

    actual_hash = sha256(archive_path)
    if actual_hash != LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256:
        archive_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise BuildError(
            "Limine archive SHA-256 mismatch: "
            f"expected {LIMINE_ARCHIVE_SHA256}, got {actual_hash}"
        )

    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(archive_path) as archive:
            safe_extract(archive, extracted)
    except (OSError, zipfile.BadZipFile) as error:
        raise BuildError(f"could not extract the pinned Limine archive: {error}") from error

    def find_asset(name: str) -> Path:
        matches = sorted(extracted.rglob(name))
        if not matches:
            raise BuildError(f"Limine {LIMINE_VERSION} archive is missing {name}")
        return matches[0]

    if sys.platform == "win32":
        limine_tool = find_asset("limine.exe")
    else:
        limine_source = find_asset("limine.c")
        limine_tool = limine_source.with_name("limine")
        if not limine_tool.is_file():
            compiler = require_tool("cc")
            print("Building Limine host utility from the pinned source...")
            subprocess.run(
                [
                    compiler,
                    "-g",
                    "-O2",
                    "-pipe",
                    "-std=c99",
                    "-D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64",
                    limine_source.name,
                    "-o",
                    str(limine_tool),
                ],
                cwd=limine_source.parent,
                check=True,
            )
        limine_tool.chmod(
            limine_tool.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH
        )
    return limine_tool, extracted


def build_image() -> None:
    if not KERNEL.is_file():
        raise BuildError("kernel ELF not found; run 'just build' first")
    xorriso = require_tool("xorriso")
    limine_tool, limine_root = ensure_limine()

    shutil.rmtree(ISO_ROOT, ignore_errors=True)
    boot_dir = ISO_ROOT / "boot" / "limine"
    efi_dir = ISO_ROOT / "EFI" / "BOOT"
    boot_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    efi_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copy2(KERNEL, ISO_ROOT / "boot" / "rustix")
    shutil.copy2(ROOT / "limine.conf", ISO_ROOT / "limine.conf")

    for name in REQUIRED_LIMINE_FILES:
        source = next(iter(sorted(limine_root.rglob(name))), None)
        if source is None:
            raise BuildError(f"Limine archive is missing required file {name}")
        if name == "BOOTX64.EFI":
            shutil.copy2(source, efi_dir / name)
        else:
            shutil.copy2(source, boot_dir / name)

    ISO_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    xorriso_command = [
        xorriso,
        "-as",
        "mkisofs",
        "-R",
        "-r",
        "-J",
        "-b",
        "boot/limine/limine-bios-cd.bin",
        "-no-emul-boot",
        "-boot-load-size",
        "4",
        "-boot-info-table",
        "-hfsplus",
        "-apm-block-size",
        "2048",
        "--efi-boot",
        "boot/limine/limine-uefi-cd.bin",
        "-efi-boot-part",
        "--efi-boot-image",
        "--protective-msdos-label",
        str(ISO_ROOT),
        "-o",
        str(ISO_PATH),
    ]
    subprocess.run(xorriso_command, cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(limine_tool), "bios-install", str(ISO_PATH)], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
    print(f"Created hybrid BIOS/UEFI image: {ISO_PATH.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def find_ovmf_firmware() -> tuple[Path, Path | None]:
    """Find a known installed OVMF image or CODE/VARS pair."""
    directories = (
        Path("/usr/share/ovmf"),
        Path("/usr/share/OVMF"),
        Path("/usr/share/qemu"),
        Path("/usr/share/edk2/ovmf"),
    )
    combined_names = ("OVMF.fd", "ovmf.fd")
    for directory in directories:
        for name in combined_names:
            firmware = directory / name
            if firmware.is_file():
                return firmware.resolve(), None

    for directory in directories:
        for suffix in ("", "_4M"):
            code = directory / f"OVMF_CODE{suffix}.fd"
            variables = directory / f"OVMF_VARS{suffix}.fd"
            if code.is_file() and variables.is_file():
                return code.resolve(), variables.resolve()

    raise BuildError(
        "OVMF firmware was not found in standard system locations; "
        "install the 'ovmf' package (for example, 'sudo apt install ovmf')"
    )


def smoke_test(
    timeout: int,
    *,
    firmware_arguments: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    additional_expected: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    uefi: bool = False,
) -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just image' first")

    serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
    serial_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    serial_log.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    serial_path = serial_log.as_posix()
    if "," in serial_path:
        raise BuildError(
            "serial log path must not contain ',': " + serial_path
        )
    serial_device = "file:" + serial_path
    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        serial_device,
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]
    command.extend(firmware_arguments)

    timed_out = False
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, timeout=timeout, check=False)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        timed_out = True
        result = None

    if not timed_out and result is not None and result.returncode != 0:
        details = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
        raise BuildError(
            f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode} before the smoke-test timeout.\n"
            f"Serial output:\n{details}"
        )

    output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
    expected = (
        "Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap",
        "bundled init ELF validated: entry=",
        "kernel HHDM aliases validated: text/rodata R/NX, data RW/NX, PAT preserved",
        "page-table transition passed:",
        "kernel heap probe passed: bootstrap exhaustion, frame-backed growth, reuse",
        "crabshell: ready (volatile RAM filesystem)",
        "root@rustix:/home/rustix# ",
    ) + additional_expected
    missing = [marker for marker in expected if marker not in output]
    tlb_flush_markers = (
        "page-table transition: global TLB flushed via CR4.PGE toggle",
        "page-table transition: CR4.PGE clear; CR3 reload flushed active translations",
    )
    if not any(marker in output for marker in tlb_flush_markers):
        missing.append("a page-table transition TLB invalidation marker")
    if missing:
        raise BuildError(
            "QEMU did not reach the expected kernel state; missing serial markers: "
            + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
            + f"\nSerial output:\n{output or '<empty>'}"
        )

    label = "UEFI boot" if uefi else "boot"
    print(f"QEMU {label} smoke test passed (bounded to {timeout}s).")
    print(f"Captured serial log: {serial_log.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def uefi_smoke_test(timeout: int, extra_expected: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> None:
    firmware, variables_template = find_ovmf_firmware()
    expected_madt = (
        "ACPI MADT copied: LAPIC=0xfee00000, 1 local APICs, "
        "1 I/O APICs, 5 overrides"
    )

    if variables_template is None:
        smoke_test(
            timeout,
            firmware_arguments=("-bios", str(firmware)),
            additional_expected=(
                expected_madt,
                "timer IRQ path passed: 3 ticks, EOI acknowledged",
                *extra_expected,
            ),
            uefi=True,
        )
        return

    TARGET_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="ovmf-", dir=TARGET_DIR) as temporary_directory:
        variables_copy = Path(temporary_directory) / "OVMF_VARS.fd"
        shutil.copyfile(variables_template, variables_copy)
        smoke_test(
            timeout,
            firmware_arguments=(
                "-drive",
                f"if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file={firmware}",
                "-drive",
                f"if=pflash,format=raw,file={variables_copy}",
            ),
            additional_expected=(
                expected_madt,
                "timer IRQ path passed: 3 ticks, EOI acknowledged",
                *extra_expected,
            ),
            uefi=True,
        )


def input_smoke_test(timeout: int) -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; build the default image first")
    firmware, variables_template = find_ovmf_firmware()
    serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-input.log"
    serial_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    serial_log.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    # Keep the QMP Unix socket on the host filesystem; WSL /mnt/c does not
    # support AF_UNIX socket paths.
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="input-smoke-") as temporary_directory:
        temporary = Path(temporary_directory)
        qmp_path = temporary / "qmp.sock"
        with socket.socket() as reservation:
            reservation.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
            serial_port = reservation.getsockname()[1]

        firmware_arguments: list[str]
        if variables_template is None:
            firmware_arguments = ["-bios", str(firmware)]
        else:
            variables_copy = temporary / "OVMF_VARS.fd"
            shutil.copyfile(variables_template, variables_copy)
            firmware_arguments = [
                "-drive",
                f"if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file={firmware}",
                "-drive",
                f"if=pflash,format=raw,file={variables_copy}",
            ]

        command = [
            qemu,
            "-machine",
            "q35",
            "-m",
            "256M",
            "-cdrom",
            str(ISO_PATH),
            "-boot",
            "d",
            "-display",
            "none",
            "-monitor",
            "none",
            "-serial",
            f"tcp:127.0.0.1:{serial_port},server=on,wait=off",
            "-qmp",
            f"unix:{qmp_path},server=on,wait=off",
            "-no-reboot",
            "-no-shutdown",
            *firmware_arguments,
        ]
        process = subprocess.Popen(
            command,
            cwd=ROOT,
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        )
        serial_connection: socket.socket | None = None
        qmp_connection: socket.socket | None = None
        serial_output = bytearray()
        qmp_buffer = bytearray()

        def connect_until_ready(address: str | tuple[str, int], family: int) -> socket.socket:
            deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
            while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                if process.poll() is not None:
                    raise BuildError(f"QEMU exited early with status {process.returncode}")
                connection = socket.socket(family, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
                connection.settimeout(0.2)
                try:
                    connection.connect(address)
                    connection.setblocking(False)
                    return connection
                except OSError:
                    connection.close()
                    time.sleep(0.05)
            raise BuildError("timed out connecting to QEMU serial/QMP sockets")

        def read_qmp_message(deadline: float) -> dict[str, object]:
            connection = qmp_connection
            if connection is None:
                raise BuildError("QMP connection is not ready")
            while b"\n" not in qmp_buffer:
                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    raise BuildError("timed out waiting for a QMP response")
                ready, _, _ = select.select([connection], [], [], remaining)
                if not ready:
                    raise BuildError("timed out waiting for a QMP response")
                chunk = connection.recv(4096)
                if not chunk:
                    raise BuildError("QEMU closed its QMP connection")
                qmp_buffer.extend(chunk)
            line, _, rest = qmp_buffer.partition(b"\n")
            qmp_buffer[:] = rest
            return json.loads(line)

        def qmp_execute(name: str, arguments: dict[str, object] | None = None) -> object:
            connection = qmp_connection
            if connection is None:
                raise BuildError("QMP connection is not ready")
            request: dict[str, object] = {"execute": name}
            if arguments is not None:
                request["arguments"] = arguments
            connection.sendall(json.dumps(request).encode("ascii") + b"\n")
            deadline = time.monotonic() + 3
            while time.monotonic() < deadline:
                response = read_qmp_message(deadline)
                if "error" in response:
                    raise BuildError(f"QMP {name} failed: {response['error']}")
                if "return" in response:
                    return response["return"]
            raise BuildError(f"timed out executing QMP command {name}")

        def wait_for_serial(marker: str, deadline: float, start_at: int = 0) -> int:
            connection = serial_connection
            if connection is None:
                raise BuildError("serial connection is not ready")
            encoded_marker = marker.encode("latin-1")
            while encoded_marker not in serial_output[start_at:]:
                remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
                if remaining <= 0:
                    raise BuildError(f"timed out waiting for serial marker {marker!r}")
                ready, _, _ = select.select([connection], [], [], min(remaining, 0.25))
                if not ready:
                    if process.poll() is not None:
                        raise BuildError(f"QEMU exited early with status {process.returncode}")
                    continue
                chunk = connection.recv(4096)
                if not chunk:
                    raise BuildError("QEMU closed its serial connection")
                serial_output.extend(chunk)
            return serial_output.index(encoded_marker, start_at) + len(encoded_marker)

        try:
            serial_connection = connect_until_ready(("127.0.0.1", serial_port), socket.AF_INET)
            qmp_connection = connect_until_ready(str(qmp_path), socket.AF_UNIX)
            qmp_connection.setblocking(False)
            greeting = read_qmp_message(time.monotonic() + 3)
            if "QMP" not in greeting:
                raise BuildError("QEMU returned an invalid QMP greeting")
            qmp_execute("qmp_capabilities")

            deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
            offset = wait_for_serial("root@rustix:/home/rustix# ", deadline)
            serial_connection.sendall(b"help\r")
            offset = wait_for_serial("Crabshell commands:", deadline, offset)
            offset = wait_for_serial("root@rustix:/home/rustix# ", deadline, offset)
            serial_connection.sendall(b"pw")
            offset = wait_for_serial("pw", deadline, offset)
            qmp_execute("human-monitor-command", {"command-line": "sendkey a"})
            offset = wait_for_serial(
                "PS/2 raw scancode IRQ: 0x1e\r\nroot@rustix:/home/rustix# pw",
                deadline,
                offset,
            )
            qmp_execute("human-monitor-command", {"command-line": "sendkey up"})
            offset = wait_for_serial(
                "PS/2 raw scancode IRQ: 0xe0\r\nroot@rustix:/home/rustix# pw",
                deadline,
                offset,
            )
            serial_connection.sendall(b"d\r")
            wait_for_serial("/home/rustix\r\nroot@rustix:/home/rustix# ", deadline, offset)

            output = serial_output.decode("latin-1")
            expected = (
                "timer IRQ path passed: 3 ticks, EOI acknowledged",
                "interrupt-driven input: UART RX ready, PS/2 raw scancodes ready",
                "kernel shell thread runtime: cooperative input wait",
                "kernel heap probe passed: bootstrap exhaustion, frame-backed growth, reuse",
                "Crabshell commands:",
                "PS/2 raw scancode IRQ: 0x1e\r\nroot@rustix:/home/rustix# pw",
                "PS/2 raw scancode IRQ: 0xe0\r\nroot@rustix:/home/rustix# pw",
                "/home/rustix\r\nroot@rustix:/home/rustix# ",
            )
            missing = [marker for marker in expected if marker not in output]
            if missing:
                raise BuildError(
                    "QEMU input smoke missed serial markers: "
                    + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
                )
            print("QEMU UART IRQ, PS/2 IRQ, and scheduler-backed input smoke passed.")
        finally:
            serial_log.write_bytes(serial_output)
            if serial_connection is not None:
                serial_connection.close()
            if qmp_connection is not None:
                qmp_connection.close()
            if process.poll() is None:
                process.terminate()
                try:
                    process.wait(timeout=3)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    process.kill()
                    process.wait(timeout=3)

    print(f"Captured input serial log: {serial_log.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def fault_smoke_test(kind: str, timeout: int) -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; build the fault-injection image first")

    serial_log = TARGET_DIR / f"rustix-qemu-fault-{kind}.log"
    serial_log.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    serial_log.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    serial_device = "file:" + serial_log.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        serial_device,
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]

    timed_out = False
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, timeout=timeout, check=False)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        timed_out = True
        result = None

    output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
    if kind == "page-fault":
        expected = (
            "fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef",
            "FATAL EXCEPTION: vector 14 (page fault)",
            "page fault address (CR2): 0x00000000deadbeef",
        )
    elif kind == "invalid-opcode":
        expected = (
            "fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2",
            "FATAL EXCEPTION: vector 6 (invalid opcode)",
        )
    elif kind == "general-protection":
        expected = (
            "fault injection: triggering general protection with invalid DS selector",
            "FATAL EXCEPTION: vector 13 (general protection fault)",
        )
    elif kind == "divide-error":
        expected = (
            "fault injection: triggering divide error with a zero divisor",
            "FATAL EXCEPTION: vector 0 (divide error)",
        )
    else:
        raise BuildError(f"unsupported fault-injection test: {kind}")

    missing = [marker for marker in expected if marker not in output]
    if missing:
        raise BuildError(
            f"QEMU did not report the expected {kind} exception; missing serial markers: "
            + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
            + f"\nSerial output:\n{output or '<empty>'}"
        )
    if "root@rustix:/home/rustix# " in output:
        raise BuildError(f"kernel reached the shell after {kind} injection\nSerial output:\n{output}")
    if "fault injection unexpectedly returned" in output:
        raise BuildError(f"{kind} instruction returned instead of faulting\nSerial output:\n{output}")
    if not timed_out:
        status = result.returncode if result is not None else "unknown"
        raise BuildError(
            f"QEMU did not remain halted after {kind} (exit status {status})\n"
            f"Serial output:\n{output}"
        )

    print(f"QEMU {kind} fault-injection test passed (halt observed within {timeout}s).")
    print(f"Captured serial log: {serial_log.relative_to(ROOT)}")


def build_kernel(features: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> None:
    command = ["cargo", "build", "--release", "--target", "x86_64-unknown-none"]
    if features:
        command.extend(["--features", ",".join(features)])
    subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=True)


def frame_smoke_workflow(timeout: int) -> None:
    failure: BuildError | OSError | subprocess.SubprocessError | None = None
    try:
        build_kernel(("probe-hhdm-frame",))
        build_image()
        smoke_test(timeout)
        serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
        output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
        markers = (
            "HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame",
            "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries",
            "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed:",
            "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released",
        )
        missing = [marker for marker in markers if marker not in output]
        if missing:
            raise BuildError(
                "QEMU did not report successful HHDM access probes; missing markers: "
                + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
                + f"\nSerial output:\n{output}"
            )
        print("QEMU HHDM, inherited-mapping, cloned-root, and candidate-map probes passed.")
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        failure = error

    try:
        build_kernel()
        build_image()
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as restore_error:
        if failure is not None:
            raise BuildError(
                f"HHDM frame workflow failed ({failure}); restoring the default image "
                f"also failed ({restore_error})"
            ) from restore_error
        raise

    if failure is not None:
        raise BuildError(
            f"HHDM frame workflow failed; the default release image was restored: {failure}"
        ) from failure
    print("Restored the default release kernel and ISO after the HHDM frame probe.")

def user_fault_smoke_workflow(timeout: int) -> None:
    failure: BuildError | OSError | subprocess.SubprocessError | None = None
    probes = (
        ("probe-user-fault", 6, "invalid opcode"),
        ("probe-user-page-fault", 14, "page fault"),
        ("probe-user-general-protection", 13, "general protection fault"),
        ("probe-user-divide-error", 0, "divide error"),
    )
    try:
        for feature, vector, name in probes:
            build_kernel((feature,))
            build_image()
            smoke_test(timeout)
            serial_log = TARGET_DIR / "rustix-qemu-serial.log"
            output = serial_log.read_text(encoding="latin-1") if serial_log.exists() else ""
            markers = (
                f"USER EXCEPTION: vector {vector} ({name})",
                f"user fault vector {vector} exited with status {128 + vector} and was reaped by kernel wait",
                "Ring 3 user fault passed: process exited, was waited on, and its root was torn down",
            )
            if vector == 14:
                markers += ("user page fault address (CR2): 0x00007fffffffe000",)
            missing = [marker for marker in markers if marker not in output]
            if missing:
                raise BuildError(
                    f"QEMU user vector {vector} did not complete process teardown; missing markers: "
                    + ", ".join(repr(marker) for marker in missing)
                    + f"\nSerial output:\n{output}"
                )
            print(f"QEMU user-mode vector {vector} ({name}) termination and teardown passed.")
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as error:
        failure = error

    try:
        build_kernel()
        build_image()
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as restore_error:
        if failure is not None:
            raise BuildError(
                f"user-fault workflow failed ({failure}); restoring the default image "
                f"also failed ({restore_error})"
            ) from restore_error
        raise

    if failure is not None:
        raise BuildError(
            f"user-fault workflow failed; the default release image was restored: {failure}"
        ) from failure
    print("Restored the default release kernel and ISO after the user-fault matrix.")

def fault_smoke_workflow(timeout: int) -> None:
    tests = (
        ("page-fault", "inject-page-fault"),
        ("general-protection", "inject-general-protection"),
        ("invalid-opcode", "inject-invalid-opcode"),

            f"fault-injection workflow failed; the default release image was restored: {failure}"
        ) from failure
    print("Restored the default release kernel and ISO after fault-injection tests.")


def run_interactive() -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just image' first")
    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        "stdio",
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise BuildError(f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode}")


def run_debug() -> None:
    qemu = require_tool("qemu-system-x86_64")
    if not ISO_PATH.is_file():
        raise BuildError("boot image not found; run 'just debug-image' first")

    command = [
        qemu,
        "-machine",
        "q35",
        "-m",
        "256M",
        "-cdrom",
        str(ISO_PATH),
        "-boot",
        "d",
        "-display",
        "none",
        "-monitor",
        "none",
        "-serial",
        "stdio",
        "-gdb",
        "tcp:127.0.0.1:1234",
        "-S",
        "-no-reboot",
        "-no-shutdown",
    ]
    print("QEMU is paused; GDB stub listening on 127.0.0.1:1234.", flush=True)
    print("Attach with the Rustix: QEMU (CodeLLDB) debug configuration.", flush=True)
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        raise BuildError(f"QEMU exited with status {result.returncode}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    subparsers.add_parser("image", help="create a pinned Limine BIOS/UEFI hybrid ISO")
    smoke = subparsers.add_parser("smoke", help="boot the ISO and check its serial output")
    smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    uefi_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "uefi-smoke", help="boot the ISO with installed OVMF firmware and check ACPI"
    )
    uefi_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    frame_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "frame-smoke", help="probe HHDM access and an inactive candidate root in QEMU"
    )
    frame_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    process_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "process-smoke", help="run bundled init in Ring 3 and verify syscall/wait/teardown"
    )
    process_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    user_fault_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "user-fault-smoke", help="test Ring 3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE termination and process teardown"
    )
    user_fault_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    active_map_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "active-map-smoke", help="probe active owned-page mapping in QEMU, then restore the image"
    )
    active_map_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    thread_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "thread-smoke", help="test cooperative and timer-preemptive kernel threads with OVMF, then restore the default image"
    )
    thread_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=20, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    input_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "input-smoke", help="test UART and PS/2 IRQ input waking the shell with OVMF"
    )
    input_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=30, help="QEMU time limit in seconds")
    fault_smoke = subparsers.add_parser(
        "fault-smoke", help="test fatal exceptions in QEMU, then restore the default image"
    )
    fault_smoke.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=10, help="per-test QEMU time limit")
    subparsers.add_parser("run", help="run the ISO with an interactive serial terminal")
    subparsers.add_parser("debug", help="run the ISO paused with a loopback GDB stub")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        if args.command == "image":
            build_image()
        elif args.command == "run":
            run_interactive()
        elif args.command == "debug":
            run_debug()
        elif args.command == "frame-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            frame_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "process-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            process_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "user-fault-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            user_fault_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "active-map-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            active_map_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "thread-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            thread_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "input-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            input_smoke_test(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "fault-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            fault_smoke_workflow(args.timeout)
        elif args.command == "uefi-smoke":
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            uefi_smoke_test(args.timeout)
        else:
            if args.timeout <= 0:
                raise BuildError("--timeout must be a positive number of seconds")
            smoke_test(args.timeout)
    except (BuildError, OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        print(f"Rustix boot workflow failed: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {
        // SAFETY: Active mapping callers provide the current virtual page and run
        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
enum LimineUserFrameMemoryError {
    OutOfBounds,
    Address(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError),
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
struct LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
impl LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    fn frame_slice_address(
        &self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        length: usize,
    ) -> Result<*mut u8, LimineUserFrameMemoryError> {
        if offset
            .checked_add(length)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE as usize)
        {
            return Err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::OutOfBounds);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Ok(core::ptr::null_mut());
        }

        let base = frame
            .hhdm_address(
                self.memory_map,
                self.hhdm_offset,
                self.physical_address_bits,
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address)?;
        let address =
            base.checked_add(offset as u64)
                .ok_or(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address(
                    rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow,
                ))?;
        Ok(address as *mut u8)
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
// SAFETY: The non-copyable Frame token and checked HHDM conversion authorize a
// complete Usable page. Each operation checks its subrange, accesses only that
