# Rustix documentation

Rustix is a 64-bit, Rust-first, Unix-like operating-system project. This index separates current implementation facts from planned interfaces: roadmap items are proposals until the corresponding code and tests exist.

## Start here

- [Project and implementation overview](architecture/overview.md)
- [Boot protocol and current entry path](architecture/boot.md)
- [Memory-management direction](architecture/memory.md)
- [ACPI table parsing foundation](architecture/acpi.md)
- [Interrupts and IRQ vector allocation](architecture/interrupts.md)
- [x86_64 drivers and hardware boundary](architecture/drivers.md)
- [Crabshell and the volatile RAM filesystem](architecture/crabshell.md)
- [Unix-like process and syscall direction](architecture/syscall-abi.md)
- [Build and toolchain guide](development/building.md)
- [Testing and verification](development/testing.md)
- [Security and unsafe-code policy](security.md)
- [Milestones and acceptance criteria](roadmap/README.md)

## Current status

The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it validates and copies memory-map metadata into an owned snapshot, captures the executable's physical and virtual bases, complete linker-defined image span, and page-aligned text/rodata/data segment bounds, reports baseline CPUID features, active/maximum address widths, read-only CR0 caching state, gated EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT values, and a bounded MTRR snapshot, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Boot-protocol pointers are checked for canonicality using the active 4- or 5-level paging width; physical map bounds and protocol-scoped HHDM range arithmetic are also validated. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 both in the working tree and from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run downloaded and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and passed the bounded QEMU boot to the shell prompt. The serial log showed memory-map and CPU reporting. GitHub Actions run [#5](https://github.com/JustEthanCodes/rustix/actions/runs/42288095710) passed `just verify` on the published `dev` commit on 2026-11-06; it does not cover later uncommitted changes. A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove commands. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met, and Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. An opt-in diagnostic QEMU path runs the bundled init in Ring 3 and validates ABI version/write/EFAULT, one-page and multi-page anonymous mappings, `Vec`/`Box` allocation through the shared userspace runtime, wait-status copyout and retry against a kernel-seeded exited-child fixture, `ENOTSUP` for a running child, exit, kernel wait/reap, process-root teardown, and CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE exits; blocking userspace wait, child scheduling, and normal-boot userspace remain unsupported, so Milestone 4 is in progress. A bounded physical-frame allocator is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`; token ownership and failed-deallocation semantics are documented and host-tested. The boot transition owns an activated clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, and the global heap begins with a 256 KiB BSS arena and 128 allocation records, with bounded frame-backed growth up to 1 MiB. The Limine base-revision 3 HHDM scope and a conservative initial mapping/alias/cache policy are documented. Pure host-tested helpers validate mapping ranges/PTE bits, parse PAT layouts, validate captured MTRR snapshots, combine PAT/MTRR types under normal caching according to Intel SDM Table 11-7, and select a PAT index only when it yields one effective type across an aligned physical range. Boot validates the captured state and prints a diagnostic effective type at PA 0. The transition preserves inherited cache attributes, adjusts kernel-image HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX, and checks the effective PAT index against the inherited mapping. `BootInfo` records raw CR3 and a validated decode of its root physical address and low-bit interpretation. Checked HHDM access is limited to complete allocator-owned usable frames and cloned table frames; the active root owns its cloned table pages while inherited leaf frames remain loader-owned. The complete linker-defined kernel-image span and requested 256 KiB initial boot-stack span are captured and validated; Limine does not report any larger allocation bounds or guard status, so Rustix does not infer a guard page. The heap has bounded frame-backed growth and an IRQ-save lock; allocation remains prohibited in IRQ/exception context. ACPI support includes bounded host-tested RSDP/SDT/RSDT/XSDT/MADT parsing and a read-only/NX boot reader that copies validated MADT data into owned state. Rustix has a tested single-vCPU APIC/PIT IRQ path, cooperative and timer-preemptive scheduling, IRQ-save locks, guarded kernel threads, bounded frame-backed heap growth, and interrupt-driven UART/PS/2 queues with a polling fallback. SMP, general-purpose process scheduling, a persistent filesystem, and Unix compatibility remain absent. The documented syscall ABI and process-root primitives are exercised only by an opt-in diagnostic process. Kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal; the opt-in user path terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and `just fault-smoke` separately verifies those four exceptions halt at CPL0. This is not a general recovery policy or physical-hardware validation. On 2026-10-21, `just verify` passed after adding CR3 decoding and the pure MTRR resolver, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. On 2026-10-22, `just verify` passed after adding bounded read-only MTRR register capture and validated PAT/MTRR policy resolution. On 2026-10-24, the final `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` runs passed after review. QEMU verified the 256 KiB stack request, cloned-root CR3 transition, kernel HHDM alias hardening, heap alignment/reuse/exhaustion probe, and shell prompt; the current emulator reports CR4.PGE clear, so it exercised CR3 invalidation with PGE disabled, while the PGE-toggle path was statically reviewed but not exercised. Milestone 2's local exit criteria are met. Hosted CI passed on the published `dev` commit, but it does not cover today's uncommitted work or establish physical-hardware behavior, a clean-room mapping policy, or exhaustive alias coverage. On 2026-11-07, `just verify` passed with 127 host tests and BIOS/OVMF QEMU coverage for APIC/PIT delivery, active mapping/TLB invalidation, cooperative scheduling, and UART/PS/2 input wakeups. On 2026-11-13, `just verify` passed with 130 host tests and extended OVMF coverage for IRQ-save lock IF restoration, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE context preservation, and input wakeups. Milestone 3's single-vCPU exit criteria are met. Milestone 4 is in progress: the process/EFAULT/ready-child-wait/running-child-ENOTSUP/teardown and CPL3/CPL0 exception-matrix smokes pass locally, while blocking userspace `wait`, general process scheduling, per-process kernel stacks, virtual memory, and a reusable userspace runtime remain pending. SMP and physical-hardware validation remain pending.

## Documentation conventions

- **Implemented** means present in the repository and checked by current code or tests.
- **Planned** means an architectural direction, not a stable ABI or delivered capability.
- Any future ABI proposal must state versioning, error behavior, memory ownership, and compatibility expectations before it is treated as stable.

# Unix-like process and syscall direction

**Status: Milestone 4 is in progress. The opt-in single-vCPU QEMU diagnostic path creates a lower-half process root sharing the validated supervisor kernel half, loads and runs a bundled static ELF in Ring 3, serves ABI-version/write/close/dup/ready-child-wait/exit and one-page anonymous-map syscalls, terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE with status `128 + vector`, and restores/reaps the root. The normal kernel does not launch userspace. Descriptors are bounded console-stream handles with inheritance, duplication, close, and exit cleanup; the diagnostic `wait` path reaps already-exited children, preserves a zombie when status copyout fails, and returns `ENOTSUP` for a running child. Blocking for that child, general process scheduling/kernel stacks, reusable ELF execution, multi-page virtual-memory allocation, and a complete userspace runtime remain unimplemented.**

Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.

## Proposed compatibility principles

- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::copy_from_user` and `copy_to_user` preflight the complete lower-half mapped range, check writable metadata for kernel-to-user copies, and operate only on owned frame tokens through `UserFrameMemory`; they never form a Rust reference from a user virtual address. Backend copy faults report the completed prefix. The diagnostic user-exception path terminates a process on supported CPL3 faults; it does not make arbitrary kernel memory accesses recoverable.
- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.

## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)

ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts, addresses, and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and bounded write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. The workspace crate `crates/rustix-user` provides typed `no_std` wrappers for ABI version, write, wait, exit, close, descriptor duplication, one-page and bounded multi-page anonymous mappings plus a raw register-level call for low-level tests; it also provides a `run_main` entry helper and an optional mmap-backed `GlobalAlloc` implementation. Error decoding, short-write handling, formatting, region handling, and the size-class heap core are host-tested. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub. The opt-in diagnostic process runtime dispatches ABI-version, bounded descriptor-authorized write, close, duplication, one-page and multi-page anonymous map/unmap, exit, and wait for already-exited children; a wait on a running child returns `ENOTSUP` because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. QEMU init checks that one-page and multi-page anonymous mappings are zeroed, writable across page boundaries, exactly unmapped, and no longer readable by the kernel copy path afterward; it also uses kernel-seeded exited/running child fixtures to verify status copyout, invalid-pointer `EFAULT` without reaping, and `ENOTSUP` for a running child. The wait fixtures test syscall mechanics, not concurrent child execution or scheduler integration. A separate kernel-side test harness waits for the synchronous process after its exit trampoline returns.

| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | ABI contract: blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. Current diagnostic support is nonblocking: it reaps an already-exited child, returns `-ENOTSUP` for a running child, and returns `-EFAULT` without reaping if status copyout fails. |
| 4 | `mmap` | `RDI`: requested byte length, `1..=4096` | Maps one zero-filled, read/write, non-executable anonymous page and returns its user address. Lengths above one page return `-E2BIG`; the first-fit address comes from the bounded anonymous region window; exhaustion returns `-ENOMEM`. |
| 5 | `munmap` | `RDI`: page-aligned anonymous base, `RSI`: exactly `4096` | Removes one exact page previously allocated by `mmap`; invalid addresses, lengths, or non-anonymous regions return `-EINVAL`. |
| 6 | `close` | `RDI`: descriptor | Closes one process-local descriptor; invalid or already-closed descriptors return `-EBADF`. |
| 7 | `dup` | `RDI`: source descriptor | Duplicates the stream into the lowest free descriptor slot at or above 3; invalid descriptors return `-EBADF`, and the fixed table limit returns `-EMFILE`. |
| 8 | `mmap_region` | `RDI`: requested byte length, `1..=1 MiB` | Maps a contiguous, zero-filled RW/NX anonymous region, rounding length up to 4 KiB. Returns its base; reservation, frame, or page-table exhaustion returns `-ENOMEM`. |
| 9 | `munmap_region` | `RDI`: exact region base, `RSI`: exact page-rounded region length | Unmaps one exact anonymous region returned by `mmap_region`; invalid ranges, lengths, or non-anonymous regions return `-EINVAL`. |

Numbers above 9 are unassigned and return `-ENOSYS`; assigning a number later is an additive extension, never a reinterpretation. `mmap`, `munmap`, `mmap_region`, `munmap_region`, `close`, and `dup` are available only in the opt-in diagnostic process runtime today. Descriptor 0 is reserved for input but v1 has no `read` or `open` call. Descriptors 1 and 2 start as stdout/stderr; child process records inherit the parent's current console-descriptor table, duplication creates an independent handle to the same stream, and process exit clears its descriptor table. The initial process is created by the kernel loader, not a syscall.

Stable v1 error numbers (returned negated in `RAX`) are: `1 EINVAL`, `2 EBADF`, `3 EFAULT`, `4 ENOMEM`, `5 ECHILD`, `6 EINTR`, `7 EIO`, `8 ENOSYS`, `9 E2BIG`, `10 EOVERFLOW`, and `11 ENOTSUP`, and `12 EMFILE`. Unknown syscall numbers return `-ENOSYS`. Pointer-plus-length ranges use checked arithmetic and must lie wholly in a mapped lower-half user range. `write` preflights the whole input range before output; a later endpoint failure may return a short count, and an error before progress returns `-EIO`. A copy fault after progress returns the completed prefix. An unmapped diagnostic `write` buffer returns `-EFAULT` before the syscall returns to userspace. `mmap` rounds any positive length up to one page, zeroes its frame before publication, and grants RW/NX access. The append-only `mmap_region`/`munmap_region` calls add exact multi-page anonymous mappings bounded to 1 MiB; mapping rolls back mapped pages and the reservation if allocation fails. Both unmap operations are restricted to exact anonymous reservations, and the kernel switches to its supervisor root, removes each PTE, and only releases each frame after the page table no longer references it. For `wait`, the optional status is copied before the matching exited child is reaped; failed copyout returns `-EFAULT` and leaves the child waitable. The current diagnostic dispatcher implements that ready-child case only and returns `-ENOTSUP` for a running child; blocking and interruption behavior remain future work. V1 has no signals, asynchronous interruption, or automatic syscall restart.

All ABI integers are fixed-width little-endian x86_64 values. The wait status is one signed 32-bit integer with no implicit padding or extra fields. No other user-visible structs exist in v1.

## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; diagnostic path integrated)

The opt-in single-vCPU process probe enters Ring 3 with a validated five-word `IRETQ` frame and enters the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated DPL-3 IDT gate. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in this first slice. The register and error contract below is the versioned v1 ABI, but the syscall surface and runtime are not general-purpose or enabled in the default boot path. The `rustix-user` crate includes typed wrappers, the `run_main` process-entry helper, complete-write and allocation-free formatting helpers, best-effort panic reporting, and an optional mmap-backed global allocator. The allocator obtains zeroed pages through `mmap`, serves power-of-two classes from 16 through 2048 bytes, rejects larger or over-aligned requests, and retains pages until process teardown; applications opt in by declaring `UserAllocator` as their global allocator. The runtime also exposes bounded multi-page `mmap_region`/`munmap_region` wrappers, validated by `rustix-init` across a page boundary. `rustix-init` exercises the entry helper and heap with `Vec` and `Box`, but the crate remains an early runtime and is not a general application or process-scheduling environment.

- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` lies inside the device-vector range (`0x20..=0xef`) and is reserved by `InterruptVectorAllocator`; generic IRQ allocation/release cannot claim it. The IDT installs a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. Its assembly entry rejects CPL0 invocation, saves all GPRs and x87/SSE state, clears the direction flag, and calls a normalized Rust dispatcher with IF clear. The opt-in process probe implements ABI-version discovery, write, exit, one-page and multi-page mapping, and wait for an already-exited child; it does not block or create children.
- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Ring-3 data and 64-bit code descriptors are appended at GDT indexes 5 and 6, with compile-time selector assertions for user data `0x2b` and user code `0x33` (RPL 3); the process probe uses these selectors in its validated entry frame.
- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`. The current synchronous QEMU probe uses the bootstrap static ring-0 stack, mapped in both the kernel and process roots; it does not allocate per-process kernel stacks or schedule among user processes. `interrupts::set_kernel_entry_stack` validates canonical upper-half address shape and alignment before updating `RSP0`, but no general process scheduler calls it. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
- **Entry frame and state:** the dedicated assembly stub saves all GPRs in the `SyscallContext` layout, passes the five-word privilege frame separately from the exception frame, and saves/restores x87/SSE state around the Rust dispatcher; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Kernel code runs with the direction flag clear. The process probe validates saved RIP/RSP against the active process mappings and accesses user buffers only through owned frame tokens. It does not block or schedule in a syscall.
- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This convention and its initial numbers/errors are versioned as ABI v1. Implemented operations remain a subset of the documented contract.
- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Initial entry uses a host-tested frame sanitizer that requires exact ring-3 selectors, a canonical lower-half instruction pointer, a lower-half stack range, 16-byte initial stack alignment, and safe flags. Syscall resume uses a separate sanitizer that keeps exact selectors, canonical lower-half address shape, and privileged-flag checks but does not impose 16-byte alignment on an in-function RSP; it replaces user flags with `0x2` (IF remains clear). Once a process is active, the dispatcher also validates the saved instruction pointer against an executable mapping and the saved stack pointer against a writable NX mapping. A malformed frame is converted into process exit rather than returned to CPL3.
- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. NMI, double fault, and machine check remain fatal even when their saved CS indicates CPL3. Other user-origin exceptions terminate the process with status `128 + vector` in the diagnostic runtime; QEMU exercises CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE. Kernel-origin #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE are separately tested as fatal. Ordinary maskable IRQs stay disabled throughout the synchronous process run.

This path depends on each process root sharing supervisor-only upper-half mappings that cover syscall/exception code, the IDT, GDT, TSS, and active kernel stack. The bundled process root and syscall/exception transitions are exercised by opt-in QEMU smokes, but the shared Limine-derived kernel mapping is not a curated kernel map or a general isolation policy. Do not enable normal boot-time Ring 3 execution until process scheduling, per-process kernel stacks, blocking wait semantics, and the remaining Milestone 4 fault/teardown criteria are implemented and validated.

### Process address spaces (design; root construction partially implemented)

Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.

Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any effectively user-accessible leaf. U/S permission is the conjunction of every entry on a path, so a U/S bit on one non-leaf alone does not grant user access. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.

The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the shared kernel owner alive. PCID-aware invalidation and SMP shootdown remain unsupported and need a separate design.

The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned tables as owned, and holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend; it is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. `SharedKernelHalf` validates and snapshots the sanitized upper root entries while borrowing the kernel owner. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` uses one exclusive backend borrow for multiple private roots, maps allocator-owned user 4 KiB leaves only in inactive lower halves, retains writable/executable permission metadata, validates the initial executable entry and writable NX stack, provides range-preflighted copy-in/copy-out through a separate `UserFrameMemory` backend, and destroys private leaf/table/root frames without freeing shared subtrees. Host tests cover four-/five-level sharing, U/S sanitization, independent mappings, permission checks, cross-page copies, unmap ownership, active-root release rejection, and rollback. The opt-in `probe-user-process` target additionally constructs and activates one root, loads the bundled ELF, serves write and ready-child wait-status copyout/exit calls using token-based copies, and restores CR3 before kernel wait/reap and teardown. The bootstrap static kernel-entry stack and Limine-derived shared kernel subtree are used; this is not a general multi-process or curated kernel-map policy. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.

### Static ELF64 image validation and page initialization (partial)

`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It bounds the program-header count, load-segment count, and total mapped pages; checks file and virtual arithmetic, page alignment and `p_align` congruence, lower-half canonical ranges, non-overlapping page spans, readable segment flags, W^X, and that the entry point lies in a non-writable executable `PT_LOAD`. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` allocates, populates, cache-selects, and maps every load page into an inactive process root. The diagnostic build reproducibly compiles `crates/rustix-init` as a static ELF64 payload; `just process-smoke` loads and runs the normal image, and `just user-fault-smoke` builds a `ud2` entry variant and validates process termination/reaping/teardown.

## ABI decisions still pending beyond v1

The initial v1 versioning, error encoding, syscall numbers, register-level request decoding, and assembly-matched syscall context layout are implemented in `src/syscall.rs`. The diagnostic `int 0x80` path sanitizes return frames and serves ABI-version, bounded descriptor-authorized write, close/dup, wait-for-exited-child, one-page and multi-page mmap/munmap, and exit calls; invalid unmapped write/status buffers return `EFAULT` without corrupting the process or consuming a waitable child. `src/process.rs` provides fixed-capacity identity/exit-state policy, and the diagnostic kernel harness performs a nonblocking kernel-side wait/reap after the user-entry trampoline returns. The userspace `wait` call can reap an already-exited child; it returns `ENOTSUP` for a running child because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. Status copyout is frame-token-based and happens before reaping, while child creation and scheduler integration are not implemented. The fixed-capacity process table now tracks stdout/stderr console handles, child inheritance, duplicate slots, close, exit cleanup, and bounded-table exhaustion; these are not general file objects, and there is no read/open support. User faults are process-terminating only while the opt-in callback is installed; QEMU covers CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and kernel-fatal coverage for the same four vectors. This does not make arbitrary kernel accesses recoverable. Still to be specified before broader process operations are process-creation/exec and file-action semantics, general descriptor-object sharing and close-on-exec behavior, read/open support, blocking wait interruption, signal-like asynchronous delivery, clocks, and any additional structure layouts.

## Suggested first user-visible slice

The first controlled `no_std` init process now runs only in the opt-in QEMU probe and exercises ABI-version discovery, descriptor duplication/write/close, EFAULT, ready-child wait/status-copyout, one-page and multi-page mmap/munmap, `Vec`/`Box` heap allocation, exit, kernel-side wait/reap, and teardown. Its exited and running wait fixtures are kernel-seeded; they do not establish child execution or scheduling. The `rustix-user` crate provides typed wrappers, a process-entry helper, short-write handling, allocation-free formatting, panic exit, and an optional size-class allocator backed by the one-page anonymous-map syscall. It remains an early runtime rather than a general process execution environment. The next work is to make process execution reusable, implement blocking userspace wait and a real child lifecycle, define per-process kernel stacks and scheduler interaction, and expand user-fault/VM tests before considering a normal-boot userspace service. Read/write/open/close and descriptor-lifetime semantics need their own complete implementation and adversarial tests before any Unix-compatibility claim.

pub(crate) unsafe fn request_user_process_exit(status: i32) {
    // SAFETY: The caller satisfies the documented ordering and single-vCPU contract.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS).write(status);
        core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Release);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).write(1);
    }
}

/// Enter a validated user frame and return only through the process-exit path.
///
/// # Safety
/// The process root must already be active in CR3, TSS.RSP0 must point to a live
/// supervisor stack mapped in both roots, syscall and user-fault callbacks must
/// be installed, and maskable interrupts must be disabled.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn enter_user(
    frame: rustix_kernel::syscall::ValidatedUserIretFrame,
) -> Result<i32, UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_none() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::NotInstalled);
    }
    let frame = frame.into_raw();
    // SAFETY: The caller establishes the root, stack, TSS, callback, and fault
    // policy invariants. The assembly returns only after a process exit request.
    Ok(unsafe { rustix_enter_user(&frame) })
}

## Current shape

This proposal is based on the current worktree; I found no relevant durable Entire design memory. I made **no edits** and left the uncommitted `UserAllocator`/runtime and multi-page mmap changes untouched.

The existing pieces are useful, but aren’t connected into a process scheduler:

- `Scheduler` already supports bounded ready/running/blocked states and wait queues (`src/scheduler.rs:65-72, 269-335`). `KernelThreadRuntime` wraps it for kernel threads, but has only two task slots and no process/root metadata (`src/kernel_threads.rs:24-29, 84-98`). Its switch paths save RSP and FPU state; they don’t switch CR3 or TSS state (`src/kernel_threads.rs:894-944, 1043-1088`).
- `ProcessTable` has four logical process records, parent/child relations, exit statuses, and peek-before-reap semantics. `spawn()` creates only a record—it does not create an address space, stack, or schedulable task, and it has no rollback for a process that never successfully starts (`src/process.rs:7-8, 370-410, 440-521`).
- The probe creates one root and one `ActiveUserProcessSyscallContext` on the synchronous caller’s stack. Its child records are fixtures, not running processes; a running-child wait returns `ENOTSUP` (`src/main.rs:2052-2067, 2228-2276, 2940-2967`). The probe runs before `run_shell` starts the kernel-thread runtime (`src/main.rs:1222-1277, 1295-1303`).
- `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` already supports a fixed set of roots, but explicitly leaves CR3 switching and TLB invalidation to callers. Its active flags don’t enforce that exactly one process root is active (`src/paging.rs:2031-2046, 2782-2817`).

## Main obstacles

1. **Privilege-entry stack collision.** TSS.RSP0 currently points at one static ring-0 stack. A parent blocked inside `int 0x80` would leave its syscall frame on that stack; a child’s next syscall would reuse and overwrite it. `set_kernel_entry_stack` exists but has no runtime caller and validates only address shape—not that the stack is mapped and owned (`src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs:128-134, 393-425`).

2. **The exit path assumes one synchronous user entry.** `rustix_enter_user` records one global resume RSP and FPU image; syscall and exception exits jump through one global pending/status trampoline (`src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs:155-166, 1055-1130`). That cannot represent suspended user tasks. A scheduled task should enter user mode on its own kernel stack, and exit by becoming non-runnable and switching away—not by returning to a global caller.

3. **Context switches don’t change address-space state.** `context.rs` saves callee-saved registers and FPU state, not CR3 or the privilege frame (`src/arch/x86_64/context.rs:1-8, 10-50`). User RIP/RSP and GPRs can remain in the interrupt/syscall frame on a task’s kernel stack, but the scheduler must switch to that task’s CR3 and set TSS.RSP0 before it resumes. The timer path needs the same integration if user-mode preemption is enabled.

4. **Wait is not connected to scheduling.** `peek_wait` and copy-before-reap are a good base, but no process-exit event wakes scheduler waiters. A blocking wait must check child state, sleep, and retry; it must not retain a mutable process-table/root borrow across the context switch. Also, the current syscall return sanitizer forces RFLAGS to `0x2`, so Ring 3 timer interrupts remain disabled (`src/syscall.rs`, `sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame`). That’s compatible with a cooperative first slice, not user-mode timer preemption.

## Incremental design

1. **Add per-task process metadata** to the fixed-capacity runtime: PID, process-root handle/CR3, per-process `UserRegionTable`, kernel-stack range/top, and pending cleanup data. Keep the dispatcher callback installed once, but have it resolve the current task’s process state instead of pointing at one active-process record. Keep the manager at a stable address for raw callback pointers.

2. **Give each user task a guarded supervisor kernel stack.** Map distinct RW/NX stacks in the shared kernel half, verify they are accessible in every process root, then update TSS.RSP0 with interrupts disabled on each task switch. The current static stack can remain a bootstrap/fallback stack, but cannot serve suspended user tasks. The shared kernel owner must remain alive.

3. **Replace the global exit trampoline with scheduler termination.** `exit` and eligible CPL3 faults should record status, mark the process exited, and switch away without returning to user mode. Reap its root and kernel stack only after the task is no longer active or resumable; keep its process-table zombie/status until its parent’s wait succeeds. Use a safe scheduler/reaper context rather than freeing the current task’s stack.

4. **Implement wait as a retry loop on a bounded exit queue.** Under IF=0, inspect `peek_wait`; if the child is running, sleep on a process-exit queue and retry after wake. On exit, copy status to the waiting process first, then call `reap_exited`; an `EFAULT` must leave the child waitable. Wake waiters after publishing the child’s exited state. Ensure no `&mut ProcessTable` or root-manager reference survives the blocking switch.

5. **Make task creation transactional.** `ProcessTable::spawn` alone publishes a running child, and `Scheduler::create_thread` immediately makes a task ready. Prepare and validate the root, ELF mappings, kernel stack, region table, and task slot before dispatch can see the child; add explicit rollback/cancel support for failures rather than leaving a phantom process or leaked frames.

The uncommitted `mmap_region`/`munmap_region` support fits this design, but each scheduled process needs its own region table. The user allocator’s pages should remain private to that process root and be reclaimed during root teardown.

## A good first QEMU slice

Keep the first slice **cooperative**: leave user RFLAGS.IF clear and avoid user timer preemption until the timer-switch path also handles CR3/TSS. Have the kernel test harness create a real child record, root, and task—no new user `spawn` syscall is needed yet. Schedule the parent first; it calls `wait` while the child is running, blocks, then the child writes and exits with status 7. The parent retries wait, verifies status copyout and reaping, and exits. A stronger variant first waits with an invalid status pointer, expects `EFAULT` without reaping, then retries with a valid pointer.

Extend `just process-smoke` to verify both processes actually ran, the parent resumed from wait, and root/stack teardown restores the frame count. Update `just user-fault-smoke` to terminate and reap a scheduled faulting task through the new exit path. Host tests should cover the wait/check/sleep/retry and wake ordering, failure rollback, and no-reap-on-copyout-fault.

**Key unsafe invariants:** IF must stay clear while changing scheduler/current-process state, CR3, TSS.RSP0, and root active flags; every task stack must remain mapped through its suspended frames; roots may only be destroyed after switching away and invalidating their translations; and no process/root/stack state may be reclaimed while a task can resume. The design remains single-vCPU—these rules do not provide SMP safety.

This was read-only analysis; I did not run tests or builds.

    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;

    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;

//!
//! Bootstrap installs exception and device-IRQ gates with maskable interrupts

#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) type UserExceptionHandler = extern "C" fn(u64, *mut ()) -> bool;

#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct UserSyscallRuntime {
    handler: UserSyscallHandler,
    exception_handler: UserExceptionHandler,
    context: *mut (),
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
static mut USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME: Option<UserSyscallRuntime> = None;
#[no_mangle]
static mut RUSTIX_USER_RESUME_RSP: u64 = 0;
#[no_mangle]
static mut RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING: u8 = 0;
#[no_mangle]
static mut RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS: i32 = 0;
#[repr(C, align(16))]
struct UserKernelFxState([u8; 512]);
#[no_mangle]
static mut RUSTIX_USER_KERNEL_FX_STATE: UserKernelFxState = UserKernelFxState([0; 512]);

/// A device interrupt callback. The callback is responsible for issuing EOI.
pub type IrqHandler = extern "C" fn();

/// Reasons an IRQ callback could not be registered.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum IrqRegistrationError {
    InvalidVector,
    InterruptsEnabled,
    AlreadyRegistered,
}

// In 64-bit mode, exception entry saves SS:RSP even for a CPL 0 fault.
#[repr(C)]
// Register dumps are only compiled with the `fatal-register-dump` feature;
// the vector/error/RIP fields are always needed for the fatal diagnostic.
#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "fatal-register-dump"), allow(dead_code))]
pub(crate) struct ExceptionContext {
    r15: u64,
    r14: u64,
    r13: u64,
    r12: u64,
    r11: u64,
    r10: u64,
    r9: u64,
    r8: u64,
    rbp: u64,
    rdi: u64,
    rsi: u64,
    rdx: u64,
    rcx: u64,
    rbx: u64,
    rax: u64,
    vector: u64,
    error_code: u64,
    rip: u64,
    cs: u64,
    rflags: u64,
    rsp: u64,
    ss: u64,
}

const _: [(); 16] = [(); size_of::<IdtEntry>()];
const _: [(); 4096] = [(); size_of::<IdtTable>()];
const _: [(); 104] = [(); size_of::<TaskStateSegment>()];
const _: [(); 176] = [(); size_of::<ExceptionContext>()];
const _: [(); 120] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, vector)];
const _: [(); 128] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, error_code)];
const _: [(); 136] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rip)];
const _: [(); 144] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, cs)];
const _: [(); 152] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rflags)];
const _: [(); 160] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rsp)];
const _: [(); 168] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, ss)];

extern "C" {
    static exception_stub_table: [usize; EXCEPTION_COUNT];
    static irq_stub_table: [usize; IRQ_STUB_COUNT];
    fn rustix_load_gdt(descriptor_table_pointer: *const DescriptorTablePointer);
    fn rustix_syscall_stub();
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    fn rustix_enter_user(frame: *const rustix_kernel::syscall::UserIretFrame) -> i32;
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    fn rustix_user_exception_exit() -> !;
}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS, exception gates, and device IRQ gates.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[5]).write(USER_DATA_DESCRIPTOR);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[6]).write(USER_CODE_DESCRIPTOR);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 7]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let irq_stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(irq_stub_table).cast::<usize>();
    for vector in IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains one stub for each allocated vector.
        let handler = unsafe { irq_stubs.add(vector - IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR).read() } as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }
    // Vector 0x80 is reserved from device allocation and uses its own DPL-3
    // interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ dispatch path.
    // SAFETY: The assembly defines this dedicated entry stub in the kernel image.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::user_interrupt_gate(
                rustix_syscall_stub as *const () as usize as u64,
            ));
    }

    // SAFETY: The final table entry is the dedicated 0xff spurious-IRQ stub.
    let spurious_handler =
        unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + IRQ_UNWIRED_COUNT).read() } as u64;
    // SAFETY: The APIC spurious vector is a valid IDT index.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(spurious_handler, 0));
    }
    // Vectors 0xf0-0xfe have no registered source; wire them to a controlled
    // fatal stop (through the shared dispatch, which halts) instead of leaving
    // non-present gates that would cascade into #GP with no diagnostics.
    for vector in IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_UNWIRED_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table provides one stub for each vector.
        let handler =
            unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + (vector - IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR)) }.read()
                as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: Every architectural exception gate is initialized in static storage.
    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Configure the active user virtual-address width used to sanitize syscall returns.
///
/// Call after boot CPU discovery and before any CPL3 code can execute.
pub fn configure_user_address_width(virtual_address_bits: u8) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.store(virtual_address_bits, Ordering::Release);
    Ok(())
}

/// Errors returned while selecting the ring-0 entry stack for a user context.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum KernelEntryStackError {
    InvalidVirtualAddressWidth,
    NonCanonical,
    NotKernelAddress,
    Misaligned,
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserRuntimeError {
    InterruptsEnabled,
    AlreadyInstalled,
    NotInstalled,
}

/// Select the stack used by the next privilege transition from CPL3 to CPL0.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must already be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and
/// `stack_top` must be the aligned top of a live, writable supervisor stack that
/// is mapped in the active address space and every address space that may run
/// before this value is changed again. Callers must update it before entering a
/// different process. The function validates the address shape, not the mapping
/// or ownership of the stack memory.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn set_kernel_entry_stack(
    stack_top: u64,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    if stack_top & 0xf != 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::Misaligned);
    }
    if !rustix_kernel::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_top, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NonCanonical);
    }
    if stack_top & (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1)) == 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NotKernelAddress);
    }

    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);
    // SAFETY: The function contract requires initialized TSS storage; the field
    // is packed, so write without creating an aligned reference to it.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(stack_top) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Restore TSS.RSP0 to the bootstrap ring-0 stack.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and the
/// caller must be executing on a different live stack before the restore.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn restore_bootstrap_kernel_entry_stack(
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: `RING0_STACK` is the initialized, fixed-size bootstrap entry stack.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: This function's contract establishes TSS initialization and IF=0.
    unsafe { set_kernel_entry_stack(ring0_top, virtual_address_bits) }
}

/// Install the syscall callback for one synchronously entered user process.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, no other CPU may access this state, and
/// `context` must remain live until the callback is cleared after user return.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn install_user_syscall_handler(
    handler: UserSyscallHandler,
    exception_handler: UserExceptionHandler,
    context: *mut (),
) -> Result<(), UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and the first implementation is single-vCPU.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::AlreadyInstalled);
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the function context live until clearing it.
    unsafe {
        runtime.write(Some(UserSyscallRuntime {
            handler,
            exception_handler,
            context,
        }))
    };
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and assembly reads these values only on this CPU.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS).write(0);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Remove the user-process syscall callback after returning to the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, and no syscall callback may be in flight.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn clear_user_syscall_handler() {
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: The API contract guarantees single-vCPU exclusion with IF clear.
    unsafe { runtime.write(None) };
}

/// Request the syscall/exception assembly exit path after restoring the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// The kernel root must be active, the process root must no longer be active,
/// and execution must be on this single CPU with maskable interrupts disabled.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn request_user_process_exit(status: i32) {
    // SAFETY: The caller satisfies the documented ordering and single-vCPU contract.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS).write(status);
        core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Release);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).write(1);
    }
}

/// Enter a validated user frame and return only through the process-exit path.
///
/// # Safety
/// The process root must already be active in CR3, TSS.RSP0 must point to a live
/// supervisor stack mapped in both roots, syscall and user-fault callbacks must
/// be installed, and maskable interrupts must be disabled.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn enter_user(
    frame: rustix_kernel::syscall::ValidatedUserIretFrame,
) -> Result<i32, UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_none() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::NotInstalled);
    }
    let frame = frame.into_raw();
    // SAFETY: The caller establishes the root, stack, TSS, callback, and fault
    // policy invariants. The assembly returns only after a process exit request.
    Ok(unsafe { rustix_enter_user(&frame) })
}

/// Register one callback for an allocated device IRQ vector.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must keep the IRQ source masked while registering and ensure it
/// is masked whenever this callback is dispatched. The caller must serialize
/// registration against IRQ dispatch on every CPU. `handler` must not allocate,
/// format output, block, or unwind; it runs with IF disabled and owns the EOI.
/// The source must remain masked until all handler state is ready.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn register_irq_handler(
    vector: u8,
    handler: IrqHandler,
) -> Result<(), IrqRegistrationError> {
    let vector = vector as usize;
    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR).contains(&vector) {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InvalidVector);
    }

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: This reads RFLAGS at CPL 0; the temporary push/pop is balanced.
    unsafe {
        asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags));
    }
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }

    // SAFETY: The API contract requires registration to be serialized with IRQ
    // dispatch, and the vector has been checked against the table bounds.
    let slot = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector)
    };
    // SAFETY: `slot` points into the initialized static callback table.
    if unsafe { slot.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::AlreadyRegistered);
    }
    // SAFETY: Registration is serialized by the caller's masking/IF contract.
    unsafe { slot.write(Some(handler)) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Device IRQ target called by the normalized assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_irq_dispatch(vector: u64) {
    // SAFETY: guard records this entry frame for the heap's debug checks; it
    // decrements automatically on every return path.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    if vector == APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR as u64 {
        return;
    }

    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR as u64..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR as u64).contains(&vector) {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }

    // SAFETY: Interrupt gates clear IF, and registration's safety contract
    // serializes writes against this read. No mutable reference is created.
    let handler = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector as usize)
            .read()
    };
    match handler {
        Some(handler) => handler(),
        None => fatal_irq_halt(),
    }
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_syscall_dispatch(context: *mut rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallContext) {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{
        sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame, SyscallArguments, UserIretFrame,
    };

    // SAFETY: The assembly entry is reached only through the DPL-3 syscall gate;
    // the stack pointer refers to its normalized GPR and hardware return frame.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    let Some(context) = (unsafe { context.as_mut() }) else {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    };
    let address_bits = USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if address_bits == 0 {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let frame = UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: context.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: context.code_selector,
        flags: context.flags,
        stack_pointer: context.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: context.stack_selector,
    };
    let frame = match sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(frame, address_bits) {
        Ok(frame) => frame.into_raw(),
        Err(_) => fatal_irq_halt(),
    };
    context.instruction_pointer = frame.instruction_pointer;
    context.code_selector = frame.code_selector;
    context.flags = frame.flags;
    context.stack_pointer = frame.stack_pointer;
    context.stack_selector = frame.stack_selector;

    let arguments = SyscallArguments {
        rdi: context.rdi,
        rsi: context.rsi,
        rdx: context.rdx,
        r10: context.r10,
        r8: context.r8,
        r9: context.r9,
    };
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    let result = {
        let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
        // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
        let runtime = unsafe { runtime.read() };
        if let Some(runtime) = runtime {
            (runtime.handler)(context, runtime.context)
        } else {
            fallback_syscall_result(context.rax, arguments)
        }
    };
    #[cfg(not(feature = "probe-user-process"))]
    let result = fallback_syscall_result(context.rax, arguments);
    context.rax = result as u64;
}

fn fallback_syscall_result(
    number: u64,
    arguments: rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallArguments,
) -> i64 {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{decode_syscall, SyscallError, SyscallRequest, ABI_VERSION};

    match decode_syscall(number, arguments) {
        Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion) => ABI_VERSION as i64,
        Ok(
            SyscallRequest::Exit { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Write { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Wait { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Mmap { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Munmap { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::MmapRegion { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::MunmapRegion { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Close { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Duplicate { .. },
        ) => SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(),
        Err(error) => error.return_value(),
    }
}

fn fatal_irq_halt() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Unknown device interrupts are fatal and must not be retried.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    if context.cs & 3 == 3 && !matches!(context.vector, 2 | 8 | 18) {
        let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
        // SAFETY: Exceptions arrive with IF clear; the diagnostic process runtime
        // is installed only for the synchronous single-vCPU user entry.
        if let Some(runtime) = unsafe { runtime.read() } {
            let depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
            crate::kprintln!(
                "USER EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x}; terminating process",
                context.vector,
                exception_name(context.vector),
                context.error_code
            );
            if context.vector == 14 {
                let fault_address: u64;
                // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is privileged and this handler runs at CPL0.
                unsafe {
                    asm!(
                        "mov {}, cr2",
                        out(reg) fault_address,
                        options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)
                    )
                };
                crate::kprintln!("user page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
            }
            if (runtime.exception_handler)(context.vector, runtime.context) {
                core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Acquire);
                // SAFETY: The callback's contract guarantees it has restored the
                // kernel root and marked the process root inactive before setting
                // this single-vCPU exit flag.
                if unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).read() } != 0 {
                    drop(depth);
                    // SAFETY: The exit callback restored CR3, completed teardown
                    // ownership transitions, and IF remains disabled. The asm
                    // trampoline restores the kernel FPU/stack continuation.
                    unsafe { rustix_user_exception_exit() };
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // SAFETY: guard records this fatal entry frame; fatal paths never return.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    // A fault raised while this handler is running (including a #DF on the
    // IST stack) must not re-enter the printing path; stop silently instead.
    if IN_FATAL_EXCEPTION.swap(true, Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant fatal diagnostics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    crate::kprintln!(
        "FATAL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} SS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RSP={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.ss,
        context.rflags,
        context.rsp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe {
            asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags))
        };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {
        // SAFETY: Active mapping callers provide the current virtual page and run
        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
enum LimineUserFrameMemoryError {
    OutOfBounds,
    Address(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError),
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
struct LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
impl LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    fn frame_slice_address(
        &self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        length: usize,
    ) -> Result<*mut u8, LimineUserFrameMemoryError> {
        if offset
            .checked_add(length)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE as usize)
        {
            return Err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::OutOfBounds);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Ok(core::ptr::null_mut());
        }

        let base = frame
            .hhdm_address(
                self.memory_map,
                self.hhdm_offset,
                self.physical_address_bits,
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address)?;
        let address =
            base.checked_add(offset as u64)
                .ok_or(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address(
                    rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow,
                ))?;
        Ok(address as *mut u8)
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
// SAFETY: The non-copyable Frame token and checked HHDM conversion authorize a
// complete Usable page. Each operation checks its subrange, accesses only that
// page, and uses raw copies rather than forming user virtual references. The
// implementation relies on Limine's mapped-usable-memory contract; hardware
// faults from a broken mapping remain fatal and are not recoverable here.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory for LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    type Error = LimineUserFrameMemoryError;

    fn copy_from_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        destination: &mut [u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let source = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, destination.len())?;
        if !destination.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source, destination.as_mut_ptr(), destination.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn copy_to_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        source: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let destination = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, source.len())?;
        if !source.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source.as_ptr(), destination, source.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

struct KernelHeapMappingContext {
    candidate: *mut (),
    allocator: *mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: *const arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
}

unsafe fn map_kernel_heap_pages(
    opaque_context: *mut (),
    first_page: usize,
    page_count: usize,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, EffectiveMemoryType, MtrrState,
        PagePermissions, PatLayout, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    if page_count == 0
        || first_page
            .checked_add(page_count)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES)
    {
        return false;
    }

    // SAFETY: The caller configures this callback only after the active root,
    // allocator, CPU snapshot, and local context are all live. The boot path is
    // single-vCPU and never returns from the stack containing that context.
    let state = unsafe { &mut *opaque_context.cast::<KernelHeapMappingContext>() };
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the retained local candidate and BootInfo
    // members. The callback is synchronous and never stores a derived reference.
    let candidate = unsafe {
        &mut *state
            .candidate
            .cast::<CandidatePageTables<'static, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>>>()
    };
    // SAFETY: The frame allocator and CPU snapshot remain owned by retained
    // BootInfo; this callback runs on the sole CPU with the heap lock held.
    let allocator = unsafe { &mut *state.allocator };
    // SAFETY: The CPU snapshot is immutable and remains live with BootInfo.
    let cpu_info = unsafe { &*state.cpu_info };

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The callback runs at CPL 0; save IF before disabling local IRQs
    // while the active page tables and allocator are mutated.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) flags) };
    let result = (|| {
        let physical_width = cpu_info.physical_address_bits?;
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(cpu_info.pat_msr_value?).ok()?;
        let mtrrs = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
            MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers.validated_layout(physical_width).ok()?,
            _ => return None,
        };
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        for (mapped, page) in (first_page..first_page + page_count).enumerate() {
            let virtual_address = KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE
                .checked_add((page as u64).checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)?)?;
            let frame = match allocator.allocate() {
                Some(frame) => frame,
                None => {
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
                virtual_address,
                frame.address(),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(physical_width),
                cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            ) {
                Ok(mapping) => mapping,
                Err(_) => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
                CachePolicy::WriteBack,
                pat,
                &mtrrs,
                cpu_info.normal_caching,
            ) {
                Ok(attributes) if attributes.effective_type() == EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack => {
                    attributes
                }
                _ => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            // SAFETY: IF is clear, the current candidate owns the active root,
            // and the allocator-issued frame is mapped RW/NX with local TLB
            // invalidation before its token becomes page-table-owned.
            if let Err(failure) =
                unsafe { candidate.map_owned_page_active(allocator, frame, mapping, attributes) }
            {
                deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, failure.frame);
                rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                return None;
            }
        }
        Some(())
    })()
    .is_some();
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
