## Milestone 5 — VFS, storage, and device ownership

Keep the current RAM filesystem as a bootstrap/test implementation. Persistence and device drivers require explicit block ownership, error handling, and recovery behavior. Split this milestone into M5a (PCI/DMA, block I/O, and a read-only/basic VFS slice) and M5b (writable storage, permissions, and platform services) so each checkpoint has a bounded validation target.

### M5a — PCI/DMA, block I/O, and read-only/basic VFS

- [ ] Define VFS node, mount, path, metadata, and file-descriptor contracts independently of a particular disk format.
- [ ] Preserve volatile RAMFS as a test backend and add tests for mount/path errors, capacity, partial I/O, and object lifetime.
- [ ] Establish bounded PCI/device discovery, including checked ACPI MCFG handling where required, before adding PCI-backed devices. Keep discovery separate from individual driver policy.
- [ ] Define DMA buffer ownership, address translation, cache synchronization, device reset, and error handling before any device can DMA into kernel memory. Scope and test the trust assumptions; do not equate PCI enumeration with safe DMA.
- [ ] Add a narrowly scoped block-device interface with request validation, timeout/error reporting, and a QEMU-supported initial device driver (such as virtio-blk) on top of the shared PCI/DMA foundations.
- [ ] Choose and document the first on-disk filesystem format before implementing writable storage. Specify partition discovery, byte order, block size, metadata limits, corruption handling, and read-only/recovery behavior; begin with a read-only mount and bounded metadata parsing.
- [ ] Test read-only mount, lookup, and read behavior against reproducible images, including malformed metadata and I/O errors. Do not expose on-disk write operations in this slice; the volatile RAMFS remains available as a writable test backend.
- [ ] Define file descriptors and basic process I/O semantics before exposing filesystem operations to applications.

### M5b — writable filesystem, permissions, and platform services

- [ ] On detected corruption, report the failure and refuse writable mounting rather than attempting automatic repair. Plan a separate offline checker/repair tool; do not repair data implicitly.
- [ ] Define crash-safe atomic replacement or equivalent transactional behavior for critical files such as account metadata and credentials. Flush the new data before replacing the old file, and test interruption at each update stage.
- [ ] Define explicit no-space errors and partial-write behavior. Never silently discard or overwrite existing user data to recover space.
- [ ] Add persistent write/read/remount/reboot and failure-injection integration tests; never claim persistence from an in-memory cache alone.
- [ ] Define the planned top-level filesystem layout: `/home`, `/root`, `/etc`, `/usr`, `/dev`, `/proc`, `/sys`, `/tmp`, `/var`, `/run`, `/mnt`, `/media`, and `/boot`, plus `/usr/sbin`. Document that `/proc` and `/sys` are future virtual interfaces, `/dev` exposes device interfaces, `/tmp` and `/run` are volatile, and mount-point and boot-file usage depends on later storage/boot design.
- [ ] Specify filesystem ownership and permission metadata. Support owner/group/other read, write, and execute permissions, default creation modes/umask, and the directory sticky bit. Use sticky-directory semantics for `/tmp` (mode equivalent to `01777`) and later `/home/Public/`, so users can create entries without removing or renaming another user's files.
- [ ] Specify that `/etc` and `/usr` are root-owned and writable only by root, while normal users may read configuration and execute permitted programs. Keep readable account metadata separate from a root-only credential file containing password hashes. Reserve `/usr/Apps` for globally installed `.app` GUI applications and `/usr/bin` for globally installed `.bin` command-line tools; `/usr/sbin` is reserved for system-administration tools if needed.
- [ ] Provide a trustworthy CSPRNG before password hashing or security-sensitive random values. Evaluate validated entropy sources (for example, supported CPU randomness instructions or a virtio RNG device) as inputs; do not treat one hardware source alone as a complete CSPRNG. Test initialization, failure, and unavailable-entropy behavior.
- [ ] Provide wall-clock time before persistent audit logs require calendar timestamps. Keep monotonic time as the source for elapsed-time and timeout calculations; define behavior when the wall clock is unavailable or invalid.
- [ ] Define kernel/platform shutdown and reboot operations, including filesystem flush ordering and failure behavior. Parse and validate ACPI FADT power-control data when needed; test the supported QEMU shutdown/reboot paths.

**M5a exit criteria:** bounded PCI discovery and the DMA ownership policy are validated for the supported QEMU device path; the block driver passes bounded request, timeout, and error tests; a reproducible image mounts the documented filesystem read-only, with lookup/read tests covering malformed metadata and device errors. No writable mount is implied.

**M5b exit criteria:** writable filesystem behavior is validated across remount and reboot, including crash/failure injection, corruption refusal, I/O errors, and exhausted-space behavior; permission and sticky-directory rules, CSPRNG failure behavior, wall-clock fallback, and supported ACPI shutdown/reboot paths are tested. Milestone 5 validates storage through test/integration harnesses; user-space utilities are verified in Milestone 6.

## Milestone 6 — initial userspace and command-line utilities

Crabshell is currently an in-kernel parser/frontend. The long-term terminal application should reuse its parser model without linking kernel internals or bypassing syscalls.

The planned filesystem layout is illustrated below. This is a directory-layout proposal, not a claim that these paths or services are implemented; `/dev`, `/proc`, and `/sys` are intended system interfaces, while `/tmp` and `/run` are volatile.

```text
/
├── boot/
├── dev/
├── etc/
├── home/
│   ├── Public/  (created when a second account is added)
│   └── test/
│       ├── Apps/
│       ├── Desktop/
│       ├── Documents/
│       ├── Downloads/
│       ├── Pictures/
│       ├── Videos/
│       ├── .bin/
│       ├── .config/
│       └── .local/
├── media/
├── mnt/
├── proc/
├── root/
├── run/
├── sys/
├── tmp/
├── usr/
│   ├── Apps/
│   ├── bin/
│   └── sbin/
└── var/
    └── log/
```

### Planned work

- [ ] Build on the minimal `init` process and syscall/runtime foundations from Milestone 4. Establish executable search, environment, current directory, descriptor inheritance, and process startup rules using the VFS.
- [ ] Design a local-account and privilege model. Reserve UID/GID 0 for root, IDs 1–999 for future system/service accounts, and assign regular users IDs starting at 1000; initially give each user a primary group with the same ID. Use local username/password authentication, with a reviewed password-hashing implementation, a unique salt, and the Milestone 5 CSPRNG; Argon2id is a candidate, but exact implementation and parameters require a later security review. Never store plaintext passwords.
- [ ] Create the first regular account through installation or first-boot setup and grant it administrator privileges. Later accounts are standard users by default; root can explicitly grant or revoke administrator status. Run a text login prompt on the serial/terminal console and start the shell under the authenticated user's identity. Do not permit direct root login during normal operation; GUI login is deferred to the GUI milestone.
- [ ] Create `/home/{username}/` for each regular user and `/root/` for the root account. Give regular-user homes `Apps/`, `Desktop/`, `Documents/`, `Downloads/`, `Pictures/`, `Videos/`, `.local/`, `.config/`, and `.bin/` directories. Homes and newly created files are private by default. Use owner/group/other read, write, and execute permissions initially; defer ACLs.
- [ ] Create `/home/Public/` when a second account is added. All users may read it and add files; only a file's owner or root may change or remove that file. Implement and test this with sticky-directory semantics rather than ordinary `rwx` bits alone.
- [ ] Keep `/etc` and `/usr` root-owned and writable only by root. Normal users may read configuration and execute permitted programs. Store readable account metadata separately from password hashes, which must be in a root-only credential file. Global `.app` files go in `/usr/Apps/`; global `.bin` tools go in `/usr/bin/`.
- [ ] Provide a root-only `userctl` command-line tool for creating, disabling, removing, and administering accounts, changing passwords, and granting or revoking administrator privileges. Account removal disables login but preserves the home directory unless file deletion is explicitly requested.
- [ ] Provide designated, administrator-controlled recovery media that can reset any local account, including an administrator account, without a separate recovery secret in the initial design. Document that this alone does not protect against physical attackers; secure boot and disk encryption are separate future security work.
- [ ] Restrict `sudo` to administrators; require the invoking administrator's password for every invocation, with no credential caching. Run the requested command as root using a restricted trusted command path, not the caller's environment. Add increasing delays after repeated failed password attempts rather than permanent account lockout. Record successful and failed privileged actions in `/var/log/` without logging passwords.
- [ ] Establish normal command lookup order as `~/.bin/` before `/usr/bin/`; `sudo` must use its restricted trusted system path instead of inheriting the user's search path.
- [ ] Port or adapt Crabshell into a userspace terminal application that uses only the documented syscall/VFS interfaces. Introduce TTY and PTY abstractions for serial and later graphical terminals so the shell does not depend on a specific device.
- [ ] Move `cp`, `mv`, `mkdir`, and future command-line utilities into separate application crates using the shared userspace runtime and `.bin` suffix. Preinstall the initial tools in the reproducible system image. Later per-user installation copies files into `~/.bin/`; global installation into `/usr/bin/` requires root. Never silently overwrite a same-named tool; defer package management, dependency tracking, and automatic updates.
- [ ] Track the installed image size and per-binary contributions as the static utility set grows. Keep `librustix` lean and `no_std`-friendly, avoid duplicating embedded resources across tools, and set explicit image/storage budgets before adding many separately linked utilities.
- [ ] Add bounded pipe buffers and a minimal process-control model: foreground process groups, `SIGINT` for `Ctrl+C`, `SIGCHLD`/wait status for child exit, and a basic `kill` mechanism. Implement these before enabling pipelines, redirection, or interrupting a foreground command. Keep semantics explicit and tested rather than claiming full POSIX job control.
- [ ] Add command-line quoting, escaping, and history only with parser tests; enable redirection and pipelines only after the corresponding descriptor, pipe, TTY/PTY, and signal semantics are implemented.
- [ ] Defer installation of single-file GUI `.app` files into `~/Apps/` or `/usr/Apps/` to the GUI milestone. Initial installation there is copying a file and removal is deleting it; global installation requires root, and name conflicts must never silently overwrite an existing app.
- [ ] Add administrator-only `shutdown` and `reboot` user commands as separate `.bin` command crates, using the Milestone 5 kernel/platform operations.
- [ ] Add integration tests for login identity, account-ID allocation, password verification and failure delays, private homes, `/home/Public/` sticky-directory behavior, `/etc` and `/usr` write restrictions, `sudo` authorization and trusted command lookup, `userctl` authorization, account recovery, process signals/wait status, pipes, foreground `Ctrl+C`, and launching tools as user processes. Verify password hashes are not exposed and credentials never appear in logs.

**Exit criteria:** the userspace shell and basic `.bin` tools run as isolated processes from a reproducible filesystem image using the shared userspace runtime; local login and account administration enforce the documented identity and permission model; account, `sudo`, recovery, TTY, process-control, and command-launch tests pass; no shell command directly calls kernel-private VFS internals.

## Milestone 7 — ARM64 (AArch64) platform support (long-term)

The current implementation targets x86_64. Add ARM64 as a separate platform backend without weakening the existing x86_64 path or implying feature parity. Start with one documented emulator configuration and expand only when its boot, memory, interrupt, and device contracts are validated.

### Planned work

- [ ] Select and document the initial AArch64 execution environment, firmware/boot protocol, Rust target, linker layout, entry state, and supported CPU/platform assumptions. Use QEMU `virt` as the first repeatable emulator target.
- [ ] Add an isolated AArch64 architecture backend and target-specific build/boot configuration; preserve the working x86_64 target and share code only where the architecture-independent contract is clear.
- [ ] Establish a minimal boot path with bounded serial diagnostics and validated boot metadata, kernel-image bounds, stack state, and usable-memory ownership. Reject unsupported or malformed handoff state visibly.
- [ ] Implement the architecture-specific exception/vector setup, translation-table and cache-maintenance operations, timer, and interrupt-controller path required by the kernel's supported runtime. Keep privileged instructions and raw MMIO access narrow and documented.
- [ ] Adapt the existing kernel services incrementally to explicit architecture interfaces. Keep features unavailable on AArch64 disabled rather than silently approximating their behavior.
- [ ] Add host tests for architecture-independent policy and repeatable AArch64 QEMU tests for boot, diagnostics, memory setup, and configured interrupt/timer behavior. Track physical-hardware validation separately.

**Exit criteria:** the documented AArch64 QEMU target boots the Rustix kernel through a validated platform initialization path, runs the explicitly supported kernel services with integration evidence, and leaves the existing x86_64 validation path passing. This milestone does not claim userspace or full feature parity across architectures.

---

## Milestone 8 — graphical console and GUI (long-term)

A GUI is intentionally downstream of stable memory management, interrupts/input, process isolation, drivers, and userspace. Keep Crabshell's parser independent so a graphical terminal frontend can reuse it.

### Planned work

- [ ] Add validated framebuffer discovery and memory ownership; implement a minimal text/graphics console without compromising serial panic diagnostics.
- [ ] Establish an input subsystem that separates raw device events from key mapping and terminal policy. Plan PS/2 and USB HID support separately; do not treat the current raw scancode poller as a keyboard driver stack.
- [ ] Define a graphics buffer ownership/presentation API, clipping rules, pixel format, and bounds/overflow checks.
- [ ] Implement a minimal compositor/windowing policy only after process isolation and input routing are ready.
- [ ] Define and launch single-file `.app` GUI applications using the documented static ELF64 format and shared userspace runtime; specify how any required resources are embedded.
- [ ] Support drag-and-drop installation of a `.app` file into `~/Apps/`; global installation into `/usr/Apps/` requires root. Reject malformed apps and never silently overwrite an existing file.
- [ ] Run Crabshell as a terminal application in a GUI window using the same parser and userspace services as the serial/TTY path, backed by the TTY/PTY interface rather than direct device access.
- [ ] Preserve serial as a headless recovery/debug console and add repeatable QEMU display/input tests.

**Exit criteria:** a documented GUI session starts from userspace, renders a terminal, accepts tested input, and does not require direct kernel-private VFS access.

---

## Milestone 9 — networking (long-term, after drivers and process isolation)

Networking is not implied by the current device drivers. The initial target should be a tightly scoped virtual-device path with clear ownership and bounded buffers.

### Planned work

- [ ] Build on the PCI discovery and DMA ownership/mapping foundations established in Milestone 5; add only networking-specific device and buffer policy here.
- [ ] Implement one virtual NIC driver with bounded queues and timeouts; test against QEMU user networking.
- [ ] Choose and document a minimal link/network protocol scope before implementation. Keep packet parsing length-checked and fuzzable on the host.
- [ ] Add interface configuration, routing, socket/descriptor ownership, and per-process access policy.
- [ ] Add adversarial packet tests and integration tests for link loss, malformed packets, queue exhaustion, and device reset.
- [ ] Add higher-level transports/services only when the required protocol semantics, tested CSPRNG/entropy-source behavior, and security model are designed.

**Exit criteria:** documented user processes can communicate through a tested virtual NIC/network stack, with malformed input and resource exhaustion handled safely. Do not claim internet, TLS, or POSIX sockets merely from a packet driver.

---

## Milestone 10 — installation, updates, and physical security (long-term)

This milestone depends on persistent storage. Local installation and update workflows can precede networking; remote update-server integration additionally depends on the networking and GUI milestones. Recovery media by itself is not protection against physical attackers.

### Planned work

- [ ] Define a reproducible installer for placing Rustix on a target disk, including partition/boot setup, first-boot account creation, failure handling, and recovery. Preserve a supported local/offline install path.
- [ ] Define system upgrade transactions with integrity checks, safe interruption behavior, and rollback or recovery after a failed upgrade. Do not report success until changes are durable.
- [ ] Add a package manager for both `.app` GUI applications and `.bin` command-line tools. Support per-user and system-wide installation/removal; system-wide changes require root. Keep package/dependency metadata and file ownership consistent with the filesystem policy.
- [ ] Require signed update metadata and packages, verified before installation. Trust Rustix's official signing keys for system updates; require explicit user trust for third-party user-app publishers or repositories. In-app updaters must use the same verification policy.
- [ ] Route system-application updates through Rustix system updates and the package manager. Allow user-installed applications to update through either a verified in-app updater or the package manager.
- [ ] Once networking and the GUI are available, let the GUI check an update server and fetch eligible system and application updates. Keep the local/offline update path available.
- [ ] Design secure boot, disk encryption, and key recovery as long-term physical-security goals. Specify the threat model and recovery-key policy before claiming protection against physical attackers.

**Exit criteria:** a documented local installation and upgrade path recovers safely from interrupted or invalid updates; package signatures and repository trust are enforced; and physical-security claims match the implemented boot and key-protection mechanisms.

---

## Cross-cutting acceptance gates

Every milestone should include the relevant subset of these gates:

1. **Design:** documented ownership, invariants, resource limits, error semantics, and unsupported cases.
2. **Tests:** host tests for pure policy and malformed/boundary input; integration tests for hardware-facing behavior.
3. **Safety:** review unsafe blocks, pointer provenance/access, integer overflow, privilege boundaries, concurrency, and cleanup/rollback paths.
4. **Build:** format, host tests, target check, and final ELF link as appropriate.
5. **Boot/integration:** QEMU tests for changes to boot, paging, descriptors, interrupts, drivers, processes, or persistence.
6. **Documentation/status:** update architecture and roadmap docs; never check off a criterion without evidence.
7. **Compatibility:** claim Unix/POSIX behavior only for the exact documented subset with conformance-style tests.
8. **Privilege boundaries:** test user/kernel fault separation, file ownership and special permission bits, credential confidentiality, trusted `sudo` command lookup, and recovery assumptions.
9. **Resource readiness:** do not begin process, VFS-cache, or driver workloads that require dynamic allocation, active mappings, DMA, wall-clock time, or secure randomness until the corresponding service and failure behavior are validated.

## Working rule

Prefer a small end-to-end vertical slice over broad, unbootable scaffolding. A source file, interface, or architecture document is not proof that the corresponding subsystem is operational. When a check cannot run, record the exact environment blocker and leave that acceptance gate pending.

fn main() {
    let root = PathBuf::from(env::var_os("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").expect("manifest directory"));
    let source = root.join("crates/rustix-init/src/main.rs");
    let linker_script = root.join("crates/rustix-init/linker.ld");
    let runtime_source = root.join("crates/rustix-user/src/lib.rs");
    let runtime_manifest = root.join("crates/rustix-user/Cargo.toml");

    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", linker_script.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", runtime_source.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", runtime_manifest.display());
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=RUSTC");

    if env::var("CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS").as_deref() != Ok("none") {
        return;
    }

    let rustc = env::var_os("RUSTC").expect("Cargo provides RUSTC");
    let out_dir = PathBuf::from(env::var_os("OUT_DIR").expect("Cargo provides OUT_DIR"));
    let runtime = out_dir.join("librustix_user.rlib");
    let runtime_status = Command::new(&rustc)
        .current_dir(&root)
        .arg("--crate-name")
        .arg("rustix_user")
        .arg("--edition=2021")
        .arg("--crate-type=rlib")
        .arg("--target=x86_64-unknown-none")
        .arg("-Cpanic=abort")
        .arg("-Copt-level=2")
        .arg("-Ccode-model=small")
        .arg("-Crelocation-model=static")
        .arg("-Ctarget-feature=-avx,-avx2,-avx512f")
        .arg(&runtime_source)
        .arg("--out-dir")
        .arg(&out_dir)
        .status()
        .expect("failed to invoke rustc for the rustix-user runtime");
    assert!(
        runtime_status.success(),
        "failed to build rustix-user runtime"
    );

    let child_output = out_dir.join("rustix-child.elf");
    let child_status = Command::new(&rustc)
        .current_dir(&root)

        .arg("--crate-name")

        .arg("--cfg=rustix_child_probe")
        .arg("--crate-type=bin")
        .arg("--target=x86_64-unknown-none")
        .arg("-Cpanic=abort")
        .arg("-Copt-level=2")
        .arg("-Ccode-model=small")
        .arg("-Crelocation-model=static")
        .arg("-Ctarget-feature=-avx,-avx2,-avx512f")
        .arg(format!("-Clink-arg=-T{}", linker_script.display()))
        .arg("-Clink-arg=--build-id=none")
        .arg("--extern")
        .arg(format!("rustix_user={}", runtime.display()))
        .arg(&source)
        .arg("-o")
        .arg(&child_output)
        .status()
        .expect("failed to invoke rustc for the child probe payload");
    assert!(child_status.success(), "failed to build child probe ELF");

    let output = out_dir.join("rustix-init.elf");
    let linker_arg = format!("-T{}", linker_script.display());
    let mut command = Command::new(rustc);
    command
        .current_dir(&root)
        .env("OUT_DIR", &out_dir)
        .arg("--crate-name")
        .arg("rustix_init")
        .arg("--edition=2021")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_fault_probe)")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_child_probe)")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_user_fault_ud)")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_user_fault_page)")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_user_fault_gp)")
        .arg("--check-cfg=cfg(rustix_user_fault_de)")
        .arg("--crate-type=bin")

        .arg(format!("-Clink-arg={linker_arg}"))

        .arg("--extern")
        .arg(format!("rustix_user={}", runtime.display()))
        .arg(&source)

    let fault_modes = [

        ),

            "rustix_user_fault_de",

    let enabled_fault_modes: Vec<_> = fault_modes

    assert!(

    if let Some((_, mode)) = enabled_fault_modes.first() {

    let status = command

    );
}

const HEAP_MESSAGE: &[u8] = b"rustix-init: heap Vec and Box round-trip ok\n";
const MULTI_PAGE_MESSAGE: &[u8] = b"rustix-init: multi-page mmap zero/write/unmap ok\n";

#[cfg(not(rustix_child_probe))]
static CHILD_ELF_IMAGE: &[u8] = include_bytes!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/rustix-child.elf"));

#[cfg(rustix_child_probe)]
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn _start() -> ! {
    if rustix_user::write_all(
        rustix_user::STDOUT,
        b"rustix-child: real child entered ring 3 and is exiting\n",
    )
    .is_err()
    {
        exit(70);
    }
    rustix_user::exit(7)
}

#[cfg(not(rustix_child_probe))]
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn _start() -> ! {
    #[cfg(rustix_fault_probe)]
    trigger_user_fault();

    #[cfg(not(rustix_fault_probe))]
    rustix_user::run_main(init_main)
}

#[cfg(all(not(rustix_fault_probe), not(rustix_child_probe)))]
fn init_main() -> i32 {
    {
        // SAFETY: The kernel maps this byte in the newly allocated initial stack
        // page and clears the page before entering this diagnostic process.
        if unsafe { (USER_STACK_BASE as *const u8).read_volatile() } != 0 {
            exit(130);
        }

        let version = rustix_user::abi_version().unwrap_or(0);
        if version != rustix_user::ABI_VERSION {
            exit(120);
        }

        if !matches!(
            rustix_user::mmap(0),
            Err(rustix_user::SyscallError::InvalidArgument)
        ) {
            exit(136);
        }
        if !matches!(
            rustix_user::mmap(rustix_user::USER_PAGE_SIZE + 1),
            Err(rustix_user::SyscallError::ArgumentListTooLong)
        ) {
            exit(137);
        }
        let protected_stack_unmap = rustix_user::syscall(
            rustix_user::SYS_MUNMAP,
            [
                USER_STACK_BASE,
                rustix_user::USER_PAGE_SIZE as u64,
                0,
                0,
                0,
                0,
            ],
        );
        if protected_stack_unmap != -1 {
            exit(138);
        }

        let anonymous_page = match rustix_user::mmap(1) {
            Ok(region) => region,
            Err(_) => exit(131),
        };
        let anonymous_pointer = anonymous_page.as_mut_ptr();
        // SAFETY: The kernel returns one mapped, zeroed, writable user page, and
        // this process has exclusive access to its new anonymous region.
        unsafe {
            if anonymous_pointer.read_volatile() != 0 {
                exit(132);
            }
            anonymous_pointer.write_volatile(0x5a);
            if anonymous_pointer.read_volatile() != 0x5a {
                exit(133);
            }
        }
        let anonymous_address = anonymous_page.address();
        if rustix_user::munmap(anonymous_page).is_err() {
            exit(134);
        }
        let unmapped_write = rustix_user::syscall(
            rustix_user::SYS_WRITE,
            [rustix_user::STDOUT, anonymous_address, 1, 0, 0, 0],
        );
        if unmapped_write != -3 {
            exit(135);
        }
        let repeated_unmap = rustix_user::syscall(
            rustix_user::SYS_MUNMAP,
            [
                anonymous_address,
                rustix_user::USER_PAGE_SIZE as u64,
                0,
                0,
                0,
                0,
            ],
        );
        if repeated_unmap != -1 {
            exit(139);
        }

        let multi_page = match rustix_user::mmap_region(rustix_user::USER_PAGE_SIZE + 1) {
            Ok(region) if region.length() == rustix_user::USER_PAGE_SIZE * 2 => region,
            _ => exit(148),
        };
        let multi_page_address = multi_page.address();
        // SAFETY: mmap_region returns two zeroed, writable pages, and these
        // accesses straddle their boundary while remaining within the mapping.
        unsafe {
            let first = multi_page.as_mut_ptr().add(rustix_user::USER_PAGE_SIZE - 1);
            let second = multi_page.as_mut_ptr().add(rustix_user::USER_PAGE_SIZE);
            if first.read_volatile() != 0 || second.read_volatile() != 0 {
                exit(149);
            }
            first.write_volatile(0xa5);
            second.write_volatile(0x5a);
            if first.read_volatile() != 0xa5 || second.read_volatile() != 0x5a {
                exit(150);
            }
        }
        let partial_multi_page_unmap = rustix_user::syscall(
            rustix_user::SYS_MUNMAP_REGION,
            [
                multi_page_address,
                rustix_user::USER_PAGE_SIZE as u64,
                0,
                0,
                0,
                0,
            ],
        );
        if partial_multi_page_unmap != -1 {
            exit(154);
        }
        // SAFETY: Rejected partial unmaps must leave the complete region mapped.
        unsafe {
            if (multi_page_address as *const u8)
                .add(rustix_user::USER_PAGE_SIZE - 1)
                .read_volatile()
                != 0xa5
            {
                exit(155);
            }
        }
        if rustix_user::munmap_region(multi_page).is_err() {
            exit(151);
        }
        let stale_multi_page_write = rustix_user::syscall(
            rustix_user::SYS_WRITE,
            [rustix_user::STDOUT, multi_page_address, 1, 0, 0, 0],
        );
        if stale_multi_page_write != -3 {
            exit(152);
        }
        if rustix_user::write_all(rustix_user::STDOUT, MULTI_PAGE_MESSAGE).is_err() {
            exit(153);
        }

        if rustix_user::write_fmt(
            rustix_user::STDOUT,
            format_args!("rustix-init: hello from ring {}\n", 3),
        )
        .is_err()
        {
            exit(121);
        }

        let invalid_write = rustix_user::syscall(
            rustix_user::SYS_WRITE,
            [rustix_user::STDOUT, 0x5000_0000, 1, 0, 0, 0],
        );
        if invalid_write != -3 {
            exit(122);
        }
        if rustix_user::write_all(rustix_user::STDOUT, FAULT_MESSAGE).is_err() {
            exit(123);
        }

        let invalid_wait =
            rustix_user::syscall(rustix_user::SYS_WAIT, [0, 0x5000_0000, 0, 0, 0, 0]);
        if invalid_wait != -3 {
            exit(124);
        }
        let mut wait_status = i32::MIN;
        let waited_pid = match rustix_user::wait(0, Some(&mut wait_status)) {
            Ok(pid) => pid,
            Err(_) => exit(125),
        };
        let waited_status = wait_status;
        if waited_pid == 0 || waited_status != 7 {
            exit(125);
        }
        if rustix_user::write_all(rustix_user::STDOUT, WAIT_MESSAGE).is_err() {
            exit(126);
        }

        let duplicate_stdout = match rustix_user::dup(rustix_user::STDOUT) {
            Ok(fd) if fd >= 3 => fd,
            _ => exit(140),
        };
        if rustix_user::write_all(duplicate_stdout, b"rustix-init: duplicated stdout works\n")
            .is_err()
        {
            exit(141);
        }
        if rustix_user::close(duplicate_stdout).is_err() {
            exit(142);
        }
        if !matches!(
            rustix_user::write(duplicate_stdout, b"closed"),
            Err(rustix_user::SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor)
        ) {
            exit(143);
        }
        if !matches!(
            rustix_user::dup(duplicate_stdout),
            Err(rustix_user::SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor)
        ) {
            exit(144);
        }
        if !matches!(
            rustix_user::close(duplicate_stdout),
            Err(rustix_user::SyscallError::BadFileDescriptor)
        ) {
            exit(145);
        }

        let values: Vec<u32> = (0..64).collect();
        let boxed = Box::new(values.iter().map(|value| u64::from(*value)).sum::<u64>());
        if *boxed != 2016 || values.len() != 64 {
            exit(146);
        }
        drop(values);
        drop(boxed);
        if rustix_user::write_all(rustix_user::STDOUT, HEAP_MESSAGE).is_err() {
            exit(147);
        }

        if !matches!(
            rustix_user::wait(0, None),
            Err(rustix_user::SyscallError::NotSupported)
        ) {
            exit(128);
        }
        if rustix_user::write_all(rustix_user::STDOUT, RUNNING_WAIT_MESSAGE).is_err() {
            exit(129);
        }
        42
    }
}

#[cfg(all(rustix_fault_probe, not(rustix_child_probe)))]
fn trigger_user_fault() -> ! {
    #[cfg(rustix_user_fault_ud)]
    // SAFETY: This payload variant deliberately raises user-mode #UD in QEMU.
    unsafe {
        asm!("ud2", options(noreturn));
    }

    #[cfg(rustix_user_fault_page)]
    // SAFETY: The diagnostic process maps one stack page at USER_STACK_BASE;
    // this reads the immediately preceding unmapped guard page from Ring 3.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "mov rax, {guard}",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            guard = const USER_STACK_GUARD_ADDRESS,
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack, readonly)
        );
    }

    #[cfg(rustix_user_fault_gp)]
    // SAFETY: DPL 0 vector 0x20 is intentionally invoked from Ring 3 to trigger
    // #GP before the interrupt handler can run.
    unsafe {
        asm!("int 0x20", options(nomem, nostack));
    }

    #[cfg(rustix_user_fault_de)]
    // SAFETY: The zero divisor deliberately produces user-mode #DE in QEMU.
    unsafe {
        asm!(
            "xor edx, edx",
            "xor eax, eax",
            "xor ecx, ecx",
            "div ecx",
            out("eax") _,
            out("edx") _,
            out("ecx") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }

    loop {
        core::hint::spin_loop();
    }
}

#[inline]
fn exit(status: i32) -> ! {
    rustix_user::exit(status)
}

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    rustix_user::panic_exit(info)
}

//! Bootstrap GDT, TSS, and interrupt entry for x86_64.
//!
//! Bootstrap installs exception and device-IRQ gates with maskable interrupts
//! disabled. APIC setup, route masking, handler registration, and explicit `sti`
//! are owned by the boot path. Kernel exceptions and selected critical user
//! exceptions remain fatal; the diagnostic user-process path can reap other CPL3 faults.

    attributes: u8,
    offset_middle: u16,
    offset_high: u32,

}

impl IdtEntry {
    const MISSING: Self = Self {
        offset_low: 0,
        selector: 0,
        ist: 0,
        attributes: 0,
        offset_middle: 0,
        offset_high: 0,
        reserved: 0,
    };

    fn interrupt_gate(handler: u64, ist: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            offset_low: handler as u16,
            selector: KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR,
            ist: ist & 0x07,
            attributes: 0x8e,
            offset_middle: (handler >> 16) as u16,
            offset_high: (handler >> 32) as u32,
            reserved: 0,
        }
    }

    fn user_interrupt_gate(handler: u64) -> Self {
        let mut entry = Self::interrupt_gate(handler, 0);
        entry.attributes = 0xee;
        entry
    }
}

const _: [(); 136] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rip)];
const _: [(); 144] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, cs)];
const _: [(); 152] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rflags)];
const _: [(); 160] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, rsp)];
const _: [(); 168] = [(); core::mem::offset_of!(ExceptionContext, ss)];

extern "C" {
    static exception_stub_table: [usize; EXCEPTION_COUNT];
    static irq_stub_table: [usize; IRQ_STUB_COUNT];
    fn rustix_load_gdt(descriptor_table_pointer: *const DescriptorTablePointer);
    fn rustix_syscall_stub();
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    fn rustix_enter_user(frame: *const rustix_kernel::syscall::UserIretFrame) -> i32;
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    fn rustix_user_exception_exit() -> !;
}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS, exception gates, and device IRQ gates.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[5]).write(USER_DATA_DESCRIPTOR);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[6]).write(USER_CODE_DESCRIPTOR);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 7]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let irq_stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(irq_stub_table).cast::<usize>();
    for vector in IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains one stub for each allocated vector.
        let handler = unsafe { irq_stubs.add(vector - IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR).read() } as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }
    // Vector 0x80 is reserved from device allocation and uses its own DPL-3
    // interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ dispatch path.
    // SAFETY: The assembly defines this dedicated entry stub in the kernel image.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::user_interrupt_gate(
                rustix_syscall_stub as *const () as usize as u64,
            ));
    }

    // SAFETY: The final table entry is the dedicated 0xff spurious-IRQ stub.
    let spurious_handler =
        unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + IRQ_UNWIRED_COUNT).read() } as u64;
    // SAFETY: The APIC spurious vector is a valid IDT index.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(spurious_handler, 0));
    }
    // Vectors 0xf0-0xfe have no registered source; wire them to a controlled
    // fatal stop (through the shared dispatch, which halts) instead of leaving
    // non-present gates that would cascade into #GP with no diagnostics.
    for vector in IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_UNWIRED_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table provides one stub for each vector.
        let handler =
            unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + (vector - IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR)) }.read()
                as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: Every architectural exception gate is initialized in static storage.
    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Configure the active user virtual-address width used to sanitize syscall returns.
///
/// Call after boot CPU discovery and before any CPL3 code can execute.
pub fn configure_user_address_width(virtual_address_bits: u8) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.store(virtual_address_bits, Ordering::Release);
    Ok(())
}

/// Errors returned while selecting the ring-0 entry stack for a user context.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum KernelEntryStackError {
    InvalidVirtualAddressWidth,
    NonCanonical,
    NotKernelAddress,
    Misaligned,
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserRuntimeError {
    InterruptsEnabled,
    AlreadyInstalled,
    NotInstalled,
    EntryDepthExceeded,
}

/// Select the stack used by the next privilege transition from CPL3 to CPL0.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must already be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and
/// `stack_top` must be the aligned top of a live, writable supervisor stack that
/// is mapped in the active address space and every address space that may run
/// before this value is changed again. Callers must update it before entering a
/// different process. The function validates the address shape, not the mapping
/// or ownership of the stack memory.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn set_kernel_entry_stack(
    stack_top: u64,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    if stack_top & 0xf != 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::Misaligned);
    }
    if !rustix_kernel::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_top, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NonCanonical);
    }
    if stack_top & (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1)) == 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NotKernelAddress);
    }

    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);
    // SAFETY: The function contract requires initialized TSS storage; the field
    // is packed, so write without creating an aligned reference to it.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(stack_top) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Restore TSS.RSP0 to the bootstrap ring-0 stack.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and the
/// caller must be executing on a different live stack before the restore.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn restore_bootstrap_kernel_entry_stack(
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: `RING0_STACK` is the initialized, fixed-size bootstrap entry stack.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: This function's contract establishes TSS initialization and IF=0.
    unsafe { set_kernel_entry_stack(ring0_top, virtual_address_bits) }
}

/// Install the syscall callback for one synchronously entered user process.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, no other CPU may access this state, and
/// `context` must remain live until the callback is cleared after user return.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn install_user_syscall_handler(
    handler: UserSyscallHandler,
    exception_handler: UserExceptionHandler,
    context: *mut (),
) -> Result<(), UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and the first implementation is single-vCPU.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::AlreadyInstalled);
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the function context live until clearing it.
    unsafe {
        runtime.write(Some(UserSyscallRuntime {
            handler,
            exception_handler,
            context,
        }))
    };
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and assembly reads these values only on this CPU.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_ENTRY_DEPTH).write(0);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Remove the user-process syscall callback after returning to the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, and no syscall callback may be in flight.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn clear_user_syscall_handler() {
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and no user-entry trampoline may remain active when
    // clearing the callback or its nesting state.
    if unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_USER_ENTRY_DEPTH).read() } != 0 {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: The API contract guarantees single-vCPU exclusion with IF clear.
    unsafe { runtime.write(None) };
}

/// Select the process context used by the installed syscall callbacks.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, the callback must be installed, and the
/// context must remain live until it is replaced or the handler is cleared.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn set_user_syscall_context(context: *mut ()) -> Result<(), UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
    let Some(mut installed) = (unsafe { runtime.read() }) else {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::NotInstalled);
    };
    installed.context = context;
    // SAFETY: The callback dispatches synchronously on this CPU with IF clear.
    unsafe { runtime.write(Some(installed)) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Request the syscall/exception assembly exit path after restoring the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// The kernel root must be active, the process root must no longer be active,
/// and execution must be on this single CPU with maskable interrupts disabled.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn request_user_process_exit(status: i32) {
    // SAFETY: The caller satisfies the documented ordering and single-vCPU contract.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS).write(status);
        core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Release);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).write(1);
    }
}

/// Enter a validated user frame and return only through the process-exit path.
///
/// # Safety
/// The process root must already be active in CR3, TSS.RSP0 must point to a live
/// supervisor stack mapped in both roots, syscall and user-fault callbacks must
/// be installed, and maskable interrupts must be disabled.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn enter_user(
    frame: rustix_kernel::syscall::ValidatedUserIretFrame,
) -> Result<i32, UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_none() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::NotInstalled);
    }
    // SAFETY: Entry depth is read with IF clear and only this CPU updates it.
    if unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_USER_ENTRY_DEPTH).read() }
        >= rustix_kernel::process::MAX_PROCESSES as u64
    {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::EntryDepthExceeded);
    }
    let frame = frame.into_raw();
    // SAFETY: The caller establishes the root, stack, TSS, callback, and fault
    // policy invariants. The assembly returns only after a process exit request.
    Ok(unsafe { rustix_enter_user(&frame) })
}

/// Register one callback for an allocated device IRQ vector.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must keep the IRQ source masked while registering and ensure it
/// is masked whenever this callback is dispatched. The caller must serialize
/// registration against IRQ dispatch on every CPU. `handler` must not allocate,
/// format output, block, or unwind; it runs with IF disabled and owns the EOI.
/// The source must remain masked until all handler state is ready.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn register_irq_handler(
    vector: u8,
    handler: IrqHandler,
) -> Result<(), IrqRegistrationError> {
    let vector = vector as usize;
    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR).contains(&vector) {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InvalidVector);
    }

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: This reads RFLAGS at CPL 0; the temporary push/pop is balanced.
    unsafe {
        asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags));
    }
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }

    // SAFETY: The API contract requires registration to be serialized with IRQ
    // dispatch, and the vector has been checked against the table bounds.
    let slot = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector)
    };
    // SAFETY: `slot` points into the initialized static callback table.
    if unsafe { slot.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::AlreadyRegistered);
    }
    // SAFETY: Registration is serialized by the caller's masking/IF contract.
    unsafe { slot.write(Some(handler)) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Device IRQ target called by the normalized assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_irq_dispatch(vector: u64) {
    // SAFETY: guard records this entry frame for the heap's debug checks; it
    // decrements automatically on every return path.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    if vector == APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR as u64 {
        return;
    }

    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR as u64..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR as u64).contains(&vector) {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }

    // SAFETY: Interrupt gates clear IF, and registration's safety contract
    // serializes writes against this read. No mutable reference is created.
    let handler = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector as usize)
            .read()
    };
    match handler {
        Some(handler) => handler(),
        None => fatal_irq_halt(),
    }
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_syscall_dispatch(context: *mut rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallContext) {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{
        sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame, SyscallArguments, UserIretFrame,
    };

    // SAFETY: The assembly entry is reached only through the DPL-3 syscall gate;
    // the stack pointer refers to its normalized GPR and hardware return frame.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    let Some(context) = (unsafe { context.as_mut() }) else {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    };
    let address_bits = USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if address_bits == 0 {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let frame = UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: context.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: context.code_selector,
        flags: context.flags,
        stack_pointer: context.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: context.stack_selector,
    };
    let frame = match sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(frame, address_bits) {
        Ok(frame) => frame.into_raw(),
        Err(_) => fatal_irq_halt(),
    };
    context.instruction_pointer = frame.instruction_pointer;
    context.code_selector = frame.code_selector;
    context.flags = frame.flags;
    context.stack_pointer = frame.stack_pointer;
    context.stack_selector = frame.stack_selector;

    let arguments = SyscallArguments {
        rdi: context.rdi,
        rsi: context.rsi,
        rdx: context.rdx,
        r10: context.r10,
        r8: context.r8,
        r9: context.r9,
    };
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    let result = {
        let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
        // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
        let runtime = unsafe { runtime.read() };
        if let Some(runtime) = runtime {
            (runtime.handler)(context, runtime.context)
        } else {
            fallback_syscall_result(context.rax, arguments)
        }
    };
    #[cfg(not(feature = "probe-user-process"))]
    let result = fallback_syscall_result(context.rax, arguments);
    context.rax = result as u64;
}

fn fallback_syscall_result(
    number: u64,
    arguments: rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallArguments,
) -> i64 {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{decode_syscall, SyscallError, SyscallRequest, ABI_VERSION};

    match decode_syscall(number, arguments) {
        Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion) => ABI_VERSION as i64,
        Ok(
            SyscallRequest::Exit { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Write { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Wait { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Mmap { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Munmap { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::MmapRegion { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::MunmapRegion { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Close { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Duplicate { .. },
        ) => SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(),
        Err(error) => error.return_value(),
    }
}

fn fatal_irq_halt() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Unknown device interrupts are fatal and must not be retried.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    if context.cs & 3 == 3 && !matches!(context.vector, 2 | 8 | 18) {
        let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
        // SAFETY: Exceptions arrive with IF clear; the diagnostic process runtime
        // is installed only for the synchronous single-vCPU user entry.
        if let Some(runtime) = unsafe { runtime.read() } {
            let depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
            crate::kprintln!(
                "USER EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x}; terminating process",
                context.vector,
                exception_name(context.vector),
                context.error_code
            );
            if context.vector == 14 {
                let fault_address: u64;
                // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is privileged and this handler runs at CPL0.
                unsafe {
                    asm!(
                        "mov {}, cr2",
                        out(reg) fault_address,
                        options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)
                    )
                };
                crate::kprintln!("user page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
            }
            if (runtime.exception_handler)(context.vector, runtime.context) {
                core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Acquire);
                // SAFETY: The callback's contract guarantees it has restored the
                // kernel root and marked the process root inactive before setting
                // this single-vCPU exit flag.
                if unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).read() } != 0 {
                    drop(depth);
                    // SAFETY: The exit callback restored CR3, completed teardown
                    // ownership transitions, and IF remains disabled. The asm
                    // trampoline restores the kernel FPU/stack continuation.
                    unsafe { rustix_user_exception_exit() };
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // SAFETY: guard records this fatal entry frame; fatal paths never return.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    // A fault raised while this handler is running (including a #DF on the
    // IST stack) must not re-enter the printing path; stop silently instead.
    if IN_FATAL_EXCEPTION.swap(true, Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant fatal diagnostics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    crate::kprintln!(
        "FATAL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} SS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RSP={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.ss,
        context.rflags,
        context.rsp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe {
            asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags))
        };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

//!
//! Bootstrap installs exception and device-IRQ gates with maskable interrupts
//! disabled. APIC setup, route masking, handler registration, and explicit `sti`
//! are owned by the boot path. Kernel exceptions and selected critical user
//! exceptions remain fatal; the diagnostic user-process path can reap other CPL3 faults.

impl IdtEntry {

        selector: 0,
        ist: 0,
        attributes: 0,

        Self {
            offset_low: handler as u16,
            selector: KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR,
            ist: ist & 0x07,
            attributes: 0x8e,
            offset_middle: (handler >> 16) as u16,
            offset_high: (handler >> 32) as u32,
            reserved: 0,

    fn user_interrupt_gate(handler: u64) -> Self {
        let mut entry = Self::interrupt_gate(handler, 0);
        entry.attributes = 0xee;

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS, exception gates, and device IRQ gates.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }
}

    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);
