    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
) -> ! {
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
    }
    halt_forever()
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
                    kprintln!(
                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
                        virtual_address,
                        pml4_index,
                        root.physical_address(),
                        root_entry
                    );
                }
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-general-protection")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering general protection with invalid DS selector");
    // SAFETY: The selector index is outside the installed GDT limit, so loading
    // it into DS deliberately raises a kernel-origin #GP in QEMU.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov ax, 0xffff",
            "mov ds, ax",
            out("ax") _,
            options(nostack)
        )
    };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-divide-error")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering divide error with a zero divisor");
    // SAFETY: Integer division by zero deliberately raises kernel-origin #DE.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "xor edx, edx",
            "xor eax, eax",
            "xor ecx, ecx",
            "div ecx",
            out("eax") _,
            out("edx") _,
            out("ecx") _,
            options(nostack)
        )
    };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

/// Set once the fatal panic path has started. A panic from inside the fatal
/// path stops silently instead of recursively printing or looping diagnostics.
static FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
    core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    // Mask maskable interrupts before any diagnostics run: another kernel
    // thread must not resume after a panic is declared, and the fatal report
    // must not be preempted mid-print.
    //
    // SAFETY: Kernel panic path runs at CPL 0; masking IF is always sound.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    if FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE.swap(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant panics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

```rustix/docs/architecture/syscall-abi.md
     1	# Unix-like process and syscall direction
     2	
     3	**Status: Milestone 4 is in progress. The opt-in single-vCPU QEMU diagnostic path creates a lower-half process root sharing the validated supervisor kernel half, loads and runs a bundled static ELF in Ring 3, serves ABI-version/write/close/dup/ready-child-wait/exit and one-page anonymous-map syscalls, terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE with status `128 + vector`, and restores/reaps the root. The normal kernel does not launch userspace. Descriptors are bounded console-stream handles with inheritance, duplication, close, and exit cleanup; the diagnostic `wait` path reaps already-exited children, preserves a zombie when status copyout fails, and returns `ENOTSUP` for a running child. Blocking for that child, general process scheduling/kernel stacks, reusable ELF execution, multi-page virtual-memory allocation, and a complete userspace runtime remain unimplemented.**
     4	
     5	Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.
     6	
     7	## Proposed compatibility principles
     8	
     9	- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
    10	- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
    11	- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
    12	- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::copy_from_user` and `copy_to_user` preflight the complete lower-half mapped range, check writable metadata for kernel-to-user copies, and operate only on owned frame tokens through `UserFrameMemory`; they never form a Rust reference from a user virtual address. Backend copy faults report the completed prefix. The diagnostic user-exception path terminates a process on supported CPL3 faults; it does not make arbitrary kernel memory accesses recoverable.
    13	- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
    14	- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.
    15	
    16	## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)
    17	
    18	ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts, addresses, and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and bounded write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. The workspace crate `crates/rustix-user` provides typed `no_std` wrappers for ABI version, write, wait, exit, close, descriptor duplication, one-page and bounded multi-page anonymous mappings plus a raw register-level call for low-level tests; it also provides a `run_main` entry helper and an optional mmap-backed `GlobalAlloc` implementation. Error decoding, short-write handling, formatting, region handling, and the size-class heap core are host-tested. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub. The opt-in diagnostic process runtime dispatches ABI-version, bounded descriptor-authorized write, close, duplication, one-page and multi-page anonymous map/unmap, exit, and wait for already-exited children; a wait on a running child returns `ENOTSUP` because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. QEMU init checks that one-page and multi-page anonymous mappings are zeroed, writable across page boundaries, exactly unmapped, and no longer readable by the kernel copy path afterward; it also uses kernel-seeded exited/running child fixtures to verify status copyout, invalid-pointer `EFAULT` without reaping, and `ENOTSUP` for a running child. The wait fixtures test syscall mechanics, not concurrent child execution or scheduler integration. A separate kernel-side test harness waits for the synchronous process after its exit trampoline returns.
    19	
    20	| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
    21	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    22	| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
    23	| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
    24	| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
    25	| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | ABI contract: blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. Current diagnostic support is nonblocking: it reaps an already-exited child, returns `-ENOTSUP` for a running child, and returns `-EFAULT` without reaping if status copyout fails. |

    39	## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; diagnostic path integrated)
    40	
    41	The opt-in single-vCPU process probe enters Ring 3 with a validated five-word `IRETQ` frame and enters the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated DPL-3 IDT gate. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in this first slice. The register and error contract below is the versioned v1 ABI, but the syscall surface and runtime are not general-purpose or enabled in the default boot path. The `rustix-user` crate includes typed wrappers, the `run_main` process-entry helper, complete-write and allocation-free formatting helpers, best-effort panic reporting, and an optional mmap-backed global allocator. The allocator obtains zeroed pages through `mmap`, serves power-of-two classes from 16 through 2048 bytes, rejects larger or over-aligned requests, and retains pages until process teardown; applications opt in by declaring `UserAllocator` as their global allocator. The runtime also exposes bounded multi-page `mmap_region`/`munmap_region` wrappers, validated by `rustix-init` across a page boundary. `rustix-init` exercises the entry helper and heap with `Vec` and `Box`, but the crate remains an early runtime and is not a general application or process-scheduling environment.
    42	
    43	- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` lies inside the device-vector range (`0x20..=0xef`) and is reserved by `InterruptVectorAllocator`; generic IRQ allocation/release cannot claim it. The IDT installs a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. Its assembly entry rejects CPL0 invocation, saves all GPRs and x87/SSE state, clears the direction flag, and calls a normalized Rust dispatcher with IF clear. The opt-in process probe implements ABI-version discovery, write, exit, one-page and multi-page mapping, and wait for an already-exited child; it does not block or create children.
    44	- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Ring-3 data and 64-bit code descriptors are appended at GDT indexes 5 and 6, with compile-time selector assertions for user data `0x2b` and user code `0x33` (RPL 3); the process probe uses these selectors in its validated entry frame.
    45	- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`. The current synchronous QEMU probe selects a bounded static 16 KiB supervisor stack slot by process ID from kernel BSS, verifies each page is writable, NX, and supervisor-only in the kernel root, then installs its top as `TSS.RSP0`; process roots share that validated upper-half mapping. After the exit trampoline returns to the bootstrap stack, the probe restores the bootstrap `RSP0`. The slot is not reclaimed and the synchronous runner does not switch among runnable user processes; a general scheduler must own and reclaim per-process entry stacks only after their saved contexts are unreachable. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
    46	- **Entry frame and state:** the dedicated assembly stub saves all GPRs in the `SyscallContext` layout, passes the five-word privilege frame separately from the exception frame, and saves/restores x87/SSE state around the Rust dispatcher; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Kernel code runs with the direction flag clear. The process probe validates saved RIP/RSP against the active process mappings and accesses user buffers only through owned frame tokens. It does not block or schedule in a syscall.
    47	- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This convention and its initial numbers/errors are versioned as ABI v1. Implemented operations remain a subset of the documented contract.
    48	- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Initial entry uses a host-tested frame sanitizer that requires exact ring-3 selectors, a canonical lower-half instruction pointer, a lower-half stack range, 16-byte initial stack alignment, and safe flags. Syscall resume uses a separate sanitizer that keeps exact selectors, canonical lower-half address shape, and privileged-flag checks but does not impose 16-byte alignment on an in-function RSP; it replaces user flags with `0x2` (IF remains clear). Once a process is active, the dispatcher also validates the saved instruction pointer against an executable mapping and the saved stack pointer against a writable NX mapping. A malformed frame is converted into process exit rather than returned to CPL3.
    49	- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. NMI, double fault, and machine check remain fatal even when their saved CS indicates CPL3. Other user-origin exceptions terminate the process with status `128 + vector` in the diagnostic runtime; QEMU exercises CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE. Kernel-origin #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE are separately tested as fatal. Ordinary maskable IRQs stay disabled throughout the synchronous process run.
    50	
    51	This path depends on each process root sharing supervisor-only upper-half mappings that cover syscall/exception code, the IDT, GDT, TSS, and active kernel stack. The bundled process root and syscall/exception transitions are exercised by opt-in QEMU smokes, but the shared Limine-derived kernel mapping is not a curated kernel map or a general isolation policy. Do not enable normal boot-time Ring 3 execution until process scheduling, scheduler-owned per-process kernel stacks, blocking wait semantics, and the remaining Milestone 4 fault/teardown criteria are implemented and validated.
    52	
    53	### Process address spaces (design; root construction partially implemented)
    54	
    55	Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.
    56	
    57	Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any effectively user-accessible leaf. U/S permission is the conjunction of every entry on a path, so a U/S bit on one non-leaf alone does not grant user access. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.
    58	
    59	The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the shared kernel owner alive. PCID-aware invalidation and SMP shootdown remain unsupported and need a separate design.

Host tests cover four-/five-level sharing, U/S sanitization, independent mappings, permission checks, cross-page copies, unmap ownership, active-root release rejection, and rollback. The opt-in `probe-user-process` target additionally constructs and activates one root, loads the bundled ELF, serves write and ready-child wait-status copyout/exit calls using token-based copies, and restores CR3 before kernel wait/reap and teardown. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.

    64	
    65	`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` allocates, populates, cache-selects, and maps every load page into an inactive process root.     66	
    67	## ABI decisions still pending beyond v1
    68	
    69	The initial v1 versioning, error encoding, syscall numbers, register-level request decoding, and assembly-matched syscall context layout are implemented in `src/syscall.rs`. The diagnostic `int 0x80` path sanitizes return frames and serves ABI-version, bounded descriptor-authorized write, close/dup, wait-for-exited-child, one-page and multi-page mmap/munmap, and exit calls; invalid unmapped write/status buffers return `EFAULT` without corrupting the process or consuming a waitable child. `src/process.rs` provides fixed-capacity identity/exit-state policy, and the diagnostic kernel harness performs a nonblocking kernel-side wait/reap after the user-entry trampoline returns. The userspace `wait` call can reap an already-exited child; it returns `ENOTSUP` for a running child because blocking user-process scheduling is not integrated. User faults are process-terminating only while the opt-in callback is installed; QEMU covers CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and kernel-fatal coverage for the same four vectors. This does not make arbitrary kernel accesses recoverable. Still to be specified before broader process operations are process-creation/exec and file-action semantics, general descriptor-object sharing and close-on-exec behavior, read/open support, blocking wait interruption, signal-like asynchronous delivery, clocks, and any additional structure layouts.

    72

Its exited and running wait fixtures are kernel-seeded; they do not establish child execution or scheduling. //! Bootstrap GDT, TSS, and interrupt entry for x86_64.
//!
//! Bootstrap installs exception and device-IRQ gates with maskable interrupts
//! disabled. APIC setup, route masking, handler registration, and explicit `sti`
//! are owned by the boot path. Kernel exceptions and selected critical user
//! exceptions remain fatal; the diagnostic user-process path can reap other CPL3 faults.

#[repr(C, packed)]

    offset_low: u16,
    selector: u16,
    ist: u8,
    attributes: u8,
    offset_middle: u16,
    offset_high: u32,
    reserved: u32,
}

impl IdtEntry {
    const MISSING: Self = Self {
        offset_low: 0,
        selector: 0,
        ist: 0,
        attributes: 0,
        offset_middle: 0,
        offset_high: 0,
        reserved: 0,
    };

    fn interrupt_gate(handler: u64, ist: u8) -> Self {
        Self {
            offset_low: handler as u16,
            selector: KERNEL_CODE_SELECTOR,
            ist: ist & 0x07,
            attributes: 0x8e,
            offset_middle: (handler >> 16) as u16,
            offset_high: (handler >> 32) as u32,
            reserved: 0,
        }
    }

    fn user_interrupt_gate(handler: u64) -> Self {
        let mut entry = Self::interrupt_gate(handler, 0);
        entry.attributes = 0xee;
        entry
    }
}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS, exception gates, and device IRQ gates.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[5]).write(USER_DATA_DESCRIPTOR);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[6]).write(USER_CODE_DESCRIPTOR);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 7]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let irq_stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(irq_stub_table).cast::<usize>();
    for vector in IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains one stub for each allocated vector.
        let handler = unsafe { irq_stubs.add(vector - IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR).read() } as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }
    // Vector 0x80 is reserved from device allocation and uses its own DPL-3
    // interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ dispatch path.
    // SAFETY: The assembly defines this dedicated entry stub in the kernel image.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::user_interrupt_gate(
                rustix_syscall_stub as *const () as usize as u64,
            ));
    }

    // SAFETY: The final table entry is the dedicated 0xff spurious-IRQ stub.
    let spurious_handler =
        unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + IRQ_UNWIRED_COUNT).read() } as u64;
    // SAFETY: The APIC spurious vector is a valid IDT index.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(spurious_handler, 0));
    }
    // Vectors 0xf0-0xfe have no registered source; wire them to a controlled
    // fatal stop (through the shared dispatch, which halts) instead of leaving
    // non-present gates that would cascade into #GP with no diagnostics.
    for vector in IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_UNWIRED_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table provides one stub for each vector.
        let handler =
            unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + (vector - IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR)) }.read()
                as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: Every architectural exception gate is initialized in static storage.
    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Configure the active user virtual-address width used to sanitize syscall returns.
///
/// Call after boot CPU discovery and before any CPL3 code can execute.
pub fn configure_user_address_width(virtual_address_bits: u8) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.store(virtual_address_bits, Ordering::Release);
    Ok(())
}

/// Select the stack used by the next privilege transition from CPL3 to CPL0.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must already be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and
/// `stack_top` must be the aligned top of a live, writable supervisor stack that
/// is mapped in the active address space and every address space that may run
/// before this value is changed again. Callers must update it before entering a
/// different process. The function validates the address shape, not the mapping
/// or ownership of the stack memory.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn set_kernel_entry_stack(
    stack_top: u64,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    if stack_top & 0xf != 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::Misaligned);
    }
    if !rustix_kernel::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_top, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NonCanonical);
    }
    if stack_top & (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1)) == 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NotKernelAddress);
    }

    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);
    // SAFETY: The function contract requires initialized TSS storage; the field
    // is packed, so write without creating an aligned reference to it.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(stack_top) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Restore TSS.RSP0 to the bootstrap ring-0 stack.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and the
/// caller must be executing on a different live stack before the restore.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn restore_bootstrap_kernel_entry_stack(
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: `RING0_STACK` is the initialized, fixed-size bootstrap entry stack.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: This function's contract establishes TSS initialization and IF=0.
    unsafe { set_kernel_entry_stack(ring0_top, virtual_address_bits) }
}

/// Install the syscall callback for one synchronously entered user process.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, no other CPU may access this state, and
/// `context` must remain live until the callback is cleared after user return.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn install_user_syscall_handler(
    handler: UserSyscallHandler,
    exception_handler: UserExceptionHandler,
    context: *mut (),
) -> Result<(), UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and the first implementation is single-vCPU.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::AlreadyInstalled);
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the function context live until clearing it.
    unsafe {
        runtime.write(Some(UserSyscallRuntime {
            handler,
            exception_handler,
            context,
        }))
    };
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and assembly reads these values only on this CPU.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_ENTRY_DEPTH).write(0);
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Remove the user-process syscall callback after returning to the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, and no syscall callback may be in flight.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn clear_user_syscall_handler() {
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and no user-entry trampoline may remain active when
    // clearing the callback or its nesting state.
    if unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_USER_ENTRY_DEPTH).read() } != 0 {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: The API contract guarantees single-vCPU exclusion with IF clear.
    unsafe { runtime.write(None) };
}

/// Select the process context used by the installed syscall callbacks.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, the callback must be installed, and the
/// context must remain live until it is replaced or the handler is cleared.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn set_user_syscall_context(context: *mut ()) -> Result<(), UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
    let Some(mut installed) = (unsafe { runtime.read() }) else {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::NotInstalled);
    };
    installed.context = context;
    // SAFETY: The callback dispatches synchronously on this CPU with IF clear.
    unsafe { runtime.write(Some(installed)) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Request the syscall/exception assembly exit path after restoring the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// The kernel root must be active, the process root must no longer be active,
/// and execution must be on this single CPU with maskable interrupts disabled.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn request_user_process_exit(status: i32) {
    // SAFETY: The caller satisfies the documented ordering and single-vCPU contract.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS).write(status);
        core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Release);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).write(1);
    }
}

/// Clear the just-consumed nested child's exit request before resuming its parent.
///
/// # Safety
/// IF must be clear, `enter_user` must have returned from the child exit path,
/// and the parent syscall dispatcher must still be suspended on this CPU.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn clear_user_process_exit() {
    // SAFETY: The child trampoline has consumed the exit and returned to the
    // kernel continuation; only this CPU accesses these single-vCPU globals.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_STATUS).write(0);
    }
}

/// Run a callback on a distinct live supervisor stack and return on the
/// original stack. The callback must return normally.
///
/// # Safety
/// `stack_top` must be 16-byte-aligned, mapped writable and supervisor-only
/// in the current root, and point to a stack not active or retained by another
/// task. `entry` must obey the SysV ABI and return.
/// Enter a validated user frame and return only through the process-exit path.
///
/// # Safety
/// The process root must already be active in CR3, TSS.RSP0 must point to a live
/// supervisor stack mapped in both roots, syscall and user-fault callbacks must
/// be installed, and maskable interrupts must be disabled.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn enter_user(
    frame: rustix_kernel::syscall::ValidatedUserIretFrame,
) -> Result<i32, UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_none() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::NotInstalled);
    }
    // SAFETY: Entry depth is read with IF clear and only this CPU updates it.
    if unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_USER_ENTRY_DEPTH).read() }
        >= rustix_kernel::process::MAX_PROCESSES as u64
    {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::EntryDepthExceeded);
    }
    let frame = frame.into_raw();
    // SAFETY: The caller establishes the root, stack, TSS, callback, and fault
    // policy invariants. The assembly returns only after a process exit request.
    Ok(unsafe { rustix_enter_user(&frame) })
}

/// Invoke a callback on a dedicated supervisor continuation stack.
///
/// # Safety
/// The caller must uphold `rustix_call_on_stack`'s mapping/lifetime contract and
/// must not retain references into the target stack across the call.
pub(crate) unsafe fn call_on_kernel_stack(
    stack_top: u64,
    entry: extern "C" fn(*mut ()) -> i32,
    context: *mut (),
) -> i32 {
    // SAFETY: The caller proves the stack and callback satisfy the assembly ABI.
    unsafe { rustix_call_on_stack(stack_top, entry, context) }
}

/// Register one callback for an allocated device IRQ vector.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must keep the IRQ source masked while registering and ensure it
/// is masked whenever this callback is dispatched. The caller must serialize
/// registration against IRQ dispatch on every CPU. `handler` must not allocate,
/// format output, block, or unwind; it runs with IF disabled and owns the EOI.
/// The source must remain masked until all handler state is ready.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn register_irq_handler(
    vector: u8,
    handler: IrqHandler,
) -> Result<(), IrqRegistrationError> {
    let vector = vector as usize;
    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR).contains(&vector) {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InvalidVector);
    }

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: This reads RFLAGS at CPL 0; the temporary push/pop is balanced.
    unsafe {
        asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags));
    }
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }

    // SAFETY: The API contract requires registration to be serialized with IRQ
    // dispatch, and the vector has been checked against the table bounds.
    let slot = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector)
    };
    // SAFETY: `slot` points into the initialized static callback table.
    if unsafe { slot.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::AlreadyRegistered);
    }
    // SAFETY: Registration is serialized by the caller's masking/IF contract.
    unsafe { slot.write(Some(handler)) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Device IRQ target called by the normalized assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_irq_dispatch(vector: u64) {
    // SAFETY: guard records this entry frame for the heap's debug checks; it
    // decrements automatically on every return path.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    if vector == APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR as u64 {
        return;
    }

    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR as u64..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR as u64).contains(&vector) {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }

    // SAFETY: Interrupt gates clear IF, and registration's safety contract
    // serializes writes against this read. No mutable reference is created.
    let handler = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector as usize)
            .read()
    };
    match handler {
        Some(handler) => handler(),
        None => fatal_irq_halt(),
    }
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_syscall_dispatch(context: *mut rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallContext) {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{
        sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame, SyscallArguments, UserIretFrame,
    };

    // SAFETY: The assembly entry is reached only through the DPL-3 syscall gate;
    // the stack pointer refers to its normalized GPR and hardware return frame.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    let Some(context) = (unsafe { context.as_mut() }) else {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    };
    let address_bits = USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if address_bits == 0 {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let frame = UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: context.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: context.code_selector,
        flags: context.flags,
        stack_pointer: context.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: context.stack_selector,
    };
    let frame = match sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(frame, address_bits) {
        Ok(frame) => frame.into_raw(),
        Err(_) => fatal_irq_halt(),
    };
    context.instruction_pointer = frame.instruction_pointer;
    context.code_selector = frame.code_selector;
    context.flags = frame.flags;
    context.stack_pointer = frame.stack_pointer;
    context.stack_selector = frame.stack_selector;

    let arguments = SyscallArguments {
        rdi: context.rdi,
        rsi: context.rsi,
        rdx: context.rdx,
        r10: context.r10,
        r8: context.r8,
        r9: context.r9,
    };
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    let result = {
        let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
        // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
        let runtime = unsafe { runtime.read() };
        if let Some(runtime) = runtime {
            (runtime.handler)(context, runtime.context)
        } else {
            fallback_syscall_result(context.rax, arguments)
        }
    };
    #[cfg(not(feature = "probe-user-process"))]
    let result = fallback_syscall_result(context.rax, arguments);
    context.rax = result as u64;
}

fn fallback_syscall_result(
    number: u64,
    arguments: rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallArguments,
) -> i64 {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{decode_syscall, SyscallError, SyscallRequest, ABI_VERSION};

    match decode_syscall(number, arguments) {
        Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion) => ABI_VERSION as i64,
        Ok(
            SyscallRequest::Exit { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Write { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Wait { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Mmap { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Munmap { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::MmapRegion { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::MunmapRegion { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Close { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Duplicate { .. },
        ) => SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(),
        Err(error) => error.return_value(),
    }
}

fn fatal_irq_halt() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Unknown device interrupts are fatal and must not be retried.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    if context.cs & 3 == 3 && !matches!(context.vector, 2 | 8 | 18) {
        let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
        // SAFETY: Exceptions arrive with IF clear; the diagnostic process runtime
        // is installed only for the synchronous single-vCPU user entry.
        if let Some(runtime) = unsafe { runtime.read() } {
            let depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
            crate::kprintln!(
                "USER EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x}; terminating process",
                context.vector,
                exception_name(context.vector),
                context.error_code
            );
            if context.vector == 14 {
                let fault_address: u64;
                // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is privileged and this handler runs at CPL0.
                unsafe {
                    asm!(
                        "mov {}, cr2",
                        out(reg) fault_address,
                        options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)
                    )
                };
                crate::kprintln!("user page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
            }
            if (runtime.exception_handler)(context.vector, runtime.context) {
                core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Acquire);
                // SAFETY: The callback's contract guarantees it has restored the
                // kernel root and marked the process root inactive before setting
                // this single-vCPU exit flag.
                if unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_USER_EXIT_PENDING).read() } != 0 {
                    drop(depth);
                    // SAFETY: The exit callback restored CR3, completed teardown
                    // ownership transitions, and IF remains disabled. The asm
                    // trampoline restores the kernel FPU/stack continuation.
                    unsafe { rustix_user_exception_exit() };
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // SAFETY: guard records this fatal entry frame; fatal paths never return.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    // A fault raised while this handler is running (including a #DF on the
    // IST stack) must not re-enter the printing path; stop silently instead.
    if IN_FATAL_EXCEPTION.swap(true, Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant fatal diagnostics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    crate::kprintln!(
        "FATAL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} SS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RSP={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.ss,
        context.rflags,
        context.rsp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe {
            asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags))
        };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

global_asm!(
    r#"
    .section .text
    .code64

    .macro RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR name, number
    .global \name
    .type \name, @function
\name:
    push 0
    push \number
    jmp rustix_exception_common
    .endm

    .macro RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR name, number
    .global \name
    .type \name, @function
\name:
    push \number
    jmp rustix_exception_common
    .endm

    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_0, 0
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_1, 1
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_2, 2
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_3, 3
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_4, 4
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_5, 5
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_6, 6
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_7, 7
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_8, 8
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_9, 9
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_10, 10
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_11, 11
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_12, 12
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_13, 13
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_14, 14
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_15, 15
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_16, 16
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_17, 17
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_18, 18
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_19, 19
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_20, 20
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_21, 21
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_22, 22
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_23, 23
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_24, 24
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_25, 25
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_26, 26
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_27, 27
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_28, 28
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_29, 29
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_30, 30
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_31, 31

    rustix_exception_common:
    cld
    push rax
    push rbx
    push rcx
    push rdx
    push rsi
    push rdi
    push rbp
    push r8
    push r9
    push r10
    push r11
    push r12
    push r13
    push r14
    push r15
    mov rdi, rsp
    and rsp, -16
    call rustix_exception_dispatch
    ud2

    .global rustix_load_gdt
    .type rustix_load_gdt, @function
rustix_load_gdt:
    lgdt [rdi]
    push 0x08
    lea rax, [rip + 2f]
    push rax
    retfq
2:
    mov ax, 0x10
    mov ds, ax
    mov es, ax
    mov ss, ax
    mov ax, 0x18
    ltr ax
    xor eax, eax
    mov fs, ax
    mov gs, ax
    ret

    .section .rodata
    .align 8
    .global exception_stub_table
exception_stub_table:
    .quad rustix_exception_0, rustix_exception_1, rustix_exception_2, rustix_exception_3
    .quad rustix_exception_4, rustix_exception_5, rustix_exception_6, rustix_exception_7
    .quad rustix_exception_8, rustix_exception_9, rustix_exception_10, rustix_exception_11
    .quad rustix_exception_12, rustix_exception_13, rustix_exception_14, rustix_exception_15
    .quad rustix_exception_16, rustix_exception_17, rustix_exception_18, rustix_exception_19
    .quad rustix_exception_20, rustix_exception_21, rustix_exception_22, rustix_exception_23
    .quad rustix_exception_24, rustix_exception_25, rustix_exception_26, rustix_exception_27
    .quad rustix_exception_28, rustix_exception_29, rustix_exception_30, rustix_exception_31

    .section .text
    # Each IRQ entry is exactly 12 bytes: push synthetic error code, push its
    # vector as imm32, then a rel32 jump to the shared GPR-saving entry.
    .macro RUSTIX_IRQ_STUB vector
    .byte 0x6a, 0
    .byte 0x68
    .long \vector
    .byte 0xe9
    .long rustix_irq_common - . - 4
    .endm

    .global rustix_irq_stub_start
rustix_irq_stub_start:
    .set irq_vector, 0x20
    .rept 208
    RUSTIX_IRQ_STUB irq_vector
    .set irq_vector, irq_vector + 1
    .endr
    .set unwired_vector, 0xf0
    .rept 15
    RUSTIX_IRQ_STUB unwired_vector
    .set unwired_vector, unwired_vector + 1
    .endr
    .global rustix_irq_spurious_stub
rustix_irq_spurious_stub:
    RUSTIX_IRQ_STUB 0xff

    rustix_irq_common:
    cld
    push rax
    push rbx
    push rcx
    push rdx
    push rsi
    push rdi
    push rbp
    push r8
    push r9
    push r10
    push r11
    push r12
    push r13
    push r14
    push r15
    # Preserve asynchronous x87/SSE state before Rust IRQ dispatch can use it.
    mov rax, qword ptr [rip + rustix_active_fpu_state_pointer]
    # A null pointer here means IRQ/FPU initialization order was broken; stop.
    test rax, rax
    jz rustix_irq_fatal_no_fx_state
    fxsave64 [rax]
    mov edi, dword ptr [rsp + 120]
    mov rbx, rsp
    and rsp, -16
    call rustix_irq_dispatch

    mov rax, qword ptr [rip + rustix_active_fpu_state_pointer]

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {
        // SAFETY: Active mapping callers provide the current virtual page and run
        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
enum LimineUserFrameMemoryError {
    OutOfBounds,
    Address(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError),
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
struct LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
impl LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    fn frame_slice_address(
        &self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        length: usize,
    ) -> Result<*mut u8, LimineUserFrameMemoryError> {
        if offset
            .checked_add(length)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE as usize)
        {
            return Err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::OutOfBounds);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Ok(core::ptr::null_mut());
        }

        let base = frame
            .hhdm_address(
                self.memory_map,
                self.hhdm_offset,
                self.physical_address_bits,
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address)?;
        let address =
            base.checked_add(offset as u64)
                .ok_or(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address(
                    rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow,
                ))?;
        Ok(address as *mut u8)
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
// SAFETY: The non-copyable Frame token and checked HHDM conversion authorize a
// complete Usable page. Each operation checks its subrange, accesses only that
// page, and uses raw copies rather than forming user virtual references. The
// implementation relies on Limine's mapped-usable-memory contract; hardware
// faults from a broken mapping remain fatal and are not recoverable here.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory for LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    type Error = LimineUserFrameMemoryError;

    fn copy_from_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        destination: &mut [u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let source = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, destination.len())?;
        if !destination.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source, destination.as_mut_ptr(), destination.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn copy_to_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        source: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let destination = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, source.len())?;
        if !source.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source.as_ptr(), destination, source.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

struct KernelHeapMappingContext {
    candidate: *mut (),
    allocator: *mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: *const arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
}

unsafe fn map_kernel_heap_pages(
    opaque_context: *mut (),
    first_page: usize,
    page_count: usize,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, EffectiveMemoryType, MtrrState,
        PagePermissions, PatLayout, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    if page_count == 0
        || first_page
            .checked_add(page_count)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES)
    {
        return false;
    }

    // SAFETY: The caller configures this callback only after the active root,
    // allocator, CPU snapshot, and local context are all live. The boot path is
    // single-vCPU and never returns from the stack containing that context.
    let state = unsafe { &mut *opaque_context.cast::<KernelHeapMappingContext>() };
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the retained local candidate and BootInfo
    // members. The callback is synchronous and never stores a derived reference.
    let candidate = unsafe {
        &mut *state
            .candidate
            .cast::<CandidatePageTables<'static, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>>>()
    };
    // SAFETY: The frame allocator and CPU snapshot remain owned by retained
    // BootInfo; this callback runs on the sole CPU with the heap lock held.
    let allocator = unsafe { &mut *state.allocator };
    // SAFETY: The CPU snapshot is immutable and remains live with BootInfo.
    let cpu_info = unsafe { &*state.cpu_info };

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The callback runs at CPL 0; save IF before disabling local IRQs
    // while the active page tables and allocator are mutated.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) flags) };
    let result = (|| {
        let physical_width = cpu_info.physical_address_bits?;
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(cpu_info.pat_msr_value?).ok()?;
        let mtrrs = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
            MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers.validated_layout(physical_width).ok()?,
            _ => return None,
        };
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        for (mapped, page) in (first_page..first_page + page_count).enumerate() {
            let virtual_address = KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE
                .checked_add((page as u64).checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)?)?;
            let frame = match allocator.allocate() {
                Some(frame) => frame,
                None => {
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
                virtual_address,
                frame.address(),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(physical_width),
                cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            ) {
                Ok(mapping) => mapping,
                Err(_) => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
                CachePolicy::WriteBack,
                pat,
                &mtrrs,
                cpu_info.normal_caching,
            ) {
                Ok(attributes) if attributes.effective_type() == EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack => {
                    attributes
                }
                _ => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            // SAFETY: IF is clear, the current candidate owns the active root,
            // and the allocator-issued frame is mapped RW/NX with local TLB
            // invalidation before its token becomes page-table-owned.
            if let Err(failure) =
                unsafe { candidate.map_owned_page_active(allocator, frame, mapping, attributes) }
            {
                deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, failure.frame);
                rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                return None;
            }
        }
        Some(())
    })()
    .is_some();
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: The mapping transaction is complete or fully rolled back.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("sti") };
    }
    result
}

fn rollback_kernel_heap_pages(
    candidate: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'static,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>,
    >,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    first_page: usize,
    mapped_pages: usize,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;

    for page in (first_page..first_page + mapped_pages).rev() {
        let Some(virtual_address) = (page as u64)
            .checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)
            .and_then(|offset| KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE.checked_add(offset))
        else {
            halt_forever();
        };
        // SAFETY: The pages belong to this transaction in the current active
        // root; unmapping invalidates their TLB entries before token return.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_forever());
        deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
    }
}

fn deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if allocator.deallocate(frame).is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

// Error payloads provide boot diagnostics through the derived `Debug` output.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Debug)]
enum AcpiMappingError {
    InvalidAcpiSpan {
        physical_start: u64,
        length: usize,
        error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError,
    },
    InvalidMapping(rustix_kernel::paging::MappingError),
    CandidateMap(
        rustix_kernel::paging::CandidateMapErrorKind<rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError>,
    ),
    CandidateWalk,
    UnexpectedCurrentCr3,
}

struct CandidateAcpiReader<'candidate, 'memory, 'map> {
    candidate: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'memory,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'map>,
    >,
    allocator: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &'map rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    cache_layout: rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    normal_caching: bool,
    candidate_cr3: u64,
    previous_cr3: u64,
    virtual_address: u64,
}

impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn remove_temporary_mapping(&mut self) {
        if let Err(error) = self.candidate.unmap_acpi_page(self.virtual_address) {
            crate::kprintln!("temporary ACPI mapping could not be removed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
}

// The legacy-reserved authorization is accepted only for RSDP reads; all
// root and child tables require ACPI-reclaimable/NVS memory-map coverage.
impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn read_mapped(
        &mut self,
        physical_start: u64,
        output: &mut [u8],
        allow_legacy_rsdp: bool,
    ) -> Result<(), AcpiMappingError> {
        use rustix_kernel::paging::{
            validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
        };

        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
            return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
        }
        if output.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let length =
            u64::try_from(output.len()).map_err(|_| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                physical_start,
                length: output.len(),
                error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
            })?;
        let span = if allow_legacy_rsdp {
            self.memory_map.validate_rsdp_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        } else {
            self.memory_map.validate_acpi_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        }
        .map_err(|error| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
            physical_start,
            length: output.len(),
            error,
        })?;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mut copied = 0usize;
        while copied < output.len() {
            let current_physical = physical_start.checked_add(copied as u64).ok_or(
                AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                    physical_start,
                    length: output.len(),
                    error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
                },
            )?;
            let physical_page = current_physical & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
            let page_offset = current_physical - physical_page;
            let page_length = (PAGE_SIZE - page_offset).min((output.len() - copied) as u64);
            let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
                self.virtual_address,
                physical_page,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
