# Memory-management direction

## What exists now

`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation/classification, canonical-address boundaries, physical-width bounds, HHDM range arithmetic, and page-rounded ACPI span authorization. `MemoryMap::validate_acpi_span` accepts at most 64 KiB of requested ACPI bytes and validates the entire 4 KiB-rounded physical extent against contiguous ACPI-reclaimable/NVS regions; this is metadata only, not a mapping or dereference grant. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The boot path additionally subtracts the validated kernel-image and boot-stack physical spans (`from_memory_map_excluding`) so a loader mislabeling them as usable cannot cause the allocator to hand out own-kernel pages. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. The active cloned page-table hierarchy owns its page-table frames; the frame allocator is otherwise not yet a general-purpose virtual-memory service.

`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.

`src/paging.rs` contains host-tested mapping and cache policy plus a bounded candidate-root builder. The CR3 decoder validates physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets its low 12 bits according to active `CR4.PCIDE`; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires known physical width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. It can encode one 4 KiB leaf PTE with supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when EFER.NXE is confirmed, and a bounded PAT index. `PatLayout` parses supplied `IA32_PAT` values and selects WB, UC, or WC indexes. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` resolve address-specific MTRR types, including fixed-range priority and defined variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. `MtrrRegisters::validated_layout` validates captured capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range presence, WC support, and variable-mask shape/alignment before producing an owned layout. Rustix supports contiguous power-of-two variable masks and explicitly rejects unsupported discontinuous masks. The layout combines address-specific MTRR type and PAT selection according to Intel SDM Table 11-7 only when `CR0.CD` and `CR0.NW` are clear. Host tests cover all 30 documented MTRR/PAT pairs and malformed inputs. A pure range selector chooses an index only when its effective type is uniform throughout all fixed/variable MTRR boundaries in an aligned extent; selected attributes remain bound to that physical extent. The selector itself does not inspect PTEs, aliases, or frame ownership. Boot reads CR0 without modifying it, validates captured MTRR/PAT state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution; this does not assert the live PTE's type. MTRR capture is bounded to 32 variable pairs and rejects excess capacity without partial state.

`CandidatePageTables` owns a separate root, bounded to 32 table frames and 256 explicitly mapped leaf records. Ordinary owned leaves require allocator-issued `Frame` tokens; a separate bounded ACPI path accepts only one read-only, supervisor, NX 4 KiB page contained in a `ValidatedAcpiSpan` and never transfers ownership of that physical page. Both paths require NXE, support four- and five-level paths, and hold one exclusive mutable borrow of the unsafe memory backend so prepared handles cannot be mixed across backends. Borrowed ACPI mappings can only be installed and removed while the candidate is inactive. The boot-only ACPI reader performs temporary CR3 switches to read validated pages and removes them before permanent activation. The default boot path clones the complete reachable Limine hierarchy, hardens kernel HHDM aliases to text/rodata R/NX and data RW/NX while preserving PAT bits, verifies critical translations, activates the cloned CR3, and retains the candidate tokens for the active root's lifetime. The CR3 transition invalidates the active PCID and toggles CR4.PGE when enabled; the same invalidation is used if verification restores the inherited root. General candidate mutation and release are rejected while active, but narrow owned-page active map/unmap operations are supported under the single-CPU, IF-disabled contract and invalidate the local TLB before ownership is returned. Host tests cover transactional rollback and ownership; `just active-map-smoke` validates active mapping, access, invalidation, and reclamation in QEMU. The type never writes CR3. The HHDM adapter derives table pointers only from complete allocator-owned `Usable` frames through checked arithmetic.

The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe reads the inherited root and follows paths for every page in kernel text/rodata/data and the requested stack span. The transition clones every reachable present table and preserves leaf mappings, then rewrites and validates the kernel-image HHDM aliases. The kernel and HHDM aliases retain the same PAT index; MTRR state is unchanged. This is not a fresh address-space policy or a hardware-level exhaustive inventory, and it does not reclaim the inherited root or bootloader memory.

The effective-type resolver follows [Intel SDM Vol. 3A §11.5.2.2, Table 11-7](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/671447/325384-sdm-vol-3abcd.pdf), which applies when normal caching is enabled (`CR0.CD=0`, `CR0.NW=0`). Its footnotes distinguish UC selected by an MTRR from UC selected by a page-table entry (the latter involves cache snooping and aliasing concerns); they also identify combinations that older manual editions called undefined but current processors supporting both PAT and MTRRs resolve as shown. The resolver does not cover legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations outside that table.

The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. Limine's inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Before activating the cloned root, Rustix splits inherited huge pages where needed and changes the kernel image HHDM aliases to the matching R/NX or RW/NX policy while retaining PAT bits. The rest of the HHDM remains inherited; an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.

The boot snapshot rejects physical map ranges beyond the reported CPUID physical-address width when available. For base-revision-3 HHDM-mapped types it validates page-rounded physical spans, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, and canonical endpoints in the active linear-address width. These checks are metadata, not proof that loader pointers are readable. Arbitrary physical access is not permitted: validated ACPI pages use the bounded read-only/NX reader; HHDM table access is limited to checked full-frame paths. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. The APIC MMIO validator rejects every known memory-map class except `Reserved` and `Unknown`; unreported ranges remain dependent on validated platform data. The active clone owns its page-table frames but leaves inherited leaf frames and the old root unreclaimed. The global heap begins with a 256 KiB BSS arena and can demand-map up to 1 MiB of allocator-backed pages in its reserved virtual range. Its IRQ-save lock prevents local interrupt reentrancy, but allocation remains forbidden in IRQ/exception handlers. Bootstrap exceptions remain fatal, while selected maskable IRQs are enabled only after APIC routes and handlers are ready.

## Active-root preservation and remaining limits

The transition clones the complete reachable inherited hierarchy rather than building a clean address space. It preserves all reachable present leaves and non-present entries, owns each cloned intermediate table, and fails closed on malformed entries, unsupported page sizes, cross-level table aliases, or fixed-capacity exhaustion. Kernel text/rodata/data HHDM aliases are then adjusted to avoid writable-executable aliases. Limine's original root and leaf frames remain intact.

- **Kernel ELF image:** `linker.ld` places `.text`, `.rodata`, `.limine_requests`, `.data`, `.bss`, and `.got` in three `PT_LOAD` segments: RX text, read-only rodata, and RW data/BSS. It exports `__kernel_start` and `__kernel_end` around the complete loadable image, plus page-aligned bounds for each segment. `BootInfo` checks that Limine's reported virtual base matches the linker start, validates ordered contiguous segment bounds covering the rounded image, derives corresponding half-open physical ranges from the executable physical base with checked arithmetic, and validates canonical virtual and reported physical address widths. The release ELF and QEMU runtime report both showed the three aligned ranges on 2026-10-21. The RX, R/NX, and RW/NX labels describe the linker segment intent; these are linker/boot metadata, not proof that the inherited page tables map every page or enforce those permissions, nor proof that loader pointers are readable. The memory-map `ExecutableAndModules` entries remain illustrative, not an authoritative kernel-image extent.
- **Active stack and `BootInfo`:** The assembly `_start` shim captures Limine's entry `RSP` before any Rust prologue. Under the SysV entry convention the synthetic return slot occupies 8 bytes, so `RSP + 8` is the exclusive stack top. Rustix requests a 256 KiB Limine stack and requires the stack-size response; `BootInfo` records and validates that requested span through the HHDM, including its `BootloaderReclaimable` backing. The loader may allocate more, and no guard page is inferred. QEMU transition tests walk all 64 requested stack pages.
- **Kernel static data:** `RAM_FILESYSTEM`, GDT, IDT, TSS, the ring-0 stack, and double-fault IST stack are static BSS/data in the kernel image. Exception entry also requires the handler code and the TSS/IDT references to remain mapped. Preserve the complete relevant data/BSS pages and stack pages.
- **Limine request data:** request records are in the kernel's writable `.limine_requests` segment. Response objects and the memory-map pointer array are bootloader-reclaimable; `capture_boot_information` copies the values used later, and the shell does not retain those pointers. Keep them mapped until the copy and validation finish; any later reclaim must be explicit rather than reclaiming the whole bootloader-reclaimable class.
- **Inherited page tables:** Limine places its page tables in bootloader-reclaimable memory, but their layout is unspecified. `BootInfo` captures raw CR3 and validates the decoded root address and active low-bit mode. The default boot path clones all reachable page-table pages into allocator-owned frames and preserves all leaf entries, then changes only the kernel-image HHDM alias permission bits while retaining cache attributes. It verifies kernel segments, the requested stack span, and the candidate-root HHDM alias before switching; afterward it verifies CR3 and the critical paths again. The inherited root and its backing pages remain untouched and are not reclaimed.
- **Devices:** COM1 uses x86 port I/O and needs no MMIO virtual mapping. Rustix does not currently request or use a framebuffer. Any future framebuffer or device-register mapping needs an explicit physical range and cache policy.

## Permissions and cache policy of the active clone

The active root preserves Limine's inherited kernel virtual mappings and their cache attributes. Before switching, Rustix requires NXE and enforces the linker permissions for every kernel-image HHDM alias: text and rodata are read-only/NX, and data/BSS/GOT are RW/NX. This prevents writable-executable aliases without discarding the HHDM alias. Huge-page leaves are split as necessary; unaffected entries retain their mappings and PAT/MTRR effective types. The remainder of the HHDM and all non-kernel aliases remain as Limine supplied them, so this is not yet a comprehensive Rustix mapping policy.

Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The boot report validates captured registers and computes a diagnostic effective type from the active PAT/MTRR values under normal caching. A separate pure selector can choose an index whose effective type remains uniform across an aligned physical range; the selector itself does not inspect PTEs or aliases. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe now compares effective types of the inherited kernel and HHDM aliases for kernel-image pages, but it is not a full alias inventory. The pure combination follows Intel SDM Table 11-7; it is not a generic rule for legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations. The active transition retains the inherited PAT and MTRR state and changes no cache-selection bits. The page-table split copies large-page PAT selection to the equivalent 4 KiB/2 MiB entries. Future MMIO mappings must still use explicit device ranges and a verified cache policy; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.

Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.

Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. `src/paging.rs` builds an owned clone in allocator-issued frames, can split inherited large pages to update leaf permissions, and supports transactional 4 KiB map/unmap operations before activation. The default boot path validates critical translations and kernel alias permissions, switches CR3 while invalidating stale global translations via a CR4.PGE toggle when needed, verifies the active root, and retains its frame tokens for the active lifetime. The inherited root and backing memory remain intact. This preserves inherited mappings rather than constructing a new address space; broader mapping inventory, non-kernel permission policy, reclamation, and a general mapping service remain future work.

## Planned memory layers

1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; table and leaf mappings use allocator-issued tokens. The active mapping smoke validates one owned page's map/access/unmap/reclamation path.
3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix runs on an active clone of Limine's hierarchy and hardens kernel-image HHDM aliases. Narrow active owned-page map/unmap operations invalidate the local TLB; this is not a clean-room address-space policy or general MMIO subsystem.
4. **Heap:** a 256 KiB BSS arena with 128 allocation records is backed by a bounded, demand-mapped extension of up to 1 MiB. Host tests and QEMU cover growth, reuse, exhaustion, and failed growth. The global allocator uses an IRQ-save spin lock, but allocation remains prohibited in interrupt context so handlers stay bounded and allocation-free.
5. **Process address spaces (partial):** `SharedKernelHalf` validates/snapshots the upper root entries, and `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` constructs multiple private roots, maps lower-half user leaves from allocator-issued frames, returns ownership on unmap, and frees private mappings/tables/root during inactive teardown. The view borrows the kernel-root owner, which must remain alive and immutable; the root set uses one exclusive backend borrow for its roots. `destroy` is permitted only after the caller switches away and invalidates the root's local non-global translations; PCID-aware teardown is unsupported. The caller still owns CR3 transitions. Mapping metadata retains writable and executable permissions, and `validate_initial_user_state` requires an executable non-writable entry page plus a writable non-executable stack page. Generic copy-in/copy-out helpers preflight lower-half mapped ranges and permissions and access owned frames through a separate `UserFrameMemory` contract. `Elf64Image::load_into_process_root` allocates, populates, cache-selects, and maps bounded ELF load pages. The opt-in `probe-user-process` diagnostic loads separate bundled init and child ELFs into independent roots. Init runs with token-based write/EFAULT handling; its wait synchronously enters the kernel-prepared child on a distinct PID-indexed entry stack while preserving the parent on a continuation stack, then resumes after child exit and copies status before reaping. The kernel harness later waits/reaps init and tears down both inactive roots. Its one-page initial stack is cleared in bounded chunks before mapping, and Ring 3 checks an untouched byte is zero. It has an unmapped page immediately below it; startup checks that page is unmapped, and `just user-fault-smoke` reads it from CPL3 and checks the resulting #PF CR2 before validating teardown. A fixed-capacity `UserRegionTable` reserves the ELF segments, stack, and guard, and provides first-fit page-rounded anonymous-region reservations within a bounded lower-half window. The opt-in process probe exposes one-page `mmap`/`munmap` calls: it zeroes RW/NX frames before mapping, switches to the kernel root for PTE changes, and only releases a frame after unmapping it. QEMU verifies a fresh mapped page, user write/read, stale-address EFAULT after unmap, and root teardown. This is still a bounded one-page-per-call VM interface, not stack growth or a general userspace memory manager. `just process-smoke` validates actual child entry/exit, blocking wait, EFAULT copyout retry, and root/frame teardown. This remains a bounded synchronous QEMU diagnostic, not scheduler-backed process execution or arbitrary userspace spawn/exec. Dynamic stack growth, general anonymous VM management, scheduler-owned/reclaimed process stacks, a curated kernel map, and complete fault recovery remain future work.

## Invariants to preserve

- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. HHDM translation and table access are limited to checked full-frame token-based paths that rely on Limine's documented mapping contract. Candidate mutations are allowed only before activation and only in owned tables. The active cloned root retains its ownership tokens and rejects mutation/release until an explicit, reviewed CR3 transition away from it.
- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables. User-accessible leaf mappings must stay in the lower canonical half; the upper half is reserved for supervisor mappings.
- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.

The active root is a full clone of Limine's reachable hierarchy with kernel HHDM alias W^X hardening, not a clean-room Rustix address space. Heap growth is bounded to a fixed virtual reservation and 1 MiB of frame-backed pages. Broader alias/MMIO coverage, frame reclamation, and physical-hardware validation remain outstanding.

# Testing and verification

## Current checks

`just verify` runs the standard development verification sequence:

1. `just fmt` — fail on formatting differences across the workspace.
2. `just test` — run host-side ACPI parser/traversal, borrowed-page mapping, IRQ vector allocator, PIT rate/time arithmetic, SPSC input-queue wraparound, scheduler, process lifecycle, descriptor-table and user-region policy, syscall request decoding, memory-map, mapping-range/PTE-bit policy, frame-allocator, heap, RAM-filesystem, Crabshell parser, and `rustix-user` syscall decoding, short-write, and formatting tests.
3. `just check` — check the `x86_64-unknown-none` kernel target.
4. `just smoke` — build the pinned hybrid ISO (including the static `rustix-init` ELF payload), boot it in QEMU's default BIOS mode, require the kernel to parse/validate the bundled init entry and load-page count, and check that Crabshell reaches its prompt within a deadline.
5. `just uefi-smoke` — boot the same ISO with OVMF and require the copied MADT report, CR3/page-table transition and TLB-flush markers, timer IRQ delivery/EOI, and shell prompt within a deadline.
6. `just active-map-smoke` and `just thread-smoke` — exercise active owned-page mapping/TLB invalidation and (under OVMF) IRQ-save lock IF restoration, cooperative event/wait behavior, timer preemption of non-yielding workers, x87/SSE state preservation, timed sleep while another ready thread repeatedly yields, guarded stacks, and frame-backed heap growth; both restore the default image.
7. `just input-smoke` — under OVMF, type a partial `pwd` over UART, inject ordinary and extended PS/2 scancodes through QMP, require each diagnostic to redraw the prompt and partial line, then finish the command and verify its output. The QMP socket is created under the host temporary directory because WSL `/mnt/c` does not support Unix sockets.
8. `just fault-smoke`, `just process-smoke`, and `just user-fault-smoke` — verify fatal kernel #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE diagnostics, then run bundled init in a diagnostic Ring 3 root. The normal process variant checks a fresh stack byte, ABI version, formatted and complete serial output, dup/write/close behavior including `-EBADF` for closed descriptors, zero-filled RW/NX one-page and multi-page anonymous mappings, user write/read, exact unmap, `-EFAULT` for stale/invalid user pointers, and a separately bundled real child entering Ring 3 and exiting with status 7. Init blocks in wait while the diagnostic synchronously enters that kernel-prepared child; an invalid status pointer returns `-EFAULT` without reaping, and retry copies status then reaps. The smoke checks init exit status 42, kernel wait/reap, and both root/frame teardown. The user-fault variants trigger #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE, require status `128 + vector`, wait/reap, and verify root teardown/kernel survival. The CPL3 #PF specifically reads the unmapped 4 KiB page immediately below the one-page initial user stack and checks the reported CR2 address. NMI/#DF/#MC remain fatal; the nested child runner is diagnostic-only, not general scheduler-backed userspace.

`just frame-smoke` builds an opt-in kernel variant that allocates one `Usable` frame, validates its HHDM address, writes and reads the whole page, clears it, returns it, and checks the prompt in QEMU. It reads the inherited root, walks all pages in the kernel image segments and requested 256 KiB stack span, compares effective PAT/MTRR types for kernel-image/HHDM aliases, and exercises a separate candidate map/unmap/release. The normal boot path in this image also clones the full reachable inherited hierarchy, hardens kernel-image HHDM aliases to text/rodata R/NX and data RW/NX while retaining PAT bits, switches CR3 with active-PCID and global-TLB invalidation, verifies the active root and critical mappings, and exercises the global heap's alignment, reuse, and deterministic exhaustion. The smoke test requires a serial marker confirming the applicable TLB invalidation path. The workflow restores the default release kernel and ISO. These probes rely on Limine's HHDM contract and do not inventory every unrelated mapping or prove physical-hardware correctness. `just fault-smoke` tests kernel-fatal page-fault, general-protection, invalid-opcode, and divide-error paths; it requires expected vector diagnostics (and CR2 for #PF), no prompt or return marker, and a halt until timeout. These fatal-path tests are distinct from `just user-fault-smoke`, which terminates a CPL3 process on #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE only when the diagnostic process runtime is installed. Diagnostic Cargo features are disabled by default and mutually exclusive, except each `probe-user-*` fault variant deliberately enables `probe-user-process`.

Keep the ACPI parser, IRQ vector allocator, PIT time arithmetic, Crabshell parser, VFS, memory-map validator, paging policy helpers, frame allocator, and fixed heap independent of hardware so ACPI signatures/checksums/MADT bounds and ACPI page-rounded span authorization, IRQ vector ownership/exhaustion, PIT divisor and elapsed-time arithmetic, syntax, path handling, address and leaf-PTE bit policy, PAT/MTRR policy, storage semantics, frame ownership, HHDM/root-range calculations, allocation alignment, reuse, and exhaustion can be tested without booting. Pure tests validate captured MTRR register snapshots, resolve the Intel SDM Table 11-7 PAT/MTRR combinations for one physical address, select a PAT index that remains uniform across MTRR boundaries in an aligned range, bind that selection to validated mapping metadata before encoding leaves, and walk synthetic four-/five-level page tables including large-page leaves. Host tests also exercise the candidate builder's owned-table walk, clone ownership, 4-/5-level mapping, 2 MiB/1 GiB splitting, permission/cache-bit preservation, active-state mutation/release guard, transactional allocation/prepare rollback, and retryable frame-release failure. Heap tests cover alignment, exact-layout free/reuse, zero-sized rejection, metadata exhaustion, and arena exhaustion. Tests reject malformed state, unsupported discontinuous masks, invalid indexes/ranges, out-of-range addresses, mismatched physical widths, and non-normal caching mode. The pure inherited-table walker does not access hardware tables; the opt-in QEMU reader and candidate backend use checked HHDM addresses. Boot-time QEMU checks a subset of live kernel/HHDM aliases but does not inventory all aliases or prove complete transition safety. Boot separately captures the registers and CR0 caching mode read-only and reports a diagnostic resolution; this is not a page-table or mapping test. The GDT/TSS/IDT and CPU-register paths are privileged kernel code. The temporary ACPI CR3/map/copy/restore path is hardware-only. The 2026-11-07 WSL2 q35 smoke reached the shell but rejected the MADT table span as `NotFullyAcpiBacked`; it did not validate a successful ACPI physical read or CR3 round-trip. QEMU boot and fault-injection checks complement, but do not replace, static review and target builds. Add tests for boundaries and failure behavior when introducing new pure kernel helpers. The kernel binary is not a host test target.

`just uefi-smoke` locates combined OVMF firmware or a matching CODE/VARS pair in standard system directories. `just thread-smoke` uses an opt-in kernel-thread probe, requires the lock-state, cooperative scheduling, non-yielding timer-preemption, and FPU-preservation markers, and restores the default release image. Split firmware uses a fresh temporary copy of the VARS template. `just input-smoke` validates UART RX and PS/2 IRQ delivery/wakeup against the normal default kernel. The OVMF checks require the expected MADT report and CR3-transition markers; install the Ubuntu `ovmf` package if no firmware is found. The BIOS smoke remains separate: if firmware places the RSDT in Reserved memory, the kernel's ACPI validation is expected to fail closed rather than accepting that table span.

## What current checks do not prove

- `cargo check` does not perform a final target link.
- A successful ELF link does not prove the boot protocol is recognized or `_start` is reached.
- Host unit tests do not validate privileged instructions, UART behavior, memory-map pointer validity, page tables, interrupts, or actual hardware. The QEMU boot path exercises the gated EFER/PAT reads and bounded MTRR capture and prints diagnostic summaries, but the prompt smoke assertion does not make those facts a mapping-safety proof.
- The automated QEMU prompt smoke test asserts the cloned CR3 transition, the applicable active-PCID/global-TLB invalidation marker, kernel HHDM alias permissions/cache preservation, heap probe, and shell prompt. The current emulator reports CR4.PGE clear; it exercises the CR3 reload path, not the PGE-toggle global flush path. `just frame-smoke` additionally exercises one allocator-owned frame, inherited paths, kernel/HHDM cache aliases, and a separate candidate mapping through Limine's HHDM contract. The clone preserves Limine's complete reachable hierarchy, but there is no clean-room mapping policy or exhaustive audit of unrelated aliases; emulator tests do not establish physical-hardware behavior. `just fault-smoke` exercises the controlled #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE fatal paths; it does not test every exception vector or general recovery.
- A separate manual QEMU session exercised directory navigation and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove operations, including `cp` replacing an existing destination and rejection of `rmdir` on a nonempty directory. This is not exhaustive shell coverage and does not prove persistence across reboot.
- There is no on-disk filesystem test, general userspace/process-scheduler test, userspace spawn/exec test, fuzz target, or physical-hardware test. `just process-smoke` validates blocking wait and real execution of one kernel-prepared child using a nested synchronous runner, not general scheduler-managed child contexts.

## Validation policy

For changes to the kernel entry, linker script, boot requests, architecture code, shell, or VFS, run `just verify`. For memory-management and ABI code, add negative tests for overflow, malformed ranges, permission failures, and invalid user pointers before exposing those paths to userspace.

Record commands actually run and any environment limitation in change summaries; never call an unexecuted build “passing.”

ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and bounded write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. Error decoding, short-write handling, formatting, region handling, and the size-class heap core are host-tested. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub. The opt-in diagnostic process runtime dispatches ABI-version, bounded descriptor-authorized write, close, duplication, one-page and multi-page anonymous map/unmap, exit, and wait. If wait finds its one kernel-prepared child running, it enters that child synchronously on a distinct continuation stack and resumes the parent only after child exit; other running-child configurations are unsupported. QEMU init checks that mappings are zeroed, writable across page boundaries, exactly unmapped, and no longer readable by the kernel copy path afterward. It also verifies real child Ring 3 entry/exit and status 7, invalid-pointer `EFAULT` without reaping, and successful wait/status-copyout on retry. This validates the bounded diagnostic execution path, not general concurrent process scheduling or a userspace process-creation syscall. A separate kernel-side harness waits for init after its exit trampoline returns.

### # Unix-like process and syscall direction › ## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented) › L23-27
```
| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | ABI contract: blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. The diagnostic supports an already-exited child and one kernel-prepared running child, which it runs synchronously before resuming the parent; other running-child cases return `-ENOTSUP`. Failed status copyout returns `-EFAULT` without reaping. |
| 4 | `mmap` | `RDI`: requested byte length, `1..=4096` | Maps one zero-filled, read/write, non-executable anonymous page and returns its user address. Lengths above one page return `-E2BIG`; the first-fit address comes from the bounded anonymous region window; exhaustion returns `-ENOMEM`. |
| 5 | `munmap` | `RDI`: page-aligned anonymous base, `RSI`: exactly `4096` | Removes one exact page previously allocated by `mmap`; invalid addresses, lengths, or non-anonymous regions return `-EINVAL`. |

## Matches in rustix/docs/architecture/interrupts.md

### # Interrupts and IRQ vector allocation › ## Current implementation › L7-8
```
`src/irq.rs` provides a host-tested, allocation-free token allocator for device vectors `0x20..=0xef` except reserved syscall vector `0x80`; exception vectors and the reserved upper range are also excluded. The IDT overrides `0x80` with a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate and assembly stub. The stub rejects CPL0 invocation, saves the full GPR set and x87/SSE state on the TSS entry stack, and dispatches a normalized syscall context with IF clear. In the opt-in process probe, the dispatcher implements ABI-version discovery, bounded write and wait-status copyout through allocator-owned user-frame copies, exit, and scheduler-independent kernel wait/reap after the synchronous entry returns. Userspace `wait` can reap an already-exited child; a running child returns `ENOTSUP` until blocking process scheduling exists. The normal build only exposes ABI-version discovery. `rustix_irq_dispatch` invokes the registered handler, returns for the APIC spurious vector without EOI, and halts on unregistered/unexpected vectors. Device handlers own their EOI. Vector registration is performed with IF clear before the corresponding I/O APIC source is unmasked.

```

The view borrows the kernel-root owner, which must remain alive and immutable; the root set uses one exclusive backend borrow for its roots. `destroy` is permitted only after the caller switches away and invalidates the root's local non-global translations; PCID-aware teardown is unsupported. The caller still owns CR3 transitions. Mapping metadata retains writable and executable permissions, and `validate_initial_user_state` requires an executable non-writable entry page plus a writable non-executable stack page. The opt-in `probe-user-process` diagnostic loads separate bundled init and child ELFs into independent roots. The kernel harness later waits/reaps init and tears down both inactive roots. Its one-page initial stack is cleared in bounded chunks before mapping, and Ring 3 checks an untouched byte is zero. ### # Unix-like process and syscall direction › ## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented) › L23-27
```
| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | ABI contract: blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. The diagnostic supports an already-exited child and one kernel-prepared running child, which it runs synchronously before resuming the parent; other running-child cases return `-ENOTSUP`. Failed status copyout returns `-EFAULT` without reaping. |
| 4 | `mmap` | `RDI`: requested byte length, `1..=4096` | Maps one zero-filled, read/write, non-executable anonymous page and returns its user address. Lengths above one page return `-E2BIG`; the first-fit address comes from the bounded anonymous region window; exhaustion returns `-ENOMEM`. |
| 5 | `munmap` | `RDI`: page-aligned anonymous base, `RSI`: exactly `4096` | Removes one exact page previously allocated by `mmap`; invalid addresses, lengths, or non-anonymous regions return `-EINVAL`. |
```

```
The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned tables as owned, and holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend; it is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. `SharedKernelHalf` validates and snapshots the sanitized upper root entries while borrowing the kernel owner. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` uses one exclusive backend borrow for multiple private roots, maps allocator-owned user 4 KiB leaves only in inactive lower halves, retains writable/executable permission metadata, validates the initial executable entry and writable NX stack, provides range-preflighted copy-in/copy-out through a separate `UserFrameMemory` backend, and destroys private leaf/table/root frames without freeing shared subtrees. Host tests cover four-/five-level sharing, U/S sanitization, independent mappings, permission checks, cross-page copies, unmap ownership, active-root release rejection, and rollback. The opt-in `probe-user-process` target constructs separate init and child roots, loads two bundled static ELFs, and runs the child only when the parent's wait observes it running. It switches CR3 and TSS entry stacks around the nested entry, uses a dedicated parent continuation stack, performs wait-status copyout before reap, and restores CR3 before kernel wait/reap and teardown. This bounded synchronous probe uses static kernel stacks and the Limine-derived shared kernel subtree; it is not general multi-process scheduling or a curated kernel-map policy. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.

The userspace wait runs one kernel-prepared child synchronously when it is still running, resumes init after child exit, and copies status before reaping; QEMU exercises that lifecycle and invalid-pointer retry. The kernel harness separately waits for init after its entry trampoline returns. # Interrupts and IRQ vector allocation

## Current implementation

`src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` installs the bootstrap GDT, TSS, exception gates for vectors 0–31, device IRQ stubs, and the APIC spurious-vector gate. Kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal. In the opt-in synchronous Ring 3 process probe, noncritical CPL3 exceptions are reported and handed to the installed process callback, which records status `128 + vector`, restores the kernel CR3, and exits through the user-entry trampoline. NMI (#2), double fault (#8), and machine check (#18) remain fatal regardless of saved CPL. QEMU exercises CPL3 #PF, #GP, #UD, and #DE termination in the diagnostic runtime; this is not a general exception or signal mechanism. Maskable interrupts start disabled and are enabled only after the validated APIC route, registered handler, and acknowledgement path are ready.

`src/irq.rs` provides a host-tested, allocation-free token allocator for device vectors `0x20..=0xef` except reserved syscall vector `0x80`; exception vectors and the reserved upper range are also excluded. The IDT overrides `0x80` with a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate and assembly stub. The stub rejects CPL0 invocation, saves the full GPR set and x87/SSE state on the TSS entry stack, and dispatches a normalized syscall context with IF clear. In the opt-in process probe, the dispatcher implements ABI-version discovery, bounded write and wait-status copyout through allocator-owned user-frame copies, exit, and wait on one kernel-prepared child. If that child is running, the diagnostic enters it synchronously on a distinct continuation stack and resumes the parent after exit; the kernel harness later waits/reaps init. This is not general scheduler-managed process execution or a userspace spawn operation. The normal build only exposes ABI-version discovery. `rustix_irq_dispatch` invokes the registered handler, returns for the APIC spurious vector without EOI, and halts on unregistered/unexpected vectors. Device handlers own their EOI. Vector registration is performed with IF clear before the corresponding I/O APIC source is unmasked.

The initial hardware target is single-vCPU QEMU `q35`: validated ACPI/MADT topology, local APIC and I/O APIC, masked legacy PIC routing, MADT-resolved ISA routes, and a periodic 8254 PIT tick near 100 Hz. OVMF smokes validate PIT delivery/EOI, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE state preservation, and UART/keyboard IRQ delivery. Host tests cover vector ownership and PIT/time arithmetic; they do not replace privileged QEMU coverage.

The scheduler is single-vCPU and supports cooperative waits/yields plus PIT-driven timer preemption. The timer handler advances ticks and sends APIC EOI before any scheduling switch. The common IRQ stub saves the interrupted x87/SSE state before Rust dispatch and restores the selected context before `IRETQ`; the context switch keeps aligned per-context FXSAVE areas. IRQ-safe spin locks save and restore the prior IF state, and the global heap uses one; scheduler mutations are separately serialized by masking local interrupts. IRQ/exception handlers remain bounded and allocation-free, and no current IRQ handler acquires the heap lock. SMP, per-CPU state, and physical-hardware validation remain future work.

# Unix-like process and syscall direction

**Status: Milestone 4 is in progress. The opt-in single-vCPU QEMU diagnostic path creates separate lower-half roots for a bundled init and a kernel-prepared child, loads both static ELF images, and runs both in Ring 3. When init waits on its running child, the diagnostic path switches from the parent root to the child root on PID-indexed TSS entry stacks and a separate kernel continuation stack; child exit returns to the parent wait, which copies status before reaping. The first invalid status pointer returns `EFAULT` without reaping, and a retry succeeds. The path also serves ABI-version/write/close/dup/anonymous-map/exit calls, terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE with status `128 + vector`, and tears down both roots. The normal kernel does not launch userspace. This is a synchronous, IF-disabled single-vCPU diagnostic runner, not a general scheduler: there is no userspace spawn/exec syscall, arbitrary runnable-child scheduling, reusable process service, stack reclamation, or interruptible wait. VM failure-injection/exhaustion coverage and broader process/runtime semantics remain incomplete.**

Rustix aims to expose a small, versioned syscall surface that can support Unix-like processes and tools. The kernel must own this interface rather than inherit an ABI accidentally from a bootloader or emulator.

## Proposed compatibility principles

- Processes have independent virtual address spaces and explicit lifecycle states.
- File descriptors are per-process integer handles to kernel-managed objects; descriptor inheritance, close-on-exec, duplication, and sharing semantics must be specified together.
- Syscalls use one documented error convention and stable numeric identifiers. New operations must not silently repurpose old numbers.
- Arguments crossing privilege boundaries are copied or validated using narrowly scoped helpers. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::copy_from_user` and `copy_to_user` preflight the complete lower-half mapped range, check writable metadata for kernel-to-user copies, and operate only on owned frame tokens through `UserFrameMemory`; they never form a Rust reference from a user virtual address. Backend copy faults report the completed prefix. The diagnostic user-exception path terminates a process on supported CPL3 faults; it does not make arbitrary kernel memory accesses recoverable.
- Blocking, interruption, cancellation, and restart behavior are explicit for each syscall class.
- A compatibility layer (for example, POSIX-shaped libc behavior) remains separate from internal kernel APIs.

## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented)

ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts, addresses, and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and bounded write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. The workspace crate `crates/rustix-user` provides typed `no_std` wrappers for ABI version, write, wait, exit, close, descriptor duplication, one-page and bounded multi-page anonymous mappings plus a raw register-level call for low-level tests; it also provides a `run_main` entry helper and an optional mmap-backed `GlobalAlloc` implementation. Error decoding, short-write handling, formatting, region handling, and the size-class heap core are host-tested. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub. The opt-in diagnostic process runtime dispatches ABI-version, bounded descriptor-authorized write, close, duplication, one-page and multi-page anonymous map/unmap, exit, and wait. If wait finds its one kernel-prepared child running, it enters that child synchronously on a distinct continuation stack and resumes the parent only after child exit; other running-child configurations are unsupported. QEMU init checks that mappings are zeroed, writable across page boundaries, exactly unmapped, and no longer readable by the kernel copy path afterward. It also verifies real child Ring 3 entry/exit and status 7, invalid-pointer `EFAULT` without reaping, and successful wait/status-copyout on retry. This validates the bounded diagnostic execution path, not general concurrent process scheduling or a userspace process-creation syscall. A separate kernel-side harness waits for init after its exit trampoline returns.

| Number | Call | Register arguments | Result / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `abi_version` | none | `0x0001_0000` (major 1, minor 0). |
| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | ABI contract: blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. The diagnostic supports an already-exited child and one kernel-prepared running child, which it runs synchronously before resuming the parent; other running-child cases return `-ENOTSUP`. Failed status copyout returns `-EFAULT` without reaping. |
| 4 | `mmap` | `RDI`: requested byte length, `1..=4096` | Maps one zero-filled, read/write, non-executable anonymous page and returns its user address. Lengths above one page return `-E2BIG`; the first-fit address comes from the bounded anonymous region window; exhaustion returns `-ENOMEM`. |
| 5 | `munmap` | `RDI`: page-aligned anonymous base, `RSI`: exactly `4096` | Removes one exact page previously allocated by `mmap`; invalid addresses, lengths, or non-anonymous regions return `-EINVAL`. |
| 6 | `close` | `RDI`: descriptor | Closes one process-local descriptor; invalid or already-closed descriptors return `-EBADF`. |
| 7 | `dup` | `RDI`: source descriptor | Duplicates the stream into the lowest free descriptor slot at or above 3; invalid descriptors return `-EBADF`, and the fixed table limit returns `-EMFILE`. |
| 8 | `mmap_region` | `RDI`: requested byte length, `1..=1 MiB` | Maps a contiguous, zero-filled RW/NX anonymous region, rounding length up to 4 KiB. Returns its base; reservation, frame, or page-table exhaustion returns `-ENOMEM`. |
| 9 | `munmap_region` | `RDI`: exact region base, `RSI`: exact page-rounded region length | Unmaps one exact anonymous region returned by `mmap_region`; invalid ranges, lengths, or non-anonymous regions return `-EINVAL`. |

Numbers above 9 are unassigned and return `-ENOSYS`; assigning a number later is an additive extension, never a reinterpretation. `mmap`, `munmap`, `mmap_region`, `munmap_region`, `close`, and `dup` are available only in the opt-in diagnostic process runtime today. Descriptor 0 is reserved for input but v1 has no `read` or `open` call. Descriptors 1 and 2 start as stdout/stderr; child process records inherit the parent's current console-descriptor table, duplication creates an independent handle to the same stream, and process exit clears its descriptor table. The initial process is created by the kernel loader, not a syscall.

Stable v1 error numbers (returned negated in `RAX`) are: `1 EINVAL`, `2 EBADF`, `3 EFAULT`, `4 ENOMEM`, `5 ECHILD`, `6 EINTR`, `7 EIO`, `8 ENOSYS`, `9 E2BIG`, `10 EOVERFLOW`, and `11 ENOTSUP`, and `12 EMFILE`. Unknown syscall numbers return `-ENOSYS`. Pointer-plus-length ranges use checked arithmetic and must lie wholly in a mapped lower-half user range. `write` preflights the whole input range before output; a later endpoint failure may return a short count, and an error before progress returns `-EIO`. A copy fault after progress returns the completed prefix. An unmapped diagnostic `write` buffer returns `-EFAULT` before the syscall returns to userspace. `mmap` rounds any positive length up to one page, zeroes its frame before publication, and grants RW/NX access. The append-only `mmap_region`/`munmap_region` calls add exact multi-page anonymous mappings bounded to 1 MiB; mapping rolls back mapped pages and the reservation if allocation fails. Both unmap operations are restricted to exact anonymous reservations, and the kernel switches to its supervisor root, removes each PTE, and only releases each frame after the page table no longer references it. For `wait`, the optional status is copied before the matching exited child is reaped; failed copyout returns `-EFAULT` and leaves the child waitable. The diagnostic can synchronously enter its one kernel-prepared child when wait observes it running, then resumes the parent after exit. This is not scheduler-backed child blocking: arbitrary process launch/scheduling, interruption, signals, asynchronous delivery, and automatic syscall restart remain future work.

All ABI integers are fixed-width little-endian x86_64 values. The wait status is one signed 32-bit integer with no implicit padding or extra fields. No other user-visible structs exist in v1.

## Initial x86_64 entry design (Milestone 4; diagnostic path integrated)

The opt-in single-vCPU process probe enters Ring 3 with a validated five-word `IRETQ` frame and enters the kernel with `int $0x80` through a dedicated DPL-3 IDT gate. This intentionally avoids `SYSCALL`/`SYSRET`, `STAR`/`LSTAR`/`FMASK`, and `SWAPGS` state transitions in this first slice. The register and error contract below is the versioned v1 ABI, but the syscall surface and runtime are not general-purpose or enabled in the default boot path. The `rustix-user` crate includes typed wrappers, the `run_main` process-entry helper, complete-write and allocation-free formatting helpers, best-effort panic reporting, and an optional mmap-backed global allocator. The allocator obtains zeroed pages through `mmap`, serves power-of-two classes from 16 through 2048 bytes, rejects larger or over-aligned requests, and retains pages until process teardown; applications opt in by declaring `UserAllocator` as their global allocator. The runtime also exposes bounded multi-page `mmap_region`/`munmap_region` wrappers, validated by `rustix-init` across a page boundary. `rustix-init` exercises the entry helper and heap with `Vec` and `Box`, but the crate remains an early runtime and is not a general application or process-scheduling environment.

- **Vector ownership:** `0x80` lies inside the device-vector range (`0x20..=0xef`) and is reserved by `InterruptVectorAllocator`; generic IRQ allocation/release cannot claim it. The IDT installs a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ stub. Its assembly entry rejects CPL0 invocation, saves all GPRs and x87/SSE state, clears the direction flag, and calls a normalized Rust dispatcher with IF clear. The opt-in process probe implements ABI-version discovery, write, exit, one-page and multi-page mapping, and wait. Its one kernel-prepared child is entered synchronously on separate per-PID entry/continuation stacks; it does not provide a userspace spawn/exec operation or general scheduling.
- **Selectors:** the current GDT uses `0x08` for kernel code, `0x10` for kernel data, and `0x18` for the two-slot TSS descriptor. Ring-3 data and 64-bit code descriptors are appended at GDT indexes 5 and 6, with compile-time selector assertions for user data `0x2b` and user code `0x33` (RPL 3); the process probe uses these selectors in its validated entry frame.
- **Privilege stack:** a CPL3-to-CPL0 interrupt uses `TSS.RSP0`. The current QEMU probe selects bounded static 16 KiB supervisor entry and continuation stack slots by process ID from kernel BSS and verifies every page is writable, NX, and supervisor-only in the kernel root. `TSS.RSP0` follows the active process; the continuation stack keeps a parent's syscall frame suspended while the diagnostic enters its prepared child. Process roots share these validated upper-half mappings. After init's exit trampoline returns to the bootstrap stack, the probe restores bootstrap `RSP0`. These static slots are not reclaimed, and this synchronous runner handles only the prepared child; a general scheduler must own and reclaim process stacks only after saved contexts are unreachable. Callers must disable local interrupts and guarantee the stack is mapped writable in every address space that can run until the next update. A future SMP design needs per-CPU TSS and entry-stack state.
- **Entry frame and state:** the dedicated assembly stub saves all GPRs in the `SyscallContext` layout, passes the five-word privilege frame separately from the exception frame, and saves/restores x87/SSE state around the Rust dispatcher; AVX remains disabled under the current CPU-state policy. Kernel code runs with the direction flag clear. The process probe validates saved RIP/RSP against the active process mappings and accesses user buffers only through owned frame tokens. The diagnostic wait can synchronously run one prepared child while the parent remains suspended; it does not integrate user processes with the kernel scheduler.
- **Initial register convention:** `RAX` carries the syscall number; arguments use `RDI`, `RSI`, `RDX`, `R10`, `R8`, and `R9`; `RAX` carries the result. This convention and its initial numbers/errors are versioned as ABI v1. Implemented operations remain a subset of the documented contract.
- **Return validation:** use `IRETQ`, not `SYSRET`. Initial entry uses a host-tested frame sanitizer that requires exact ring-3 selectors, a canonical lower-half instruction pointer, a lower-half stack range, 16-byte initial stack alignment, and safe flags. Syscall resume uses a separate sanitizer that keeps exact selectors, canonical lower-half address shape, and privileged-flag checks but does not impose 16-byte alignment on an in-function RSP; it replaces user flags with `0x2` (IF remains clear). Once a process is active, the dispatcher also validates the saved instruction pointer against an executable mapping and the saved stack pointer against a writable NX mapping. A malformed frame is converted into process exit rather than returned to CPL3.
- **NMI and interrupt policy:** no GS-base swap is needed on this entry path. NMI, double fault, and machine check remain fatal even when their saved CS indicates CPL3. Other user-origin exceptions terminate the process with status `128 + vector` in the diagnostic runtime; QEMU exercises CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE. Kernel-origin #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE are separately tested as fatal. Ordinary maskable IRQs stay disabled throughout the synchronous process run.

This path depends on each process root sharing supervisor-only upper-half mappings that cover syscall/exception code, the IDT, GDT, TSS, and active kernel stacks. The bundled init/child roots and nested syscall/exception transitions are exercised by opt-in QEMU smokes, but the shared Limine-derived kernel mapping is not a curated kernel map or a general isolation policy. Do not enable normal boot-time Ring 3 execution until userspace process creation, scheduler-managed user contexts, scheduler-owned/reclaimed per-process kernel stacks, general wait-queue semantics, and the remaining Milestone 4 fault/teardown criteria are implemented and validated.

### Process address spaces (design; root construction partially implemented)

Use a separate four- or five-level root per process. The initial source is the retained active clone of Limine's hierarchy, not a curated clean-room root. Each process root owns its root page, all lower-half intermediate tables, and every user leaf frame. Keep the kernel-root owner alive for the lifetime of every process root. Copy only upper-half top-level entries from that owner into each process root; these entries are non-owning references to shared kernel subtrees, not deep copies, and must never be released by a process teardown. Do not copy lower-half entries from the kernel root.

Before publishing a shared kernel subtree, validate its page-table structure and physical bounds and reject any effectively user-accessible leaf. U/S permission is the conjunction of every entry on a path, so a U/S bit on one non-leaf alone does not grant user access. When copying upper-half root entries, clear their U/S bit as defense in depth; a user leaf then cannot become accessible if a lower entry changes. `paging::validate_supervisor_kernel_half` implements the bounded, read-only structural/effective-permission preflight, but it does not install roots or prove physical backing is readable; the supplied reader must provide that access guarantee. Sharing the active clone means every accepted upper-half supervisor mapping and alias is present in every process CR3. This is not a curated kernel map or kernel-page-table isolation, and it provides no transient-execution protection. User mappings remain private to one process, are confined to the lower canonical half, preserve W^X, and are non-global in the first implementation.

The kernel address-space owner is the only authority allowed to modify shared upper-half tables. Mutations must be serialized with local interrupts disabled on the current single-vCPU system and invalidate the affected local translation before the mapping change is relied on. A process root may not edit or reclaim shared tables. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::destroy` releases only private user leaves, intermediate tables, and the root; the caller must first switch CR3 to a different live root and invalidate this root's local non-global translations. Keep the shared kernel owner alive. PCID-aware invalidation and SMP shootdown remain unsupported and need a separate design.

The current `CandidatePageTables` deep-clones the inherited hierarchy, tracks all cloned tables as owned, and holds an exclusive mutable borrow of one memory backend; it is not itself the process-address-space abstraction. `SharedKernelHalf` validates and snapshots the sanitized upper root entries while borrowing the kernel owner. `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` uses one exclusive backend borrow for multiple private roots, maps allocator-owned user 4 KiB leaves only in inactive lower halves, retains writable/executable permission metadata, validates the initial executable entry and writable NX stack, provides range-preflighted copy-in/copy-out through a separate `UserFrameMemory` backend, and destroys private leaf/table/root frames without freeing shared subtrees. Host tests cover four-/five-level sharing, U/S sanitization, independent mappings, permission checks, cross-page copies, unmap ownership, active-root release rejection, and rollback. The opt-in `probe-user-process` target constructs separate init and child roots, loads two bundled static ELFs, and runs the child only when the parent's wait observes it running. It switches CR3 and TSS entry stacks around the nested entry, uses a dedicated parent continuation stack, performs wait-status copyout before reap, and restores CR3 before kernel wait/reap and teardown. This bounded synchronous probe uses static kernel stacks and the Limine-derived shared kernel subtree; it is not general multi-process scheduling or a curated kernel-map policy. Keep the kernel owner alive and immutable for the shared view's lifetime; callers must use a distinct page-table backend for process-owned tables.

### Static ELF64 image validation and page initialization (partial)

`src/elf.rs` parses little-endian x86_64 `ET_EXEC` images without allocation. It bounds the program-header count, load-segment count, and total mapped pages; checks file and virtual arithmetic, page alignment and `p_align` congruence, lower-half canonical ranges, non-overlapping page spans, readable segment flags, W^X, and that the entry point lies in a non-writable executable `PT_LOAD`. It rejects dynamic/interpreter and TLS segments and executable-stack requests. This initial format intentionally requires page-aligned load offsets/addresses and supports at most 64 program headers, 16 load segments, and 64 load pages. `populate_segment_page` copies one load page into an allocator-owned frame through `UserFrameMemory`, zero-filling bytes beyond the file payload. `load_into_process_root` allocates, populates, cache-selects, and maps every load page into an inactive process root. The diagnostic build reproducibly compiles `crates/rustix-init` as a static ELF64 payload; `just process-smoke` loads and runs the normal image, and `just user-fault-smoke` builds a `ud2` entry variant and validates process termination/reaping/teardown.

## ABI decisions still pending beyond v1

The initial v1 versioning, error encoding, syscall numbers, register-level request decoding, and assembly-matched syscall context layout are implemented in `src/syscall.rs`. The diagnostic `int 0x80` path sanitizes return frames and serves ABI-version, bounded descriptor-authorized write, close/dup, wait, one-page and multi-page mmap/munmap, and exit calls; invalid unmapped write/status buffers return `EFAULT` without corrupting the process or consuming a waitable child. `src/process.rs` provides fixed-capacity identity/exit-state policy. The userspace wait runs one kernel-prepared child synchronously when it is still running, resumes init after child exit, and copies status before reaping; QEMU exercises that lifecycle and invalid-pointer retry. The kernel harness separately waits for init after its entry trampoline returns. This does not implement a userspace process-creation syscall, scheduler-managed user contexts, arbitrary child scheduling, or interruptible wait. The fixed-capacity process table now tracks stdout/stderr console handles, child inheritance, duplicate slots, close, exit cleanup, and bounded-table exhaustion; these are not general file objects, and there is no read/open support. User faults are process-terminating only while the opt-in callback is installed; QEMU covers CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and kernel-fatal coverage for the same four vectors. This does not make arbitrary kernel accesses recoverable. Still to be specified before broader process operations are process-creation/exec and file-action semantics, general descriptor-object sharing and close-on-exec behavior, read/open support, blocking wait interruption, signal-like asynchronous delivery, clocks, and any additional structure layouts.

## Suggested first user-visible slice

The first controlled `no_std` init and a separately bundled child run only in the opt-in QEMU probe. Init exercises ABI-version discovery, descriptor duplication/write/close, EFAULT, a blocking wait that enters the real child, status-copyout retry, one-page and multi-page mmap/munmap, `Vec`/`Box` allocation, exit, kernel-side wait/reap, and teardown. The child writes a marker and exits with status 7; QEMU verifies the parent's retry reaps it. `rustix-user` provides typed wrappers, a process-entry helper, short-write handling, allocation-free formatting, panic exit, and an optional size-class allocator backed by mmap. This remains a diagnostic rather than a general process-execution environment: userspace spawn/exec, scheduler-managed user contexts and stacks, arbitrary runnable children, and VM failure/exhaustion tests remain work before a normal-boot userspace service. Read/write/open/close and descriptor-lifetime semantics need their own complete implementation and adversarial tests before any Unix-compatibility claim.

### # Boot protocol and kernel entry › ## Failure behavior and limitations › L35-36
```
An unsupported Limine base revision, missing required responses (including the stack-size response), bad pointers/alignment, invalid HHDM values, invalid image or segment bounds, invalid requested-stack spans, excessive counts, null entries, address arithmetic overflow, and invalid or overlapping physical ranges reject the complete boot snapshot. If an RSDP response is present but has a null address or its initial page-rounded mapping extent is not fully covered by validated ACPI regions, the complete snapshot is rejected; no RSDP response is allowed and reported as ACPI unavailable. Later ACPI table-read or cache-policy failures are reported as MADT unavailable and do not enable interrupts. `_start` halts before starting Crabshell rather than continuing with partial memory metadata. Structural checks cannot establish that a non-null loader pointer is mapped and readable; that remains an explicit trust assumption of the Limine handoff. The installed exception handlers print fatal context and halt; no fault recovery is provided. The validated one-vCPU APIC path enables selected timer/UART/keyboard IRQs after handler registration, while unregistered IRQs halt. COM1 output uses a bounded polling loop so a non-responsive UART does not block forever.

```
ABI version `1.0` is identified by `abi_version()`, syscall number `0`, returning `0x0001_0000` in `RAX`. In v1, `RAX` returns a signed 64-bit result: nonnegative values are success (including byte counts, addresses, and PIDs); errors are negative stable error numbers. ABI versioning is append-only: existing syscall numbers, argument meanings, layouts, and error values never change or get reused. There is no POSIX compatibility claim. `src/syscall.rs` implements the stable number/error constants, host-tested request decoding and bounded write service, and the assembly-matched syscall context layout. The workspace crate `crates/rustix-user` provides typed `no_std` wrappers for ABI version, write, wait, exit, close, descriptor duplication, one-page and bounded multi-page anonymous mappings plus a raw register-level call for low-level tests; it also provides a `run_main` entry helper and an optional mmap-backed `GlobalAlloc` implementation. Error decoding, short-write handling, formatting, region handling, and the size-class heap core are host-tested. `interrupts.rs` installs the DPL-3 gate and dedicated entry stub. The opt-in diagnostic process runtime dispatches ABI-version, bounded descriptor-authorized write, close, duplication, one-page and multi-page anonymous map/unmap, exit, and wait. If wait finds its one kernel-prepared child running, it enters that child synchronously on a distinct continuation stack and resumes the parent only after child exit; other running-child configurations are unsupported. QEMU init checks that mappings are zeroed, writable across page boundaries, exactly unmapped, and no longer readable by the kernel copy path afterward. It also verifies real child Ring 3 entry/exit and status 7, invalid-pointer `EFAULT` without reaping, and successful wait/status-copyout on retry. This validates the bounded diagnostic execution path, not general concurrent process scheduling or a userspace process-creation syscall. A separate kernel-side harness waits for init after its exit trampoline returns.

### # Unix-like process and syscall direction › ## Initial syscall ABI v1 contract (specified; register decoding implemented) › L23-27
```
| 1 | `exit` | `RDI`: signed 32-bit status in the low 32 bits (upper bits ignored) | Does not return; status is retained exactly by the parent wait record. |
| 2 | `write` | `RDI`: fd, `RSI`: user buffer, `RDX`: byte length | Returns bytes accepted; a short positive result is valid. Initial descriptors 1 and 2 are stdout/stderr console streams; other descriptors return `-EBADF`. Maximum request is 4096 bytes; zero length returns 0 without validating the pointer. |
| 3 | `wait` | `RDI`: child PID (0 means any child), `RSI`: optional user pointer to signed 32-bit exit status | ABI contract: blocks until a matching child exits and returns its PID. A non-null status output must be writable before the child is reaped; no matching child returns `-ECHILD`. The diagnostic supports an already-exited child and one kernel-prepared running child, which it runs synchronously before resuming the parent; other running-child cases return `-ENOTSUP`. Failed status copyout returns `-EFAULT` without reaping. |
| 4 | `mmap` | `RDI`: requested byte length, `1..=4096` | Maps one zero-filled, read/write, non-executable anonymous page and returns its user address. Lengths above one page return `-E2BIG`; the first-fit address comes from the bounded anonymous region window; exhaustion returns `-ENOMEM`. |
| 5 | `munmap` | `RDI`: page-aligned anonymous base, `RSI`: exactly `4096` | Removes one exact page previously allocated by `mmap`; invalid addresses, lengths, or non-anonymous regions return `-EINVAL`. |
```

On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 both in the working tree and from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run downloaded and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and passed the bounded QEMU boot to the shell prompt. GitHub Actions run [#5](https://github.com/JustEthanCodes/rustix/actions/runs/42288095710) passed `just verify` on the published `dev` commit on 2026-11-06; it does not cover later uncommitted changes. A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove commands. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met, and Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. An opt-in diagnostic QEMU path runs the bundled init in Ring 3 and validates ABI version/write/EFAULT, wait-status copyout and retry against a kernel-seeded exited-child fixture, exit, kernel wait/reap, process-root teardown, and CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE exits; blocking userspace wait, child scheduling, and normal-boot userspace remain unsupported, so Milestone 4 is in progress. A bounded physical-frame allocator is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`; token ownership and failed-deallocation semantics are documented and host-tested. The boot transition owns an activated clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, and the global heap begins with a 256 KiB BSS arena and 128 allocation records, with bounded frame-backed growth up to 1 MiB. The Limine base-revision 3 HHDM scope and a conservative initial mapping/alias/cache policy are documented. Pure host-tested helpers validate mapping ranges/PTE bits, parse PAT layouts, validate captured MTRR snapshots, combine PAT/MTRR types under normal caching according to Intel SDM Table 11-7, and select a PAT index only when it yields one effective type across an aligned physical range. Boot validates the captured state and prints a diagnostic effective type at PA 0. The transition preserves inherited cache attributes, adjusts kernel-image HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX, and checks the effective PAT index against the inherited mapping. `BootInfo` records raw CR3 and a validated decode of its root physical address and low-bit interpretation. Checked HHDM access is limited to complete allocator-owned usable frames and cloned table frames; the active root owns its cloned table pages while inherited leaf frames remain loader-owned. The complete linker-defined kernel-image span and requested 256 KiB initial boot-stack span are captured and validated; Limine does not report any larger allocation bounds or guard status, so Rustix does not infer a guard page. The heap has bounded frame-backed growth and an IRQ-save lock; allocation remains prohibited in IRQ/exception context. ACPI support includes bounded host-tested RSDP/SDT/RSDT/XSDT/MADT parsing and a read-only/NX boot reader that copies validated MADT data into owned state. Rustix has a tested single-vCPU APIC/PIT IRQ path, cooperative and timer-preemptive scheduling, IRQ-save locks, guarded kernel threads, bounded frame-backed heap growth, and interrupt-driven UART/PS/2 queues with a polling fallback. SMP, general-purpose process scheduling, a persistent filesystem, and Unix compatibility remain absent. The documented syscall ABI and process-root primitives are exercised only by an opt-in diagnostic process. This is not a general recovery policy or physical-hardware validation. # Unix-like process and syscall direction

**Status: Milestone 4 is in progress. The opt-in single-vCPU QEMU diagnostic path creates a lower-half process root sharing the validated supervisor kernel half, loads and runs a bundled static ELF in Ring 3, serves ABI-version/write/ready-child-wait/exit syscalls, terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE with status `128 + vector`, and restores/reaps the root. The normal kernel does not launch userspace. The diagnostic `wait` path reaps already-exited children, preserves a zombie when status copyout fails, and returns `ENOTSUP` for a running child; blocking for that child, general process scheduling/kernel stacks, virtual-memory allocation, and a userspace runtime remain unimplemented.**

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
