    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
                    kprintln!(
                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
                        virtual_address,
                        pml4_index,
                        root.physical_address(),
                        root_entry
                    );
                }
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");

    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.

            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",

    halt_forever();
}

/// Set once the fatal panic path has started. A panic from inside the fatal
/// path stops silently instead of recursively printing or looping diagnostics.
static FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
    core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    // Mask maskable interrupts before any diagnostics run: another kernel
    // thread must not resume after a panic is declared, and the fatal report
    // must not be preempted mid-print.
    //
    // SAFETY: Kernel panic path runs at CPL 0; masking IF is always sound.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    if FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE.swap(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant panics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

    24	/// Build the fresh stack frame consumed by the x86_64 cooperative switch.
    25	///
    26	/// The saved-register order is R15, R14, R13, R12, RBP, RBX, followed by the
    27	/// trampoline return address. The returned address is 16-byte aligned; after
    28	/// six pops and `ret`, the trampoline observes the SysV entry alignment
    29	/// (`RSP % 16 == 8`). This helper only prepares bounded inline stack storage.
    30	pub fn initialize_thread_context_stack(
    31	    stack: &mut [usize],
    32	    saved_registers: [usize; 6],
    33	    trampoline: usize,
    34	) -> Option<usize> {
    35	    const REGISTER_SLOTS: usize = 6;
    36	    const FRAME_SLOTS: usize = REGISTER_SLOTS + 1;
    37	    let word_size = core::mem::size_of::<usize>();
    38	    let frame_bytes = FRAME_SLOTS.checked_mul(word_size)?;
    39	    let stack_bytes = stack.len().checked_mul(word_size)?;
    40	    let stack_start = stack.as_mut_ptr() as usize;
    41	    let stack_end = stack_start.checked_add(stack_bytes)?;
    42	    let frame_start = stack_end.checked_sub(frame_bytes)? & !15usize;
    43	    let frame_offset = frame_start.checked_sub(stack_start)?;
    44	    if frame_offset % word_size != 0 {
    45	        return None;
    46	    }

    51	    }
    52

    54	    stack[first_slot + REGISTER_SLOTS] = trampoline;
    55	    Some(frame_start)
    56	}

fn switch_process_to_kernel_root<M: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    state: &ActiveUserProcessSyscallContext,
    roots: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
) {
    // SAFETY: Syscall entry has IF clear and runs on a stack mapped in both roots.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(state.kernel_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != state.kernel_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The kernel root is active and no other CPU can use this process root.
    if unsafe { roots.mark_inactive(state.process) }.is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
fn switch_kernel_to_process_root<M: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    state: &ActiveUserProcessSyscallContext,
    roots: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
) {
    // SAFETY: The process root is owned and mapped for this synchronous run;
    // the kernel/TSS stacks are shared and IF remains clear across the switch.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(state.process_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != state.process_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: CR3 now names this process root, and the shared kernel owner and
    // root set remain live until this synchronous process exits.
    if unsafe { roots.mark_active(state.process) }.is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

   172	## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI
   173	
   174	Userspace begins only after page tables, exception handling, scheduling, and controlled memory allocation are trustworthy. The syscall ABI is a product interface and must not emerge accidentally from internal functions. Milestone 3's single-vCPU IRQ-safe locking and timer-preemption gate is locally validated; this enables scheduler progress but does not by itself make user code isolated or safe. SMP remains outside this milestone.
   175	
   176	### Planned work
   177	
   178	- [x] Decide and document the initial x86_64 user-entry/syscall mechanism, register convention, selector/MSR setup, per-CPU state requirements, and safe return path. The design uses a DPL-3 `int $0x80` gate and validated `IRETQ`, with no syscall MSRs or `SWAPGS`. Vector `0x80` is excluded from the device allocator; the GDT installs asserted Ring 3 selectors, and the gate saves GPR/x87/SSE state and sanitizes return flags. The opt-in process probe exercises entry/return and mapping-aware return checks; it uses the static bootstrap entry stack and is not general process scheduling. Revisit the entry model if per-process stacks or SMP requirements change.
   179	- [x] Define per-process address-space construction without deep-cloning the entire kernel page-table tree for every process. The design shares validated supervisor-only upper-half subtrees, keeps lower-half tables and user frames process-owned, and specifies kernel-owner lifetime, teardown, permission, and local TLB rules. Implementation and validation remain pending.
   180	- [x] Complete the initial user/kernel page-permission and process-owned address-space path, including teardown and local TLB invalidation rules. The implementation shares validated supervisor-only kernel entries, maps/unmaps private lower-half user frames, retains executable/writable metadata, validates the initial entry and writable NX stack, and destroys the root only after switching away. Host tests cover ownership and rollback; `just verify` validates one activation/return/teardown cycle and frame-count restoration in QEMU. General concurrent process scheduling, scheduler-owned/reclaimed kernel stacks, curated kernel mappings, and broader isolation guarantees remain pending.
   181	- [x] Complete copy-in/copy-out semantics for the initial implemented syscall set. Frame-token-based helpers preflight ranges and permissions; bounded `write` and `wait` use them. Host tests cover cross-page copies, permissions, partial writes, and descriptor errors. `just process-smoke` verifies invalid write/status pointers return `-EFAULT` without kernel corruption or consuming the child, then successfully copies status and reaps after the real child exits. QEMU fault smokes verify CPL3 termination and fatal CPL0 separation for #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE. Transfer semantics for future syscalls remain pending.
   182	- [x] Specify v1 version discovery, initial syscall numbers/argument meanings, fixed-width layouts, negative error encoding, bounded partial-write/copy behavior, wait semantics, no-restart policy, and append-only compatibility before exposing calls. The contract is documented in `docs/architecture/syscall-abi.md`; host-tested decoding and the dedicated gate/stub are implemented. The diagnostic path exercises ABI-version, descriptor-authorized write, close/dup, wait on a real kernel-prepared child, one-page/multi-page mmap/munmap, and exit. The child runs synchronously while the parent wait is suspended; general scheduling/launch, arbitrary children, and interruption remain pending. Future read/open, general file-object semantics, signals, and clocks need implementation/specification.
   183	- [ ] Complete process lifecycle and descriptor-table semantics: create/load, exit, wait, close, duplication/inheritance, and cleanup. The diagnostic path binds exit/reap to process roots and runs a real kernel-prepared child when init waits; status copyout precedes reap, and invalid status pointers leave the exited child waitable. The fixed-capacity table inherits console stream handles on spawn, supports close/dup with lowest-free descriptor allocation, clears handles on exit, and returns `EMFILE` on exhaustion; host tests cover defaults, inheritance, duplicate independence, invalid/closed entries, slot reuse, capacity, and exit cleanup, while `just process-smoke` exercises dup/write/close and real child wait from Ring 3. A userspace create/exec operation, scheduler-managed runnable contexts, general wait queue behavior, stack reclamation, and general file-object/process ownership remain unimplemented. The QEMU diagnostic validates distinct static entry/continuation stacks by PID but does not hand process contexts to the kernel scheduler.
   184	- [ ] Integrate a general-purpose static ELF64 process loader and execution path. The bounded allocation-free parser validates `PT_LOAD` bounds, alignment, permissions, lower-half ranges, overlaps, file bounds, and executable entry points. The opt-in diagnostic now prepares and runs both bundled init and child ELFs from independent roots, with mapped stacks, but the loader is still an internal harness helper rather than a reusable process-launch/exec service; malformed-load paths are host-tested. Use `.bin` for command-line programs and `.app` for GUI applications as role-based suffixes for the same underlying format. `.app` is a Rustix single-file application suffix, not an Apple/macOS app bundle; initially require application resources to be embedded or absent.
   185	- [x] Complete and validate the initial user-mode exception policy. The diagnostic runtime terminates noncritical CPL3 faults with status `128 + vector`, while kernel-origin faults and NMI/#DF/#MC remain fatal. QEMU exercises #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE from CPL3 and #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE from CPL0; this does not provide recovery for arbitrary kernel accesses or all architectural vectors.
   186	- [ ] Define user virtual-memory regions, stack bounds/guard behavior, and a minimal anonymous allocation interface such as `mmap`/`munmap` (or a documented equivalent) before running general user programs. The diagnostic init reserves its ELF segments, one-page stack, and unmapped guard in a host-tested fixed-capacity `UserRegionTable`; anonymous reservations are first-fit within a bounded lower-half window and reject overlap, overflow, invalid ranges, and capacity exhaustion. The opt-in ABI maps one zero-filled RW/NX page per `mmap` call (requested length 1–4096) and adds append-only `mmap_region`/`munmap_region` calls for exact anonymous regions up to 1 MiB.      1	//! Fixed-capacity policy state for single-vCPU kernel threads.
     2	//!
     3	//! This module does not own stacks, switch CPU contexts, or access hardware.
     4	//! Its caller must serialize every call, including against timer IRQs (the
     5	//! runtime does so by disabling local interrupts around policy mutations). A
     6	//! thread is either ready, the sole running thread, blocked on exactly
     7	//! one live wait queue, or exited. Exited slots remain occupied until `reap`.
     8	//! Dispatch scans slots in deterministic round-robin order; waiters are woken
     9	//! in FIFO order. All storage is inline and bounded by the const capacities.
    10	
    11	/// Opaque identity for a thread slot allocation.
    12	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    13	pub struct ThreadId {
    14	    slot: usize,
    15	    generation: u64,
    16	}
    17

    20	        self.slot
    21	    }
    22	}

    24	/// Build the fresh stack frame consumed by the x86_64 cooperative switch.
    25	///
    26	/// The saved-register order is R15, R14, R13, R12, RBP, RBX, followed by the
    27	/// trampoline return address. The returned address is 16-byte aligned; after
    28	/// six pops and `ret`, the trampoline observes the SysV entry alignment
    29	/// (`RSP % 16 == 8`). This helper only prepares bounded inline stack storage.
    30	pub fn initialize_thread_context_stack(
    31	    stack: &mut [usize],
    32	    saved_registers: [usize; 6],
    33	    trampoline: usize,
    34	) -> Option<usize> {
    35	    const REGISTER_SLOTS: usize = 6;
    36	    const FRAME_SLOTS: usize = REGISTER_SLOTS + 1;
    37	    let word_size = core::mem::size_of::<usize>();
    38	    let frame_bytes = FRAME_SLOTS.checked_mul(word_size)?;
    39	    let stack_bytes = stack.len().checked_mul(word_size)?;
    40	    let stack_start = stack.as_mut_ptr() as usize;
    41	    let stack_end = stack_start.checked_add(stack_bytes)?;
    42	    let frame_start = stack_end.checked_sub(frame_bytes)? & !15usize;
    43	    let frame_offset = frame_start.checked_sub(stack_start)?;
    44	    if frame_offset % word_size != 0 {
    45	        return None;
    46	    }
    47	    let first_slot = frame_offset / word_size;
    48	    let frame_end = first_slot.checked_add(FRAME_SLOTS)?;
    49	    if frame_end > stack.len() || frame_start & 15 != 0 {
    50	        return None;
    51	    }
    52	
    53	    stack[first_slot..first_slot + REGISTER_SLOTS].copy_from_slice(&saved_registers);
    54	    stack[first_slot + REGISTER_SLOTS] = trampoline;
    55	    Some(frame_start)
    56	}

Boot-protocol pointers are checked for canonicality using the active 4- or 5-level paging width; physical map bounds and protocol-scoped HHDM range arithmetic are also validated. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 both in the working tree and from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run downloaded and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and passed the bounded QEMU boot to the shell prompt. The serial log showed memory-map and CPU reporting. GitHub Actions run [#5](https://github.com/JustEthanCodes/rustix/actions/runs/42288095710) passed `just verify` on the published `dev` commit on 2026-11-06; it does not cover later uncommitted changes. A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove commands. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met, and Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. An opt-in diagnostic QEMU path runs the bundled init in Ring 3 and validates ABI version/write/EFAULT, wait-status copyout and retry against a kernel-seeded exited-child fixture, `ENOTSUP` for a running child, exit, kernel wait/reap, process-root teardown, and CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE exits; blocking userspace wait, child scheduling, and normal-boot userspace remain unsupported, so Milestone 4 is in progress. A bounded physical-frame allocator is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`; token ownership and failed-deallocation semantics are documented and host-tested. The boot transition owns an activated clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, and the global heap begins with a 256 KiB BSS arena and 128 allocation records, with bounded frame-backed growth up to 1 MiB. The Limine base-revision 3 HHDM scope and a conservative initial mapping/alias/cache policy are documented. Pure host-tested helpers validate mapping ranges/PTE bits, parse PAT layouts, validate captured MTRR snapshots, combine PAT/MTRR types under normal caching according to Intel SDM Table 11-7, and select a PAT index only when it yields one effective type across an aligned physical range. Boot validates the captured state and prints a diagnostic effective type at PA 0. The transition preserves inherited cache attributes, adjusts kernel-image HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX, and checks the effective PAT index against the inherited mapping. `BootInfo` records raw CR3 and a validated decode of its root physical address and low-bit interpretation. Checked HHDM access is limited to complete allocator-owned usable frames and cloned table frames; the active root owns its cloned table pages while inherited leaf frames remain loader-owned. The complete linker-defined kernel-image span and requested 256 KiB initial boot-stack span are captured and validated; Limine does not report any larger allocation bounds or guard status, so Rustix does not infer a guard page. The heap has bounded frame-backed growth and an IRQ-save lock; allocation remains prohibited in IRQ/exception context. ACPI support includes bounded host-tested RSDP/SDT/RSDT/XSDT/MADT parsing and a read-only/NX boot reader that copies validated MADT data into owned state. Rustix has a tested single-vCPU APIC/PIT IRQ path, cooperative and timer-preemptive scheduling, IRQ-save locks, guarded kernel threads, bounded frame-backed heap growth, and interrupt-driven UART/PS/2 queues with a polling fallback. SMP, general-purpose process scheduling, a persistent filesystem, and Unix compatibility remain absent. The documented syscall ABI and process-root primitives are exercised only by an opt-in diagnostic process. Kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal; the opt-in user path terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and `just fault-smoke` separately verifies those four exceptions halt at CPL0. This is not a general recovery policy or physical-hardware validation. On 2026-10-21, `just verify` passed after adding CR3 decoding and the pure MTRR resolver, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. On 2026-10-22, `just verify` passed after adding bounded read-only MTRR register capture and validated PAT/MTRR policy resolution. On 2026-10-24, the final `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` runs passed after review. QEMU verified the 256 KiB stack request, cloned-root CR3 transition, kernel HHDM alias hardening, heap alignment/reuse/exhaustion probe, and shell prompt; the current emulator reports CR4.PGE clear, so it exercised CR3 invalidation with PGE disabled, while the PGE-toggle path was statically reviewed but not exercised. Milestone 2's local exit criteria are met. Hosted CI passed on the published `dev` commit, but it does not cover today's uncommitted work or establish physical-hardware behavior, a clean-room mapping policy, or exhaustive alias coverage. On 2026-11-07, `just verify` passed with 127 host tests and BIOS/OVMF QEMU coverage for APIC/PIT delivery, active mapping/TLB invalidation, cooperative scheduling, and UART/PS/2 input wakeups. On 2026-11-13, `just verify` passed with 130 host tests and extended OVMF coverage for IRQ-save lock IF restoration, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE context preservation, and input wakeups. Milestone 3's single-vCPU exit criteria are met. Milestone 4 is in progress: the process/EFAULT/ready-child-wait/running-child-ENOTSUP/teardown and CPL3/CPL0 exception-matrix smokes pass locally, while blocking userspace `wait`, general process scheduling, per-process kernel stacks, virtual memory, and a reusable userspace runtime remain pending. Vector `0x80` is excluded from the device allocator; the GDT installs asserted Ring 3 selectors, and the gate saves GPR/x87/SSE state and sanitizes return flags. Revisit the entry model if per-process stacks or SMP requirements change.

fn switch_process_to_kernel_root<M: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    state: &ActiveUserProcessSyscallContext,
    roots: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
) {
    // SAFETY: Syscall entry has IF clear and runs on a stack mapped in both roots.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(state.kernel_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != state.kernel_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The kernel root is active and no other CPU can use this process root.
    if unsafe { roots.mark_inactive(state.process) }.is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

pub fn zero_user_frame<U: UserFrameMemory>(
    frame: &Frame,
    user_memory: &mut U,
) -> Result<(), U::Error> {
    const ZERO_CHUNK: [u8; 128] = [0; 128];

    for offset in (0..PAGE_SIZE as usize).step_by(ZERO_CHUNK.len()) {
        user_memory.copy_to_frame(frame, offset, &ZERO_CHUNK)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn reap_exited_stacks<M: CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    runtime: &mut KernelThreadRuntime,
    candidate: &mut CandidatePageTables<'_, M>,
    allocator: &mut FrameAllocator,
) {
    for slot in 0..MAX_THREADS {
        let Some(thread) = runtime.thread_ids[slot] else {
            continue;
        };
        if runtime.policy.state(thread) != Ok(ThreadState::Exited) {
            continue;
        }
        let stack_start =
            runtime.stack_virtual_starts[slot].unwrap_or_else(|| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        rollback_stack(candidate, allocator, stack_start, THREAD_STACK_PAGES);
        runtime
            .policy
            .reap(thread)
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_on_stack_cleanup_failure());
        runtime.thread_ids[slot] = None;
        runtime.stack_virtual_starts[slot] = None;
        runtime.entries[slot] = None;
        runtime.arguments[slot] = 0;
        runtime.deadlines[slot] = None;
    }
}

fn allocate_and_map_user_page<M, U>(
    state: &mut ActiveUserProcessSyscallContext,
    roots: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    virtual_address: u64,
) -> Result<(), rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallError>
where
    M: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory,
{
    use rustix_kernel::paging::zero_user_frame;
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallError;

    let Some(allocator) = (unsafe { state.allocator.as_mut() }) else {
        halt_forever();
    };
    let frame = allocator.allocate().ok_or(SyscallError::OutOfMemory)?;
    if zero_user_frame(&frame, user_memory).is_err() {
        if allocator.deallocate(frame).is_err() {
            halt_forever();
        }
        return Err(SyscallError::Io);
    }
    let (mapping, cache_attributes) = match user_mapping_attributes(state, virtual_address, &frame)
    {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            if allocator.deallocate(frame).is_err() {
                halt_forever();
            }
            return Err(error);
        }
    };
    match roots.map_user_page(allocator, state.process, frame, mapping, cache_attributes) {
        Ok(()) => Ok(()),
        Err(failure) => {
            let error = page_map_error_to_syscall(failure.cause);
            if allocator.deallocate(failure.frame).is_err() {
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error)
        }
    }
}

    roots: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
) {
    // SAFETY: Syscall entry has IF clear and runs on a stack mapped in both roots.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(state.kernel_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != state.kernel_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The kernel root is active and no other CPU can use this process root.
    if unsafe { roots.mark_inactive(state.process) }.is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

//! Fixed-capacity process identity and parent/child exit-state policy.
//!
//! This module does not own address spaces or block in the scheduler. Callers
//! must pair each process ID with its root and retry `try_wait` after a child
//! state change; a `Running` result means a syscall caller still has to block.

pub const MAX_PROCESSES: usize = 4;
pub const MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS: usize = 8;

/// ID zero belongs to the kernel supervisor and is never assigned to userspace.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, Ord, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
pub struct ProcessId(u64);

impl ProcessId {
    pub const fn get(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
}

pub const KERNEL_PROCESS_ID: ProcessId = ProcessId(0);

pub const MAX_USER_REGIONS: usize = 32;
pub const USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START: u64 = 0x0000_4000_0000_0000;
pub const USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_END: u64 = 0x0000_4000_0100_0000;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserRegionKind {
    Image,
    Stack,
    Guard,
    Anonymous,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct UserRegion {
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
    kind: UserRegionKind,
}

impl UserRegion {

        self.start
    }

    pub const fn end(self) -> u64 {
        self.end
    }

    pub const fn length(self) -> u64 {
        self.end - self.start
    }

    pub const fn kind(self) -> UserRegionKind {
        self.kind
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct UserStackLayout {
    stack_region: UserRegion,
    guard_region: UserRegion,

}

impl UserStackLayout {

        self.stack_region
    }

    pub const fn guard_region(self) -> UserRegion {
        self.guard_region
    }

    pub const fn stack_pointer(self) -> u64 {
        self.stack_pointer
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserRegionError {
    InvalidAddressWidth,
    EmptyRange,
    UnalignedRange,
    AddressOverflow,
    NonCanonicalRange,
    Overlap,
    Capacity,
    AnonymousAddressSpaceExhausted,
    NotAnonymousRegion,
}

/// Bounded user virtual-region reservations for one address space.
///
/// Region reservations are metadata only: page ownership and page-table changes
/// remain the responsibility of the process-root mapping APIs. Guard regions are
/// reserved here but intentionally have no backing mapping.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct UserRegionTable {
    regions: [Option<UserRegion>; MAX_USER_REGIONS],
}

impl UserRegionTable {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            regions: [None; MAX_USER_REGIONS],
        }
    }

    /// Reserve a page-aligned lower-half range, including an unmapped guard range.
    pub fn reserve(
        &mut self,
        start: u64,
        length: u64,
        kind: UserRegionKind,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<UserRegion, UserRegionError> {
        validate_user_region_range(start, length, virtual_address_bits)?;
        let end = start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if self
            .regions
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .any(|region| start < region.end && region.start < end)
        {
            return Err(UserRegionError::Overlap);
        }
        let slot = self
            .regions
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::Capacity)?;
        let region = UserRegion { start, end, kind };
        self.regions[slot] = Some(region);
        Ok(region)
    }

    /// Transactionally reserve validated ELF load pages, a stack, and its guard.
    ///
    /// `stack_base` is the low address of the mapped stack. The initial stack
    /// pointer is the one-past end address. No page tables or backing frames are
    /// changed; the caller remains responsible for loading the image and mapping
    /// the stack. At least one stack and one guard page are required.
    pub fn reserve_elf_layout(
        &mut self,
        image: &crate::elf::Elf64Image<'_>,
        stack_base: u64,
        stack_pages: u64,
        guard_pages: u64,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<UserStackLayout, UserRegionError> {
        if stack_pages == 0 || guard_pages == 0 {
            return Err(UserRegionError::EmptyRange);
        }
        let page_size = crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
        let stack_length = stack_pages
            .checked_mul(page_size)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let guard_length = guard_pages
            .checked_mul(page_size)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let guard_base = stack_base
            .checked_sub(guard_length)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let stack_pointer = stack_base
            .checked_add(stack_length)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;

        let mut staged = *self;
        for segment in image.segments() {
            let page_count = u64::try_from(segment.page_count())
                .map_err(|_| UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let length = page_count
                .checked_mul(page_size)
                .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
            staged.reserve(
                segment.virtual_start(),
                length,
                UserRegionKind::Image,
                virtual_address_bits,
            )?;
        }
        let guard_region = staged.reserve(
            guard_base,
            guard_length,
            UserRegionKind::Guard,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let stack_region = staged.reserve(
            stack_base,
            stack_length,
            UserRegionKind::Stack,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        *self = staged;
        Ok(UserStackLayout {
            stack_region,
            guard_region,
            stack_pointer,
        })
    }

    /// Reserve the first free range in the bounded anonymous-map window.
    ///
    /// The requested byte length is rounded up to a page. Allocations are
    /// read/write, non-executable by policy; this table does not install PTEs.
    pub fn allocate_anonymous(
        &mut self,
        requested_length: u64,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<UserRegion, UserRegionError> {
        if requested_length == 0 {
            return Err(UserRegionError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
            return Err(UserRegionError::InvalidAddressWidth);
        }
        if self.regions.iter().all(Option::is_some) {
            return Err(UserRegionError::Capacity);
        }
        let page_size = crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
        let length = requested_length
            .checked_add(page_size - 1)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?
            & !(page_size - 1);
        let mut candidate = USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START;
        loop {
            let end = candidate
                .checked_add(length)
                .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
            if end > USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_END {
                return Err(UserRegionError::AnonymousAddressSpaceExhausted);
            }
            let overlap = self
                .regions
                .iter()
                .flatten()
                .filter(|region| candidate < region.end && region.start < end)
                .min_by_key(|region| region.end);
            if let Some(region) = overlap {
                candidate = region.end;
                continue;
            }
            return self.reserve(
                candidate,
                length,
                UserRegionKind::Anonymous,
                virtual_address_bits,
            );
        }
    }

    /// Release only an exact anonymous reservation; image, stack, and guard
    /// regions cannot be released through this operation.
    pub fn release_anonymous(
        &mut self,
        start: u64,
        length: u64,
    ) -> Result<UserRegion, UserRegionError> {
        if length == 0 {
            return Err(UserRegionError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if (start | length) & (crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(UserRegionError::UnalignedRange);
        }
        let end = start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let slot = self.regions.iter().position(|region| {
            region.is_some_and(|region| {
                region.start == start
                    && region.end == end
                    && region.kind == UserRegionKind::Anonymous
            })
        });
        let Some(slot) = slot else {
            return Err(UserRegionError::NotAnonymousRegion);
        };
        Ok(self.regions[slot]
            .take()
            .expect("matching anonymous reservation remains present"))
    }

    pub fn regions(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = UserRegion> + '_ {
        self.regions.iter().flatten().copied()
    }
}

impl Default for UserRegionTable {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Maximum number of pages accepted for a process's initial user stack.
pub const MAX_INITIAL_USER_STACK_PAGES: u64 = 16;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserProgramPrepareErrorKind {
    InvalidElf,
    RootCreation,
    RegionReservation,
    ElfLoad,
    StackGuard,
    StackAllocation,
    StackInitialization,
    StackMapping,
    InvalidInitialState,
    InvalidIretFrame,
    CachePolicy(&'static str),
}

impl UserProgramPrepareErrorKind {
    pub const fn message(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::InvalidElf => "ELF image validation failed",
            Self::RootCreation => "process root creation failed",
            Self::RegionReservation => "ELF, stack, or guard reservation failed",
            Self::ElfLoad => "ELF image could not be loaded",
            Self::StackGuard => "stack guard is not unmapped",
            Self::StackAllocation => "no frame available for the user stack",
            Self::StackInitialization => "user stack frame could not be zeroed",
            Self::StackMapping => "user stack page could not be mapped",
            Self::InvalidInitialState => "ELF entry or user stack failed validation",
            Self::InvalidIretFrame => "initial user IRET frame was rejected",
            Self::CachePolicy(message) => message,
        }
    }
}

/// Resources that a caller must retry cleaning up when preparation fails.
/// `process` remains owned by `roots`; `frame` is an allocated frame that was
/// not installed in that process root.
pub struct UserProgramPrepareError {
    pub kind: UserProgramPrepareErrorKind,
    pub process: Option<crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle>,
    pub frame: Option<crate::frame::Frame>,
}

/// A loaded ELF image and its validated initial Ring 3 entry state.
pub struct PreparedUserProgram {
    pub process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    pub regions: UserRegionTable,
    pub user_frame: crate::syscall::ValidatedUserIretFrame,
}

fn cleanup_failed_user_program<M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    roots: &mut crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    allocator: &mut crate::frame::FrameAllocator,
    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    kind: UserProgramPrepareErrorKind,
    frame: Option<crate::frame::Frame>,
) -> UserProgramPrepareError {
    let retained_process = roots.destroy(allocator, process).err().map(|_| process);
    let retained_frame = frame.and_then(|frame| match allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        Ok(()) => None,
        Err(error) => Some(error.frame),
    });
    UserProgramPrepareError {
        kind,
        process: retained_process,
        frame: retained_frame,
    }
}

/// Load a static ELF image into a fresh process root and prepare its guarded,
/// zero-filled initial user stack. All limits are explicit and failures return
/// any root or frame whose ownership could not be reclaimed.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
pub fn prepare_user_program<M, U, F>(
    roots: &mut crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    allocator: &mut crate::frame::FrameAllocator,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    image_bytes: &[u8],
    stack_base: u64,
    stack_pages: u64,
    guard_pages: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    user_code_selector: u16,
    user_data_selector: u16,
    select_cache: &mut F,
) -> Result<PreparedUserProgram, UserProgramPrepareError>
where
    M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
    F: FnMut(
        crate::paging::ValidatedMappingRange,
    ) -> Result<crate::paging::SelectedCacheAttributes, &'static str>,
{
    use crate::paging::{validate_mapping_range, PagePermissions, PAGE_SIZE};

    let image = crate::elf::Elf64Image::parse(image_bytes, virtual_address_bits).map_err(|_| {
        UserProgramPrepareError {
            kind: UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::InvalidElf,
            process: None,
            frame: None,
        }
    })?;
    if stack_pages == 0 || stack_pages > MAX_INITIAL_USER_STACK_PAGES || guard_pages == 0 {
        return Err(UserProgramPrepareError {
            kind: UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::RegionReservation,
            process: None,
            frame: None,
        });
    }
    let process = match roots.create(allocator) {
        Ok(process) => process,
        Err(failure) => {
            let frame = failure.frame;
            let frame = frame.and_then(|frame| match allocator.deallocate(frame) {
                Ok(()) => None,
                Err(error) => Some(error.frame),
            });
            return Err(UserProgramPrepareError {
                kind: UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::RootCreation,
                process: None,
                frame,
            });
        }
    };
    let mut regions = UserRegionTable::new();
    let stack_layout = match regions.reserve_elf_layout(
        &image,
        stack_base,
        stack_pages,
        guard_pages,
        virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(layout) => layout,
        Err(_) => {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::RegionReservation,
                None,
            ));
        }
    };
    if let Err(failure) =
        image.load_into_process_root(roots, allocator, process, user_memory, &mut *select_cache)
    {
        return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
            roots,
            allocator,
            process,
            UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::ElfLoad,
            failure.frame,
        ));
    }

    let mut guard_probe = [0u8; 1];
    // SAFETY: The scratch byte is kernel stack storage, disjoint from user frames.
    // The reserved guard range must have no mapped user backing.
    match unsafe {
        roots.copy_from_user(
            process,
            stack_layout.guard_region().start(),
            &mut guard_probe,
            user_memory,
        )
    } {
        Err(failure) if matches!(failure.cause, crate::paging::ProcessUserCopyError::Unmapped) => {}
        _ => {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackGuard,
                None,
            ));
        }
    }

    for offset in (0..stack_layout.stack_region().length()).step_by(PAGE_SIZE as usize) {
        let frame = match allocator.allocate() {
            Some(frame) => frame,
            None => {
                return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                    roots,
                    allocator,
                    process,
                    UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackAllocation,
                    None,
                ));
            }
        };
        if crate::paging::zero_user_frame(&frame, user_memory).is_err() {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackInitialization,
                Some(frame),
            ));
        }
        let Some(virtual_address) = stack_layout.stack_region().start().checked_add(offset) else {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackMapping,
                Some(frame),
            ));
        };
        let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            frame.address(),
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: true,
            },
            Some(physical_address_bits),
            virtual_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(mapping) => mapping,
            Err(_) => {
                return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                    roots,
                    allocator,
                    process,
                    UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackMapping,
                    Some(frame),
                ));
            }
        };
        let cache_attributes = match select_cache(mapping) {
            Ok(attributes) => attributes,
            Err(message) => {
                return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                    roots,
                    allocator,
                    process,
                    UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::CachePolicy(message),
                    Some(frame),
                ));
            }
        };
        if let Err(failure) =
            roots.map_user_page(allocator, process, frame, mapping, cache_attributes)
        {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackMapping,
                Some(failure.frame),
            ));
        }
    }

    if roots
        .validate_initial_user_state(process, image.entry_point(), stack_layout.stack_pointer())
        .is_err()
    {
        return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
            roots,
            allocator,
            process,
            UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::InvalidInitialState,
            None,
        ));
    }
    let raw_frame = crate::syscall::UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: image.entry_point(),
        code_selector: u64::from(user_code_selector),
        flags: crate::syscall::SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer: stack_layout.stack_pointer(),
        stack_selector: u64::from(user_data_selector),
    };
    let user_frame = match crate::syscall::sanitize_user_iret_frame(raw_frame, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(_) => {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::InvalidIretFrame,
                None,
            ));
        }
    };

    Ok(PreparedUserProgram {
        process,
        regions,
        user_frame,
    })
}

fn validate_user_region_range(
    start: u64,
    length: u64,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), UserRegionError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(UserRegionError::InvalidAddressWidth);
    }
    if length == 0 {
        return Err(UserRegionError::EmptyRange);
    }
    let page_size = crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    if (start | length) & (page_size - 1) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRegionError::UnalignedRange);
    }
    let end = start
        .checked_add(length)
        .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
    let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
    if start >= lower_half_end
        || end > lower_half_end
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(start, virtual_address_bits)
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(end - 1, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(UserRegionError::NonCanonicalRange);
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ProcessState {
    Running,
    Exited(i32),
}

/// A nonblocking observation of a child. `try_wait` reaps an exited child; `peek_wait` does not.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum WaitResult {
    Running { pid: ProcessId },
    Exited { pid: ProcessId, status: i32 },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ProcessTableError {
    Capacity,
    InitialProcessAlreadyExists,
    InvalidProcess,
    InvalidParent,
    ParentExited,
    AlreadyExited,
    NoChild,
    ChildStillRunning,
    BadFileDescriptor,
    DescriptorTableFull,

}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct ProcessRecord {
    pid: ProcessId,
    parent: ProcessId,
    state: ProcessState,
    descriptors: [Option<crate::syscall::ConsoleStream>; MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS],
}

fn initial_console_descriptors() -> [Option<crate::syscall::ConsoleStream>; MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS]
{
    let mut descriptors = [None; MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS];
    descriptors[1] = Some(crate::syscall::ConsoleStream::Stdout);
    descriptors[2] = Some(crate::syscall::ConsoleStream::Stderr);
    descriptors
}

/// Bounded, allocation-free process lifecycle records for the first user slice.
///
/// Exited records remain waitable zombies until their parent calls `try_wait`.
/// If a parent exits first, its children are reparented to the kernel supervisor
/// so their exit records remain reapable. This table models only inherited console
/// stream descriptors; file objects and address-space ownership live elsewhere.
pub struct ProcessTable {
    records: [Option<ProcessRecord>; MAX_PROCESSES],
    next_pid: Option<u64>,
}

impl ProcessTable {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            records: [None; MAX_PROCESSES],
            next_pid: Some(1),
        }
    }

    /// Register the one boot-created process under the kernel supervisor.
    pub fn create_initial(&mut self) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        if self
            .records
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .any(|record| record.parent == KERNEL_PROCESS_ID)
        {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::InitialProcessAlreadyExists);
        }
        self.insert(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, initial_console_descriptors())
    }

    /// Register a child of a currently running process.
    pub fn spawn(&mut self, parent: ProcessId) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        let parent_record = self
            .record(parent)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)?;
        if parent_record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited);
        }
        self.insert(parent, parent_record.descriptors)
    }

    /// Record an exit status without reclaiming the process identity.
    pub fn exit(&mut self, pid: ProcessId, status: i32) -> Result<(), ProcessTableError> {
        let index = self
            .records
            .iter()
            .position(|record| record.is_some_and(|record| record.pid == pid))
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidProcess)?;
        let record = self.records[index]
            .as_mut()
            .expect("process slot was found");
        if record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::AlreadyExited);
        }
        record.state = ProcessState::Exited(status);
        record.descriptors = [None; MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS];
        for child in self.records.iter_mut().flatten() {
            if child.parent == pid {
                child.parent = KERNEL_PROCESS_ID;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Inspect a matching child without consuming an exited record.
    ///
    /// `child_pid == 0` selects any child, preferring the lowest-PID exited child.
    /// This split lets callers validate/copy exit status before reaping a zombie.
    pub fn peek_wait(
        &self,
        parent: ProcessId,
        child_pid: u64,
    ) -> Result<WaitResult, ProcessTableError> {
        if parent != KERNEL_PROCESS_ID {
            let parent_record = self
                .record(parent)
                .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)?;
            if parent_record.state != ProcessState::Running {
                return Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited);
            }
        }

        let mut found_child = false;
        let mut running: Option<ProcessId> = None;
        let mut exited: Option<(ProcessId, i32)> = None;
        for record in self.records.iter().flatten().filter(|record| {
            record.parent == parent && (child_pid == 0 || record.pid.get() == child_pid)
        }) {
            found_child = true;
            match record.state {
                ProcessState::Running => {
                    if running.is_none_or(|pid| record.pid < pid) {
                        running = Some(record.pid);
                    }
                }
                ProcessState::Exited(status) => {
                    if exited.is_none_or(|(pid, _)| record.pid < pid) {
                        exited = Some((record.pid, status));
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        if let Some((pid, status)) = exited {
            return Ok(WaitResult::Exited { pid, status });
        }
        if let Some(pid) = running {
            return Ok(WaitResult::Running { pid });
        }
        if found_child {
            unreachable!("a matching child must be running or exited");
        }
        Err(ProcessTableError::NoChild)
    }

    /// Reap one specific exited child after its status has been consumed.
    pub fn reap_exited(
        &mut self,
        parent: ProcessId,
        child_pid: ProcessId,
    ) -> Result<WaitResult, ProcessTableError> {
        let result = self.peek_wait(parent, child_pid.get())?;
        let WaitResult::Exited { pid, status } = result else {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::ChildStillRunning);
        };
        let index = self
            .records
            .iter()
            .position(|record| {
                record.is_some_and(|record| record.pid == pid && record.parent == parent)
            })
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::NoChild)?;
        self.records[index] = None;
        Ok(WaitResult::Exited { pid, status })
    }

    /// Inspect or reap a matching child without blocking.
    ///
    /// `child_pid == 0` selects any child, preferring the lowest-PID exited child.
    pub fn try_wait(
        &mut self,
        parent: ProcessId,
        child_pid: u64,
    ) -> Result<WaitResult, ProcessTableError> {
        let result = self.peek_wait(parent, child_pid)?;
        if let WaitResult::Exited { pid, .. } = result {
            let _ = self.reap_exited(parent, pid)?;
        }
        Ok(result)
    }

    pub fn state(&self, pid: ProcessId) -> Option<ProcessState> {
        self.record(pid).map(|record| record.state)
    }

    pub fn live_records(&self) -> usize {
        self.records.iter().flatten().count()
    }

    /// Resolve one live descriptor to its bounded console-stream target.
    pub fn descriptor_stream(
        &self,
        pid: ProcessId,
        descriptor: u64,
    ) -> Option<crate::syscall::ConsoleStream> {
        let descriptor = usize::try_from(descriptor).ok()?;
        self.record(pid)?
            .descriptors
            .get(descriptor)
            .copied()
            .flatten()
    }

    /// Close one descriptor without affecting duplicated descriptors to the same stream.
    pub fn close_descriptor(
        &mut self,
        pid: ProcessId,
        descriptor: u64,
    ) -> Result<(), ProcessTableError> {
        let descriptor =
            usize::try_from(descriptor).map_err(|_| ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)?;
        let record = self
            .records
            .iter_mut()
            .flatten()
            .find(|record| record.pid == pid)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidProcess)?;
        if record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::AlreadyExited);
        }
        let entry = record
            .descriptors
            .get_mut(descriptor)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)?;
        entry.take().ok_or(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Duplicate a descriptor into the lowest free slot at or above descriptor 3.
    pub fn duplicate_descriptor(
        &mut self,
        pid: ProcessId,
        descriptor: u64,
    ) -> Result<u64, ProcessTableError> {
        let source = self
            .descriptor_stream(pid, descriptor)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)?;
        let record = self
            .records
            .iter_mut()
            .flatten()
            .find(|record| record.pid == pid)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidProcess)?;
        if record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::AlreadyExited);
        }
        let slot = record
            .descriptors
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .skip(3)
            .find_map(|(index, descriptor)| descriptor.is_none().then_some(index))
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::DescriptorTableFull)?;
        record.descriptors[slot] = Some(source);
        Ok(slot as u64)
    }

    fn insert(
        &mut self,
        parent: ProcessId,
        descriptors: [Option<crate::syscall::ConsoleStream>; MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS],
    ) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        let slot = self
            .records
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::Capacity)?;
        let pid = self.next_pid.ok_or(ProcessTableError::ProcessIdExhausted)?;
        self.next_pid = pid.checked_add(1);
        let pid = ProcessId(pid);
        self.records[slot] = Some(ProcessRecord {
            pid,
            parent,
            state: ProcessState::Running,
            descriptors,
        });
        Ok(pid)
    }

    fn record(&self, pid: ProcessId) -> Option<&ProcessRecord> {
        self.records
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .find(|record| record.pid == pid)
    }
}

impl Default for ProcessTable {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        ProcessState, ProcessTable, ProcessTableError, UserRegionError, UserRegionKind,
        UserRegionTable, WaitResult, KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, MAX_PROCESSES, MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS,
        USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START,
    };

    #[test]
    fn child_exit_status_is_retained_until_exact_wait_reaps_it() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, child.get()),
            Ok(WaitResult::Running { pid: child })
        );
        processes.exit(child, -17).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), Some(ProcessState::Exited(-17)));
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, child.get()),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: child,
                status: -17,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), None);
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, child.get()),
            Err(ProcessTableError::NoChild)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn peek_wait_keeps_a_zombie_until_status_consumption_succeeds() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let parent = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(parent).unwrap();
        processes.exit(child, 41).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.peek_wait(parent, child.get()),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: child,
                status: 41,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), Some(ProcessState::Exited(41)));
        assert_eq!(
            processes.reap_exited(parent, child),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: child,
                status: 41,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), None);
        assert_eq!(
            processes.reap_exited(parent, child),
            Err(ProcessTableError::NoChild)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reaping_a_running_child_is_rejected_without_mutation() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let parent = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(parent).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.reap_exited(parent, child),
            Err(ProcessTableError::ChildStillRunning)
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), Some(ProcessState::Running));
    }

    #[test]
    fn wait_any_prefers_the_lowest_pid_zombie_and_keeps_running_children() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let first = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();
        let second = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();
        processes.exit(second, 23).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, 0),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: second,
                status: 23,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, 0),
            Ok(WaitResult::Running { pid: first })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn exiting_parent_reparents_children_to_kernel_supervisor() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();
        processes.exit(init, 0).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, 0),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: init,
                status: 0,
            })
        );
        processes.exit(child, 7).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, child.get()),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: child,
                status: 7,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn capacity_and_invalid_lifecycle_operations_are_explicit() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.spawn(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID),
            Err(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)
        );
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.create_initial(),
            Err(ProcessTableError::InitialProcessAlreadyExists)
        );
        let children: [Option<super::ProcessId>; MAX_PROCESSES - 1] =
            core::array::from_fn(|_| None);
        let mut children = children;
        for child in &mut children {
            *child = Some(processes.spawn(init).unwrap());
        }
        assert_eq!(processes.live_records(), MAX_PROCESSES);
        assert_eq!(processes.spawn(init), Err(ProcessTableError::Capacity));

        let child = children[0].unwrap();
        processes.exit(child, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.exit(child, 2),
            Err(ProcessTableError::AlreadyExited)
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.spawn(child), Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited));
    }

    #[test]
    fn descriptors_start_with_console_streams_and_are_inherited_by_children() {
        use crate::syscall::ConsoleStream;

        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let parent = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(processes.descriptor_stream(parent, 0), None);
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(parent, 1),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(parent, 2),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stderr)
        );

        let duplicate = processes.duplicate_descriptor(parent, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(duplicate, 3);
        let child = processes.spawn(parent).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(child, 1),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(child, 3),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );

        processes.close_descriptor(parent, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(processes.descriptor_stream(parent, 1), None);
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(parent, 3),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(child, 1),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn descriptor_operations_reject_invalid_entries_reuse_slots_and_report_capacity() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let process = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(processes.descriptor_stream(process, u64::MAX), None);
        assert_eq!(
            processes.close_descriptor(process, 0),
            Err(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.duplicate_descriptor(process, 0),
            Err(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)
        );

        let first = processes.duplicate_descriptor(process, 1).unwrap();
        processes.close_descriptor(process, first).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(processes.descriptor_stream(process, first), None);
        assert_eq!(processes.duplicate_descriptor(process, 2), Ok(first));
        for descriptor in [4, 5, 6, 7] {
            assert_eq!(processes.duplicate_descriptor(process, 1), Ok(descriptor));
        }
        assert_eq!(
            processes.duplicate_descriptor(process, 1),
            Err(ProcessTableError::DescriptorTableFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.close_descriptor(process, u64::MAX),
            Err(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn exiting_process_closes_all_descriptors_and_children_keep_their_copies() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let parent = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(parent).unwrap();
        processes.duplicate_descriptor(parent, 1).unwrap();

        processes.exit(parent, 0).unwrap();
        for descriptor in 0..MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS as u64 {
            assert_eq!(processes.descriptor_stream(parent, descriptor), None);
        }
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(child, 1),
            Some(crate::syscall::ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn anonymous_regions_round_up_skip_reserved_ranges_and_reuse_after_release() {
        let mut regions = UserRegionTable::new();
        regions
            .reserve(
                USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START,
                crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                UserRegionKind::Guard,
                48,
            )
            .unwrap();

        let anonymous = regions.allocate_anonymous(1, 48).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            anonymous.start(),
            USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START + crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE
        );
        assert_eq!(anonymous.length(), crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(anonymous.kind(), UserRegionKind::Anonymous);
        assert_eq!(
            regions.release_anonymous(anonymous.start(), anonymous.length()),
            Ok(anonymous)
        );

        let reused = regions
            .allocate_anonymous(crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE, 48)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused.start(), anonymous.start());
    }

    #[test]
    fn anonymous_regions_cannot_overlap_reserved_or_release_nonanonymous_ranges() {
        let mut regions = UserRegionTable::new();
        let stack = regions
            .reserve(
                0x7000_0000,
                crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                UserRegionKind::Stack,
                48,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            regions.reserve(stack.start(), stack.length(), UserRegionKind::Anonymous, 48),
            Err(UserRegionError::Overlap)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            regions.release_anonymous(stack.start(), stack.length()),
            Err(UserRegionError::NotAnonymousRegion)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_regions_reject_invalid_width_alignment_overflow_and_upper_half() {
        let mut regions = UserRegionTable::new();
        assert_eq!(
            regions.reserve(0x1000, crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE, UserRegionKind::Image, 47),
            Err(UserRegionError::InvalidAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            regions.reserve(0x1001, crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE, UserRegionKind::Image, 48),
            Err(UserRegionError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            regions.reserve(
                u64::MAX - (crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                UserRegionKind::Image,
                48
            ),
            Err(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            regions.reserve(
                0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                UserRegionKind::Image,
                48
            ),
            Err(UserRegionError::NonCanonicalRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            regions.allocate_anonymous(0, 48),
            Err(UserRegionError::EmptyRange)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn anonymous_region_capacity_and_window_exhaustion_are_explicit() {
        let mut regions = UserRegionTable::new();
        for slot in 0..super::MAX_USER_REGIONS {
            regions
                .reserve(
                    0x1000_0000 + slot as u64 * crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                    crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                    UserRegionKind::Image,
                    48,
                )
                .unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(
            regions.allocate_anonymous(crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE, 48),
            Err(UserRegionError::Capacity)
        );

        let mut full_window = UserRegionTable::new();
        full_window
            .reserve(
                USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START,
                super::USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_END - USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START,
                UserRegionKind::Guard,
                48,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            full_window.allocate_anonymous(crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE, 48),
            Err(UserRegionError::AnonymousAddressSpaceExhausted)
        );
    }
}

macro_rules! kprintln {
    () => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
    ($($argument:tt)*) => {{
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!($($argument)*));
        crate::arch::x86_64::serial::print(format_args!("\r\n"));
    }};
}

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {
        // SAFETY: Active mapping callers provide the current virtual page and run
        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
enum LimineUserFrameMemoryError {
    OutOfBounds,
    Address(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError),
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
struct LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'a> {
