//! Fixed-capacity process identity and parent/child exit-state policy.
//!
//! This module does not own address spaces or block in the scheduler. Callers
//! must pair each process ID with its root and retry `try_wait` after a child
//! state change; a `Running` result means a syscall caller still has to block.

pub const MAX_PROCESSES: usize = 4;
pub const MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS: usize = 8;

/// ID zero belongs to the kernel supervisor and is never assigned to userspace.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, Ord, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
pub struct ProcessId(u64);

impl ProcessId {
    pub const fn get(self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
}

pub const KERNEL_PROCESS_ID: ProcessId = ProcessId(0);

pub const MAX_USER_REGIONS: usize = 32;
pub const USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START: u64 = 0x0000_4000_0000_0000;
pub const USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_END: u64 = 0x0000_4000_0100_0000;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserRegionKind {
    Image,
    Stack,
    Guard,
    Anonymous,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct UserRegion {
    start: u64,
    end: u64,
    kind: UserRegionKind,
}

impl UserRegion {
    pub const fn start(self) -> u64 {
        self.start
    }

    pub const fn end(self) -> u64 {
        self.end
    }

    pub const fn length(self) -> u64 {
        self.end - self.start
    }

    pub const fn kind(self) -> UserRegionKind {
        self.kind
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub struct UserStackLayout {
    stack_region: UserRegion,
    guard_region: UserRegion,
    stack_pointer: u64,
}

impl UserStackLayout {
    pub const fn stack_region(self) -> UserRegion {
        self.stack_region
    }

    pub const fn guard_region(self) -> UserRegion {
        self.guard_region
    }

    pub const fn stack_pointer(self) -> u64 {
        self.stack_pointer
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserRegionError {
    InvalidAddressWidth,
    EmptyRange,
    UnalignedRange,
    AddressOverflow,
    NonCanonicalRange,
    Overlap,
    Capacity,
    AnonymousAddressSpaceExhausted,
    NotAnonymousRegion,
}

/// Bounded user virtual-region reservations for one address space.
///
/// Region reservations are metadata only: page ownership and page-table changes
/// remain the responsibility of the process-root mapping APIs. Guard regions are
/// reserved here but intentionally have no backing mapping.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct UserRegionTable {
    regions: [Option<UserRegion>; MAX_USER_REGIONS],
}

impl UserRegionTable {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            regions: [None; MAX_USER_REGIONS],
        }
    }

    /// Reserve a page-aligned lower-half range, including an unmapped guard range.
    pub fn reserve(
        &mut self,
        start: u64,
        length: u64,
        kind: UserRegionKind,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<UserRegion, UserRegionError> {
        validate_user_region_range(start, length, virtual_address_bits)?;
        let end = start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if self
            .regions
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .any(|region| start < region.end && region.start < end)
        {
            return Err(UserRegionError::Overlap);
        }
        let slot = self
            .regions
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::Capacity)?;
        let region = UserRegion { start, end, kind };
        self.regions[slot] = Some(region);
        Ok(region)
    }

    /// Transactionally reserve validated ELF load pages, a stack, and its guard.
    ///
    /// `stack_base` is the low address of the mapped stack. The initial stack
    /// pointer is the one-past end address. No page tables or backing frames are
    /// changed; the caller remains responsible for loading the image and mapping
    /// the stack. At least one stack and one guard page are required.
    pub fn reserve_elf_layout(
        &mut self,
        image: &crate::elf::Elf64Image<'_>,
        stack_base: u64,
        stack_pages: u64,
        guard_pages: u64,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<UserStackLayout, UserRegionError> {
        if stack_pages == 0 || guard_pages == 0 {
            return Err(UserRegionError::EmptyRange);
        }
        let page_size = crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
        let stack_length = stack_pages
            .checked_mul(page_size)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let guard_length = guard_pages
            .checked_mul(page_size)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let guard_base = stack_base
            .checked_sub(guard_length)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let stack_pointer = stack_base
            .checked_add(stack_length)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;

        let mut staged = *self;
        for segment in image.segments() {
            let page_count = u64::try_from(segment.page_count())
                .map_err(|_| UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
            let length = page_count
                .checked_mul(page_size)
                .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
            staged.reserve(
                segment.virtual_start(),
                length,
                UserRegionKind::Image,
                virtual_address_bits,
            )?;
        }
        let guard_region = staged.reserve(
            guard_base,
            guard_length,
            UserRegionKind::Guard,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let stack_region = staged.reserve(
            stack_base,
            stack_length,
            UserRegionKind::Stack,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        *self = staged;
        Ok(UserStackLayout {
            stack_region,
            guard_region,
            stack_pointer,
        })
    }

    /// Reserve the first free range in the bounded anonymous-map window.
    ///
    /// The requested byte length is rounded up to a page. Allocations are
    /// read/write, non-executable by policy; this table does not install PTEs.
    pub fn allocate_anonymous(
        &mut self,
        requested_length: u64,
        virtual_address_bits: u8,
    ) -> Result<UserRegion, UserRegionError> {
        if requested_length == 0 {
            return Err(UserRegionError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
            return Err(UserRegionError::InvalidAddressWidth);
        }
        if self.regions.iter().all(Option::is_some) {
            return Err(UserRegionError::Capacity);
        }
        let page_size = crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
        let length = requested_length
            .checked_add(page_size - 1)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?
            & !(page_size - 1);
        let mut candidate = USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START;
        loop {
            let end = candidate
                .checked_add(length)
                .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
            if end > USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_END {
                return Err(UserRegionError::AnonymousAddressSpaceExhausted);
            }
            let overlap = self
                .regions
                .iter()
                .flatten()
                .filter(|region| candidate < region.end && region.start < end)
                .min_by_key(|region| region.end);
            if let Some(region) = overlap {
                candidate = region.end;
                continue;
            }
            return self.reserve(
                candidate,
                length,
                UserRegionKind::Anonymous,
                virtual_address_bits,
            );
        }
    }

    /// Release only an exact anonymous reservation; image, stack, and guard
    /// regions cannot be released through this operation.
    pub fn release_anonymous(
        &mut self,
        start: u64,
        length: u64,
    ) -> Result<UserRegion, UserRegionError> {
        if length == 0 {
            return Err(UserRegionError::EmptyRange);
        }
        if (start | length) & (crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0 {
            return Err(UserRegionError::UnalignedRange);
        }
        let end = start
            .checked_add(length)
            .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
        let slot = self.regions.iter().position(|region| {
            region.is_some_and(|region| {
                region.start == start
                    && region.end == end
                    && region.kind == UserRegionKind::Anonymous
            })
        });
        let Some(slot) = slot else {
            return Err(UserRegionError::NotAnonymousRegion);
        };
        Ok(self.regions[slot]
            .take()
            .expect("matching anonymous reservation remains present"))
    }

    pub fn regions(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = UserRegion> + '_ {
        self.regions.iter().flatten().copied()
    }
}

impl Default for UserRegionTable {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

/// Maximum number of pages accepted for a process's initial user stack.
pub const MAX_INITIAL_USER_STACK_PAGES: u64 = 16;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserProgramPrepareErrorKind {
    InvalidElf,
    RootCreation,
    RegionReservation,
    ElfLoad,
    StackGuard,
    StackAllocation,
    StackInitialization,
    StackMapping,
    InvalidInitialState,
    InvalidIretFrame,
    CachePolicy(&'static str),
}

impl UserProgramPrepareErrorKind {
    pub const fn message(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::InvalidElf => "ELF image validation failed",
            Self::RootCreation => "process root creation failed",
            Self::RegionReservation => "ELF, stack, or guard reservation failed",
            Self::ElfLoad => "ELF image could not be loaded",
            Self::StackGuard => "stack guard is not unmapped",
            Self::StackAllocation => "no frame available for the user stack",
            Self::StackInitialization => "user stack frame could not be zeroed",
            Self::StackMapping => "user stack page could not be mapped",
            Self::InvalidInitialState => "ELF entry or user stack failed validation",
            Self::InvalidIretFrame => "initial user IRET frame was rejected",
            Self::CachePolicy(message) => message,
        }
    }
}

/// Resources that a caller must retry cleaning up when preparation fails.
/// `process` remains owned by `roots`; `frame` is an allocated frame that was
/// not installed in that process root.
#[must_use = "retry cleanup for any process root or frame retained by this error"]
pub struct UserProgramPrepareError {
    pub kind: UserProgramPrepareErrorKind,
    pub process: Option<crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle>,
    pub frame: Option<crate::frame::Frame>,
}

impl UserProgramPrepareError {
    /// Retry reclaiming every resource retained by this failure.
    pub fn cleanup<M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory>(
        mut self,
        roots: &mut crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
        allocator: &mut crate::frame::FrameAllocator,
    ) -> Result<(), Self> {
        if let Some(process) = self.process.take() {
            if roots.destroy(allocator, process).is_err() {
                self.process = Some(process);
                return Err(self);
            }
        }
        if let Some(frame) = self.frame.take() {
            if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
                self.frame = Some(error.frame);
                return Err(self);
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl core::fmt::Debug for UserProgramPrepareError {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
        formatter
            .debug_struct("UserProgramPrepareError")
            .field("kind", &self.kind)
            .field("process_retained", &self.process.is_some())
            .field("frame_retained", &self.frame.is_some())
            .finish()
    }
}

/// A loaded ELF image and its validated initial Ring 3 entry state.
pub struct PreparedUserProgram {
    pub process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    pub regions: UserRegionTable,
    pub user_frame: crate::syscall::ValidatedUserIretFrame,
}

fn cleanup_failed_user_program<M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory>(
    roots: &mut crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    allocator: &mut crate::frame::FrameAllocator,
    process: crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceHandle,
    kind: UserProgramPrepareErrorKind,
    frame: Option<crate::frame::Frame>,
) -> UserProgramPrepareError {
    let retained_process = roots.destroy(allocator, process).err().map(|_| process);
    let retained_frame = frame.and_then(|frame| match allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        Ok(()) => None,
        Err(error) => Some(error.frame),
    });
    UserProgramPrepareError {
        kind,
        process: retained_process,
        frame: retained_frame,
    }
}

/// Load a static ELF image into a fresh process root and prepare its guarded,
/// zero-filled initial user stack. All limits are explicit and failures return
/// any root or frame whose ownership could not be reclaimed.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
pub fn prepare_user_program<M, U, F>(
    roots: &mut crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
    allocator: &mut crate::frame::FrameAllocator,
    user_memory: &mut U,
    image_bytes: &[u8],
    stack_base: u64,
    stack_pages: u64,
    guard_pages: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    user_code_selector: u16,
    user_data_selector: u16,
    select_cache: &mut F,
) -> Result<PreparedUserProgram, UserProgramPrepareError>
where
    M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory,
    U: crate::paging::UserFrameMemory,
    F: FnMut(
        crate::paging::ValidatedMappingRange,
    ) -> Result<crate::paging::SelectedCacheAttributes, &'static str>,
{
    use crate::paging::{validate_mapping_range, PagePermissions, PAGE_SIZE};

    let image = crate::elf::Elf64Image::parse(image_bytes, virtual_address_bits).map_err(|_| {
        UserProgramPrepareError {
            kind: UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::InvalidElf,
            process: None,
            frame: None,
        }
    })?;
    if stack_pages == 0 || stack_pages > MAX_INITIAL_USER_STACK_PAGES || guard_pages == 0 {
        return Err(UserProgramPrepareError {
            kind: UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::RegionReservation,
            process: None,
            frame: None,
        });
    }
    let process = match roots.create(allocator) {
        Ok(process) => process,
        Err(failure) => {
            let frame = failure.frame;
            let frame = frame.and_then(|frame| match allocator.deallocate(frame) {
                Ok(()) => None,
                Err(error) => Some(error.frame),
            });
            return Err(UserProgramPrepareError {
                kind: UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::RootCreation,
                process: None,
                frame,
            });
        }
    };
    let mut regions = UserRegionTable::new();
    let stack_layout = match regions.reserve_elf_layout(
        &image,
        stack_base,
        stack_pages,
        guard_pages,
        virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(layout) => layout,
        Err(_) => {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::RegionReservation,
                None,
            ));
        }
    };
    if let Err(failure) =
        image.load_into_process_root(roots, allocator, process, user_memory, &mut *select_cache)
    {
        return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
            roots,
            allocator,
            process,
            UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::ElfLoad,
            failure.frame,
        ));
    }

    let mut guard_probe = [0u8; 1];
    // SAFETY: The scratch byte is kernel stack storage, disjoint from user frames.
    // The reserved guard range must have no mapped user backing.
    match unsafe {
        roots.copy_from_user(
            process,
            stack_layout.guard_region().start(),
            &mut guard_probe,
            user_memory,
        )
    } {
        Err(failure) if matches!(failure.cause, crate::paging::ProcessUserCopyError::Unmapped) => {}
        _ => {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackGuard,
                None,
            ));
        }
    }

    for offset in (0..stack_layout.stack_region().length()).step_by(PAGE_SIZE as usize) {
        let frame = match allocator.allocate() {
            Some(frame) => frame,
            None => {
                return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                    roots,
                    allocator,
                    process,
                    UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackAllocation,
                    None,
                ));
            }
        };
        if crate::paging::zero_user_frame(&frame, user_memory).is_err() {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackInitialization,
                Some(frame),
            ));
        }
        let Some(virtual_address) = stack_layout.stack_region().start().checked_add(offset) else {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackMapping,
                Some(frame),
            ));
        };
        let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
            virtual_address,
            frame.address(),
            PAGE_SIZE,
            PagePermissions {
                writable: true,
                executable: false,
                user_accessible: true,
            },
            Some(physical_address_bits),
            virtual_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(mapping) => mapping,
            Err(_) => {
                return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                    roots,
                    allocator,
                    process,
                    UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackMapping,
                    Some(frame),
                ));
            }
        };
        let cache_attributes = match select_cache(mapping) {
            Ok(attributes) => attributes,
            Err(message) => {
                return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                    roots,
                    allocator,
                    process,
                    UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::CachePolicy(message),
                    Some(frame),
                ));
            }
        };
        if let Err(failure) =
            roots.map_user_page(allocator, process, frame, mapping, cache_attributes)
        {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::StackMapping,
                Some(failure.frame),
            ));
        }
    }

    if roots
        .validate_initial_user_state(process, image.entry_point(), stack_layout.stack_pointer())
        .is_err()
    {
        return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
            roots,
            allocator,
            process,
            UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::InvalidInitialState,
            None,
        ));
    }
    let raw_frame = crate::syscall::UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: image.entry_point(),
        code_selector: u64::from(user_code_selector),
        flags: crate::syscall::SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer: stack_layout.stack_pointer(),
        stack_selector: u64::from(user_data_selector),
    };
    let user_frame = match crate::syscall::sanitize_user_iret_frame(raw_frame, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(_) => {
            return Err(cleanup_failed_user_program(
                roots,
                allocator,
                process,
                UserProgramPrepareErrorKind::InvalidIretFrame,
                None,
            ));
        }
    };

    Ok(PreparedUserProgram {
        process,
        regions,
        user_frame,
    })
}

fn validate_user_region_range(
    start: u64,
    length: u64,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), UserRegionError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(UserRegionError::InvalidAddressWidth);
    }
    if length == 0 {
        return Err(UserRegionError::EmptyRange);
    }
    let page_size = crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    if (start | length) & (page_size - 1) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRegionError::UnalignedRange);
    }
    let end = start
        .checked_add(length)
        .ok_or(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)?;
    let lower_half_end = 1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1);
    if start >= lower_half_end
        || end > lower_half_end
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(start, virtual_address_bits)
        || !crate::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(end - 1, virtual_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(UserRegionError::NonCanonicalRange);
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ProcessState {
    Running,
    Exited(i32),
}

/// A nonblocking observation of a child. `try_wait` reaps an exited child; `peek_wait` does not.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum WaitResult {
    Running { pid: ProcessId },
    Exited { pid: ProcessId, status: i32 },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum ProcessTableError {
    Capacity,
    InitialProcessAlreadyExists,
    InvalidProcess,
    InvalidParent,
    ParentExited,
    AlreadyExited,
    NoChild,
    ChildStillRunning,
    BadFileDescriptor,
    DescriptorTableFull,
    ProcessIdExhausted,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
struct ProcessRecord {
    pid: ProcessId,
    parent: ProcessId,
    state: ProcessState,
    descriptors: [Option<crate::syscall::ConsoleStream>; MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS],
}

fn initial_console_descriptors() -> [Option<crate::syscall::ConsoleStream>; MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS]
{
    let mut descriptors = [None; MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS];
    descriptors[1] = Some(crate::syscall::ConsoleStream::Stdout);
    descriptors[2] = Some(crate::syscall::ConsoleStream::Stderr);
    descriptors
}

/// Bounded, allocation-free process lifecycle records for the first user slice.
///
/// Exited records remain waitable zombies until their parent calls `try_wait`.
/// If a parent exits first, its children are reparented to the kernel supervisor
/// so their exit records remain reapable. This table models only inherited console
/// stream descriptors; file objects and address-space ownership live elsewhere.
pub struct ProcessTable {
    records: [Option<ProcessRecord>; MAX_PROCESSES],
    next_pid: Option<u64>,
}

impl ProcessTable {
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            records: [None; MAX_PROCESSES],
            next_pid: Some(1),
        }
    }

    /// Register the one boot-created process under the kernel supervisor.
    pub fn create_initial(&mut self) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        if self
            .records
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .any(|record| record.parent == KERNEL_PROCESS_ID)
        {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::InitialProcessAlreadyExists);
        }
        self.insert(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, initial_console_descriptors())
    }

    /// Register a child of a currently running process.
    pub fn spawn(&mut self, parent: ProcessId) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        let parent_record = self
            .record(parent)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)?;
        if parent_record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited);
        }
        self.insert(parent, parent_record.descriptors)
    }

    /// Record an exit status without reclaiming the process identity.
    pub fn exit(&mut self, pid: ProcessId, status: i32) -> Result<(), ProcessTableError> {
        let index = self
            .records
            .iter()
            .position(|record| record.is_some_and(|record| record.pid == pid))
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidProcess)?;
        let record = self.records[index]
            .as_mut()
            .expect("process slot was found");
        if record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::AlreadyExited);
        }
        record.state = ProcessState::Exited(status);
        record.descriptors = [None; MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS];
        for child in self.records.iter_mut().flatten() {
            if child.parent == pid {
                child.parent = KERNEL_PROCESS_ID;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Inspect a matching child without consuming an exited record.
    ///
    /// `child_pid == 0` selects any child, preferring the lowest-PID exited child.
    /// This split lets callers validate/copy exit status before reaping a zombie.
    pub fn peek_wait(
        &self,
        parent: ProcessId,
        child_pid: u64,
    ) -> Result<WaitResult, ProcessTableError> {
        if parent != KERNEL_PROCESS_ID {
            let parent_record = self
                .record(parent)
                .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)?;
            if parent_record.state != ProcessState::Running {
                return Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited);
            }
        }

        let mut found_child = false;
        let mut running: Option<ProcessId> = None;
        let mut exited: Option<(ProcessId, i32)> = None;
        for record in self.records.iter().flatten().filter(|record| {
            record.parent == parent && (child_pid == 0 || record.pid.get() == child_pid)
        }) {
            found_child = true;
            match record.state {
                ProcessState::Running => {
                    if running.is_none_or(|pid| record.pid < pid) {
                        running = Some(record.pid);
                    }
                }
                ProcessState::Exited(status) => {
                    if exited.is_none_or(|(pid, _)| record.pid < pid) {
                        exited = Some((record.pid, status));
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        if let Some((pid, status)) = exited {
            return Ok(WaitResult::Exited { pid, status });
        }
        if let Some(pid) = running {
            return Ok(WaitResult::Running { pid });
        }
        if found_child {
            unreachable!("a matching child must be running or exited");
        }
        Err(ProcessTableError::NoChild)
    }

    /// Reap one specific exited child after its status has been consumed.
    pub fn reap_exited(
        &mut self,
        parent: ProcessId,
        child_pid: ProcessId,
    ) -> Result<WaitResult, ProcessTableError> {
        let result = self.peek_wait(parent, child_pid.get())?;
        let WaitResult::Exited { pid, status } = result else {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::ChildStillRunning);
        };
        let index = self
            .records
            .iter()
            .position(|record| {
                record.is_some_and(|record| record.pid == pid && record.parent == parent)
            })
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::NoChild)?;
        self.records[index] = None;
        Ok(WaitResult::Exited { pid, status })
    }

    /// Inspect or reap a matching child without blocking.
    ///
    /// `child_pid == 0` selects any child, preferring the lowest-PID exited child.
    pub fn try_wait(
        &mut self,
        parent: ProcessId,
        child_pid: u64,
    ) -> Result<WaitResult, ProcessTableError> {
        let result = self.peek_wait(parent, child_pid)?;
        if let WaitResult::Exited { pid, .. } = result {
            let _ = self.reap_exited(parent, pid)?;
        }
        Ok(result)
    }

    pub fn state(&self, pid: ProcessId) -> Option<ProcessState> {
        self.record(pid).map(|record| record.state)
    }

    pub fn live_records(&self) -> usize {
        self.records.iter().flatten().count()
    }

    /// Resolve one live descriptor to its bounded console-stream target.
    pub fn descriptor_stream(
        &self,
        pid: ProcessId,
        descriptor: u64,
    ) -> Option<crate::syscall::ConsoleStream> {
        let descriptor = usize::try_from(descriptor).ok()?;
        self.record(pid)?
            .descriptors
            .get(descriptor)
            .copied()
            .flatten()
    }

    /// Close one descriptor without affecting duplicated descriptors to the same stream.
    pub fn close_descriptor(
        &mut self,
        pid: ProcessId,
        descriptor: u64,
    ) -> Result<(), ProcessTableError> {
        let descriptor =
            usize::try_from(descriptor).map_err(|_| ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)?;
        let record = self
            .records
            .iter_mut()
            .flatten()
            .find(|record| record.pid == pid)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidProcess)?;
        if record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::AlreadyExited);
        }
        let entry = record
            .descriptors
            .get_mut(descriptor)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)?;
        entry.take().ok_or(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Duplicate a descriptor into the lowest free slot at or above descriptor 3.
    pub fn duplicate_descriptor(
        &mut self,
        pid: ProcessId,
        descriptor: u64,
    ) -> Result<u64, ProcessTableError> {
        let source = self
            .descriptor_stream(pid, descriptor)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)?;
        let record = self
            .records
            .iter_mut()
            .flatten()
            .find(|record| record.pid == pid)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidProcess)?;
        if record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::AlreadyExited);
        }
        let slot = record
            .descriptors
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .skip(3)
            .find_map(|(index, descriptor)| descriptor.is_none().then_some(index))
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::DescriptorTableFull)?;
        record.descriptors[slot] = Some(source);
        Ok(slot as u64)
    }

    fn insert(
        &mut self,
        parent: ProcessId,
        descriptors: [Option<crate::syscall::ConsoleStream>; MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS],
    ) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        let slot = self
            .records
            .iter()
            .position(Option::is_none)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::Capacity)?;
        let pid = self.next_pid.ok_or(ProcessTableError::ProcessIdExhausted)?;
        self.next_pid = pid.checked_add(1);
        let pid = ProcessId(pid);
        self.records[slot] = Some(ProcessRecord {
            pid,
            parent,
            state: ProcessState::Running,
            descriptors,
        });
        Ok(pid)
    }

    fn record(&self, pid: ProcessId) -> Option<&ProcessRecord> {
        self.records
            .iter()
            .flatten()
            .find(|record| record.pid == pid)
    }
}

impl Default for ProcessTable {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        ProcessState, ProcessTable, ProcessTableError, UserRegionError, UserRegionKind,
        UserRegionTable, WaitResult, KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, MAX_PROCESSES, MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS,
        USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START,
    };

    #[test]
    fn child_exit_status_is_retained_until_exact_wait_reaps_it() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, child.get()),
            Ok(WaitResult::Running { pid: child })
        );
        processes.exit(child, -17).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), Some(ProcessState::Exited(-17)));
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, child.get()),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: child,
                status: -17,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), None);
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, child.get()),
            Err(ProcessTableError::NoChild)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn peek_wait_keeps_a_zombie_until_status_consumption_succeeds() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let parent = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(parent).unwrap();
        processes.exit(child, 41).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.peek_wait(parent, child.get()),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: child,
                status: 41,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), Some(ProcessState::Exited(41)));
        assert_eq!(
            processes.reap_exited(parent, child),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: child,
                status: 41,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), None);
        assert_eq!(
            processes.reap_exited(parent, child),
            Err(ProcessTableError::NoChild)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn reaping_a_running_child_is_rejected_without_mutation() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let parent = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(parent).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.reap_exited(parent, child),
            Err(ProcessTableError::ChildStillRunning)
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.state(child), Some(ProcessState::Running));
    }

    #[test]
    fn wait_any_prefers_the_lowest_pid_zombie_and_keeps_running_children() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let first = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();
        let second = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();
        processes.exit(second, 23).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, 0),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: second,
                status: 23,
            })
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(init, 0),
            Ok(WaitResult::Running { pid: first })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn exiting_parent_reparents_children_to_kernel_supervisor() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(init).unwrap();
        processes.exit(init, 0).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, 0),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: init,
                status: 0,
            })
        );
        processes.exit(child, 7).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.try_wait(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, child.get()),
            Ok(WaitResult::Exited {
                pid: child,
                status: 7,
            })
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn capacity_and_invalid_lifecycle_operations_are_explicit() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.spawn(KERNEL_PROCESS_ID),
            Err(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)
        );
        let init = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.create_initial(),
            Err(ProcessTableError::InitialProcessAlreadyExists)
        );
        let children: [Option<super::ProcessId>; MAX_PROCESSES - 1] =
            core::array::from_fn(|_| None);
        let mut children = children;
        for child in &mut children {
            *child = Some(processes.spawn(init).unwrap());
        }
        assert_eq!(processes.live_records(), MAX_PROCESSES);
        assert_eq!(processes.spawn(init), Err(ProcessTableError::Capacity));

        let child = children[0].unwrap();
        processes.exit(child, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.exit(child, 2),
            Err(ProcessTableError::AlreadyExited)
        );
        assert_eq!(processes.spawn(child), Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited));
    }

    #[test]
    fn descriptors_start_with_console_streams_and_are_inherited_by_children() {
        use crate::syscall::ConsoleStream;

        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let parent = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(processes.descriptor_stream(parent, 0), None);
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(parent, 1),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(parent, 2),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stderr)
        );

        let duplicate = processes.duplicate_descriptor(parent, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(duplicate, 3);
        let child = processes.spawn(parent).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(child, 1),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(child, 3),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );

        processes.close_descriptor(parent, 1).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(processes.descriptor_stream(parent, 1), None);
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(parent, 3),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(child, 1),
            Some(ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn descriptor_operations_reject_invalid_entries_reuse_slots_and_report_capacity() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let process = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(processes.descriptor_stream(process, u64::MAX), None);
        assert_eq!(
            processes.close_descriptor(process, 0),
            Err(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.duplicate_descriptor(process, 0),
            Err(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)
        );

        let first = processes.duplicate_descriptor(process, 1).unwrap();
        processes.close_descriptor(process, first).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(processes.descriptor_stream(process, first), None);
        assert_eq!(processes.duplicate_descriptor(process, 2), Ok(first));
        for descriptor in [4, 5, 6, 7] {
            assert_eq!(processes.duplicate_descriptor(process, 1), Ok(descriptor));
        }
        assert_eq!(
            processes.duplicate_descriptor(process, 1),
            Err(ProcessTableError::DescriptorTableFull)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            processes.close_descriptor(process, u64::MAX),
            Err(ProcessTableError::BadFileDescriptor)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn exiting_process_closes_all_descriptors_and_children_keep_their_copies() {
        let mut processes = ProcessTable::new();
        let parent = processes.create_initial().unwrap();
        let child = processes.spawn(parent).unwrap();
        processes.duplicate_descriptor(parent, 1).unwrap();

        processes.exit(parent, 0).unwrap();
        for descriptor in 0..MAX_PROCESS_DESCRIPTORS as u64 {
            assert_eq!(processes.descriptor_stream(parent, descriptor), None);
        }
        assert_eq!(
            processes.descriptor_stream(child, 1),
            Some(crate::syscall::ConsoleStream::Stdout)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn anonymous_regions_round_up_skip_reserved_ranges_and_reuse_after_release() {
        let mut regions = UserRegionTable::new();
        regions
            .reserve(
                USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START,
                crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                UserRegionKind::Guard,
                48,
            )
            .unwrap();

        let anonymous = regions.allocate_anonymous(1, 48).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            anonymous.start(),
            USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START + crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE
        );
        assert_eq!(anonymous.length(), crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE);
        assert_eq!(anonymous.kind(), UserRegionKind::Anonymous);
        assert_eq!(
            regions.release_anonymous(anonymous.start(), anonymous.length()),
            Ok(anonymous)
        );

        let reused = regions
            .allocate_anonymous(crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE, 48)
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(reused.start(), anonymous.start());
    }

    #[test]
    fn anonymous_regions_cannot_overlap_reserved_or_release_nonanonymous_ranges() {
        let mut regions = UserRegionTable::new();
        let stack = regions
            .reserve(
                0x7000_0000,
                crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                UserRegionKind::Stack,
                48,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            regions.reserve(stack.start(), stack.length(), UserRegionKind::Anonymous, 48),
            Err(UserRegionError::Overlap)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            regions.release_anonymous(stack.start(), stack.length()),
            Err(UserRegionError::NotAnonymousRegion)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_regions_reject_invalid_width_alignment_overflow_and_upper_half() {
        let mut regions = UserRegionTable::new();
        assert_eq!(
            regions.reserve(0x1000, crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE, UserRegionKind::Image, 47),
            Err(UserRegionError::InvalidAddressWidth)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            regions.reserve(0x1001, crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE, UserRegionKind::Image, 48),
            Err(UserRegionError::UnalignedRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            regions.reserve(
                u64::MAX - (crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE - 1),
                crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                UserRegionKind::Image,
                48
            ),
            Err(UserRegionError::AddressOverflow)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            regions.reserve(
                0x0000_8000_0000_0000,
                crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                UserRegionKind::Image,
                48
            ),
            Err(UserRegionError::NonCanonicalRange)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            regions.allocate_anonymous(0, 48),
            Err(UserRegionError::EmptyRange)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn anonymous_region_capacity_and_window_exhaustion_are_explicit() {
        let mut regions = UserRegionTable::new();
        for slot in 0..super::MAX_USER_REGIONS {
            regions
                .reserve(
                    0x1000_0000 + slot as u64 * crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                    crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
                    UserRegionKind::Image,
                    48,
                )
                .unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(
            regions.allocate_anonymous(crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE, 48),
            Err(UserRegionError::Capacity)
        );

        let mut full_window = UserRegionTable::new();
        full_window
            .reserve(
                USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START,
                super::USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_END - USER_ANONYMOUS_MAP_START,
                UserRegionKind::Guard,
                48,
            )
            .unwrap();
        assert_eq!(
            full_window.allocate_anonymous(crate::paging::PAGE_SIZE, 48),
            Err(UserRegionError::AnonymousAddressSpaceExhausted)
        );
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader for LimineHhdmPageTableReader<'_> {
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let table_end = table_physical
            .checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        if !self.memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
            table_physical,
            table_end,
            rustix_kernel::memory::RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
        ) {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::NotLimineMapped);
        }
        let table_address = self.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            self.hhdm_offset,
            table_physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )?;
        let entry_address = table_address
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The complete table page was restricted to bootloader-reclaimable
        // memory and its HHDM address arithmetic was checked. The reader relies
        // on the Limine base-revision-3 mapping contract and never returns a ref.
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }
}

struct LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

// SAFETY: `prepare_table` accepts only an allocator-issued frame and validates
// its complete usable span and HHDM address. Handles are only used while the
// candidate retains the frame token and this unique backend borrow.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory for LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_> {
    type PreparedTable = u64;
    type Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError;

    fn prepare_table(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
    ) -> Result<Self::PreparedTable, Self::Error> {
        frame.hhdm_address(
            self.memory_map,
            self.hhdm_offset,
            Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            self.virtual_address_bits,
        )
    }

    unsafe fn read_entry(
        &self,
        table: Self::PreparedTable,
        index: u16,
    ) -> Result<u64, Self::Error> {
        if index >= 512 {
            return Err(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::InvalidHhdmRange);
        }
        let entry_address = table
            .checked_add(u64::from(index) * core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64)
            .ok_or(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow)?;
        // SAFETY: The unsafe trait contract requires `table` to be the prepared
        // HHDM address of a complete writable frame; the index is in [0, 512).
        Ok(unsafe { (entry_address as *const u64).read_volatile() })
    }

    unsafe fn clear_table(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable) {
        let entries = table as *mut u64;
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a handle prepared by this backend for a
        // complete writable frame retained by its candidate.
        unsafe {
            for index in 0..512 {
                entries.add(index).write_volatile(0);
            }
        }
    }

    unsafe fn write_entry(&mut self, table: Self::PreparedTable, index: u16, value: u64) {
        if index >= 512 {
            return;
        }
        let entry = (table as *mut u64).wrapping_add(usize::from(index));
        // SAFETY: The caller provides a prepared complete frame and an index in
        // range; this writes one entry without creating a Rust reference.
        unsafe { entry.write_volatile(value) };
    }

    unsafe fn invalidate_page(&mut self, virtual_address: u64) {
        // SAFETY: Active mapping callers provide the current virtual page and run
        // at CPL 0 with exclusive local page-table ownership.
        unsafe {
            core::arch::asm!(
                "invlpg [{}]",
                in(reg) virtual_address,
                options(nostack, preserves_flags)
            );
        }
    }
}

enum LimineUserFrameMemoryError {
    OutOfBounds,
    Address(rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError),
}

struct LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'a> {
    memory_map: &'a rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
impl LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    fn frame_slice_address(
        &self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        length: usize,
    ) -> Result<*mut u8, LimineUserFrameMemoryError> {
        if offset
            .checked_add(length)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE as usize)
        {
            return Err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::OutOfBounds);
        }
        if length == 0 {
            return Ok(core::ptr::null_mut());
        }

        let base = frame
            .hhdm_address(
                self.memory_map,
                self.hhdm_offset,
                self.physical_address_bits,
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address)?;
        let address =
            base.checked_add(offset as u64)
                .ok_or(LimineUserFrameMemoryError::Address(
                    rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow,
                ))?;
        Ok(address as *mut u8)
    }
}

#[cfg(any(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame", feature = "probe-user-process"))]
// SAFETY: The non-copyable Frame token and checked HHDM conversion authorize a
// complete Usable page. Each operation checks its subrange, accesses only that
// page, and uses raw copies rather than forming user virtual references. The
// implementation relies on Limine's mapped-usable-memory contract; hardware
// faults from a broken mapping remain fatal and are not recoverable here.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory for LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory<'_> {
    type Error = LimineUserFrameMemoryError;

    fn copy_from_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        destination: &mut [u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let source = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, destination.len())?;
        if !destination.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source, destination.as_mut_ptr(), destination.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn copy_to_frame(
        &mut self,
        frame: &rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
        offset: usize,
        source: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        let destination = self.frame_slice_address(frame, offset, source.len())?;
        if !source.is_empty() {
            // SAFETY: The frame subrange was checked and the HHDM address was
            // validated for the full allocator-owned frame. `copy` permits overlap.
            unsafe { core::ptr::copy(source.as_ptr(), destination, source.len()) };
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

struct KernelHeapMappingContext {
    candidate: *mut (),
    allocator: *mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    cpu_info: *const arch::x86_64::cpu::CpuInfo,
}

unsafe fn map_kernel_heap_pages(
    opaque_context: *mut (),
    first_page: usize,
    page_count: usize,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, EffectiveMemoryType, MtrrState,
        PagePermissions, PatLayout, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    if page_count == 0
        || first_page
            .checked_add(page_count)
            .is_none_or(|end| end > KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_MAX_PAGES)
    {
        return false;
    }

    // SAFETY: The caller configures this callback only after the active root,
    // allocator, CPU snapshot, and local context are all live. The boot path is
    // single-vCPU and never returns from the stack containing that context.
    let state = unsafe { &mut *opaque_context.cast::<KernelHeapMappingContext>() };
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the retained local candidate and BootInfo
    // members. The callback is synchronous and never stores a derived reference.
    let candidate = unsafe {
        &mut *state
            .candidate
            .cast::<CandidatePageTables<'static, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>>>()
    };
    // SAFETY: The frame allocator and CPU snapshot remain owned by retained
    // BootInfo; this callback runs on the sole CPU with the heap lock held.
    let allocator = unsafe { &mut *state.allocator };
    // SAFETY: The CPU snapshot is immutable and remains live with BootInfo.
    let cpu_info = unsafe { &*state.cpu_info };

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The callback runs at CPL 0; save IF before disabling local IRQs
    // while the active page tables and allocator are mutated.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", "cli", out(reg) flags) };
    let result = (|| {
        let physical_width = cpu_info.physical_address_bits?;
        let pat = PatLayout::from_msr_value(cpu_info.pat_msr_value?).ok()?;
        let mtrrs = match &cpu_info.mtrr {
            MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers.validated_layout(physical_width).ok()?,
            _ => return None,
        };
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        for (mapped, page) in (first_page..first_page + page_count).enumerate() {
            let virtual_address = KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE
                .checked_add((page as u64).checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)?)?;
            let frame = match allocator.allocate() {
                Some(frame) => frame,
                None => {
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
                virtual_address,
                frame.address(),
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(physical_width),
                cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            ) {
                Ok(mapping) => mapping,
                Err(_) => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            let attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
                CachePolicy::WriteBack,
                pat,
                &mtrrs,
                cpu_info.normal_caching,
            ) {
                Ok(attributes) if attributes.effective_type() == EffectiveMemoryType::WriteBack => {
                    attributes
                }
                _ => {
                    deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
                    rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                    return None;
                }
            };
            // SAFETY: IF is clear, the current candidate owns the active root,
            // and the allocator-issued frame is mapped RW/NX with local TLB
            // invalidation before its token becomes page-table-owned.
            if let Err(failure) =
                unsafe { candidate.map_owned_page_active(allocator, frame, mapping, attributes) }
            {
                deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, failure.frame);
                rollback_kernel_heap_pages(candidate, allocator, first_page, mapped);
                return None;
            }
        }
        Some(())
    })()
    .is_some();
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        // SAFETY: The mapping transaction is complete or fully rolled back.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("sti") };
    }
    result
}

fn rollback_kernel_heap_pages(
    candidate: &mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'static,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'static>,
    >,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    first_page: usize,
    mapped_pages: usize,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;

    for page in (first_page..first_page + mapped_pages).rev() {
        let Some(virtual_address) = (page as u64)
            .checked_mul(PAGE_SIZE)
            .and_then(|offset| KERNEL_HEAP_GROWTH_VIRTUAL_BASE.checked_add(offset))
        else {
            halt_forever();
        };
        // SAFETY: The pages belong to this transaction in the current active
        // root; unmapping invalidates their TLB entries before token return.
        let frame = unsafe { candidate.unmap_owned_page_active(virtual_address) }
            .unwrap_or_else(|_| halt_forever());
        deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(allocator, frame);
    }
}

fn deallocate_kernel_heap_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if allocator.deallocate(frame).is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
}

struct CandidateAcpiReader<'candidate, 'memory, 'map> {
    candidate: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<
        'memory,
        LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'map>,
    >,
    allocator: &'candidate mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &'map rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    cache_layout: rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    normal_caching: bool,
    candidate_cr3: u64,
    previous_cr3: u64,
    virtual_address: u64,
}

impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn remove_temporary_mapping(&mut self) {
        if let Err(error) = self.candidate.unmap_acpi_page(self.virtual_address) {
            crate::kprintln!("temporary ACPI mapping could not be removed: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    }
}

// The legacy-reserved authorization is accepted only for RSDP reads; all
// root and child tables require ACPI-reclaimable/NVS memory-map coverage.
impl CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    fn read_mapped(
        &mut self,
        physical_start: u64,
        output: &mut [u8],
        allow_legacy_rsdp: bool,
    ) -> Result<(), AcpiMappingError> {
        use rustix_kernel::paging::{
            validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
        };

        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
            return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
        }
        if output.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let length =
            u64::try_from(output.len()).map_err(|_| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                physical_start,
                length: output.len(),
                error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
            })?;
        let span = if allow_legacy_rsdp {
            self.memory_map.validate_rsdp_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        } else {
            self.memory_map.validate_acpi_span(
                physical_start,
                length,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
            )
        }
        .map_err(|error| AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
            physical_start,
            length: output.len(),
            error,
        })?;
        let permissions = PagePermissions {
            writable: false,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: false,
        };
        let mut copied = 0usize;
        while copied < output.len() {
            let current_physical = physical_start.checked_add(copied as u64).ok_or(
                AcpiMappingError::InvalidAcpiSpan {
                    physical_start,
                    length: output.len(),
                    error: rustix_kernel::memory::AcpiSpanError::AddressOverflow,
                },
            )?;
            let physical_page = current_physical & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
            let page_offset = current_physical - physical_page;
            let page_length = (PAGE_SIZE - page_offset).min((output.len() - copied) as u64);
            let mapping = validate_mapping_range(
                self.virtual_address,
                physical_page,
                PAGE_SIZE,
                permissions,
                Some(self.physical_address_bits),
                self.virtual_address_bits,
            )
            .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            let cache_attributes = mapping
                .select_cache_attributes(
                    CachePolicy::Uncacheable,
                    self.pat,
                    &self.cache_layout,
                    self.normal_caching,
                )
                .map_err(AcpiMappingError::InvalidMapping)?;
            self.candidate
                .map_acpi_page(self.allocator, span, mapping, cache_attributes)
                .map_err(|failure| AcpiMappingError::CandidateMap(failure.cause))?;

            let candidate_mapping_is_valid = matches!(
                self.candidate.walk(self.virtual_address),
                Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
                    if translation.physical_address == physical_page
                        && translation.permissions == permissions
            );
            if !candidate_mapping_is_valid {
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::CandidateWalk);
            }
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }

            // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of the current inherited
            // hierarchy with all critical paths verified; this temporary page is
            // supervisor R/NX and the candidate remains owned by this stack.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.candidate_cr3) };
            // SAFETY: The CR3 write above installed the candidate root and maskable
            // interrupts remain disabled during this single-core bootstrap read.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_active() };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.candidate_cr3 {
                // SAFETY: Restoring the previous validated root preserves all code,
                // stack, data, and exception mappings needed by this path.
                unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
                if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                    halt_forever();
                }
                // SAFETY: The verified CR3 is no longer the candidate root.
                unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
                self.remove_temporary_mapping();
                return Err(AcpiMappingError::UnexpectedCurrentCr3);
            }

            let source = (self.virtual_address + page_offset) as *const u8;
            for offset in 0..page_length as usize {
                // SAFETY: The exact physical page is temporarily mapped R/NX in
                // the active candidate and this byte lies within its 4 KiB leaf.
                output[copied + offset] = unsafe { source.add(offset).read_volatile() };
            }

            // SAFETY: The prior root remains allocated and its critical mappings
            // were verified before this temporary switch.
            unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(self.previous_cr3) };
            if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != self.previous_cr3 {
                halt_forever();
            }
            // SAFETY: The previous root was restored and verified above.
            unsafe { self.candidate.mark_inactive() };
            self.remove_temporary_mapping();
            copied += page_length as usize;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

// SAFETY: `read_mapped` authorizes ordinary table reads only through validated
// ACPI map regions; its separate RSDP entry point permits only the bounded legacy
// reserved window recognized by `MemoryMap::validate_rsdp_span`.
unsafe impl rustix_kernel::acpi::AcpiPhysicalReader for CandidateAcpiReader<'_, '_, '_> {
    type Error = AcpiMappingError;

    fn read(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, false)
    }

    fn read_rsdp(&mut self, physical_start: u64, output: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        self.read_mapped(physical_start, output, true)
    }
}

// Capture Limine's entry RSP before a Rust prologue changes it. The synthetic
// return slot is part of the SysV entry stack; realign before calling Rust.
core::arch::global_asm!(
    ".section .text",
    ".code64",
    ".global _start",
    ".type _start, @function",
    "_start:",
    "mov rdi, rsp",
    "and rsp, -16",
    "call rustix_start",
    "ud2",
    ".size _start, . - _start",
);

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_start(entry_rsp: u64) -> ! {
    // Keep interrupts masked until FPU state and the IRQ save destination are ready.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::cpu::initialize_fpu_state() {
        kprintln!("required x87/SSE state unavailable: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    kernel_threads::initialize_fpu_context();
    kprintln!("Rustix kernel: x86_64 Rust bootstrap");
    kprintln!("x87/SSE context state enabled with FXSAVE/FXRSTOR; AVX disabled");
    arch::x86_64::interrupts::initialize();
    kprintln!("x86_64 exception diagnostics: enabled (IRQs remain disabled)");
    let mut boot_info = match boot::capture_boot_information(entry_rsp) {
        Ok(boot_info) => boot_info,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("boot information rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = arch::x86_64::interrupts::configure_user_address_width(
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        kprintln!("user syscall address-width setup failed: {:?}", error);
        halt_forever();
    }
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    let init_image = match rustix_kernel::elf::Elf64Image::parse(
        INIT_ELF_IMAGE,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(image) => image,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("bundled init ELF rejected: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    #[cfg(target_os = "none")]
    kprintln!(
        "bundled init ELF validated: entry={:#x}, load pages={}",
        init_image.entry_point(),
        init_image.load_page_count()
    );
    boot::report_boot_information(&boot_info);

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
    probe_hhdm_frame(&mut boot_info);

    #[cfg(any(
        feature = "inject-page-fault",
        feature = "inject-invalid-opcode",
        feature = "inject-general-protection",
        feature = "inject-divide-error"
    ))]
    run_fault_injection();

    activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(&mut boot_info)
}

fn activate_cloned_page_tables_and_run(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) -> ! {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        encode_cr3_value, CandidatePageTables, PageWalkConfig, PageWalkOutcome, PAGE_SIZE,
    };

    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let inherited_root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: inherited CR3: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: NXE is not enabled");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let config = PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "page-table transition failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    if let Err(error) =
        candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &reader, inherited_root)
    {
        kprintln!(
            "page-table transition failed to clone inherited root: {:?}",
            error
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    let spans = [
        (
            "kernel text",
            segments.text.virtual_start,
            segments.text.physical_start,
            segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel rodata",
            segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            segments.rodata.physical_start,
            segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "kernel data",
            segments.data.virtual_start,
            segments.data.physical_start,
            segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
        ),
        (
            "active boot stack",
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
            boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        ),
    ];
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: {} was not preserved",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    if !harden_kernel_hhdm_aliases(
        &mut candidate,
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        KernelAliasHardeningContext {
            memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
            hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
            segments: boot_info.kernel_image_segments,
            reader: &reader,
            inherited_root,
            config,
        },
    ) {
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    kprintln!("kernel HHDM aliases validated: text/rodata R/NX, data RW/NX, PAT preserved");
    let candidate_root = candidate
        .root_physical_address()
        .expect("a live candidate retains its root frame");
    let root_hhdm_address = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        candidate_root,
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let root_alias = match candidate.walk(root_hhdm_address) {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation))
            if translation.physical_address == candidate_root =>
        {
            translation
        }
        result => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: candidate root HHDM alias: {:?}",
                result
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    if !root_alias.permissions.writable || root_alias.permissions.user_accessible {
        kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: candidate root alias permissions are unsafe");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let new_cr3 = match encode_cr3_value(
        candidate_root,
        inherited_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("page-table transition rejected: new CR3: {:?}", error);
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let inherited_cr3 = boot_info.inherited_cr3_raw;
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
        kprintln!("page-table transition aborted: active CR3 changed before switch");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Some(rsdp_physical_address) = boot_info.rsdp_physical_address {
        match load_acpi_madt(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            rsdp_physical_address,
            new_cr3,
            inherited_cr3,
        ) {
            Ok(madt) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "ACPI MADT copied: LAPIC={:#x}, {} local APICs, {} I/O APICs, {} overrides",
                    madt.local_apic_address,
                    madt.local_apics().count(),
                    madt.io_apics().count(),
                    madt.interrupt_overrides().count()
                );
                boot_info.acpi_madt = Some(madt);
            }
            Err(error) => kprintln!("ACPI MADT unavailable: {:?}", error),
        }
    }
    let apic_virtual_addresses = match boot_info.acpi_madt.as_ref() {
        Some(madt) => match map_bootstrap_apic_pages(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
            madt,
            &boot_info.memory_map,
            (
                boot_info.kernel_physical_base,
                boot_info.kernel_physical_end,
            ),
        ) {
            Ok(addresses) => Some(addresses),
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("APIC MMIO mappings unavailable: {}", error);
                None
            }
        },
        None => None,
    };
    match candidate.validate_supervisor_kernel_half() {
        Ok(table_count) => kprintln!(
            "kernel upper-half preflight passed: {} shared supervisor tables",
            table_count
        ),
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "page-table transition rejected: unsafe kernel upper half: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    }
    // SAFETY: The candidate is a complete clone of every present inherited
    // hierarchy entry, with all referenced intermediate tables owned and the
    // critical code/data/stack paths compared before this point. The inherited
    // root's paging mode, address widths, PAT/MTRR state, and low CR3 mode are
    // preserved; interrupts remain disabled through this transition and are enabled
    // later only after the selected APIC routes and handlers are ready.
    let global_tlb_flushed = unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(new_cr3) };
    if global_tlb_flushed {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: global TLB flushed via CR4.PGE toggle");
    } else {
        kprintln!("page-table transition: CR4.PGE clear; CR3 reload flushed active translations");
    }
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != new_cr3
        || !spans
            .iter()
            .all(|(_, virtual_start, physical_start, length)| {
                candidate_span_matches_source(
                    &candidate,
                    &reader,
                    inherited_root,
                    config,
                    *virtual_start,
                    *physical_start,
                    *length,
                )
            })
    {
        // SAFETY: The inherited root and its backing memory remain untouched and
        // mapped by the candidate, so restoring its validated CR3 value is safe.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(inherited_cr3) };
        if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != inherited_cr3 {
            kprintln!("page-table transition failed to restore inherited CR3; candidate retained");
            halt_forever();
        }
        kprintln!("page-table transition failed post-switch verification; restored inherited CR3");
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    // SAFETY: CR3 matches `new_cr3` and post-switch translation checks passed;
    // interrupts are disabled and the candidate root must remain allocated.
    unsafe { candidate.mark_active() };
    kprintln!(
        "page-table transition passed: active CR3={:#x}, cloned root={:#x}, {} owned tables",
        new_cr3,
        candidate_root,
        candidate.table_count()
    );

    #[cfg(feature = "probe-active-mapping")]
    {
        if let Err(error) = probe_active_mapping(
            &mut candidate,
            &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
            &boot_info.cpu_info,
        ) {
            kprintln!("active mapping probe failed: {}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
        kprintln!("active mapping probe passed: mapped, accessed, unmapped, reclaimed frame");
    }

    let mut vector_allocator = rustix_kernel::irq::InterruptVectorAllocator::new();
    let mut timer_vector = None;
