        MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers
            .validated_layout(physical_address_bits)
            .map_err(|_| "MTRR state is invalid for process mappings")?,
        _ => return Err("MTRR state unavailable for process mappings"),
    };
    let mut select_cache = |mapping: rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMappingRange| {
        mapping
            .select_cache_attributes(
                CachePolicy::WriteBack,
                pat,
                &mtrr_layout,
                cpu_info.normal_caching,
            )
            .map_err(|_| "no uniform write-back cache policy for process page")
    };
    let mut process_memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut roots = match ProcessAddressSpaceRoots::new(&kernel_half, &mut process_memory, config) {
        Ok(roots) => roots,
        Err(failure) => {
            if let Some(frame) = failure.frame {
                allocator
                    .deallocate(frame)
                    .map_err(|_| "process-root manager frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            }
            return Err("process-root manager creation failed");
        }
    };
    let process = match roots.create(allocator) {
        Ok(process) => process,
        Err(failure) => {
            if let Some(frame) = failure.frame {
                allocator
                    .deallocate(frame)
                    .map_err(|_| "process-root frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            }
            return Err("process root creation failed");
        }
    };
    let mut user_memory = LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits: Some(physical_address_bits),
        virtual_address_bits: cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut user_regions = rustix_kernel::process::UserRegionTable::new();
    const USER_STACK_BASE: u64 = 0x0000_7fff_ffff_f000;
    let stack_layout = match user_regions.reserve_elf_layout(
        &init_image,
        USER_STACK_BASE,
        1,
        1,
        cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(layout) => layout,
        Err(_) => {
            roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                "process root could not be destroyed after image/stack reservation failed"
            })?;
            return Err("ELF image, stack, or guard could not be reserved");
        }
    };

    if let Err(failure) = init_image.load_into_process_root(
        &mut roots,
        allocator,
        process,
        &mut user_memory,
        &mut select_cache,
    ) {
        if let Some(frame) = failure.frame {
            allocator
                .deallocate(frame)
                .map_err(|_| "unmapped ELF frame could not be reclaimed")?;
        }
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "partially loaded process root could not be destroyed")?;
        return Err("bundled init ELF could not be loaded into the process root");
    }

    let mut guard_probe = [0u8; 1];
    // SAFETY: The destination is kernel stack storage and does not alias any
    // user frame owned by this process. A valid guard must fail as unmapped.
    match unsafe {
        roots.copy_from_user(
            process,
            stack_layout.guard_region().start(),
            &mut guard_probe,
            &mut user_memory,
        )
    } {
        Err(failure)
            if matches!(
                failure.cause,
                rustix_kernel::paging::ProcessUserCopyError::Unmapped
            ) => {}
        _ => {
            roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                "process root could not be destroyed after stack-guard validation failed"
            })?;
            return Err("the page below the user stack is not an unmapped guard");
        }
    }
    let stack_frame = match allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after stack allocation failed")?;
            return Err("no frame available for the user stack");
        }
    };
    if rustix_kernel::paging::zero_user_frame(&stack_frame, &mut user_memory).is_err() {
        allocator
            .deallocate(stack_frame)
            .map_err(|_| "partially zeroed stack frame could not be reclaimed")?;
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after stack zeroing failed")?;
        return Err("user stack frame could not be zeroed");
    }
    let stack_mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        stack_layout.stack_region().start(),
        stack_frame.address(),
        stack_layout.stack_region().length(),
        PagePermissions {
            writable: true,
            executable: false,
            user_accessible: true,
        },
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(_) => {
            allocator
                .deallocate(stack_frame)
                .map_err(|_| "unmapped stack frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after stack validation failed")?;
            return Err("user stack mapping range was rejected");
        }
    };
    let stack_cache = match select_cache(stack_mapping) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            allocator
                .deallocate(stack_frame)
                .map_err(|_| "unmapped stack frame could not be reclaimed")?;
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after cache selection failed")?;
            return Err(error);
        }
    };
    if let Err(failure) =
        roots.map_user_page(allocator, process, stack_frame, stack_mapping, stack_cache)
    {
        allocator
            .deallocate(failure.frame)
            .map_err(|_| "unmapped stack frame could not be reclaimed")?;
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after stack mapping failed")?;
        return Err("user stack page could not be mapped");
    }

    if roots
        .validate_initial_user_state(
            process,
            init_image.entry_point(),
            stack_layout.stack_pointer(),
        )
        .is_err()
    {
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after entry validation failed")?;
        return Err("ELF entry or writable NX stack validation failed");
    }

    let mut process_table = rustix_kernel::process::ProcessTable::new();
    let process_id = process_table
        .create_initial()
        .map_err(|_| "initial process record could not be created")?;
    let (process_kernel_stack_top, process_continuation_stack_top) =
        match process_kernel_stack_tops(candidate, process_id) {
            Some(stacks) => stacks,
            None => {
                roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                    "process root could not be destroyed after kernel-stack validation failed"
                })?;
                return Err("per-process kernel stacks are not mapped RW/NX and supervisor-only");
            }
        };
    kprintln!(
        "Ring 3 entry and continuation stacks validated: pid={}, entry={:#x}, continuation={:#x}",
        process_id.get(),
        process_kernel_stack_top,
        process_continuation_stack_top
    );

    let child_program = match prepare_user_program(
        &mut roots,
        allocator,
        &mut user_memory,
        CHILD_ELF_IMAGE,
        USER_STACK_BASE,
        physical_address_bits,
        cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        &mut select_cache,
    ) {
        Ok(program) => program,
        Err(error) => {
            roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                "parent process root could not be destroyed after child load failed"
            })?;
            return Err(error);
        }
    };
    let child_process_id = match process_table.spawn(process_id) {
        Ok(child) => child,
        Err(_) => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
                .map_err(|_| {
                    "child root could not be destroyed after process-record creation failed"
                })?;
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "parent root could not be destroyed after child setup failed")?;
            return Err("child process record could not be created");
        }
    };
    let (child_kernel_stack_top, child_continuation_stack_top) =
        match process_kernel_stack_tops(candidate, child_process_id) {
            Some(stacks) => stacks,
            None => {
                roots
                    .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
                    .map_err(|_| {
                        "child root could not be destroyed after child stack validation failed"
                    })?;
                roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                    "parent root could not be destroyed after child stack validation failed"
                })?;
                return Err("child kernel stacks are not mapped RW/NX and supervisor-only");
            }
        };
    let root_address = match roots.root_physical_address(process) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(_) => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
                .map_err(|_| "child root could not be destroyed after parent root lookup failed")?;
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after root lookup failed")?;
            return Err("process root address is unavailable");
        }
    };
    let child_root_address = match roots.root_physical_address(child_program.process) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(_) => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
                .map_err(|_| "child root could not be destroyed after child root lookup failed")?;
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "parent root could not be destroyed after child root lookup failed")?;
            return Err("child process root address is unavailable");
        }
    };
    let kernel_cr3 = arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw();
    let kernel_cr3_root = match rustix_kernel::paging::parse_cr3_root(
        kernel_cr3,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        cpu_info.pcid_enabled,
    ) {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(_) => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
                .map_err(|_| {
                    "child root could not be destroyed after kernel CR3 validation failed"
                })?;
            roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                "process root could not be destroyed after kernel CR3 validation failed"
            })?;
            return Err("active kernel CR3 could not be validated");
        }
    };
    let process_cr3 = match rustix_kernel::paging::encode_cr3_value(
        root_address,
        kernel_cr3_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(_) => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
                .map_err(|_| {
                    "child root could not be destroyed after parent CR3 encoding failed"
                })?;
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, process)
                .map_err(|_| "process root could not be destroyed after CR3 encoding failed")?;
            return Err("process CR3 encoding failed");
        }
    };
    let child_process_cr3 = match rustix_kernel::paging::encode_cr3_value(
        child_root_address,
        kernel_cr3_root.low_bits(),
        physical_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(value) => value,
        Err(_) => {
            roots
                .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
                .map_err(|_| "child root could not be destroyed after child CR3 encoding failed")?;
            roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                "parent root could not be destroyed after child CR3 encoding failed"
            })?;
            return Err("child process CR3 encoding failed");
        }
    };
    let raw_user_frame = rustix_kernel::syscall::UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: init_image.entry_point(),
        code_selector: u64::from(arch::x86_64::interrupts::USER_CODE_SELECTOR),
        flags: rustix_kernel::syscall::SAFE_USER_RFLAGS,
        stack_pointer: stack_layout.stack_pointer(),
        stack_selector: u64::from(arch::x86_64::interrupts::USER_DATA_SELECTOR),
    };
    let user_frame =
        match rustix_kernel::syscall::sanitize_user_iret_frame(
            raw_user_frame,
            cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(frame) => frame,
            Err(_) => {
                roots.destroy(allocator, child_program.process).map_err(|_| {
                "child root could not be destroyed after parent IRET frame validation failed"
            })?;
                roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                    "process root could not be destroyed after IRET frame validation failed"
                })?;
                return Err("initial user IRET frame was rejected");
            }
        };

    let mut child_regions = child_program.regions;
    let mut child_context = ActiveUserProcessSyscallContext {
        roots: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(roots).cast(),
        user_memory: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(user_memory).cast(),
        allocator: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(*allocator),
        user_regions: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(child_regions),
        process_table: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(process_table),
        mtrr_layout: core::ptr::addr_of!(mtrr_layout),
        process: child_program.process,
        process_id: child_process_id,
        kernel_cr3,
        process_cr3: child_process_cr3,
        kernel_entry_stack_top: child_kernel_stack_top,
        kernel_continuation_stack_top: child_continuation_stack_top,
        user_frame: child_program.user_frame,
        child_context: core::ptr::null_mut(),
        pat,
        normal_caching: cpu_info.normal_caching,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut process_context = ActiveUserProcessSyscallContext {
        roots: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(roots).cast(),
        user_memory: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(user_memory).cast(),
        allocator: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(*allocator),
        user_regions: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(user_regions),
        process_table: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(process_table),
        mtrr_layout: core::ptr::addr_of!(mtrr_layout),
        process,
        process_id,
        kernel_cr3,
        process_cr3,
        kernel_entry_stack_top: process_kernel_stack_top,
        kernel_continuation_stack_top: process_continuation_stack_top,
        user_frame,
        child_context: core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(child_context),
        pat,
        normal_caching: cpu_info.normal_caching,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    // SAFETY: IF was disabled by the caller; all pointer targets remain live
    // until the synchronous user entry returns through its exit syscall.
    if unsafe {
        arch::x86_64::interrupts::install_user_syscall_handler(
            dispatch_active_user_process_syscall,
            dispatch_active_user_process_exception,
            core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(process_context).cast(),
        )
    }
    .is_err()
    {
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
            .map_err(|_| "child root could not be destroyed after syscall handler setup failed")?;
        roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
            "process root could not be destroyed after syscall handler setup failed"
        })?;
        return Err("user syscall handler setup failed");
    }
    // SAFETY: The selected process stack is a live, mapped RW/NX supervisor
    // range in the shared kernel half, TSS is initialized, and IF remains clear.
    if unsafe {
        arch::x86_64::interrupts::set_kernel_entry_stack(
            process_kernel_stack_top,
            cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        )
    }
    .is_err()
    {
        // SAFETY: No user entry or syscall is in flight; the installed callback
        // can be cleared while the kernel root is active and IF remains clear.
        unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::clear_user_syscall_handler() };
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
            .map_err(|_| {
                "child root could not be destroyed after kernel-entry stack setup failed"
            })?;
        roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
            "process root could not be destroyed after kernel-entry stack setup failed"
        })?;
        return Err("per-process kernel entry stack could not be installed in TSS");
    }
    // SAFETY: The process root shares the validated supervisor kernel half and
    // contains the selected kernel stack mapping; interrupts remain disabled.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::cpu::write_cr3_with_global_flush(process_cr3) };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != process_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: CR3 now names the process root, and this synchronous caller keeps
    // both the shared kernel owner and process-root set alive through exit.
    if unsafe { roots.mark_active(process) }.is_err() {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The mapped entry/stack were validated above; syscall/fault dispatch
    // are installed and maskable interrupts remain disabled through process exit.
    let exit_status = match unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::enter_user(user_frame) } {
        Ok(status) => status,
        Err(_) => halt_forever(),
    };
    if arch::x86_64::cpu::read_cr3_raw() != kernel_cr3 {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The user exit trampoline returned to the bootstrap stack, so the
    // process-specific entry stack can no longer be active and IF is still clear.
    if unsafe {
        arch::x86_64::interrupts::restore_bootstrap_kernel_entry_stack(
            cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        )
    }
    .is_err()
    {
        halt_forever();
    }
    // SAFETY: The exit trampoline returned to the kernel root with IF=0 and no
    // syscall callback remains in flight.
    unsafe { arch::x86_64::interrupts::clear_user_syscall_handler() };
    let wait_result =
        match process_table.try_wait(rustix_kernel::process::KERNEL_PROCESS_ID, process_id.get()) {
            Ok(result) => result,
            Err(_) => {
                roots
                    .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
                    .map_err(|_| {
                        "inactive child root could not be destroyed after kernel wait failed"
                    })?;
                roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
                    "inactive process root could not be destroyed after wait failed"
                })?;
                return Err("kernel wait could not inspect the init process");
            }
        };
    #[cfg(any(
        feature = "probe-user-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-page-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-general-protection",
        feature = "probe-user-divide-error"
    ))]
    let expected_status = 128 + PROBE_USER_FAULT_VECTOR as i32;
    #[cfg(not(any(
        feature = "probe-user-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-page-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-general-protection",
        feature = "probe-user-divide-error"
    )))]
    let expected_status = 42;
    if !matches!(
        wait_result,
        rustix_kernel::process::WaitResult::Exited { pid, status }
            if pid == process_id && status == exit_status && status == expected_status
    ) {
        kprintln!(
            "process wait validation mismatch: result={:?}, init pid={}, trampoline status={}, expected status={}",
            wait_result,
            process_id.get(),
            exit_status,
            expected_status
        );
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
            .map_err(|_| "inactive child root could not be destroyed after init wait mismatch")?;
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "inactive process root could not be destroyed after wait mismatch")?;
        return Err("init exit status was not retained and reaped as expected");
    }
    if matches!(
        process_table.state(child_process_id),
        Some(rustix_kernel::process::ProcessState::Running)
    ) && process_table.exit(child_process_id, 127).is_err()
    {
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
            .map_err(|_| "inactive child root could not be destroyed after child cleanup failed")?;
        roots.destroy(allocator, process).map_err(|_| {
            "inactive parent root could not be destroyed after child cleanup failed"
        })?;
        return Err("unstarted child process could not be exited during cleanup");
    }
    if process_table.state(child_process_id).is_some()
        && !matches!(
            process_table.try_wait(
                rustix_kernel::process::KERNEL_PROCESS_ID,
                child_process_id.get()
            ),
            Ok(rustix_kernel::process::WaitResult::Exited { pid, .. })
                if pid == child_process_id
        )
    {
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
            .map_err(|_| "inactive child root could not be destroyed after child reap failed")?;
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "inactive parent root could not be destroyed after child reap failed")?;
        return Err("remaining child process record could not be reaped");
    }
    if process_table.live_records() != 0 {
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
            .map_err(|_| "inactive child root could not be destroyed after process-table leak")?;
        roots
            .destroy(allocator, process)
            .map_err(|_| "inactive process root could not be destroyed after process-table leak")?;
        return Err("process records remained after process teardown");
    }
    roots
        .destroy(allocator, child_program.process)
        .map_err(|_| "inactive child process root teardown failed")?;
    roots
        .destroy(allocator, process)
        .map_err(|_| "inactive process root teardown failed")?;
    if allocator.free_frames() != initial_free_frames {
        return Err("process-root teardown did not restore the frame count");
    }
    #[cfg(not(any(
        feature = "probe-user-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-page-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-general-protection",
        feature = "probe-user-divide-error"
    )))]
    kprintln!(
        "init process exited with status {} and was reaped by kernel wait",
        exit_status
    );
    #[cfg(any(
        feature = "probe-user-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-page-fault",
        feature = "probe-user-general-protection",
        feature = "probe-user-divide-error"
    ))]
    kprintln!(
        "user fault vector {} exited with status {} and was reaped by kernel wait",
        PROBE_USER_FAULT_VECTOR,
        exit_status
    );
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_hhdm_frame(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::frame::FRAME_SIZE;
    use rustix_kernel::paging::UserFrameMemory;

    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: no free frame");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let hhdm_address = match frame.hhdm_address(
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("HHDM frame probe rejected frame translation: {:?}", error);
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut user_memory = LimineHhdmUserFrameMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut expected = [0; 64];
    for (index, byte) in expected.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *byte = index as u8 ^ 0x5a;
    }
    let mut observed = [0; 64];
    let copy_round_trip = user_memory
        .copy_to_frame(&frame, 128, &expected)
        .and_then(|()| user_memory.copy_from_frame(&frame, 128, &mut observed));
    let mut out_of_bounds = [0; 2];
    let bounds_rejected = user_memory
        .copy_from_frame(&frame, FRAME_SIZE as usize - 1, &mut out_of_bounds)
        .is_err();
    let empty_copy = user_memory
        .copy_to_frame(&frame, FRAME_SIZE as usize, &[])
        .is_ok();
    let mut verified =
        copy_round_trip.is_ok() && observed == expected && bounds_rejected && empty_copy;
    let words = (FRAME_SIZE / core::mem::size_of::<u64>() as u64) as usize;
    let page = hhdm_address as *mut u64;
    // SAFETY: The non-copyable `Frame` token is held exclusively; its full page
    // is within validated `Usable` memory and its HHDM arithmetic was checked.
    // Limine base revision 3 guarantees usable memory in the HHDM, and no other
    // Rustix mapping aliases this newly allocated frame. This is an opt-in QEMU
    // probe; a broken loader mapping would fault and be caught by the fatal path.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index)
                .write_volatile(0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64);
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            if page.add(index).read_volatile() != (0xa5a5_0000_0000_0000 ^ index as u64) {
                verified = false;
                break;
            }
        }
        for index in 0..words {
            page.add(index).write_volatile(0);
        }
    }

    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
    if !verified {
        kprintln!("HHDM frame probe failed: readback mismatch");
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!("HHDM frame probe passed: wrote, read, cleared, and reclaimed one frame");
    probe_inherited_root(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_inherited_root(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address;

    let root = match boot_info.inherited_cr3_root {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: CR3 decode rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let address = match inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
        root,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(address) => address,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited root probe failed: HHDM validation rejected: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let entries = address as *const u64;
    let mut present_entries = 0;
    // SAFETY: The complete root page was validated as bootloader-reclaimable
    // and its HHDM range arithmetic was checked. The Limine base-revision-3
    // contract maps that region; this read-only opt-in probe trusts that handoff.
    unsafe {
        for index in 0..512 {
            if entries.add(index).read_volatile() & 1 != 0 {
                present_entries += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    kprintln!(
        "inherited root HHDM probe passed: read 512 entries, {} present",
        present_entries
    );
    let physical_address_bits = match boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits {
        Some(bits) => bits,
        None => {
            kprintln!("inherited page-table walk failed: physical width unknown");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let reader = LimineHhdmPageTableReader {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let segments = boot_info.kernel_image_segments;
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_inherited_mapping(
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        "active boot stack",
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
        boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
    );

    let pat_value = match boot_info.cpu_info.pat_msr_value {
        Some(value) => value,
        None => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: active PAT value unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let pat = match rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value) {
        Ok(pat) => pat,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid PAT layout: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: invalid MTRR state: {:?}", error);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: non-normal CR0 caching mode");
        halt_forever();
    }
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel text",
        segments.text.virtual_start,
        segments.text.physical_start,
        segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel rodata",
        segments.rodata.virtual_start,
        segments.rodata.physical_start,
        segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
    );
    verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
        boot_info,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        "kernel data",
        segments.data.virtual_start,
        segments.data.physical_start,
        segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
    );
    probe_cloned_page_tables(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        &boot_info.memory_map,
        boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        &reader,
        root,
        config,
        [
            (
                "kernel text",
                segments.text.virtual_start,
                segments.text.physical_start,
                segments.text.virtual_end - segments.text.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel rodata",
                segments.rodata.virtual_start,
                segments.rodata.physical_start,
                segments.rodata.virtual_end - segments.rodata.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "kernel data",
                segments.data.virtual_start,
                segments.data.physical_start,
                segments.data.virtual_end - segments.data.virtual_start,
            ),
            (
                "active boot stack",
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_physical_start,
                boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_end - boot_info.boot_stack_virtual_start,
            ),
        ],
    );
    probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info);
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_cloned_page_tables(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    memory_map: &rustix_kernel::memory::MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    spans: [(&str, u64, u64, u64); 4],
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables;

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map,
        hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate = match CandidatePageTables::new(allocator, &mut memory, config) {
        Ok(candidate) => candidate,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                error.cause
            );
            if let Some(frame) = error.frame {
                release_probe_frame(allocator, frame);
            }
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    if let Err(error) = candidate.clone_inherited_hierarchy(allocator, source_reader, source_root) {
        kprintln!("candidate clone probe failed: {:?}", error);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
    }
    for (label, virtual_start, physical_start, length) in spans {
        if !candidate_span_matches_source(
            &candidate,
            source_reader,
            source_root,
            config,
            virtual_start,
            physical_start,
            length,
        ) {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone probe failed: {} translation mismatch",
                label
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, allocator);
        }
    }
    let table_count = candidate.table_count();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate clone probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate inherited-root clone probe passed: {} owned table pages preserve critical paths; CR3 unchanged",
        table_count
    );
}

fn candidate_span_matches_source(
    candidate: &rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    source_reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    source_root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) -> bool {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let Some(virtual_address) = virtual_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let Some(expected_physical) = physical_start.checked_add(offset) else {
            return false;
        };
        let source_result =
            walk_virtual_address(source_reader, source_root, virtual_address, config);
        let candidate_result = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
        let (source_translation, candidate_translation) = match (source_result, candidate_result) {
            (Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(source)), Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(candidate))) => {
                (source, candidate)
            }
            (source, candidate) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate clone walk mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}",
                    virtual_address,
                    source,
                    candidate
                );
                return false;
            }
        };
        if !source_translation.same_effective_mapping(candidate_translation)
            || candidate_translation.physical_address != expected_physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate clone translation mismatch at {:#018x}: inherited={:?}, candidate={:?}, expected PA={:#x}",
                virtual_address,
                source_translation,
                candidate_translation,
                expected_physical
            );
            return false;
        }
        let Some(next_offset) = offset.checked_add(rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE) else {
            return false;
        };
        offset = next_offset;
    }
    true
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn probe_candidate_page_tables(boot_info: &mut boot::BootInfo) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{
        validate_mapping_range, CachePolicy, CandidatePageTables, PagePermissions, PageWalkOutcome,
    };

    let Some(physical_address_bits) = boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits else {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: physical width unknown");
        halt_forever();
    };
    if !boot_info.cpu_info.nx_enabled || !boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: NXE or normal caching unavailable");
        halt_forever();
    }
    let pat_value = boot_info
        .cpu_info
        .pat_msr_value
        .expect("inherited cache-alias probe validated active PAT");
    let pat = rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout::from_msr_value(pat_value).unwrap_or_else(|error| {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid PAT: {:?}",
            error
        );
        halt_forever();
    });
    let registers = match &boot_info.cpu_info.mtrr {
        rustix_kernel::paging::MtrrState::Captured(registers) => registers,
        _ => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: captured MTRR state unavailable");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mtrrs = match registers.validated_layout(physical_address_bits) {
        Ok(mtrrs) => mtrrs,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid MTRR: {:?}",
                error
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let config = rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig {
        levels: if boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits == 57 {
            5
        } else {
            4
        },
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        nx_enabled: true,
        page_2m_supported: true,
        page_1g_supported: boot_info.cpu_info.has_1g_pages,
    };
    let virtual_address = 0xffff_9000_ffff_f000;
    let permissions = PagePermissions {
        writable: true,
        executable: false,
        user_accessible: false,
    };
    let frame = match boot_info.frame_allocator.allocate() {
        Some(frame) => frame,
        None => {
            kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: no leaf frame available");
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let mapping = match validate_mapping_range(
        virtual_address,
        frame.address(),
        rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
        permissions,
        Some(physical_address_bits),
        config.virtual_address_bits,
    ) {
        Ok(mapping) => mapping,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: invalid mapping: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };
    let cache_attributes = match mapping.select_cache_attributes(
        CachePolicy::WriteBack,
        pat,
        &mtrrs,
        boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
    ) {
        Ok(attributes) => attributes,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed: cache policy: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
            halt_forever();
        }
    };

    let mut memory = LimineHhdmCandidateMemory {
        memory_map: &boot_info.memory_map,
        hhdm_offset: boot_info.hhdm_offset,
        physical_address_bits,
        virtual_address_bits: boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
    };
    let mut candidate =
        match CandidatePageTables::new(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, &mut memory, config) {
            Ok(candidate) => candidate,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "candidate page-table probe failed to create root: {:?}",
                    error.cause
                );
                release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, frame);
                if let Some(root_frame) = error.frame {
                    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, root_frame);
                }
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
    let root = candidate.root_physical_address();
    let frame_address = frame.address();
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.map_owned_page(
        &mut boot_info.frame_allocator,
        frame,
        mapping,
        cache_attributes,
    ) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to map leaf: {:?}",
            failure.cause
        );
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, failure.frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }

    let walk = candidate.walk(virtual_address);
    let returned_frame = match candidate.unmap_owned_page(virtual_address) {
        Ok(frame) => frame,
        Err(error) => {
            kprintln!(
                "candidate page-table probe failed to unmap leaf: {:?}",
                error
            );
            release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
        }
    };
    let translation_valid = match &walk {
        Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => {
            translation.physical_address == frame_address
                && translation.page_size == rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE
                && translation.permissions == permissions
                && translation.pat_index == cache_attributes.pat_index()
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    if returned_frame.address() != frame_address {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table probe failed: unmap returned the wrong frame");
        release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    release_probe_frame(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator, returned_frame);
    if !translation_valid {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed: candidate walk: {:?}",
            walk
        );
        release_candidate_after_probe_failure(candidate, &mut boot_info.frame_allocator);
    }
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(&mut boot_info.frame_allocator) {
        kprintln!(
            "candidate page-table probe failed to release frames: {:?}",
            failure
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
    kprintln!(
        "candidate page-table probe passed: mapped, walked, unmapped, and released root {:#x}; CR3 unchanged",
        root.expect("candidate retains root until release")
    );
}

fn release_candidate_after_probe_failure(
    candidate: rustix_kernel::paging::CandidatePageTables<'_, LimineHhdmCandidateMemory<'_>>,
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
) -> ! {
    if let Err(failure) = candidate.release(allocator) {
        kprintln!("candidate page-table cleanup also failed: {:?}", failure);
    }
    halt_forever()
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_inherited_mapping(
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    label: &str,
    virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    let mut first_translation: Option<rustix_kernel::paging::PageTranslation> = None;
    let mut permissions_uniform = true;
    let mut pat_index_uniform = true;
    while offset < length {
        let virtual_address = match virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let expected_physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} physical overflow",
                    label
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, virtual_address, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level }) => {
                if level == rustix_kernel::paging::PageLevel::Pml4 {
                    let pml4_index = ((virtual_address >> 39) & 0x1ff) as u16;
                    let root_entry = reader.read_entry(root.physical_address(), pml4_index);
                    kprintln!(
                        "inherited mapping PML4 detail: VA={:#018x}, index={}, root={:#x}, entry={:?}",
                        virtual_address,
                        pml4_index,
                        root.physical_address(),
                        root_entry
                    );
                }
                kprintln!(
                    "inherited mapping probe failed: {} absent at {:?}",
                    label,
                    level
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!("inherited mapping probe failed: {}: {:?}", label, error);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if translation.physical_address != expected_physical {
            kprintln!(
                "inherited mapping probe failed: {} {:#018x} mapped to {:#018x}, expected {:#018x}",
                label,
                virtual_address,
                translation.physical_address,
                expected_physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        if let Some(first) = first_translation {
            permissions_uniform &= translation.permissions == first.permissions;
            pat_index_uniform &= translation.pat_index == first.pat_index;
        } else {
            first_translation = Some(translation);
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    if let Some(first) = first_translation {
        kprintln!(
            "inherited mapping probe passed: {} ({} pages), first permissions={:?}, PAT index={}, leaf size={}, uniform permissions={}, uniform PAT index={}",
            label,
            pages,
            first.permissions,
            first.pat_index,
            first.page_size,
            permissions_uniform,
            pat_index_uniform
        );
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-hhdm-frame")]
fn verify_kernel_cache_aliases(
    boot_info: &boot::BootInfo,
    reader: &impl rustix_kernel::paging::PageTableReader<
        Error = rustix_kernel::memory::HhdmAddressError,
    >,
    root: rustix_kernel::paging::Cr3Root,
    config: rustix_kernel::paging::PageWalkConfig,
    pat: rustix_kernel::paging::PatLayout,
    mtrrs: &rustix_kernel::paging::ValidatedMtrrLayout,
    label: &str,
    kernel_virtual_start: u64,
    physical_start: u64,
    length: u64,
) {
    use rustix_kernel::paging::{walk_virtual_address, PageWalkOutcome};

    let mut offset = 0;
    let mut pages = 0;
    while offset < length {
        let physical = match physical_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} physical overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_virtual = match kernel_virtual_start.checked_add(offset) {
            Some(address) => address,
            None => {
                kprintln!("cache-alias probe failed: {} virtual overflow", label);
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_virtual = match boot_info.memory_map.limine_hhdm_address(
            boot_info.hhdm_offset,
            physical,
            rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE,
            boot_info.cpu_info.physical_address_bits,
            boot_info.cpu_info.active_linear_address_bits,
        ) {
            Ok(address) => address,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM range: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let kernel_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, kernel_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_translation = match walk_virtual_address(reader, root, hhdm_virtual, config) {
            Ok(PageWalkOutcome::Mapped(translation)) => translation,
            result => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM walk: {:?}",
                    label,
                    result
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_translation.physical_address != physical
            || hhdm_translation.physical_address != physical
        {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias probe failed: {} physical {:#018x} has inconsistent translations",
                label,
                physical
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        let kernel_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            kernel_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} kernel PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        let hhdm_type = match mtrrs.effective_memory_type_for(
            physical,
            pat,
            hhdm_translation.pat_index,
            boot_info.cpu_info.normal_caching,
        ) {
            Ok(memory_type) => memory_type,
            Err(error) => {
                kprintln!(
                    "cache-alias probe failed: {} HHDM PAT/MTRR: {:?}",
                    label,
                    error
                );
                halt_forever();
            }
        };
        if kernel_type != hhdm_type {
            kprintln!(
                "cache-alias conflict: {} PA {:#018x}, kernel {:?} vs HHDM {:?}",
                label,
                physical,
                kernel_type,
                hhdm_type
            );
            halt_forever();
        }
        pages += 1;
        offset += rustix_kernel::paging::PAGE_SIZE;
    }
    kprintln!(
        "cache-alias probe passed: {} ({} pages; effective types match)",
        label,
        pages
    );
}

fn release_probe_frame(
    allocator: &mut rustix_kernel::frame::FrameAllocator,
    frame: rustix_kernel::frame::Frame,
) {
    if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
        kprintln!(
            "HHDM frame probe failed to return its frame: {:?}",
            error.error
        );
        halt_forever();
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-page-fault")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering page fault at 0x00000000deadbeef");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately reads an unmapped
    // low virtual address; the installed page-fault handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov rax, 0xdeadbeef",
            "mov rax, qword ptr [rax]",
            out("rax") _,
            options(nostack)
        );
    }
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-invalid-opcode")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering invalid opcode with ud2");
    // SAFETY: This is an opt-in QEMU test that deliberately raises #UD; the
    // installed invalid-opcode handler is expected to halt.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("ud2", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-general-protection")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering general protection with invalid DS selector");
    // SAFETY: The selector index is outside the installed GDT limit, so loading
    // it into DS deliberately raises a kernel-origin #GP in QEMU.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "mov ax, 0xffff",
            "mov ds, ax",
            out("ax") _,
            options(nostack)
        )
    };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

#[cfg(feature = "inject-divide-error")]
fn run_fault_injection() {
    kprintln!("fault injection: triggering divide error with a zero divisor");
    // SAFETY: Integer division by zero deliberately raises kernel-origin #DE.
    unsafe {
        core::arch::asm!(
            "xor edx, edx",
            "xor eax, eax",
            "xor ecx, ecx",
            "div ecx",
            out("eax") _,
            out("edx") _,
            out("ecx") _,
            options(nostack)
        )
    };
    kprintln!("fault injection unexpectedly returned");
    halt_forever();
}

/// Set once the fatal panic path has started. A panic from inside the fatal
/// path stops silently instead of recursively printing or looping diagnostics.
static FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE: core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool =
    core::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

#[panic_handler]
fn panic(info: &PanicInfo<'_>) -> ! {
    // Mask maskable interrupts before any diagnostics run: another kernel
    // thread must not resume after a panic is declared, and the fatal report
    // must not be preempted mid-print.
    //
    // SAFETY: Kernel panic path runs at CPL 0; masking IF is always sound.
    unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    if FATAL_PANIC_ACTIVE.swap(true, core::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant panics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    arch::x86_64::serial::initialize();
    kprintln!("KERNEL PANIC: {}", info);
    halt_forever()
}

fn halt_forever() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: The bootstrap has no interrupt handlers or scheduler to resume.
        unsafe { core::arch::asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

# Rustix roadmap

This roadmap describes an incremental path from the current bare-metal kernel to a useful Unix-like operating system. It is a dependency plan, not a schedule or a claim of compatibility. Features become current only after the implementation, tests, and exit criteria below agree.

## How to read status

- A checked box means the source/design work exists; it does **not** imply the code compiled, linked, booted, or passed an integration test.
- A milestone is not complete until its stated exit criteria are met and the evidence is recorded.
- Hardware work needs target build and emulator evidence. Host tests cannot validate privileged instructions, bootloader pointers, page tables, device I/O, or exception-entry assembly.
- Future work is intentionally not represented by placeholder APIs or dummy implementations.

## Current status

- **Milestone 0: local exit criteria met from a clean detached worktree; hosted CI observed.** On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 from both the working tree and a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory. On 2026-11-06, GitHub Actions run [#5](https://github.com/JustEthanCodes/rustix/actions/runs/42288095710) completed successfully on `dev` at `770f9c742dd07a00f6b53274ea05a1eca010d146`; its `kernel-and-boot-smoke` job ran `just verify`. This verifies hosted CI on that remote commit, not today’s uncommitted changes.
- **Milestone 1: validation criteria met for the current Limine path.** The bounded boot snapshot, memory-range classification, and CPUID reporting were covered by host tests and QEMU reporting; the Limine pointer-readability trust boundary remains explicit.
- **Milestone 2: local exit criteria met on 2026-10-24; hosted CI observed, physical-hardware validation pending.** The boot path owns and activates a clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, preserves inherited mappings, hardens kernel HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX while retaining PAT attributes, invalidates stale translations on CR3 transitions, and retains table-frame tokens. `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` passed after final review; QEMU exercised the active-PCID/CR3 invalidation path with CR4.PGE clear. The PGE-toggle path is statically reviewed but was not exercised by this QEMU configuration. The successful 2026-11-06 hosted `just verify` run covers the published Milestone 2 state, but not today's uncommitted changes. Broad mapping policy, reclamation, IRQ-safe allocation, and physical-hardware validation remain outside this milestone's completed scope.
- **Milestone 3: single-vCPU exit criteria met locally on 2026-11-13; hosted CI and physical-hardware validation remain pending.** `just verify` passed with 130 host tests, target check/build, BIOS and OVMF boot smokes, active-map/TLB invalidation, IRQ-save lock checks, timer preemption of non-yielding workers with x87/SSE state preservation, cooperative wait/input behavior, and UART/PS/2 IRQ wakeup. SMP and physical-hardware validation remain deferred. See the evidence and limits below. **Milestone 4: in progress.** The opt-in QEMU diagnostic now runs separate init and child ELFs in Ring 3; init's wait synchronously enters its kernel-prepared running child, resumes after child exit, preserves the zombie across invalid status copyout, and reaps it on retry. `just process-smoke` and the CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE process-termination smokes passed locally after this change. This is not scheduler-backed process execution: userspace spawn/exec, general child scheduling and stack ownership/reclamation, reusable process launch, and VM failure-injection/exhaustion validation remain open. Milestones 5 and later are planned. There is no ARM64 platform support, general-purpose userspace, persistent filesystem, GUI, or networking stack.

## Dependency path

```text
Reliable boot
    -> validated boot state
    -> owned mappings + frame allocation + heap + fault diagnostics
    -> timer/IRQ model + scheduler + IRQ-safe locking + timer preemption
    -> isolated processes + syscall ABI
    -> M5a PCI/DMA + block I/O + read-only/basic VFS
    -> M5b writable filesystem + permissions + platform services
    -> userland utilities
    -> graphical terminal and other optional services
```

Some device-driver work can proceed in parallel after the core ownership, locking, and testing rules exist. It must not bypass them with direct, unreviewed hardware access.

## Milestone 1 — validated boot state and machine diagnostics (DONE)

### Source work present

- [x] Preserve usable, reserved, ACPI, bad-memory, bootloader-reclaimable, executable/module, framebuffer, and unknown region classifications.

The pointer-readability trust boundary remains documented and must be reconsidered before adding another boot source.

## Milestone 2 — memory ownership, paging, heap, and exceptions (DONE)

This milestone establishes a safe basis for future allocation and kernel services. HHDM access is limited to checked full-frame token paths that rely on Limine's documented contract. The boot path clones the complete reachable inherited hierarchy and activates it only after validating the requested stack span, kernel segments, candidate-root HHDM alias, and kernel-image HHDM permissions.

### Source work present

- [x] Fixed-capacity frame allocator over validated `Usable` ranges, with page alignment, first-MiB reservation, deallocation, coalescing, bounded metadata, and host tests (`src/frame.rs`).
- [x] Initialize allocator metadata from the boot snapshot and expose counts through Crabshell `meminfo`.
- [x] Specify frame-token ownership and failure semantics: `Frame` is non-copyable, failed deallocation returns the token without changing allocator state, and the current API documents (but does not enforce) one allocator instance per physical map.
- [x] Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT and fatal handlers for exception vectors 0–31.
- [x] Give double faults a dedicated IST stack; report saved register/error context and CR2/error bits for page faults.
- [x] Keep maskable IRQ delivery disabled; current exception handling is fatal-only.

### Required memory-management work

- [x] Read `CR4.LA57` and `CPUID.80000008H` when available to report active/max address widths; validate Limine pointers against active canonical width and host-test 48-/57-bit boundaries.
- [x] Document base revision 3 HHDM region coverage, page-boundary behavior, and x86 permissions/cache attributes. HHDM access is limited to opt-in, checked frame and candidate-table probes relying on the protocol contract; there is no general physical-memory service.
- [x] Reject physical map ranges outside the reported CPUID width when available; validate page-rounded HHDM address arithmetic/canonicality for base revision 3 mapped types. This is protocol-derived validation, not a page-table walk or proof of pointer readability.
- [x] Record current transition-critical objects, their mapping sources/permissions, and unresolved bounds in `docs/architecture/memory.md`.
- [x] Capture Limine's executable physical/virtual bases and resolve the complete linker-defined half-open kernel-image span in `BootInfo`; validate the linker/loader base agreement, canonical virtual span, arithmetic, and reported physical width.
- [x] Capture and validate the linker-defined page-aligned text, rodata, and data segment bounds in `BootInfo`; host-test their ordering, contiguity, rounded image coverage, and derived physical ranges. `just verify` reported all three in QEMU on 2026-10-21. This metadata does not prove inherited page-table coverage or live permissions.
- [x] Request a 256 KiB Limine x86_64 stack, require its response, and capture/validate the requested span from entry `RSP`; verify its HHDM translation and `BootloaderReclaimable` backing. `just frame-smoke` walked all 64 pages in QEMU. This request fixed stack-frame overflow in the diagnostic path.
- [x] Record that Limine guarantees at least the requested stack size but does not report the larger allocation's exact bounds or guard status; preserve the requested 256 KiB span and do not infer a guard page.
- [x] Decode the inherited CR3 root address and interpret its low bits using the reported physical-address width and active `CR4.PCIDE` state; host-test reserved-bit and width rejection. `just frame-smoke` reads the root, walks kernel segments and the requested stack span, compares effective PAT/MTRR types for kernel-image/HHDM aliases, and exercises the active-root transition.
- [x] Document the active clone's kernel alias W^X policy, inherited cache behavior, MMIO limits, huge-page splitting, stack bounds, and inherited-root preservation in `docs/architecture/memory.md`.
- [x] Clone every reachable present inherited page-table hierarchy entry into allocator-owned table frames, preserving inherited leaves and non-present entries. Validate kernel segments, the full requested stack span, candidate-root HHDM access, and critical paths; keep the inherited root and backing frames untouched.
- [x] Add pure host-tested 4 KiB mapping-range validation and leaf-PTE bit encoding. Validation requires alignment, checked bounds, known physical width, canonical virtual ranges, and W^X; encoding bounds the physical width and PAT index and requires NXE for non-executable entries. These helpers alone do not prove frame ownership, mapping coverage, or PAT cache semantics, and do not touch tables.
- [x] Implement a bounded candidate-root builder for 4 KiB mappings backed by allocator-issued table and leaf tokens. It requires NXE, uses range-bound PAT attributes, restricts walks to owned tables, and holds a unique mutable backend borrow. Mapping preflights the path and prepares all missing tables before linking them; host tests cover 4-/5-level paths, W^X, ownership rejection, and rollback. An active-state guard prevents candidate mutation/release while CR3 names its root.
- [x] Ensure candidate mapping failure (including frame exhaustion and prepare failure) rolls back partial page-table allocations without changing the active root. Host tests cover rollback and retryable release failure; `just frame-smoke` maps, walks, unmaps, and releases a separate candidate mapping in QEMU.
- [x] Validate and activate the cloned root in QEMU, preserving CR3 low-bit mode, invalidating the active PCID, and flushing global translations when CR4.PGE is enabled; verify the active CR3 plus critical translations after the switch. On failure, restore and verify the inherited root with the same TLB invalidation before releasing the inactive candidate.
- [x] Add host tests for raw PTE-bit encoding and parsing a supplied PAT layout to find WB/UC/WC indexes.
- [x] Read EFER.NXE only when NX is supported and read `IA32_PAT` only when PAT is supported; report these read-only values and recognized PAT indexes at boot.
- [x] Host-test that rejected deallocations preserve free-range state and return the frame token for unaligned, unmanaged, already-free, and range-table-full cases.
- [x] Add a pure host-tested MTRR decoder/resolver for supplied fixed and variable register values, including disabled-MTRR behavior and overlap rules. Host tests and `just verify` passed on 2026-10-21.
- [x] Capture supported MTRR capability, default-type, fixed-range, and variable-range registers read-only at boot. Retain at most 32 variable pairs; report capacity overflow explicitly without a partial snapshot. Host tests cover feature gating, supported fixed/variable register reads, unsupported fixed ranges, and capacity overflow. `just verify` passed on 2026-10-22; the QEMU serial log reported the live MTRR summary.
- [x] Validate captured MTRR capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range availability, WC support, and variable-range mask/alignment; resolve the Intel SDM Table 11-7 PAT/MTRR combinations for one physical address only when `CR0.CD=0` and `CR0.NW=0`. Host tests cover all 30 documented type pairs and malformed inputs. Boot validates the captured PAT/MTRR state and prints a diagnostic resolution at PA 0; `just verify` passed on 2026-10-22. This policy helper does not establish the cache type of an inherited mapping.
- [x] Add a pure range-level PAT selector that returns an index only when it yields the requested effective type across every fixed/variable MTRR transition in the aligned physical range. Host tests cover variable boundaries, fixed-range transitions, no-uniform-index failure, and malformed range inputs. This remains policy-only and does not inspect live PTEs or aliases.
- [x] Compose range-level PAT selection with validated mapping metadata; bind the selected attributes to the physical extent and use them to encode individual 4 KiB leaves. Host tests cover a range crossing variable-MTRR types, width mismatch, and rejecting attributes for a different extent. This does not inspect inherited PTEs, establish frame ownership, or detect cache aliases.
- [x] Calculate HHDM addresses only for allocator-issued frame tokens whose complete page remains in a validated `Usable` region, with known physical width and checked protocol bounds. `just frame-smoke` passed in QEMU: one frame was written, read, cleared, and returned to the allocator. This relies on Limine's base revision 3 HHDM guarantee and does not inspect live PTEs or validate arbitrary physical addresses.
- [x] Validate the inherited CR3 root's numeric HHDM location only when its page lies wholly in a validated `BootloaderReclaimable` region and address-width arithmetic passes. Host tests reject unknown widths and other region types; `just frame-smoke` reads the 512 root entries in QEMU and confirms the HHDM access.
- [x] Add a bounded read-only 4-/5-level page-table walker with synthetic host tests for translations, permissions, PAT selection bits, 2 MiB pages, and absent entries. The opt-in QEMU probe follows every page in linker-defined text/rodata/data spans and the requested stack span, checking translations and effective cache types for kernel-image/HHDM aliases.
- [x] Add host-tested candidate page-table mapping/unmapping and transactional ownership handling; `just frame-smoke` verifies a separate candidate root can map, walk, unmap, and release one frame without changing CR3. The default boot path separately activates an inherited-root clone after critical translation and kernel-alias permission/cache checks.
- [x] Harden kernel-image HHDM aliases before activation: text/rodata become R/NX and data/BSS become RW/NX. Split inherited 1 GiB/2 MiB mappings as needed while preserving translation and PAT bits. Host tests cover both large-page splits; QEMU verifies every kernel-image alias retains its physical translation, desired permissions, and PAT index.
- [x] Add a 256 KiB BSS-backed global heap with 128 allocation records, first-fit aligned placement, exact-layout free/reuse, deterministic arena/metadata exhaustion, and an explicit prohibition on interrupt-context allocation. Host tests cover alignment, reuse, exhaustion, and invalid frees; the QEMU boot probe exercises the global allocator before entering the shell. The arena is fixed and does not grow from physical frames.

### Required exception/descriptor validation

- [x] Source contains GDT/TSS/IDT setup and normalized stubs for architectural exception vectors 0–31; double fault uses IST1.
- [x] Target-assemble/link and inspect the stubs and descriptor setup; ELF disassembly confirms call-stack alignment and the error-code normalization paths, while compile-time size assertions pin the IDT, TSS, and exception-context layouts.
- [x] Add QEMU fault-injection tests for a controlled page fault and invalid opcode. `just fault-smoke` verifies vector diagnostics, the exact CR2 address, no shell prompt or return marker, and that QEMU remains halted until its timeout; it then restores the default release kernel and ISO.
- [x] Boot the descriptor setup and both tested exception paths in QEMU. These checks cover only the injected page fault and invalid opcode, not all vectors or physical hardware.

**Exit criteria:** met locally on 2026-10-24. `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` passed after final review, covering host tests, the target build, active cloned-root boot, frame and candidate-map probes, heap behavior, and fatal page-fault/invalid-opcode diagnostics. The QEMU configuration reported CR4.PGE clear and exercised the CR3 reload path; the PGE-toggle global-TLB path is statically reviewed but was not exercised in QEMU. The active hierarchy preserves Limine's complete reachable mapping graph and hardens the kernel-image HHDM aliases; it is not a clean-room address-space policy, does not reclaim the old root or leaf frames, and has no general active mapping service. Hosted CI passed on the published `dev` state on 2026-11-06; physical-hardware validation remains pending, and the hosted run does not cover today's uncommitted changes.
