# Memory-management direction

## What exists now

`src/memory.rs` contains an allocation-free `MemoryMapBuilder` that copies Limine ranges into validated half-open physical regions. It rejects empty ranges, `base + length` overflow, overlapping ranges, empty maps, and maps exceeding the fixed 256-region capacity. Known Limine types remain distinct, and unknown type values are preserved. Host-side tests cover range validation/classification, canonical-address boundaries, physical-width bounds, HHDM range arithmetic, and page-rounded ACPI span authorization. `MemoryMap::validate_acpi_span` accepts at most 64 KiB of requested ACPI bytes and validates the entire 4 KiB-rounded physical extent against contiguous ACPI-reclaimable/NVS regions; this is metadata only, not a mapping or dereference grant. `src/boot.rs` stores the resulting map in an owned boot snapshot and reports usable bytes.

`src/frame.rs` provides a fixed-capacity allocator core with host-side tests. It only manages complete 4 KiB frames inside validated `Usable` regions, reserves the first MiB, and coalesces adjacent free ranges. The boot path additionally subtracts the validated kernel-image and boot-stack physical spans (`from_memory_map_excluding`) so a loader mislabeling them as usable cannot cause the allocator to hand out own-kernel pages. The ownership contract assumes one allocator instance per physical map: within that instance, each eligible frame is owned either by its free-range table or by a non-copyable `Frame` token while allocated. The public constructor does not enforce unique instances, so callers must not initialize multiple allocators for the same physical map; the boot path retains one allocator in `BootInfo`. `allocate` returns `None` when no free frame remains. `deallocate` consumes the token only on success; on any error, including free-range-table exhaustion, it returns a `DeallocationError` containing the original token and leaves allocator state unchanged. The range tables each have a fixed `MAX_FRAME_RANGES` capacity, so fragmentation can prevent a frame from being returned until nearby ranges coalesce. The active cloned page-table hierarchy owns its page-table frames; the frame allocator is otherwise not yet a general-purpose virtual-memory service.

`Frame::address()` is a physical address value, not a dereferenceable pointer and not a proof that the frame is mapped. CPU diagnostics now read `CR4.LA57` to report the active linear-address width (48 or 57 bits) and query `CPUID.80000008H` for physical and maximum linear-address widths when available. Boot-protocol pointers are checked against the active width, with host tests for 48- and 57-bit canonical boundaries. These facts do not prove that any physical address is mapped.

`src/paging.rs` contains host-tested mapping and cache policy plus a bounded candidate-root builder. The CR3 decoder validates physical-address width and reserved bits and interprets its low 12 bits according to active `CR4.PCIDE`; it does not dereference the root. The mapping-range validator requires known physical width, checked aligned bounds, canonical virtual endpoints in one canonical half, and rejects writable-executable permissions. It can encode one 4 KiB leaf PTE with supervisor/user and write permissions, NX when EFER.NXE is confirmed, and a bounded PAT index. `PatLayout` parses supplied `IA32_PAT` values and selects WB, UC, or WC indexes. `MtrrMemoryType`, `VariableMtrr`, `FixedMtrrRanges`, and `MtrrLayout` resolve address-specific MTRR types, including fixed-range priority and defined variable-overlap rules; undefined overlaps fail closed. `MtrrRegisters::validated_layout` validates captured capability/default-type bits, register counts and fixed-range presence, WC support, and variable-mask shape/alignment before producing an owned layout. Rustix supports contiguous power-of-two variable masks and explicitly rejects unsupported discontinuous masks. The layout combines address-specific MTRR type and PAT selection according to Intel SDM Table 11-7 only when `CR0.CD` and `CR0.NW` are clear. Host tests cover all 30 documented MTRR/PAT pairs and malformed inputs. A pure range selector chooses an index only when its effective type is uniform throughout all fixed/variable MTRR boundaries in an aligned extent; selected attributes remain bound to that physical extent. The selector itself does not inspect PTEs, aliases, or frame ownership. Boot reads CR0 without modifying it, validates captured MTRR/PAT state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution; this does not assert the live PTE's type. MTRR capture is bounded to 32 variable pairs and rejects excess capacity without partial state.

`CandidatePageTables` owns a separate root, bounded to 32 table frames and 256 explicitly mapped leaf records. Ordinary owned leaves require allocator-issued `Frame` tokens; a separate bounded ACPI path accepts only one read-only, supervisor, NX 4 KiB page contained in a `ValidatedAcpiSpan` and never transfers ownership of that physical page. Both paths require NXE, support four- and five-level paths, and hold one exclusive mutable borrow of the unsafe memory backend so prepared handles cannot be mixed across backends. Borrowed ACPI mappings can only be installed and removed while the candidate is inactive. The boot-only ACPI reader performs temporary CR3 switches to read validated pages and removes them before permanent activation. The default boot path clones the complete reachable Limine hierarchy, hardens kernel HHDM aliases to text/rodata R/NX and data RW/NX while preserving PAT bits, verifies critical translations, activates the cloned CR3, and retains the candidate tokens for the active root's lifetime. The CR3 transition invalidates the active PCID and toggles CR4.PGE when enabled; the same invalidation is used if verification restores the inherited root. General candidate mutation and release are rejected while active, but narrow owned-page active map/unmap operations are supported under the single-CPU, IF-disabled contract and invalidate the local TLB before ownership is returned. Host tests cover transactional rollback and ownership; `just active-map-smoke` validates active mapping, access, invalidation, and reclamation in QEMU. The type never writes CR3. The HHDM adapter derives table pointers only from complete allocator-owned `Usable` frames through checked arithmetic.

The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe reads the inherited root and follows paths for every page in kernel text/rodata/data and the requested stack span. The transition clones every reachable present table and preserves leaf mappings, then rewrites and validates the kernel-image HHDM aliases. The kernel and HHDM aliases retain the same PAT index; MTRR state is unchanged. This is not a fresh address-space policy or a hardware-level exhaustive inventory, and it does not reclaim the inherited root or bootloader memory.

The effective-type resolver follows [Intel SDM Vol. 3A §11.5.2.2, Table 11-7](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/671447/325384-sdm-vol-3abcd.pdf), which applies when normal caching is enabled (`CR0.CD=0`, `CR0.NW=0`). Its footnotes distinguish UC selected by an MTRR from UC selected by a page-table entry (the latter involves cache snooping and aliasing concerns); they also identify combinations that older manual editions called undefined but current processors supporting both PAT and MTRRs resolve as shown. The resolver does not cover legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations outside that table.

The requested Limine base revision is 3. Its protocol maps only `Usable`, `BootloaderReclaimable`, `ExecutableAndModules`, and `Framebuffer` memory-map regions into the HHDM; reserved, ACPI, bad, and unknown regions are not in that mapping set. HHDM mappings use at least 4 KiB granularity and may cover page-aligned bytes beyond unaligned region boundaries. Limine's inherited HHDM mappings are supervisor RWX, normally write-back cached, with framebuffer mappings write-combining when PAT is available. Before activating the cloned root, Rustix splits inherited huge pages where needed and changes the kernel image HHDM aliases to the matching R/NX or RW/NX policy while retaining PAT bits. The rest of the HHDM remains inherited; an HHDM offset is not a blanket physical-memory access grant. See the [Limine base revision 3 protocol](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine-protocol/blob/trunk/PROTOCOL.md#base-revision-3) and its memory-layout/caching sections.

The boot snapshot rejects physical map ranges beyond the reported CPUID physical-address width when available. For base-revision-3 HHDM-mapped types it validates page-rounded physical spans, checked `offset + address` arithmetic, and canonical endpoints in the active linear-address width. These checks are metadata, not proof that loader pointers are readable. Arbitrary physical access is not permitted: validated ACPI pages use the bounded read-only/NX reader; HHDM table access is limited to checked full-frame paths. Rustix-owned mappings should be non-executable by default; MMIO requires an explicit device range and cache policy, and guard regions must remain unmapped. The APIC MMIO validator rejects every known memory-map class except `Reserved` and `Unknown`; unreported ranges remain dependent on validated platform data. The active clone owns its page-table frames but leaves inherited leaf frames and the old root unreclaimed. The global heap begins with a 256 KiB BSS arena and can demand-map up to 1 MiB of allocator-backed pages in its reserved virtual range. Its IRQ-save lock prevents local interrupt reentrancy, but allocation remains forbidden in IRQ/exception handlers. Bootstrap exceptions remain fatal, while selected maskable IRQs are enabled only after APIC routes and handlers are ready.

## Active-root preservation and remaining limits

The transition clones the complete reachable inherited hierarchy rather than building a clean address space. It preserves all reachable present leaves and non-present entries, owns each cloned intermediate table, and fails closed on malformed entries, unsupported page sizes, cross-level table aliases, or fixed-capacity exhaustion. Kernel text/rodata/data HHDM aliases are then adjusted to avoid writable-executable aliases. Limine's original root and leaf frames remain intact.

- **Kernel ELF image:** `linker.ld` places `.text`, `.rodata`, `.limine_requests`, `.data`, `.bss`, and `.got` in three `PT_LOAD` segments: RX text, read-only rodata, and RW data/BSS. It exports `__kernel_start` and `__kernel_end` around the complete loadable image, plus page-aligned bounds for each segment. `BootInfo` checks that Limine's reported virtual base matches the linker start, validates ordered contiguous segment bounds covering the rounded image, derives corresponding half-open physical ranges from the executable physical base with checked arithmetic, and validates canonical virtual and reported physical address widths. The release ELF and QEMU runtime report both showed the three aligned ranges on 2026-10-21. The RX, R/NX, and RW/NX labels describe the linker segment intent; these are linker/boot metadata, not proof that the inherited page tables map every page or enforce those permissions, nor proof that loader pointers are readable. The memory-map `ExecutableAndModules` entries remain illustrative, not an authoritative kernel-image extent.
- **Active stack and `BootInfo`:** The assembly `_start` shim captures Limine's entry `RSP` before any Rust prologue. Under the SysV entry convention the synthetic return slot occupies 8 bytes, so `RSP + 8` is the exclusive stack top. Rustix requests a 256 KiB Limine stack and requires the stack-size response; `BootInfo` records and validates that requested span through the HHDM, including its `BootloaderReclaimable` backing. The loader may allocate more, and no guard page is inferred. QEMU transition tests walk all 64 requested stack pages.
- **Kernel static data:** `RAM_FILESYSTEM`, GDT, IDT, TSS, the ring-0 stack, and double-fault IST stack are static BSS/data in the kernel image. Exception entry also requires the handler code and the TSS/IDT references to remain mapped. Preserve the complete relevant data/BSS pages and stack pages.
- **Limine request data:** request records are in the kernel's writable `.limine_requests` segment. Response objects and the memory-map pointer array are bootloader-reclaimable; `capture_boot_information` copies the values used later, and the shell does not retain those pointers. Keep them mapped until the copy and validation finish; any later reclaim must be explicit rather than reclaiming the whole bootloader-reclaimable class.
- **Inherited page tables:** Limine places its page tables in bootloader-reclaimable memory, but their layout is unspecified. `BootInfo` captures raw CR3 and validates the decoded root address and active low-bit mode. The default boot path clones all reachable page-table pages into allocator-owned frames and preserves all leaf entries, then changes only the kernel-image HHDM alias permission bits while retaining cache attributes. It verifies kernel segments, the requested stack span, and the candidate-root HHDM alias before switching; afterward it verifies CR3 and the critical paths again. The inherited root and its backing pages remain untouched and are not reclaimed.
- **Devices:** COM1 uses x86 port I/O and needs no MMIO virtual mapping. Rustix does not currently request or use a framebuffer. Any future framebuffer or device-register mapping needs an explicit physical range and cache policy.

## Permissions and cache policy of the active clone

The active root preserves Limine's inherited kernel virtual mappings and their cache attributes. Before switching, Rustix requires NXE and enforces the linker permissions for every kernel-image HHDM alias: text and rodata are read-only/NX, and data/BSS/GOT are RW/NX. This prevents writable-executable aliases without discarding the HHDM alias. Huge-page leaves are split as necessary; unaffected entries retain their mappings and PAT/MTRR effective types. The remainder of the HHDM and all non-kernel aliases remain as Limine supplied them, so this is not yet a comprehensive Rustix mapping policy.

Preserve the inherited PAT/MTRR configuration during the first transition. The boot report validates captured registers and computes a diagnostic effective type from the active PAT/MTRR values under normal caching. A separate pure selector can choose an index whose effective type remains uniform across an aligned physical range; the selector itself does not inspect PTEs or aliases. The opt-in `just frame-smoke` probe now compares effective types of the inherited kernel and HHDM aliases for kernel-image pages, but it is not a full alias inventory. The pure combination follows Intel SDM Table 11-7; it is not a generic rule for legacy PCD/PWT-only selection or model-specific combinations. The active transition retains the inherited PAT and MTRR state and changes no cache-selection bits. The page-table split copies large-page PAT selection to the equivalent 4 KiB/2 MiB entries. Future MMIO mappings must still use explicit device ranges and a verified cache policy; do not infer MMIO from generic reserved memory-map entries. COM1 uses port I/O and requires no MMIO mapping.

Do not use huge pages in the first root; add them only when physical coverage, permissions, and cache attributes are uniform across the entire huge-page extent. Future Rustix-owned downward-growing stacks should have at least one 4 KiB unmapped guard page below them. The Limine bootstrap stack has no known guard, so none may be assumed there.

Never modify Limine's active page tables in place. `src/paging.rs` builds an owned clone in allocator-issued frames, can split inherited large pages to update leaf permissions, and supports transactional 4 KiB map/unmap operations before activation. The default boot path validates critical translations and kernel alias permissions, switches CR3 while invalidating stale global translations via a CR4.PGE toggle when needed, verifies the active root, and retains its frame tokens for the active lifetime. The inherited root and backing memory remain intact. This preserves inherited mappings rather than constructing a new address space; broader mapping inventory, non-kernel permission policy, reclamation, and a general mapping service remain future work.

## Planned memory layers

1. **Validated physical regions:** implemented as a fixed-capacity owned snapshot; allocator ownership and reclaim policy remain future work.
2. **Frame allocator integration:** the bounded core is initialized from `BootInfo`; table and leaf mappings use allocator-issued tokens. The active mapping smoke validates one owned page's map/access/unmap/reclamation path.
3. **Kernel virtual memory:** Rustix runs on an active clone of Limine's hierarchy and hardens kernel-image HHDM aliases. Narrow active owned-page map/unmap operations invalidate the local TLB; this is not a clean-room address-space policy or general MMIO subsystem.
4. **Heap:** a 256 KiB BSS arena with 128 allocation records is backed by a bounded, demand-mapped extension of up to 1 MiB. Host tests and QEMU cover growth, reuse, exhaustion, and failed growth. The global allocator uses an IRQ-save spin lock, but allocation remains prohibited in interrupt context so handlers stay bounded and allocation-free.
5. **Process address spaces (partial):** `SharedKernelHalf` validates/snapshots the upper root entries, and `ProcessAddressSpaceRoots` constructs multiple private roots, maps lower-half user leaves from allocator-issued frames, returns ownership on unmap, and frees private mappings/tables/root during inactive teardown. The view borrows the kernel-root owner, which must remain alive and immutable; the root set uses one exclusive backend borrow for its roots. `destroy` is permitted only after the caller switches away and invalidates the root's local non-global translations; PCID-aware teardown is unsupported. The caller still owns CR3 transitions. Mapping metadata retains writable and executable permissions, and `validate_initial_user_state` requires an executable non-writable entry page plus a writable non-executable stack page. Generic copy-in/copy-out helpers preflight lower-half mapped ranges and permissions and access owned frames through a separate `UserFrameMemory` contract. `Elf64Image::load_into_process_root` allocates, populates, cache-selects, and maps bounded ELF load pages. The opt-in `probe-user-process` diagnostic loads separate bundled init and child ELFs into independent roots. Init runs with token-based write/EFAULT handling; its wait synchronously enters the kernel-prepared child on a distinct PID-indexed entry stack while preserving the parent on a continuation stack, then resumes after child exit and copies status before reaping. The kernel harness later waits/reaps init and tears down both inactive roots. Its one-page initial stack is cleared in bounded chunks before mapping, and Ring 3 checks an untouched byte is zero. It has an unmapped page immediately below it; startup checks that page is unmapped, and `just user-fault-smoke` reads it from CPL3 and checks the resulting #PF CR2 before validating teardown. A fixed-capacity `UserRegionTable` reserves the ELF segments, stack, and guard, and provides first-fit page-rounded anonymous-region reservations within a bounded lower-half window. The opt-in process probe exposes one-page `mmap`/`munmap` calls: it zeroes RW/NX frames before mapping, switches to the kernel root for PTE changes, and only releases a frame after unmapping it. QEMU verifies a fresh mapped page, user write/read, stale-address EFAULT after unmap, and root teardown. This is still a bounded one-page-per-call VM interface, not stack growth or a general userspace memory manager. `just process-smoke` validates actual child entry/exit, blocking wait, EFAULT copyout retry, and root/frame teardown. This remains a bounded synchronous QEMU diagnostic, not scheduler-backed process execution or arbitrary userspace spawn/exec. Dynamic stack growth, general anonymous VM management, scheduler-owned/reclaimed process stacks, a curated kernel map, and complete fault recovery remain future work.

`process::prepare_user_program` is the reusable static-image preparation layer: it creates a fresh private root, loads validated ELF segments, reserves an unmapped guard, maps a zero-filled RW/NX stack of 1–16 pages, and validates the initial user entry/IRET frame. Failures clean up transactionally where possible; any root or unattached frame that cannot be reclaimed is returned in a must-use error with a retryable `cleanup` method. The opt-in runner uses this API for both bundled init and child, but process scheduling, syscall-visible spawn/exec, and scheduler-owned kernel stacks are not part of this service. Host tests verify multi-page stack zeroing and rollback after injected table-preparation, cache-policy, and bounded frame-exhaustion failures. The `CandidatePageTableMemory` contract currently treats individual `write_entry` operations as infallible, so tests cannot inject a write failure mid-PTE transaction.

## Invariants to preserve

- Physical ranges use checked arithmetic and the half-open convention `[start, end)`.
- Only complete frames in validated `Usable` regions enter the allocator; the first MiB remains reserved. Firmware and loader-reclaimable regions are not silently promoted to free memory.
- Under the single-allocator-per-physical-map contract, a frame is represented by one allocator-free range or one caller-owned, non-copyable `Frame` token. Only a successful `deallocate` transfers the token back to the allocator; errors return the token and leave allocator ranges and accounting unchanged. The current public constructor relies on callers to enforce unique allocator instances.
- `allocate` returns `None` on frame exhaustion. Metadata-capacity exhaustion is an explicit error, never silent loss of a frame.
- A `Frame` address is physical, not directly dereferenceable. HHDM translation and table access are limited to checked full-frame token-based paths that rely on Limine's documented mapping contract. Candidate mutations are allowed only before activation and only in owned tables. The active cloned root retains its ownership tokens and rejects mutation/release until an explicit, reviewed CR3 transition away from it.
- Mapping changes validate alignment, canonical addresses, ownership, and permissions before touching tables. User-accessible leaf mappings must stay in the lower canonical half; the upper half is reserved for supervisor mappings.
- User-controlled addresses are validated on every syscall boundary; prior validation is not a substitute for access checks during later copies.
- Tests cover unaligned edges, exact-boundary allocations, arithmetic overflow, overlaps, exhaustion, and unchanged state/ownership on failure.

The active root is a full clone of Limine's reachable hierarchy with kernel HHDM alias W^X hardening, not a clean-room Rustix address space. Heap growth is bounded to a fixed virtual reservation and 1 MiB of frame-backed pages. Broader alias/MMIO coverage, frame reclamation, and physical-hardware validation remain outstanding.

# Rustix documentation

Rustix is a 64-bit, Rust-first, Unix-like operating-system project. This index separates current implementation facts from planned interfaces: roadmap items are proposals until the corresponding code and tests exist.

## Start here

- [Project and implementation overview](architecture/overview.md)
- [Boot protocol and current entry path](architecture/boot.md)
- [Memory-management direction](architecture/memory.md)
- [ACPI table parsing foundation](architecture/acpi.md)
- [Interrupts and IRQ vector allocation](architecture/interrupts.md)
- [x86_64 drivers and hardware boundary](architecture/drivers.md)
- [Crabshell and the volatile RAM filesystem](architecture/crabshell.md)
- [Unix-like process and syscall direction](architecture/syscall-abi.md)
- [Build and toolchain guide](development/building.md)
- [Testing and verification](development/testing.md)
- [Security and unsafe-code policy](security.md)
- [Milestones and acceptance criteria](roadmap/README.md)

## Current status

The repository contains a bare-metal `no_std` Rust kernel for `x86_64-unknown-none`. After Limine handoff it validates and copies memory-map metadata into an owned snapshot, captures the executable's physical and virtual bases, complete linker-defined image span, and page-aligned text/rodata/data segment bounds, reports baseline CPUID features, active/maximum address widths, read-only CR0 caching state, gated EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT values, and a bounded MTRR snapshot, seeds a volatile RAM filesystem, and runs Crabshell over the COM1 serial console. Boot-protocol pointers are checked for canonicality using the active 4- or 5-level paging width; physical map bounds and protocol-scoped HHDM range arithmetic are also validated. Crabshell's allocation-free parser is a separate crate; the kernel handles command execution. On 2026-10-16, `just verify` passed in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 both in the working tree and from a clean detached worktree with an empty `target` directory; the clean run downloaded and built the pinned Limine host utility, created the image, and passed the bounded QEMU boot to the shell prompt. The serial log showed memory-map and CPU reporting. GitHub Actions run [#5](https://github.com/JustEthanCodes/rustix/actions/runs/42288095710) passed `just verify` on the published `dev` commit on 2026-11-06; it does not cover later uncommitted changes. A separate interactive QEMU session exercised `help`, `ls`, `meminfo`, directory navigation, and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove commands. Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met, and Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. An opt-in diagnostic QEMU path runs separately bundled init and child ELFs in Ring 3 and validates ABI version/write/EFAULT, one-page and multi-page anonymous mappings, `Vec`/`Box` allocation through the shared userspace runtime, real child execution during a suspended parent wait, status-copyout failure/retry, child and init reap, root teardown, and CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE exits. The kernel process module now provides reusable static-ELF/root/guard/stack preparation (up to 16 initial stack pages) with retryable ownership cleanup; host tests cover multi-page zeroing and injected table-preparation/cache-policy/frame-exhaustion rollback. The opt-in diagnostic uses this API for both bundled init and child, but its synchronous IF-disabled nested runner is not general scheduler-backed process launching, so Milestone 4 remains in progress. A bounded physical-frame allocator is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`; token ownership and failed-deallocation semantics are documented and host-tested. The boot transition owns an activated clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, and the global heap begins with a 256 KiB BSS arena and 128 allocation records, with bounded frame-backed growth up to 1 MiB. The Limine base-revision 3 HHDM scope and a conservative initial mapping/alias/cache policy are documented. Pure host-tested helpers validate mapping ranges/PTE bits, parse PAT layouts, validate captured MTRR snapshots, combine PAT/MTRR types under normal caching according to Intel SDM Table 11-7, and select a PAT index only when it yields one effective type across an aligned physical range. Boot validates the captured state and prints a diagnostic effective type at PA 0. The transition preserves inherited cache attributes, adjusts kernel-image HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX, and checks the effective PAT index against the inherited mapping. `BootInfo` records raw CR3 and a validated decode of its root physical address and low-bit interpretation. Checked HHDM access is limited to complete allocator-owned usable frames and cloned table frames; the active root owns its cloned table pages while inherited leaf frames remain loader-owned. The complete linker-defined kernel-image span and requested 256 KiB initial boot-stack span are captured and validated; Limine does not report any larger allocation bounds or guard status, so Rustix does not infer a guard page. The heap has bounded frame-backed growth and an IRQ-save lock; allocation remains prohibited in IRQ/exception context. ACPI support includes bounded host-tested RSDP/SDT/RSDT/XSDT/MADT parsing and a read-only/NX boot reader that copies validated MADT data into owned state. Rustix has a tested single-vCPU APIC/PIT IRQ path, cooperative and timer-preemptive scheduling, IRQ-save locks, guarded kernel threads, bounded frame-backed heap growth, and interrupt-driven UART/PS/2 queues with a polling fallback. SMP, general-purpose process scheduling, a persistent filesystem, and Unix compatibility remain absent. The documented syscall ABI and process-root primitives are exercised only by an opt-in diagnostic process. Kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal; the opt-in user path terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and `just fault-smoke` separately verifies those four exceptions halt at CPL0. This is not a general recovery policy or physical-hardware validation. On 2026-10-21, `just verify` passed after adding CR3 decoding and the pure MTRR resolver, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. On 2026-10-22, `just verify` passed after adding bounded read-only MTRR register capture and validated PAT/MTRR policy resolution. On 2026-10-24, the final `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` runs passed after review. QEMU verified the 256 KiB stack request, cloned-root CR3 transition, kernel HHDM alias hardening, heap alignment/reuse/exhaustion probe, and shell prompt; the current emulator reports CR4.PGE clear, so it exercised CR3 invalidation with PGE disabled, while the PGE-toggle path was statically reviewed but not exercised. Milestone 2's local exit criteria are met. Hosted CI passed on the published `dev` commit, but it does not cover today's uncommitted work or establish physical-hardware behavior, a clean-room mapping policy, or exhaustive alias coverage. On 2026-11-07, `just verify` passed with 127 host tests and BIOS/OVMF QEMU coverage for APIC/PIT delivery, active mapping/TLB invalidation, cooperative scheduling, and UART/PS/2 input wakeups. On 2026-11-13, `just verify` passed with 130 host tests and extended OVMF coverage for IRQ-save lock IF restoration, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE context preservation, and input wakeups. Milestone 3's single-vCPU exit criteria are met. Milestone 4 is in progress: after the child-runner change, `just process-smoke` validates a real child, blocking wait, copyout retry, teardown, and the CPL3/CPL0 exception matrix has passed. The runner is diagnostic-only; userspace spawn/exec, general process scheduling and scheduler-owned/reclaimed stacks, exhaustive VM exhaustion/mid-PTE-write injection, and normal-boot userspace remain pending. SMP and physical-hardware validation remain pending.

## Documentation conventions

- **Implemented** means present in the repository and checked by current code or tests.
- **Planned** means an architectural direction, not a stable ABI or delivered capability.
- Any future ABI proposal must state versioning, error behavior, memory ownership, and compatibility expectations before it is treated as stable.

# Testing and verification

## Current checks

`just verify` runs the standard development verification sequence:

1. `just fmt` — fail on formatting differences across the workspace.
2. `just test` — run host-side ACPI parser/traversal, borrowed-page mapping, IRQ vector allocator, PIT rate/time arithmetic, SPSC input-queue wraparound, scheduler, process lifecycle, descriptor-table and user-region policy, reusable ELF/root/guard/stack preparation, injected rollback, and bounded frame-exhaustion behavior, syscall request decoding, memory-map, mapping-range/PTE-bit policy, frame-allocator, heap, RAM-filesystem, Crabshell parser, and `rustix-user` syscall decoding, short-write, and formatting tests.
3. `just check` — check the `x86_64-unknown-none` kernel target.
4. `just smoke` — build the pinned hybrid ISO (including the static `rustix-init` ELF payload), boot it in QEMU's default BIOS mode, require the kernel to parse/validate the bundled init entry and load-page count, and check that Crabshell reaches its prompt within a deadline.
5. `just uefi-smoke` — boot the same ISO with OVMF and require the copied MADT report, CR3/page-table transition and TLB-flush markers, timer IRQ delivery/EOI, and shell prompt within a deadline.
6. `just active-map-smoke` and `just thread-smoke` — exercise active owned-page mapping/TLB invalidation and (under OVMF) IRQ-save lock IF restoration, cooperative event/wait behavior, timer preemption of non-yielding workers, x87/SSE state preservation, timed sleep while another ready thread repeatedly yields, guarded stacks, and frame-backed heap growth; both restore the default image.
7. `just input-smoke` — under OVMF, type a partial `pwd` over UART, inject ordinary and extended PS/2 scancodes through QMP, require each diagnostic to redraw the prompt and partial line, then finish the command and verify its output. The QMP socket is created under the host temporary directory because WSL `/mnt/c` does not support Unix sockets.
8. `just fault-smoke`, `just process-smoke`, and `just user-fault-smoke` — verify fatal kernel #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE diagnostics, then run bundled init in a diagnostic Ring 3 root. The normal process variant checks a fresh stack byte, ABI version, formatted and complete serial output, dup/write/close behavior including `-EBADF` for closed descriptors, zero-filled RW/NX one-page and multi-page anonymous mappings, user write/read, exact unmap, `-EFAULT` for stale/invalid user pointers, and a separately bundled real child entering Ring 3 and exiting with status 7. Init blocks in wait while the diagnostic synchronously enters that kernel-prepared child; an invalid status pointer returns `-EFAULT` without reaping, and retry copies status then reaps. The smoke checks init exit status 42, kernel wait/reap, and both root/frame teardown. The user-fault variants trigger #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE, require status `128 + vector`, wait/reap, and verify root teardown/kernel survival. The CPL3 #PF specifically reads the unmapped 4 KiB page immediately below the one-page initial user stack and checks the reported CR2 address. NMI/#DF/#MC remain fatal; the nested child runner is diagnostic-only, not general scheduler-backed userspace.

`just frame-smoke` builds an opt-in kernel variant that allocates one `Usable` frame, validates its HHDM address, writes and reads the whole page, clears it, returns it, and checks the prompt in QEMU. It reads the inherited root, walks all pages in the kernel image segments and requested 256 KiB stack span, compares effective PAT/MTRR types for kernel-image/HHDM aliases, and exercises a separate candidate map/unmap/release. The normal boot path in this image also clones the full reachable inherited hierarchy, hardens kernel-image HHDM aliases to text/rodata R/NX and data RW/NX while retaining PAT bits, switches CR3 with active-PCID and global-TLB invalidation, verifies the active root and critical mappings, and exercises the global heap's alignment, reuse, and deterministic exhaustion. The smoke test requires a serial marker confirming the applicable TLB invalidation path. The workflow restores the default release kernel and ISO. These probes rely on Limine's HHDM contract and do not inventory every unrelated mapping or prove physical-hardware correctness. `just fault-smoke` tests kernel-fatal page-fault, general-protection, invalid-opcode, and divide-error paths; it requires expected vector diagnostics (and CR2 for #PF), no prompt or return marker, and a halt until timeout. These fatal-path tests are distinct from `just user-fault-smoke`, which terminates a CPL3 process on #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE only when the diagnostic process runtime is installed. Diagnostic Cargo features are disabled by default and mutually exclusive, except each `probe-user-*` fault variant deliberately enables `probe-user-process`.

Keep the ACPI parser, IRQ vector allocator, PIT time arithmetic, Crabshell parser, VFS, memory-map validator, paging policy helpers, frame allocator, and fixed heap independent of hardware so ACPI signatures/checksums/MADT bounds and ACPI page-rounded span authorization, IRQ vector ownership/exhaustion, PIT divisor and elapsed-time arithmetic, syntax, path handling, address and leaf-PTE bit policy, PAT/MTRR policy, storage semantics, frame ownership, HHDM/root-range calculations, allocation alignment, reuse, and exhaustion can be tested without booting. Pure tests validate captured MTRR register snapshots, resolve the Intel SDM Table 11-7 PAT/MTRR combinations for one physical address, select a PAT index that remains uniform across MTRR boundaries in an aligned range, bind that selection to validated mapping metadata before encoding leaves, and walk synthetic four-/five-level page tables including large-page leaves. Host tests also exercise the candidate builder's owned-table walk, clone ownership, 4-/5-level mapping, 2 MiB/1 GiB splitting, permission/cache-bit preservation, active-state mutation/release guard, transactional allocation/prepare rollback, retryable frame-release failure, and process preparation rollback after injected table-preparation/cache failures. Heap tests cover alignment, exact-layout free/reuse, zero-sized rejection, metadata exhaustion, and arena exhaustion. Tests reject malformed state, unsupported discontinuous masks, invalid indexes/ranges, out-of-range addresses, mismatched physical widths, and non-normal caching mode. The pure inherited-table walker does not access hardware tables; the opt-in QEMU reader and candidate backend use checked HHDM addresses. Boot-time QEMU checks a subset of live kernel/HHDM aliases but does not inventory all aliases or prove complete transition safety. Boot separately captures the registers and CR0 caching mode read-only and reports a diagnostic resolution; this is not a page-table or mapping test. The GDT/TSS/IDT and CPU-register paths are privileged kernel code. The temporary ACPI CR3/map/copy/restore path is hardware-only. The 2026-11-07 WSL2 q35 smoke reached the shell but rejected the MADT table span as `NotFullyAcpiBacked`; it did not validate a successful ACPI physical read or CR3 round-trip. QEMU boot and fault-injection checks complement, but do not replace, static review and target builds. Add tests for boundaries and failure behavior when introducing new pure kernel helpers. The kernel binary is not a host test target.

`just uefi-smoke` locates combined OVMF firmware or a matching CODE/VARS pair in standard system directories. `just thread-smoke` uses an opt-in kernel-thread probe, requires the lock-state, cooperative scheduling, non-yielding timer-preemption, and FPU-preservation markers, and restores the default release image. Split firmware uses a fresh temporary copy of the VARS template. `just input-smoke` validates UART RX and PS/2 IRQ delivery/wakeup against the normal default kernel. The OVMF checks require the expected MADT report and CR3-transition markers; install the Ubuntu `ovmf` package if no firmware is found. The BIOS smoke remains separate: if firmware places the RSDT in Reserved memory, the kernel's ACPI validation is expected to fail closed rather than accepting that table span.

## What current checks do not prove

- `cargo check` does not perform a final target link.
- A successful ELF link does not prove the boot protocol is recognized or `_start` is reached.
- Host unit tests do not validate privileged instructions, UART behavior, memory-map pointer validity, page tables, interrupts, or actual hardware. The QEMU boot path exercises the gated EFER/PAT reads and bounded MTRR capture and prints diagnostic summaries, but the prompt smoke assertion does not make those facts a mapping-safety proof.
- The automated QEMU prompt smoke test asserts the cloned CR3 transition, the applicable active-PCID/global-TLB invalidation marker, kernel HHDM alias permissions/cache preservation, heap probe, and shell prompt. The current emulator reports CR4.PGE clear; it exercises the CR3 reload path, not the PGE-toggle global flush path. `just frame-smoke` additionally exercises one allocator-owned frame, inherited paths, kernel/HHDM cache aliases, and a separate candidate mapping through Limine's HHDM contract. The clone preserves Limine's complete reachable hierarchy, but there is no clean-room mapping policy or exhaustive audit of unrelated aliases; emulator tests do not establish physical-hardware behavior. `just fault-smoke` exercises the controlled #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE fatal paths; it does not test every exception vector or general recovery.
- A separate manual QEMU session exercised directory navigation and file create/write/append/read/copy/move/remove operations, including `cp` replacing an existing destination and rejection of `rmdir` on a nonempty directory. This is not exhaustive shell coverage and does not prove persistence across reboot.
- There is no on-disk filesystem test, general userspace/process-scheduler test, userspace spawn/exec test, fuzz target, or physical-hardware test. `just process-smoke` validates blocking wait and real execution of one kernel-prepared child using a nested synchronous runner, not general scheduler-managed child contexts.

## Validation policy

For changes to the kernel entry, linker script, boot requests, architecture code, shell, or VFS, run `just verify`. For memory-management and ABI code, add negative tests for overflow, malformed ranges, permission failures, and invalid user pointers before exposing those paths to userspace.

Record commands actually run and any environment limitation in change summaries; never call an unexecuted build “passing.”

## Current blockers and decisions
The major M4 gap is **general scheduler-managed Ring 3 process execution**: there is no userspace spawn/exec operation, process contexts are not integrated into the scheduler, and process kernel stacks are not scheduler-owned/reclaimed. Broader VM exhaustion and PTE-write failure coverage are also incomplete.

Scheduler safety findings:
- `enter_user` requires IF clear; the initial safe user RFLAGS currently has interrupts disabled.
- Timer preemption in `src/kernel_threads.rs` switches existing kernel-thread stack/FX contexts. It does not switch process CR3 or TSS `RSP0`.
- The process diagnostic uses PID-indexed static entry/continuation stacks and manually switches roots.
- Do **not** simply enable IF or add Ring 3 scheduling without a reviewed plan covering interrupt return frames, per-context TSS stack selection, CR3 transitions, shared mappings, scheduler ownership, and teardown.

## Next
1. Recheck `git status`, diff, and the edited M4 docs; confirm the docs match the current code and tests.
2. Continue from the scheduler/process lifecycle gap. Follow `.entire/agent-guide.md`: Brain first, then Graph for each code-location/relationship investigation; Graph again when tracing new dependencies.

## Pitfalls
- A test fixture initially used the literal `b"\\x7fELF"` instead of the ELF magic; corrected to `b"\x7fELF"`.
- User-copy helpers cap one copy at 4096 bytes, so the two-page stack test must check each page separately.
- Frame exhaustion can occur while loading ELF pages (`ElfLoad`), not only during stack allocation. The test now accepts either exhaustion stage while asserting roots/frames are reclaimed.
- Reusing `CandidateTestMemory` across repeated attempts accumulated prepared pages and hit its fixed capacity; reset the backend between injected-failure attempts.
- A previous `just verify` attempt in an earlier session timed out/stalled during the fault matrix; the latest full run completed successfully.

     3	Use Graph EVERY time you need to find code or a code relationship, not only at the

     8	
     9	The brief answers why, and what was decided; the query answers where, and what
    10	depends on it. Step 2 holds for small edits, follow-up work, and tasks that already
    11	name the file: a named file answers where code is, not what else depends on it. Do
    12	not skip either step on the grounds that the available context feels sufficient, and
    13	do not treat having done one as having done the other.

    18	    entire graph neighbors --repo . --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --symbol <Name> --direction in
    19	    entire graph impact --repo . --head --max-context-bytes 4096 --symbol <Name>
    20	
    21	query finds the code for a description. def shows what a named symbol is.
    22	neighbors lists callers (--direction in) or callees (--direction out). impact gives
    23	the blast radius before you change a symbol. Use these, not grep, for definitions,
    24	callers, references and dependents. Use grep/rg only for literal strings, config
    25	keys, environment-variable names and file names.

**Tool Call: Read file `docs/architecture/interrupts.md`**

```rustix/docs/architecture/interrupts.md
     1	# Interrupts and IRQ vector allocation
     2	
     3	## Current implementation
     4	
     5	`src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` installs the bootstrap GDT, TSS, exception gates for vectors 0–31, device IRQ stubs, and the APIC spurious-vector gate. Kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal. In the opt-in synchronous Ring 3 process probe, noncritical CPL3 exceptions are reported and handed to the installed process callback, which records status `128 + vector`, restores the kernel CR3, and exits through the user-entry trampoline. NMI (#2), double fault (#8), and machine check (#18) remain fatal regardless of saved CPL. QEMU exercises CPL3 #PF, #GP, #UD, and #DE termination in the diagnostic runtime; this is not a general exception or signal mechanism. Maskable interrupts start disabled and are enabled only after the validated APIC route, registered handler, and acknowledgement path are ready.
     6	
     7	`src/irq.rs` provides a host-tested, allocation-free token allocator for device vectors `0x20..=0xef` except reserved syscall vector `0x80`; exception vectors and the reserved upper range are also excluded. The IDT overrides `0x80` with a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate and assembly stub. The stub rejects CPL0 invocation, saves the full GPR set and x87/SSE state on the TSS entry stack, and dispatches a normalized syscall context with IF clear. In the opt-in process probe, the dispatcher implements ABI-version discovery, bounded write and wait-status copyout through allocator-owned user-frame copies, exit, and wait on one kernel-prepared child. If that child is running, the diagnostic enters it synchronously on a distinct continuation stack and resumes the parent after exit; the kernel harness later waits/reaps init. This is not general scheduler-managed process execution or a userspace spawn operation. The normal build only exposes ABI-version discovery. `rustix_irq_dispatch` invokes the registered handler, returns for the APIC spurious vector without EOI, and halts on unregistered/unexpected vectors. Device handlers own their EOI. Vector registration is performed with IF clear before the corresponding I/O APIC source is unmasked.
     8	
     9	The initial hardware target is single-vCPU QEMU `q35`: validated ACPI/MADT topology, local APIC and I/O APIC, masked legacy PIC routing, MADT-resolved ISA routes, and a periodic 8254 PIT tick near 100 Hz. OVMF smokes validate PIT delivery/EOI, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE state preservation, and UART/keyboard IRQ delivery. Host tests cover vector ownership and PIT/time arithmetic; they do not replace privileged QEMU coverage.
    10	
    11	The scheduler is single-vCPU and supports cooperative waits/yields plus PIT-driven timer preemption. The timer handler advances ticks and sends APIC EOI before any scheduling switch. The common IRQ stub saves the interrupted x87/SSE state before Rust dispatch and restores the selected context before `IRETQ`; the context switch keeps aligned per-context FXSAVE areas. IRQ-safe spin locks save and restore the prior IF state, and the global heap uses one; scheduler mutations are separately serialized by masking local interrupts. IRQ/exception handlers remain bounded and allocation-free, and no current IRQ handler acquires the heap lock. SMP, per-CPU state, and physical-hardware validation remain future work.

   172	## Milestone 4 — isolated processes and syscall ABI
   173	
   174	Userspace begins only after page tables, exception handling, scheduling, and controlled memory allocation are trustworthy. The syscall ABI is a product interface and must not emerge accidentally from internal functions. Milestone 3's single-vCPU IRQ-safe locking and timer-preemption gate is locally validated; this enables scheduler progress but does not by itself make user code isolated or safe. SMP remains outside this milestone.
   175	
   176	### Planned work
   177	
   178	- [x] Decide and document the initial x86_64 user-entry/syscall mechanism, register convention, selector/MSR setup, per-CPU state requirements, and safe return path. The design uses a DPL-3 `int $0x80` gate and validated `IRETQ`, with no syscall MSRs or `SWAPGS`. Vector `0x80` is excluded from the device allocator; the GDT installs asserted Ring 3 selectors, and the gate saves GPR/x87/SSE state and sanitizes return flags. The opt-in process probe exercises entry/return and mapping-aware return checks; it uses the static bootstrap entry stack and is not general process scheduling. Revisit the entry model if per-process stacks or SMP requirements change.
   179	- [x] Define per-process address-space construction without deep-cloning the entire kernel page-table tree for every process. The design shares validated supervisor-only upper-half subtrees, keeps lower-half tables and user frames process-owned, and specifies kernel-owner lifetime, teardown, permission, and local TLB rules. Implementation and validation remain pending.
   180	- [x] Complete the initial user/kernel page-permission and process-owned address-space path, including teardown and local TLB invalidation rules. The implementation shares validated supervisor-only kernel entries, maps/unmaps private lower-half user frames, retains executable/writable metadata, validates the initial entry and writable NX stack, and destroys the root only after switching away. Host tests cover ownership and rollback; `just verify` validates one activation/return/teardown cycle and frame-count restoration in QEMU. General concurrent process scheduling, scheduler-owned/reclaimed kernel stacks, curated kernel mappings, and broader isolation guarantees remain pending.
   181	- [x] Complete copy-in/copy-out semantics for the initial implemented syscall set. Frame-token-based helpers preflight ranges and permissions; bounded `write` and `wait` use them. Host tests cover cross-page copies, permissions, partial writes, and descriptor errors. `just process-smoke` verifies invalid write/status pointers return `-EFAULT` without kernel corruption or consuming the child, then successfully copies status and reaps after the real child exits. QEMU fault smokes verify CPL3 termination and fatal CPL0 separation for #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE. Transfer semantics for future syscalls remain pending.
   182	- [x] Specify v1 version discovery, initial syscall numbers/argument meanings, fixed-width layouts, negative error encoding, bounded partial-write/copy behavior, wait semantics, no-restart policy, and append-only compatibility before exposing calls. The contract is documented in `docs/architecture/syscall-abi.md`; host-tested decoding and the dedicated gate/stub are implemented. The diagnostic path exercises ABI-version, descriptor-authorized write, close/dup, wait on a real kernel-prepared child, one-page/multi-page mmap/munmap, and exit. The child runs synchronously while the parent wait is suspended; general scheduling/launch, arbitrary children, and interruption remain pending. Future read/open, general file-object semantics, signals, and clocks need implementation/specification.
   183	- [ ] Complete process lifecycle and descriptor-table semantics: create/load, exit, wait, close, duplication/inheritance, and cleanup. The diagnostic path binds exit/reap to process roots and runs a real kernel-prepared child when init waits; status copyout precedes reap, and invalid status pointers leave the exited child waitable. The fixed-capacity table inherits console stream handles on spawn, supports close/dup with lowest-free descriptor allocation, clears handles on exit, and returns `EMFILE` on exhaustion; host tests cover defaults, inheritance, duplicate independence, invalid/closed entries, slot reuse, capacity, and exit cleanup, while `just process-smoke` exercises dup/write/close and real child wait from Ring 3. A userspace create/exec operation, scheduler-managed runnable contexts, general wait queue behavior, stack reclamation, and general file-object/process ownership remain unimplemented. The QEMU diagnostic validates distinct static entry/continuation stacks by PID but does not hand process contexts to the kernel scheduler.
   184	- [ ] Integrate a general-purpose static ELF64 process loader and execution path. The bounded allocation-free parser validates `PT_LOAD` bounds, alignment, permissions, lower-half ranges, overlaps, file bounds, and executable entry points. `process::prepare_user_program` is now a reusable kernel API that creates a private root, loads a validated image, reserves an unmapped guard, maps a zero-filled RW/NX initial stack of up to 16 pages, and validates the initial Ring 3 IRET frame. Host tests exercise a two-page stack and cleanup after injected page-table preparation, bounded frame-exhaustion, and late cache-policy failures; `just process-smoke` uses this API for both bundled init and child ELFs. This is preparation, not a public spawn/exec syscall or scheduler-managed execution, so the milestone item remains open. Use `.bin` for command-line programs and `.app` for GUI applications as role-based suffixes for the same underlying format. `.app` is a Rustix single-file application suffix, not an Apple/macOS app bundle; initially require application resources to be embedded or absent.
   185	- [x] Complete and validate the initial user-mode exception policy. The diagnostic runtime terminates noncritical CPL3 faults with status `128 + vector`, while kernel-origin faults and NMI/#DF/#MC remain fatal. QEMU exercises #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE from CPL3 and #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE from CPL0; this does not provide recovery for arbitrary kernel accesses or all architectural vectors.
   186	- [ ] Define user virtual-memory regions, stack bounds/guard behavior, and a minimal anonymous allocation interface such as `mmap`/`munmap` (or a documented equivalent) before running general user programs. The diagnostic reserves ELF segments, a bounded 1–16-page initial stack, and an unmapped guard; `UserRegionTable` host tests cover first-fit anonymous reservations, overlap, overflow, invalid ranges, and capacity exhaustion. The opt-in ABI maps zero-filled RW/NX pages and exact anonymous regions up to 1 MiB; QEMU checks cross-page access, partial-unmap rejection, stale-address `EFAULT`, and teardown/frame restoration. Host tests now inject page-table preparation, bounded frame exhaustion, and late cache-policy failures during reusable process preparation and assert root/frame rollback. The `crates/rustix-user` workspace crate supplies typed syscall wrappers, `run_main`, panic reporting, short-write-safe output, allocation-free formatting, and an opt-in spinlock-protected size-class allocator backed by one-page mmap calls. Host tests cover the allocator's alignment, reuse, class separation, and exhaustion behavior; `rustix-init` opts in and validates `Vec`/`Box` allocation in `just process-smoke`. The allocator supports requests through 2048 bytes with alignment no greater than 2048, and retains mapped pages until process teardown. This is not a general userspace process runtime: independent downstream-app integration and general process scheduling remain outstanding.
   188	- [x] Complete the first controlled user-visible target: a reproducibly built minimal `no_std` `rustix-init` loaded from a non-filesystem source. `just process-smoke` runs init and a separately bundled child ELF in Ring 3, exercises ABI version/write/blocking wait/exit, verifies `-EFAULT`, real child status 7 with copyout retry, init status 42, kernel wait/reap, and teardown. Scheduler-backed launch/exec failure cases, exhaustive VM exhaustion, mid-PTE-write injection (not supported by the current infallible write contract), and general file-object descriptor semantics remain pending alongside those features.

+/// A bounded multi-page anonymous mapping returned by [`mmap_region`].
+pub struct MappedPages {
+    address: u64,
+    length: usize,
+}
+
+impl MappedPages {
+    pub const fn address(&self) -> u64 {
+        self.address
+    }
+
+    pub const fn length(&self) -> usize {
+        self.length
+    }
+
+    pub const fn as_mut_ptr(&self) -> *mut u8 {
+        self.address as *mut u8
+    }
+}
+
+/// Map a zero-filled read/write, non-executable anonymous region.
+///
+/// The requested size is rounded up to a 4096-byte page. The current bounded
+/// ABI supports regions up to [`MAX_MAPPED_REGION_SIZE`] bytes.
+pub fn mmap_region(requested_length: usize) -> Result<MappedPages, SyscallError> {
+    let address = decode_result(syscall(
+        SYS_MMAP_REGION,
+        [requested_length as u64, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
+    ))?;
+    let rounded_length = requested_length
+        .checked_add(USER_PAGE_SIZE - 1)
+        .ok_or(SyscallError::Overflow)?
+        & !(USER_PAGE_SIZE - 1);
+    Ok(MappedPages {
+        address,
+        length: rounded_length,
+    })
+}

Milestone 0's local exit criteria are met, and Milestone 1's validation criteria are met for the current Limine path. This is a kernel-mode shell, not a user process. An opt-in diagnostic QEMU path runs separately bundled init and child ELFs in Ring 3 and validates ABI version/write/EFAULT, one-page and multi-page anonymous mappings, `Vec`/`Box` allocation through the shared userspace runtime, real child execution during a suspended parent wait, status-copyout failure/retry, child and init reap, root teardown, and CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE exits. The kernel process module now provides reusable static-ELF/root/guard/stack preparation (up to 16 initial stack pages) with retryable ownership cleanup; host tests cover multi-page zeroing and injected table-preparation/cache-policy/frame-exhaustion rollback. The opt-in diagnostic uses this API for both bundled init and child, but its synchronous IF-disabled nested runner is not general scheduler-backed process launching, so Milestone 4 remains in progress. A bounded physical-frame allocator is initialized from the validated map and reported by `meminfo`; token ownership and failed-deallocation semantics are documented and host-tested. The boot transition owns an activated clone of Limine's reachable page-table hierarchy, and the global heap begins with a 256 KiB BSS arena and 128 allocation records, with bounded frame-backed growth up to 1 MiB. The Limine base-revision 3 HHDM scope and a conservative initial mapping/alias/cache policy are documented. Pure host-tested helpers validate mapping ranges/PTE bits, parse PAT layouts, validate captured MTRR snapshots, combine PAT/MTRR types under normal caching according to Intel SDM Table 11-7, and select a PAT index only when it yields one effective type across an aligned physical range. Boot validates the captured state and prints a diagnostic effective type at PA 0. The transition preserves inherited cache attributes, adjusts kernel-image HHDM aliases to R/NX or RW/NX, and checks the effective PAT index against the inherited mapping. `BootInfo` records raw CR3 and a validated decode of its root physical address and low-bit interpretation. Checked HHDM access is limited to complete allocator-owned usable frames and cloned table frames; the active root owns its cloned table pages while inherited leaf frames remain loader-owned. The complete linker-defined kernel-image span and requested 256 KiB initial boot-stack span are captured and validated; Limine does not report any larger allocation bounds or guard status, so Rustix does not infer a guard page. The heap has bounded frame-backed growth and an IRQ-save lock; allocation remains prohibited in IRQ/exception context. ACPI support includes bounded host-tested RSDP/SDT/RSDT/XSDT/MADT parsing and a read-only/NX boot reader that copies validated MADT data into owned state. Rustix has a tested single-vCPU APIC/PIT IRQ path, cooperative and timer-preemptive scheduling, IRQ-save locks, guarded kernel threads, bounded frame-backed heap growth, and interrupt-driven UART/PS/2 queues with a polling fallback. SMP, general-purpose process scheduling, a persistent filesystem, and Unix compatibility remain absent. The documented syscall ABI and process-root primitives are exercised only by an opt-in diagnostic process. Kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal; the opt-in user path terminates CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE and `just fault-smoke` separately verifies those four exceptions halt at CPL0. This is not a general recovery policy or physical-hardware validation. On 2026-10-21, `just verify` passed after adding CR3 decoding and the pure MTRR resolver, including host tests, target check, release build, ISO creation, and QEMU prompt smoke. On 2026-10-22, `just verify` passed after adding bounded read-only MTRR register capture and validated PAT/MTRR policy resolution. On 2026-10-24, the final `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` runs passed after review. QEMU verified the 256 KiB stack request, cloned-root CR3 transition, kernel HHDM alias hardening, heap alignment/reuse/exhaustion probe, and shell prompt; the current emulator reports CR4.PGE clear, so it exercised CR3 invalidation with PGE disabled, while the PGE-toggle path was statically reviewed but not exercised. Milestone 2's local exit criteria are met. Hosted CI passed on the published `dev` commit, but it does not cover today's uncommitted work or establish physical-hardware behavior, a clean-room mapping policy, or exhaustive alias coverage. On 2026-11-07, `just verify` passed with 127 host tests and BIOS/OVMF QEMU coverage for APIC/PIT delivery, active mapping/TLB invalidation, cooperative scheduling, and UART/PS/2 input wakeups. On 2026-11-13, `just verify` passed with 130 host tests and extended OVMF coverage for IRQ-save lock IF restoration, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE context preservation, and input wakeups. Milestone 3's single-vCPU exit criteria are met. Milestone 4 is in progress: after the child-runner change, `just process-smoke` validates a real child, blocking wait, copyout retry, teardown, and the CPL3/CPL0 exception matrix has passed. The runner is diagnostic-only; userspace spawn/exec, general process scheduling and scheduler-owned/reclaimed stacks, exhaustive VM exhaustion/mid-PTE-write injection, and normal-boot userspace remain pending. SMP and physical-hardware validation remain pending.

    /// Register a child of a currently running process.
    pub fn spawn(&mut self, parent: ProcessId) -> Result<ProcessId, ProcessTableError> {
        let parent_record = self
            .record(parent)
            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidParent)?;
        if parent_record.state != ProcessState::Running {
            return Err(ProcessTableError::ParentExited);
        }
        self.insert(parent, parent_record.descriptors)
    }

    /// Record an exit status without reclaiming the process identity.
    pub fn exit(&mut self, pid: ProcessId, status: i32) -> Result<(), ProcessTableError> {
        let index = self
            .records
            .iter()

            .ok_or(ProcessTableError::InvalidProcess)?;
        let record = self.records[index]

pub fn initialize_thread_context_stack(
    stack: &mut [usize],
    saved_registers: [usize; 6],
    trampoline: usize,
) -> Option<usize> {
    const REGISTER_SLOTS: usize = 6;
    const FRAME_SLOTS: usize = REGISTER_SLOTS + 1;
    let word_size = core::mem::size_of::<usize>();
    let frame_bytes = FRAME_SLOTS.checked_mul(word_size)?;
    let stack_bytes = stack.len().checked_mul(word_size)?;
    let stack_start = stack.as_mut_ptr() as usize;
    let stack_end = stack_start.checked_add(stack_bytes)?;
    let frame_start = stack_end.checked_sub(frame_bytes)? & !15usize;
    let frame_offset = frame_start.checked_sub(stack_start)?;
    if frame_offset % word_size != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let first_slot = frame_offset / word_size;
    let frame_end = first_slot.checked_add(FRAME_SLOTS)?;
    if frame_end > stack.len() || frame_start & 15 != 0 {
        return None;
    }

    stack[first_slot..first_slot + REGISTER_SLOTS].copy_from_slice(&saved_registers);

pub const fn limine_x86_64_stack_bounds(
    entry_rsp: u64,
    virtual_bits: u8,
    stack_size: u64,
) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {
    if entry_rsp & 0xf != 8 {
        return None;
    }
    let Some(stack_end) = entry_rsp.checked_add(8) else {
        return None;
    };
    if stack_size < LIMINE_X86_64_MIN_STACK_SIZE {
        return None;
    }
    let Some(stack_start) = stack_end.checked_sub(stack_size) else {
        return None;
    };
    let stack_last = stack_end - 1;
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_start, virtual_bits)
        || !is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_last, virtual_bits)
    {
        return None;
    }
    let sign_bit = 1u64 << (virtual_bits - 1);
    if stack_start & sign_bit != stack_last & sign_bit {
        return None;
    }
    Some((stack_start, stack_end))
}

    pub fn cleanup<M: crate::paging::CandidatePageTableMemory>(
        mut self,
        roots: &mut crate::paging::ProcessAddressSpaceRoots<'_, '_, '_, M>,
        allocator: &mut crate::frame::FrameAllocator,
    ) -> Result<(), Self> {
        if let Some(process) = self.process.take() {
            if roots.destroy(allocator, process).is_err() {
                self.process = Some(process);
                return Err(self);
            }
        }
        if let Some(frame) = self.frame.take() {
            if let Err(error) = allocator.deallocate(frame) {
                self.frame = Some(error.frame);
                return Err(self);
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

//! Checked x86_64 mapping policy and a bounded owned page-table builder.
//!
//! Pure helpers validate addresses, permissions, and cache policy. Candidate
//! table access is delegated to an unsafe backend contract. This module never
//! writes CR3; callers may activate a validated hierarchy through the explicit
//! unsafe ownership marker after performing their architecture-specific switch.

use crate::frame::{Frame, FrameAllocator, FrameError};
use crate::memory::{
    is_canonical_virtual_address, physical_range_fits_address_width, HhdmAddressError, MemoryMap,
    RegionKind, ValidatedAcpiSpan, ValidatedMmioSpan,
};

/// Base page size supported by the initial Rustix mapping policy.
pub const PAGE_SIZE: u64 = 4096;

/// The physical root address and interpretation of CR3's low bits.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cr3Root {
    physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
}

impl Cr3Root {
    pub const fn physical_address(self) -> u64 {
        self.physical_address
    }

    pub const fn low_bits(self) -> Cr3LowBits {
        self.low_bits
    }
}

/// CR3's low bits are either a PCID or the paging-structure cache controls.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3LowBits {
    Pcid(u16),
    CacheControls {
        page_level_write_through: bool,
        page_level_cache_disable: bool,
    },
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3Error {
    UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth,
    InvalidRootAddress,
    ReservedBits,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cr3RootAccessError {
    NotBootloaderReclaimable,
    Hhdm(HhdmAddressError),
}

/// Decode the currently active CR3 value without dereferencing its root table.
///
/// The caller supplies the reported physical-address width and whether CR4.PCIDE
/// is active, since those determine the valid address and low-bit encodings.
/// Encode a replacement CR3 value while preserving the active low-bit mode.
///
/// PCID is retained but the no-flush bit is always cleared so the selected PCID
/// is invalidated on load. Legacy PWT/PCD controls are preserved unchanged.
pub fn encode_cr3_value(
    root_physical_address: u64,
    low_bits: Cr3LowBits,
    physical_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3Error> {
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }
    let root_end = root_physical_address
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress)?;
    if root_physical_address & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(
            root_physical_address,
            root_end,
            physical_address_bits,
        )
    {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidRootAddress);
    }
    let low = match low_bits {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid(pcid) if pcid <= 0x0fff => u64::from(pcid),
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid(_) => return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits),
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through,
            page_level_cache_disable,
        } => {
            (u64::from(page_level_write_through) << 3) | (u64::from(page_level_cache_disable) << 4)
        }
    };
    Ok(root_physical_address | low)
}

pub fn parse_cr3_root(
    raw: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    pcid_enabled: bool,
) -> Result<Cr3Root, Cr3Error> {
    let physical_address_bits =
        physical_address_bits.ok_or(Cr3Error::UnknownPhysicalAddressWidth)?;
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&physical_address_bits) {
        return Err(Cr3Error::InvalidPhysicalAddressWidth);
    }

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let low_mask = if pcid_enabled {
        PAGE_SIZE - 1
    } else {
        (1 << 3) | (1 << 4)
    };
    if raw & !(physical_mask | low_mask) != 0 {
        return Err(Cr3Error::ReservedBits);
    }

    let low_bits = if pcid_enabled {
        Cr3LowBits::Pcid((raw & (PAGE_SIZE - 1)) as u16)
    } else {
        Cr3LowBits::CacheControls {
            page_level_write_through: raw & (1 << 3) != 0,
            page_level_cache_disable: raw & (1 << 4) != 0,
        }
    };

    Ok(Cr3Root {
        physical_address: raw & physical_mask,
        low_bits,
    })
}

/// Calculate the protocol-backed HHDM address of Limine's inherited root page.
///
/// This requires the root page to be wholly contained in bootloader-reclaimable
/// memory, as specified for Limine page tables. It does not dereference the page
/// or prove that the active hierarchy contains the HHDM mapping.
pub fn inherited_cr3_root_hhdm_address(
    root: Cr3Root,
    memory_map: &MemoryMap,
    hhdm_offset: u64,
    physical_address_bits: Option<u8>,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<u64, Cr3RootAccessError> {
    let physical_start = root.physical_address();
    let physical_end = physical_start
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm(HhdmAddressError::AddressOverflow))?;
    if !memory_map.range_is_within_region_kind(
        physical_start,
        physical_end,
        RegionKind::BootloaderReclaimable,
    ) {
        return Err(Cr3RootAccessError::NotBootloaderReclaimable);
    }
    memory_map
        .limine_hhdm_address(
            hhdm_offset,
            physical_start,
            PAGE_SIZE,
            physical_address_bits,
            virtual_address_bits,
        )
        .map_err(Cr3RootAccessError::Hhdm)
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageLevel {
    Pml5,
    Pml4,
    Pdpt,
    Pd,
    Pt,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageWalkConfig {
    pub levels: u8,
    pub physical_address_bits: u8,
    pub virtual_address_bits: u8,
    pub nx_enabled: bool,
    pub page_2m_supported: bool,
    pub page_1g_supported: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PageTranslation {
    pub physical_address: u64,
    pub leaf_physical_base: u64,
    pub page_size: u64,
    pub permissions: PagePermissions,
    pub pat_index: u8,
    pub raw_leaf_entry: u64,
}

impl PageTranslation {
    /// Compare effective mapping policy while allowing equivalent large-page splits.
    ///
    /// Physical address, permissions, PAT index, global/software flags, and
    /// other stable leaf attributes must match. Leaf size, physical base, and
    /// hardware-maintained accessed/dirty bits may differ after a page split.
    pub const fn same_effective_mapping(self, other: Self) -> bool {
        const IGNORED_LEAF_BITS: u64 = PTE_ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK | (1 << 5) | (1 << 6) | (1 << 7);

        self.physical_address == other.physical_address
            && self.permissions.writable == other.permissions.writable
            && self.permissions.executable == other.permissions.executable
            && self.permissions.user_accessible == other.permissions.user_accessible
            && self.pat_index == other.pat_index
            && self.raw_leaf_entry & !IGNORED_LEAF_BITS == other.raw_leaf_entry & !IGNORED_LEAF_BITS
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageWalkOutcome {
    NotPresent { level: PageLevel },
    Mapped(PageTranslation),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageTableEntryError {
    PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
    NxDisabled,
    LargePageUnsupported,
    LargePageAtInvalidLevel,
    LargePageMisaligned,
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PageWalkError<E> {
    InvalidConfiguration,
    NonCanonicalAddress,
    InvalidRoot,
    InvalidEntry {
        level: PageLevel,
        error: PageTableEntryError,
    },
    Reader(E),
}

/// Read one raw entry from a table at a validated physical page address.
pub trait PageTableReader {
    type Error;

    fn read_entry(&self, table_physical: u64, index: u16) -> Result<u64, Self::Error>;
}

/// Translate one virtual address by following at most five page-table entries.
///
/// The reader owns all physical-memory access policy. This walker does not turn
/// physical addresses into pointers, modify tables, or infer effective cache
/// types from the leaf PAT selector.
pub fn walk_virtual_address<R: PageTableReader>(
    reader: &R,
    root: Cr3Root,
    virtual_address: u64,
    config: PageWalkConfig,
) -> Result<PageWalkOutcome, PageWalkError<R::Error>> {
    if !(12..=MAX_PTE_PHYSICAL_ADDRESS_BITS).contains(&config.physical_address_bits)
        || (config.levels != 4 && config.levels != 5)
        || config.virtual_address_bits != if config.levels == 4 { 48 } else { 57 }
    {
        return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidConfiguration);
    }
    if !is_canonical_virtual_address(virtual_address, config.virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(PageWalkError::NonCanonicalAddress);
    }
    let root_physical = root.physical_address();
    let root_end = root_physical
        .checked_add(PAGE_SIZE)
        .ok_or(PageWalkError::InvalidRoot)?;
    if root_physical & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) != 0
        || !physical_range_fits_address_width(root_physical, root_end, config.physical_address_bits)
    {
        return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidRoot);
    }

    const PRESENT: u64 = 1;
    const WRITABLE: u64 = 1 << 1;
    const USER: u64 = 1 << 2;
    const WRITE_THROUGH: u64 = 1 << 3;
    const CACHE_DISABLE: u64 = 1 << 4;
    const PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT: u64 = 1 << 7;
    const LARGE_PAGE_PAT: u64 = 1 << 12;
    const NO_EXECUTE: u64 = 1 << 63;
    const ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK: u64 = 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000;

    let physical_mask = ((1u64 << config.physical_address_bits) - 1) & !(PAGE_SIZE - 1);
    let mut table_physical = root_physical;
    let mut writable = true;
    let mut user_accessible = true;
    let mut executable = true;
    let mut level_number = config.levels;

    loop {
        let shift = 12 + 9 * (level_number - 1);
        let index = ((virtual_address >> shift) & 0x1ff) as u16;
        let entry = reader
            .read_entry(table_physical, index)
            .map_err(PageWalkError::Reader)?;
        let level = match level_number {
            5 => PageLevel::Pml5,
            4 => PageLevel::Pml4,
            3 => PageLevel::Pdpt,
            2 => PageLevel::Pd,
            1 => PageLevel::Pt,
            _ => return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidConfiguration),
        };
        if entry & PRESENT == 0 {
            return Ok(PageWalkOutcome::NotPresent { level });
        }

        let address_field = entry & ADDRESS_FIELD_MASK;
        if address_field & !physical_mask != 0 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
            });
        }
        if !config.nx_enabled && entry & NO_EXECUTE != 0 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::NxDisabled,
            });
        }
        writable &= entry & WRITABLE != 0;
        user_accessible &= entry & USER != 0;
        executable &= entry & NO_EXECUTE == 0;

        let large_page = level_number > 1 && entry & PAGE_SIZE_OR_PAT != 0;
        let leaf_shift = if level_number == 1 {
            12
        } else if large_page && level_number == 2 && config.page_2m_supported {
            21
        } else if large_page && level_number == 3 && config.page_1g_supported {
            30
        } else if large_page && level_number <= 3 {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageUnsupported,
            });
        } else if large_page {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageAtInvalidLevel,
            });
        } else {
            table_physical = address_field;
            level_number -= 1;
            continue;
        };

        if large_page {
            let reserved_alignment_bits = ((1u64 << leaf_shift) - 1) & !0x1fff;
            if entry & reserved_alignment_bits != 0 {
                return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                    level,
                    error: PageTableEntryError::LargePageMisaligned,
                });
            }
        }
        let page_size = 1u64 << leaf_shift;
        let leaf_physical_base = address_field & !(page_size - 1);
        let leaf_physical_end =
            leaf_physical_base
                .checked_add(page_size)
                .ok_or(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                    level,
                    error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
                })?;
        if !physical_range_fits_address_width(
            leaf_physical_base,
            leaf_physical_end,
            config.physical_address_bits,
        ) {
            return Err(PageWalkError::InvalidEntry {
                level,
                error: PageTableEntryError::PhysicalAddressOutOfRange,
