/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS, exception gates, and device IRQ gates.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[5]).write(USER_DATA_DESCRIPTOR);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[6]).write(USER_CODE_DESCRIPTOR);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 7]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let irq_stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(irq_stub_table).cast::<usize>();
    for vector in IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains one stub for each allocated vector.
        let handler = unsafe { irq_stubs.add(vector - IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR).read() } as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }
    // Vector 0x80 is reserved from device allocation and uses its own DPL-3
    // interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ dispatch path.
    // SAFETY: The assembly defines this dedicated entry stub in the kernel image.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::user_interrupt_gate(
                rustix_syscall_stub as *const () as usize as u64,
            ));
    }

    // SAFETY: The final table entry is the dedicated 0xff spurious-IRQ stub.
    let spurious_handler =
        unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + IRQ_UNWIRED_COUNT).read() } as u64;
    // SAFETY: The APIC spurious vector is a valid IDT index.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(spurious_handler, 0));
    }
    // Vectors 0xf0-0xfe have no registered source; wire them to a controlled
    // fatal stop (through the shared dispatch, which halts) instead of leaving
    // non-present gates that would cascade into #GP with no diagnostics.
    for vector in IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_UNWIRED_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table provides one stub for each vector.
        let handler =
            unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + (vector - IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR)) }.read()
                as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: Every architectural exception gate is initialized in static storage.
    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Configure the active user virtual-address width used to sanitize syscall returns.
///
/// Call after boot CPU discovery and before any CPL3 code can execute.
pub fn configure_user_address_width(virtual_address_bits: u8) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.store(virtual_address_bits, Ordering::Release);
    Ok(())
}

/// Errors returned while selecting the ring-0 entry stack for a user context.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum KernelEntryStackError {
    InvalidVirtualAddressWidth,
    NonCanonical,
    NotKernelAddress,
    Misaligned,
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserRuntimeError {
    InterruptsEnabled,
    AlreadyInstalled,
    NotInstalled,
    InvalidEntryState,
}

/// Select the stack used by the next privilege transition from CPL3 to CPL0.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must already be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and
/// `stack_top` must be the aligned top of a live, writable supervisor stack that
/// is mapped in the active address space and every address space that may run
/// before this value is changed again. Callers must update it before entering a
/// different process. The function validates the address shape, not the mapping
/// or ownership of the stack memory.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn set_kernel_entry_stack(
    stack_top: u64,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    if stack_top & 0xf != 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::Misaligned);
    }
    if !rustix_kernel::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_top, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NonCanonical);
    }
    if stack_top & (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1)) == 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NotKernelAddress);
    }

    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);
    // SAFETY: The function contract requires initialized TSS storage; the field
    // is packed, so write without creating an aligned reference to it.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(stack_top) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Restore TSS.RSP0 to the bootstrap ring-0 stack.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and the
/// caller must be executing on a different live stack before the restore.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn restore_bootstrap_kernel_entry_stack(
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: `RING0_STACK` is the initialized, fixed-size bootstrap entry stack.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: This function's contract establishes TSS initialization and IF=0.
    unsafe { set_kernel_entry_stack(ring0_top, virtual_address_bits) }
}

/// Install the syscall callback for one synchronously entered user process.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, no other CPU may access this state, and
/// `context` must remain live until the callback is cleared after user return.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn install_user_syscall_handler(
    handler: UserSyscallHandler,
    exception_handler: UserExceptionHandler,
) -> Result<(), UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and the first implementation is single-vCPU.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::AlreadyInstalled);
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the function context live until clearing it.
    unsafe {
        runtime.write(Some(UserSyscallRuntime {
            handler,
            exception_handler,
        }))
    };
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and assembly reads this single-vCPU pointer only while
    // a Ring 3 entry is active.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_ACTIVE_USER_ENTRY).write(core::ptr::null_mut()) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Remove the user-process syscall callback after returning to the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, and no syscall callback may be in flight.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn clear_user_syscall_handler() {
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and no user-entry trampoline may remain active when
    // clearing the callback or its process-local state.
    if !unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_ACTIVE_USER_ENTRY).read() }.is_null() {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: The API contract guarantees single-vCPU exclusion with IF clear.
    unsafe { runtime.write(None) };
}

/// Request the syscall/exception assembly exit path after restoring the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// The kernel root must be active, the process root must no longer be active,
/// and execution must be on this single CPU with maskable interrupts disabled.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn request_user_process_exit(status: i32) {
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and the active entry points to the live process state
    // whose syscall or exception callback is currently executing.
    let state = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_ACTIVE_USER_ENTRY).read() };
    if state.is_null() {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*state).exit_status).write(status);
        core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Release);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*state).exit_pending).write(1);
    }
}

/// Run a callback on a distinct live supervisor stack and return on the
/// original stack. The callback must return normally.
///
/// # Safety
/// Enter a validated user frame and return only through the process-exit path.
///
/// # Safety
/// The process root must already be active in CR3, TSS.RSP0 must point to a live
/// supervisor stack mapped in both roots, syscall and user-fault callbacks must
/// be installed, and maskable interrupts must be disabled.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn enter_user(
    frame: rustix_kernel::syscall::ValidatedUserIretFrame,
    state: *mut UserEntryState,
    syscall_context: *mut (),
) -> Result<i32, UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_none() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::NotInstalled);
    }
    if state.is_null() || (state as usize) & 0xf != 0 || syscall_context.is_null() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InvalidEntryState);
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller provides one unique, aligned, live state record for
    // this user entry; it remains writable until the entry returns.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*state).syscall_context).write(syscall_context) };
    let frame = frame.into_raw();
    // SAFETY: The caller establishes the root, stack, callback, and fault
    // policy invariants. The assembly returns only after this entry exits.
    Ok(unsafe { rustix_enter_user(&frame, state) })
}

/// Invoke a callback on a dedicated supervisor continuation stack.
///
/// # Safety
/// The caller must uphold `rustix_call_on_stack`'s mapping/lifetime contract and
/// must not retain references into the target stack across the call.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn call_on_kernel_stack(
    stack_top: u64,
    entry: extern "C" fn(*mut ()) -> i32,
    context: *mut (),
) -> i32 {
    // SAFETY: The caller proves the stack and callback satisfy the assembly ABI.
    unsafe { rustix_call_on_stack(stack_top, entry, context) }
}

/// Register one callback for an allocated device IRQ vector.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must keep the IRQ source masked while registering and ensure it
/// is masked whenever this callback is dispatched. The caller must serialize
/// registration against IRQ dispatch on every CPU. `handler` must not allocate,
/// format output, block, or unwind; it runs with IF disabled and owns the EOI.
/// The source must remain masked until all handler state is ready.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn register_irq_handler(
    vector: u8,
    handler: IrqHandler,
) -> Result<(), IrqRegistrationError> {
    let vector = vector as usize;
    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR).contains(&vector) {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InvalidVector);
    }

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: This reads RFLAGS at CPL 0; the temporary push/pop is balanced.
    unsafe {
        asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags));
    }
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }

    // SAFETY: The API contract requires registration to be serialized with IRQ
    // dispatch, and the vector has been checked against the table bounds.
    let slot = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector)
    };
    // SAFETY: `slot` points into the initialized static callback table.
    if unsafe { slot.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::AlreadyRegistered);
    }
    // SAFETY: Registration is serialized by the caller's masking/IF contract.
    unsafe { slot.write(Some(handler)) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Device IRQ target called by the normalized assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_irq_dispatch(vector: u64) {
    // SAFETY: guard records this entry frame for the heap's debug checks; it
    // decrements automatically on every return path.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    if vector == APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR as u64 {
        return;
    }

    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR as u64..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR as u64).contains(&vector) {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }

    // SAFETY: Interrupt gates clear IF, and registration's safety contract
    // serializes writes against this read. No mutable reference is created.
    let handler = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector as usize)
            .read()
    };
    match handler {
        Some(handler) => handler(),
        None => fatal_irq_halt(),
    }
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_syscall_dispatch(context: *mut rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallContext) {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{
        sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame, SyscallArguments, UserIretFrame,
    };

    // SAFETY: The assembly entry is reached only through the DPL-3 syscall gate;
    // the stack pointer refers to its normalized GPR and hardware return frame.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    let Some(context) = (unsafe { context.as_mut() }) else {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    };
    let address_bits = USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if address_bits == 0 {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let frame = UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: context.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: context.code_selector,
        flags: context.flags,
        stack_pointer: context.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: context.stack_selector,
    };
    let frame = match sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(frame, address_bits) {
        Ok(frame) => frame.into_raw(),
        Err(_) => fatal_irq_halt(),
    };
    context.instruction_pointer = frame.instruction_pointer;
    context.code_selector = frame.code_selector;
    context.flags = frame.flags;
    context.stack_pointer = frame.stack_pointer;
    context.stack_selector = frame.stack_selector;

    let arguments = SyscallArguments {
        rdi: context.rdi,
        rsi: context.rsi,
        rdx: context.rdx,
        r10: context.r10,
        r8: context.r8,
        r9: context.r9,
    };
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    let result = {
        let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
        // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the function table.
        let runtime = unsafe { runtime.read() };
        if let Some(runtime) = runtime {
            let state = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_ACTIVE_USER_ENTRY).read() };
            if state.is_null() {
                fatal_irq_halt();
            }
            // SAFETY: The active process state was installed by `enter_user` and
            // remains live on its kernel context while this syscall is handled.
            let callback_context = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!((*state).syscall_context).read() };
            (runtime.handler)(context, callback_context)
        } else {
            fallback_syscall_result(context.rax, arguments)
        }
    };
    #[cfg(not(feature = "probe-user-process"))]
    let result = fallback_syscall_result(context.rax, arguments);
    context.rax = result as u64;
}

fn fallback_syscall_result(
    number: u64,
    arguments: rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallArguments,
) -> i64 {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{decode_syscall, SyscallError, SyscallRequest, ABI_VERSION};

    match decode_syscall(number, arguments) {
        Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion) => ABI_VERSION as i64,
        Ok(
            SyscallRequest::Exit { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Write { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Wait { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Mmap { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Munmap { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::MmapRegion { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::MunmapRegion { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Close { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Duplicate { .. },
        ) => SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(),
        Err(error) => error.return_value(),
    }
}

fn fatal_irq_halt() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Unknown device interrupts are fatal and must not be retried.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    if context.cs & 3 == 3 && !matches!(context.vector, 2 | 8 | 18) {
        let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
        // SAFETY: Exceptions arrive with IF clear; the diagnostic process runtime
        // is installed only for the synchronous single-vCPU user entry.
        if let Some(runtime) = unsafe { runtime.read() } {
            let state = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_ACTIVE_USER_ENTRY).read() };
            if state.is_null() {
                fatal_irq_halt();
            }
            // SAFETY: The active process entry remains live through its exception
            // callback and exit trampoline.
            let callback_context = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!((*state).syscall_context).read() };
            let depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
            crate::kprintln!(
                "USER EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x}; terminating process",
                context.vector,
                exception_name(context.vector),
                context.error_code
            );
            if context.vector == 14 {
                let fault_address: u64;
                // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is privileged and this handler runs at CPL0.
                unsafe {
                    asm!(
                        "mov {}, cr2",
                        out(reg) fault_address,
                        options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)
                    )
                };
                crate::kprintln!("user page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
            }
            if (runtime.exception_handler)(context.vector, callback_context) {
                core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Acquire);
                // SAFETY: The callback's contract guarantees it has restored the
                // kernel root and marked the process root inactive before setting
                // this entry's exit flag.
                if unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!((*state).exit_pending).read() } != 0 {
                    drop(depth);
                    // SAFETY: The exit callback restored CR3, completed teardown
                    // ownership transitions, and IF remains disabled. The asm
                    // trampoline restores the kernel FPU/stack continuation.
                    unsafe { rustix_user_exception_exit() };
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // SAFETY: guard records this fatal entry frame; fatal paths never return.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    // A fault raised while this handler is running (including a #DF on the
    // IST stack) must not re-enter the printing path; stop silently instead.
    if IN_FATAL_EXCEPTION.swap(true, Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant fatal diagnostics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    crate::kprintln!(
        "FATAL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} SS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RSP={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.ss,
        context.rflags,
        context.rsp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe {
            asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags))
        };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

global_asm!(
    r#"
    .section .text
    .code64

    .macro RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR name, number
    .global \name
    .type \name, @function
\name:
    push 0
    push \number
    jmp rustix_exception_common
    .endm

    .macro RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR name, number
    .global \name
    .type \name, @function
\name:
    push \number
    jmp rustix_exception_common
    .endm

    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_0, 0
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_1, 1
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_2, 2
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_3, 3
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_4, 4
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_5, 5
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_6, 6
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_7, 7
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_8, 8
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_9, 9
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_10, 10
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_11, 11
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_12, 12
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_13, 13
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_14, 14
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_15, 15
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_16, 16
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_17, 17
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_18, 18
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_19, 19
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_20, 20
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_21, 21
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_22, 22
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_23, 23
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_24, 24
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_25, 25
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_26, 26
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_27, 27
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_28, 28
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_29, 29
    RUSTIX_ISR_ERROR rustix_exception_30, 30
    RUSTIX_ISR_NO_ERROR rustix_exception_31, 31

    rustix_exception_common:
    cld
    push rax
    push rbx
    push rcx
    push rdx
    push rsi
    push rdi
    push rbp
    push r8
    push r9
    push r10
    push r11
    push r12
    push r13
    push r14
    push r15
    mov rdi, rsp
    and rsp, -16

    fn rustix_user_exception_exit() -> !;
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    #[link_name = "rustix_call_on_stack"]
    fn rustix_call_on_stack(
        stack_top: u64,
        entry: extern "C" fn(*mut ()) -> i32,
        context: *mut (),
    ) -> i32;
}

/// Install a private kernel GDT/TSS, exception gates, and device IRQ gates.
///
/// The bootstrap runs with maskable interrupts disabled. This routine leaves
/// them disabled and does not modify CR3 or the inherited page-table hierarchy.
pub fn initialize() {
    // SAFETY: Single-core bootstrap ownership; the descriptor tables are private
    // static storage and are initialized before any gate is loaded.
    unsafe {
        asm!("cli", options(nomem, nostack));
        initialize_tss();
        initialize_gdt();
        initialize_idt();
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_tss() {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    let double_fault_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(DOUBLE_FAULT_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: These pointers refer to the ends of distinct, aligned static stacks.
    let double_fault_top = unsafe { double_fault_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);

    // The architectural TSS fields are packed; use unaligned raw writes rather
    // than creating references to their potentially unaligned storage.
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(ring0_top);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).ist1).write_unaligned(double_fault_top);
    }
}

unsafe fn initialize_gdt() {
    let tss_base = core::ptr::addr_of!(TSS) as u64;
    let tss_limit = (size_of::<TaskStateSegment>() - 1) as u64;
    let low = (tss_limit & 0xffff)
        | ((tss_base & 0x00ff_ffff) << 16)
        | (TSS_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE << 40)
        | ((tss_limit & 0x000f_0000) << 32)
        | ((tss_base & 0xff00_0000) << 32);
    let high = tss_base >> 32;

    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[0]).write(0);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[1]).write(0x00af_9a00_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[2]).write(0x00cf_9200_0000_ffff);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[3]).write(low);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[4]).write(high);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[5]).write(USER_DATA_DESCRIPTOR);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(GDT[6]).write(USER_CODE_DESCRIPTOR);
    }

    let gdtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<[u64; 7]>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(GDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: `GDT` and its TSS descriptor are initialized and remain live.
    unsafe { rustix_load_gdt(&gdtr) };
}

unsafe fn initialize_idt() {
    let idt_entries = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IDT.0).cast::<IdtEntry>();
    let stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(exception_stub_table).cast::<usize>();

    for vector in 0..EXCEPTION_COUNT {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains exactly 32 stub addresses.
        let handler = unsafe { stubs.add(vector).read() } as u64;
        let ist = if vector == 8 { 1 } else { 0 };
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, ist));
        }
    }

    let irq_stubs = core::ptr::addr_of!(irq_stub_table).cast::<usize>();
    for vector in IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table contains one stub for each allocated vector.
        let handler = unsafe { irq_stubs.add(vector - IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR).read() } as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }
    // Vector 0x80 is reserved from device allocation and uses its own DPL-3
    // interrupt gate rather than the generic device-IRQ dispatch path.
    // SAFETY: The assembly defines this dedicated entry stub in the kernel image.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(USER_SYSCALL_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::user_interrupt_gate(
                rustix_syscall_stub as *const () as usize as u64,
            ));
    }

    // SAFETY: The final table entry is the dedicated 0xff spurious-IRQ stub.
    let spurious_handler =
        unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + IRQ_UNWIRED_COUNT).read() } as u64;
    // SAFETY: The APIC spurious vector is a valid IDT index.
    unsafe {
        idt_entries
            .add(APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR)
            .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(spurious_handler, 0));
    }
    // Vectors 0xf0-0xfe have no registered source; wire them to a controlled
    // fatal stop (through the shared dispatch, which halts) instead of leaving
    // non-present gates that would cascade into #GP with no diagnostics.
    for vector in IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_UNWIRED_LAST_VECTOR {
        // SAFETY: The assembly table provides one stub for each vector.
        let handler =
            unsafe { irq_stubs.add(IRQ_VECTOR_COUNT + (vector - IRQ_UNWIRED_FIRST_VECTOR)) }.read()
                as u64;
        // SAFETY: `vector` is bounded by the statically allocated 256-entry IDT.
        unsafe {
            idt_entries
                .add(vector)
                .write(IdtEntry::interrupt_gate(handler, 0));
        }
    }

    let idtr = DescriptorTablePointer {
        limit: (size_of::<IdtTable>() - 1) as u16,
        base: core::ptr::addr_of!(IDT) as u64,
    };
    // SAFETY: Every architectural exception gate is initialized in static storage.
    unsafe { asm!("lidt [{}]", in(reg) &idtr, options(readonly, nostack, preserves_flags)) };
}

/// Configure the active user virtual-address width used to sanitize syscall returns.
///
/// Call after boot CPU discovery and before any CPL3 code can execute.
pub fn configure_user_address_width(virtual_address_bits: u8) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.store(virtual_address_bits, Ordering::Release);
    Ok(())
}

/// Errors returned while selecting the ring-0 entry stack for a user context.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum KernelEntryStackError {
    InvalidVirtualAddressWidth,
    NonCanonical,
    NotKernelAddress,
    Misaligned,
}

#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
pub enum UserRuntimeError {
    InterruptsEnabled,
    AlreadyInstalled,
    NotInstalled,
    InvalidEntryState,
}

/// Select the stack used by the next privilege transition from CPL3 to CPL0.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must already be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and
/// `stack_top` must be the aligned top of a live, writable supervisor stack that
/// is mapped in the active address space and every address space that may run
/// before this value is changed again. Callers must update it before entering a
/// different process. The function validates the address shape, not the mapping
/// or ownership of the stack memory.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn set_kernel_entry_stack(
    stack_top: u64,
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    if !matches!(virtual_address_bits, 48 | 57) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::InvalidVirtualAddressWidth);
    }
    if stack_top & 0xf != 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::Misaligned);
    }
    if !rustix_kernel::memory::is_canonical_virtual_address(stack_top, virtual_address_bits) {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NonCanonical);
    }
    if stack_top & (1u64 << (virtual_address_bits - 1)) == 0 {
        return Err(KernelEntryStackError::NotKernelAddress);
    }

    let tss = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(TSS);
    // SAFETY: The function contract requires initialized TSS storage; the field
    // is packed, so write without creating an aligned reference to it.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*tss).rsp0).write_unaligned(stack_top) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Restore TSS.RSP0 to the bootstrap ring-0 stack.
///
/// # Safety
/// The TSS must be initialized, local interrupts must be disabled, and the
/// caller must be executing on a different live stack before the restore.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn restore_bootstrap_kernel_entry_stack(
    virtual_address_bits: u8,
) -> Result<(), KernelEntryStackError> {
    let ring0_stack = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RING0_STACK).cast::<u8>();
    // SAFETY: `RING0_STACK` is the initialized, fixed-size bootstrap entry stack.
    let ring0_top = unsafe { ring0_stack.add(STACK_SIZE) } as u64;
    // SAFETY: This function's contract establishes TSS initialization and IF=0.
    unsafe { set_kernel_entry_stack(ring0_top, virtual_address_bits) }
}

/// Install the syscall callback for one synchronously entered user process.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, no other CPU may access this state, and
/// `context` must remain live until the callback is cleared after user return.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn install_user_syscall_handler(
    handler: UserSyscallHandler,
    exception_handler: UserExceptionHandler,
) -> Result<(), UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and the first implementation is single-vCPU.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::AlreadyInstalled);
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller keeps the function context live until clearing it.
    unsafe {
        runtime.write(Some(UserSyscallRuntime {
            handler,
            exception_handler,
        }))
    };
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and assembly reads this single-vCPU pointer only while
    // a Ring 3 entry is active.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(RUSTIX_ACTIVE_USER_ENTRY).write(core::ptr::null_mut()) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Remove the user-process syscall callback after returning to the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// Local interrupts must be disabled, and no syscall callback may be in flight.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn clear_user_syscall_handler() {
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and no user-entry trampoline may remain active when
    // clearing the callback or its process-local state.
    if !unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_ACTIVE_USER_ENTRY).read() }.is_null() {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: The API contract guarantees single-vCPU exclusion with IF clear.
    unsafe { runtime.write(None) };
}

/// Request the syscall/exception assembly exit path after restoring the kernel root.
///
/// # Safety
/// The kernel root must be active, the process root must no longer be active,
/// and execution must be on this single CPU with maskable interrupts disabled.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn request_user_process_exit(status: i32) {
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and the active entry points to the live process state
    // whose syscall or exception callback is currently executing.
    let state = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_ACTIVE_USER_ENTRY).read() };
    if state.is_null() {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*state).exit_status).write(status);
        core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Release);
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*state).exit_pending).write(1);
    }
}

/// Run a callback on a distinct live supervisor stack and return on the
/// original stack. The callback must return normally.
///
/// # Safety
/// Enter a validated user frame and return only through the process-exit path.
///
/// # Safety
/// The process root must already be active in CR3, TSS.RSP0 must point to a live
/// supervisor stack mapped in both roots, syscall and user-fault callbacks must
/// be installed, and maskable interrupts must be disabled.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn enter_user(
    frame: rustix_kernel::syscall::ValidatedUserIretFrame,
    state: *mut UserEntryState,
    syscall_context: *mut (),
) -> Result<i32, UserRuntimeError> {
    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: The temporary stack operation is balanced at CPL 0.
    unsafe { asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags)) };
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }
    let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
    // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the runtime slot.
    if unsafe { runtime.read() }.is_none() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::NotInstalled);
    }
    if state.is_null() || (state as usize) & 0xf != 0 || syscall_context.is_null() {
        return Err(UserRuntimeError::InvalidEntryState);
    }
    // SAFETY: The caller provides one unique, aligned, live state record for
    // this user entry; it remains writable until the entry returns.
    unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*state).syscall_context).write(syscall_context) };
    let frame = frame.into_raw();
    // SAFETY: The caller establishes the root, stack, callback, and fault
    // policy invariants. The assembly returns only after this entry exits.
    Ok(unsafe { rustix_enter_user(&frame, state) })
}

/// Invoke a callback on a dedicated supervisor continuation stack.
///
/// # Safety
/// The caller must uphold `rustix_call_on_stack`'s mapping/lifetime contract and
/// must not retain references into the target stack across the call.
#[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
pub(crate) unsafe fn call_on_kernel_stack(
    stack_top: u64,
    entry: extern "C" fn(*mut ()) -> i32,
    context: *mut (),
) -> i32 {
    // SAFETY: The caller proves the stack and callback satisfy the assembly ABI.
    unsafe { rustix_call_on_stack(stack_top, entry, context) }
}

/// Register one callback for an allocated device IRQ vector.
///
/// # Safety
///
/// The caller must keep the IRQ source masked while registering and ensure it
/// is masked whenever this callback is dispatched. The caller must serialize
/// registration against IRQ dispatch on every CPU. `handler` must not allocate,
/// format output, block, or unwind; it runs with IF disabled and owns the EOI.
/// The source must remain masked until all handler state is ready.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub unsafe fn register_irq_handler(
    vector: u8,
    handler: IrqHandler,
) -> Result<(), IrqRegistrationError> {
    let vector = vector as usize;
    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR).contains(&vector) {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InvalidVector);
    }

    let flags: u64;
    // SAFETY: This reads RFLAGS at CPL 0; the temporary push/pop is balanced.
    unsafe {
        asm!("pushfq", "pop {}", out(reg) flags, options(preserves_flags));
    }
    if flags & (1 << 9) != 0 {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::InterruptsEnabled);
    }

    // SAFETY: The API contract requires registration to be serialized with IRQ
    // dispatch, and the vector has been checked against the table bounds.
    let slot = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of_mut!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector)
    };
    // SAFETY: `slot` points into the initialized static callback table.
    if unsafe { slot.read() }.is_some() {
        return Err(IrqRegistrationError::AlreadyRegistered);
    }
    // SAFETY: Registration is serialized by the caller's masking/IF contract.
    unsafe { slot.write(Some(handler)) };
    Ok(())
}

/// Device IRQ target called by the normalized assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_irq_dispatch(vector: u64) {
    // SAFETY: guard records this entry frame for the heap's debug checks; it
    // decrements automatically on every return path.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    if vector == APIC_SPURIOUS_VECTOR as u64 {
        return;
    }

    if !(IRQ_FIRST_VECTOR as u64..=IRQ_LAST_VECTOR as u64).contains(&vector) {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }

    // SAFETY: Interrupt gates clear IF, and registration's safety contract
    // serializes writes against this read. No mutable reference is created.
    let handler = unsafe {
        core::ptr::addr_of!(IRQ_HANDLERS)
            .cast::<Option<IrqHandler>>()
            .add(vector as usize)
            .read()
    };
    match handler {
        Some(handler) => handler(),
        None => fatal_irq_halt(),
    }
}

#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_syscall_dispatch(context: *mut rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallContext) {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{
        sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame, SyscallArguments, UserIretFrame,
    };

    // SAFETY: The assembly entry is reached only through the DPL-3 syscall gate;
    // the stack pointer refers to its normalized GPR and hardware return frame.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    let Some(context) = (unsafe { context.as_mut() }) else {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    };
    let address_bits = USER_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_BITS.load(Ordering::Acquire);
    if address_bits == 0 {
        fatal_irq_halt();
    }
    let frame = UserIretFrame {
        instruction_pointer: context.instruction_pointer,
        code_selector: context.code_selector,
        flags: context.flags,
        stack_pointer: context.stack_pointer,
        stack_selector: context.stack_selector,
    };
    let frame = match sanitize_user_syscall_return_frame(frame, address_bits) {
        Ok(frame) => frame.into_raw(),
        Err(_) => fatal_irq_halt(),
    };
    context.instruction_pointer = frame.instruction_pointer;
    context.code_selector = frame.code_selector;
    context.flags = frame.flags;
    context.stack_pointer = frame.stack_pointer;
    context.stack_selector = frame.stack_selector;

    let arguments = SyscallArguments {
        rdi: context.rdi,
        rsi: context.rsi,
        rdx: context.rdx,
        r10: context.r10,
        r8: context.r8,
        r9: context.r9,
    };
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    let result = {
        let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
        // SAFETY: IF is clear and only this CPU can update the function table.
        let runtime = unsafe { runtime.read() };
        if let Some(runtime) = runtime {
            let state = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_ACTIVE_USER_ENTRY).read() };
            if state.is_null() {
                fatal_irq_halt();
            }
            // SAFETY: The active process state was installed by `enter_user` and
            // remains live on its kernel context while this syscall is handled.
            let callback_context = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!((*state).syscall_context).read() };
            (runtime.handler)(context, callback_context)
        } else {
            fallback_syscall_result(context.rax, arguments)
        }
    };
    #[cfg(not(feature = "probe-user-process"))]
    let result = fallback_syscall_result(context.rax, arguments);
    context.rax = result as u64;
}

fn fallback_syscall_result(
    number: u64,
    arguments: rustix_kernel::syscall::SyscallArguments,
) -> i64 {
    use rustix_kernel::syscall::{decode_syscall, SyscallError, SyscallRequest, ABI_VERSION};

    match decode_syscall(number, arguments) {
        Ok(SyscallRequest::AbiVersion) => ABI_VERSION as i64,
        Ok(
            SyscallRequest::Exit { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Write { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Wait { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Mmap { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Munmap { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::MmapRegion { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::MunmapRegion { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Close { .. }
            | SyscallRequest::Duplicate { .. },
        ) => SyscallError::NotSupported.return_value(),
        Err(error) => error.return_value(),
    }
}

fn fatal_irq_halt() -> ! {
    loop {
        // SAFETY: Unknown device interrupts are fatal and must not be retried.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

/// Fatal exception target called by the assembly stubs.
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn rustix_exception_dispatch(context: *const ExceptionContext) -> ! {
    // SAFETY: The common assembly stub passes a pointer to its normalized stack
    // frame, which remains live for the duration of this non-returning handler.
    let context = unsafe { &*context };
    #[cfg(feature = "probe-user-process")]
    if context.cs & 3 == 3 && !matches!(context.vector, 2 | 8 | 18) {
        let runtime = core::ptr::addr_of!(USER_SYSCALL_RUNTIME);
        // SAFETY: Exceptions arrive with IF clear; the diagnostic process runtime
        // is installed only for the synchronous single-vCPU user entry.
        if let Some(runtime) = unsafe { runtime.read() } {
            let state = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!(RUSTIX_ACTIVE_USER_ENTRY).read() };
            if state.is_null() {
                fatal_irq_halt();
            }
            // SAFETY: The active process entry remains live through its exception
            // callback and exit trampoline.
            let callback_context = unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!((*state).syscall_context).read() };
            let depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
            crate::kprintln!(
                "USER EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x}; terminating process",
                context.vector,
                exception_name(context.vector),
                context.error_code
            );
            if context.vector == 14 {
                let fault_address: u64;
                // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is privileged and this handler runs at CPL0.
                unsafe {
                    asm!(
                        "mov {}, cr2",
                        out(reg) fault_address,
                        options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags)
                    )
                };
                crate::kprintln!("user page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
            }
            if (runtime.exception_handler)(context.vector, callback_context) {
                core::sync::atomic::compiler_fence(Ordering::Acquire);
                // SAFETY: The callback's contract guarantees it has restored the
                // kernel root and marked the process root inactive before setting
                // this entry's exit flag.
                if unsafe { core::ptr::addr_of!((*state).exit_pending).read() } != 0 {
                    drop(depth);
                    // SAFETY: The exit callback restored CR3, completed teardown
                    // ownership transitions, and IF remains disabled. The asm
                    // trampoline restores the kernel FPU/stack continuation.
                    unsafe { rustix_user_exception_exit() };
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // SAFETY: guard records this fatal entry frame; fatal paths never return.
    let _depth = InterruptContextGuard::enter();
    // A fault raised while this handler is running (including a #DF on the
    // IST stack) must not re-enter the printing path; stop silently instead.
    if IN_FATAL_EXCEPTION.swap(true, Ordering::Acquire) {
        loop {
            // SAFETY: Re-entrant fatal diagnostics are deliberately silent.
            unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
        }
    }
    crate::kprintln!(
        "FATAL EXCEPTION: vector {} ({}) error={:#018x} RIP={:#018x}",
        context.vector,
        exception_name(context.vector),
        context.error_code,
        context.rip
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "CS={:#06x} SS={:#06x} RFLAGS={:#018x} RSP={:#018x}",
        context.cs,
        context.ss,
        context.rflags,
        context.rsp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RAX={:#018x} RBX={:#018x} RCX={:#018x}",
        context.rax,
        context.rbx,
        context.rcx
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "RDX={:#018x} RSI={:#018x} RDI={:#018x} RBP={:#018x}",
        context.rdx,
        context.rsi,
        context.rdi,
        context.rbp
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R8={:#018x} R9={:#018x} R10={:#018x} R11={:#018x}",
        context.r8,
        context.r9,
        context.r10,
        context.r11
    );
    #[cfg(feature = "fatal-register-dump")]
    crate::kprintln!(
        "R12={:#018x} R13={:#018x} R14={:#018x} R15={:#018x}",
        context.r12,
        context.r13,
        context.r14,
        context.r15
    );

    if context.vector == 14 {
        crate::kprintln!(
            "page fault: present={} write={} user={} reserved={} instruction-fetch={}",
            context.error_code & 1 != 0,
            context.error_code & 2 != 0,
            context.error_code & 4 != 0,
            context.error_code & 8 != 0,
            context.error_code & 16 != 0
        );
        let fault_address: u64;
        // SAFETY: Reading CR2 is a privileged x86_64 operation in this handler.
        unsafe {
            asm!("mov {}, cr2", out(reg) fault_address, options(nomem, nostack, preserves_flags))
        };
        crate::kprintln!("page fault address (CR2): {:#018x}", fault_address);
    }

    loop {
        // SAFETY: Fatal exceptions are not recoverable in the current kernel.
        unsafe { asm!("cli; hlt", options(nomem, nostack)) };
    }
}

fn exception_name(vector: u64) -> &'static str {
    match vector {
        0 => "divide error",
        1 => "debug",
        2 => "non-maskable interrupt",
        3 => "breakpoint",
        4 => "overflow",
        5 => "bound range",
        6 => "invalid opcode",
        7 => "device not available",
        8 => "double fault",
        9 => "coprocessor segment overrun",
        10 => "invalid TSS",
        11 => "segment not present",
        12 => "stack-segment fault",
        13 => "general protection fault",
        14 => "page fault",
        16 => "x87 floating-point",
        17 => "alignment check",
        18 => "machine check",
        19 => "SIMD floating-point",
        20 => "virtualization",
        21 => "control protection",
        28 => "hypervisor injection",
        29 => "VMM communication",
        30 => "security exception",
        _ => "reserved or architecture-specific exception",
    }
}

# Rustix agent instructions

These instructions apply to every coding agent working in this repository. Read this file before changing code. For the architecture and detailed subsystem contracts, use the linked documents under `docs/`; this file summarizes the rules agents must preserve.

## Project mission

Rustix is an experimental 64-bit, Unix-like operating system with its own Rust kernel. Limine is the external boot protocol/loader only. Do not describe Limine, a host shell, or a userspace project as the Rustix kernel.

The kernel is `no_std` and targets `x86_64-unknown-none`. Rust is the implementation language for kernel and OS components. The repository currently uses a Python standard-library script only to assemble and smoke-test the boot image; it does not replace kernel or OS functionality.

Unix-like behavior is a long-term design goal, not a claim of POSIX compatibility. Make unsupported behavior explicit rather than approximating it silently.

## Current project status — read before planning

The source contains:

- A Limine-based x86_64 kernel entry, linker layout, serial diagnostics, and boot-memory reporting.
- Separate allocation-free `no_std` `crabshell` parser and `rustix-user` early runtime crates, plus a kernel-mode COM1 shell frontend. `rustix-user` wraps ABI-version, write, wait, exit, descriptor, and bounded anonymous-map calls; it is not yet a general userspace runtime.
- A volatile, fixed-capacity RAM filesystem used by the shell.
- A validated, fixed-capacity boot memory-map snapshot, CPUID/address-width reporting, read-only CR0 caching-mode reporting, and gated read-only EFER.NXE/IA32_PAT/MTRR reporting.
- A fixed-capacity physical frame allocator retained in `BootInfo`; Crabshell's `meminfo` command reports counts. `src/paging.rs` provides a bounded candidate-root builder with transactional owned-page mappings, and the default path clones and activates the inherited hierarchy while hardening kernel-image HHDM aliases and retaining page-table tokens. The global heap starts with a 256 KiB BSS arena and has a bounded frame-backed extension of up to 1 MiB in a reserved virtual range.
- Pure 4 KiB mapping-range validation, leaf-PTE bit encoding, PAT layout parsing, and host-tested MTRR/PAT policy in `src/paging.rs`; these helpers check alignment, address widths, canonical virtual ranges, W^X, NXE input, PAT indices, captured-register validity, MTRR overlap rules, and Intel SDM Table 11-7 effective types under normal caching. Discontinuous variable-MTRR masks are explicitly unsupported. A pure selector chooses a PAT index only when its effective type remains uniform across all MTRR boundaries in an aligned physical range, and range-bound selected attributes can encode 4 KiB leaves. The bounded candidate builder stores its unique mutable table-memory backend borrow, uses allocator-issued `Frame` tokens for table pages and leaf mappings, restricts walks to owned tables, and rolls back failures. Active candidates reject mutation and release. Boot captures CR0 caching mode, EFER.NXE, `IA32_PAT`, and a bounded MTRR snapshot read-only when supported, validates the captured state, and reports a diagnostic PA 0 resolution. QEMU checks the requested 256 KiB stack, active CR3 clone, kernel-image HHDM alias permissions/cache preservation, and heap allocation behavior; the old root and its leaf frames are not reclaimed.
- Bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT setup, fatal kernel exception handlers for vectors 0–31, and a validated single-vCPU xAPIC/I/O APIC path with masked-first IRQ routes, EOI, spurious/unexpected-vector policy, and PIT-driven preemption. The scheduler supports cooperative waits/yields and timer preemption; `src/sync.rs` provides IRQ-save locks, and timer context switches preserve x87/SSE state with FXSAVE/FXRSTOR while AVX/XSAVE remains disabled. Double faults use an IST stack and page faults report CR2. OVMF validation covers timer/preemption, UART, and PS/2 IRQ delivery; opt-in QEMU tests cover fatal CPL0 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE exceptions and Ring 3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE process exits. NMI, double fault, machine check, and all kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal; other user-exception vectors, SMP, and physical-hardware validation remain pending.

Important incomplete work:

- Milestone 0's local exit criteria were met on 2026-10-16: `just verify` passed from both the working tree and a clean detached worktree in WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04. The detached worktree had an empty `target` directory, so the run exercised fresh Limine download/host-tool compilation, formatting, 19 host tests, target check, optimized build, image creation, and the 20-second QEMU prompt smoke test. GitHub Actions run [#5](https://github.com/JustEthanCodes/rustix/actions/runs/42288095710) also passed `just verify` on the published `dev` commit `770f9c742dd07a00f6b53274ea05a1eca010d146` on 2026-11-06; it does not cover current uncommitted work.
- A separate interactive `just run` session exercised directory navigation and create/write/append/read/copy/move/list/remove operations; `cp` replaced an existing destination, `rmdir` rejected a nonempty directory and succeeded after its child was removed, and unsupported `memtest` was rejected as expected. Boot snapshot tests and QEMU boot-metadata reporting were exercised. Structural checks still cannot prove that a Limine-provided non-null pointer is mapped or readable; that remains a loader trust boundary.
- Milestone 2's local exit criteria were met on 2026-10-24 after final review and successful `just verify`, `just frame-smoke`, and `just fault-smoke` runs. The frame allocator specifies token ownership and preserves the token on failed deallocation; unique allocator-instance use is still caller-enforced. The active root is an allocator-owned clone of Limine's reachable hierarchy, with critical translations checked, kernel-image HHDM aliases set R/NX or RW/NX while PAT bits are preserved, and CR3 transitions flushing the current translations and global entries when PGE is enabled. QEMU exercised the PGE-clear CR3 reload path; the PGE-toggle path is statically reviewed but not exercised by this configuration. QEMU also exercised the 256 KiB requested stack, fixed BSS heap alignment/reuse/exhaustion, frame probes, and fatal page-fault/invalid-opcode paths. Host tests cover clone/table ownership, huge-page splitting, active-state guards, frame rollback, and heap behavior. Hosted CI passed on the published `dev` state on 2026-11-06; physical-hardware validation remains unobserved. The old root and inherited leaf frames are retained; there is no clean-room address-space policy, broad mapping policy, or frame reclamation. IRQ-safe locking exists, but allocation remains prohibited in interrupt context.
- Milestone 3's single-vCPU exit criteria were met locally on 2026-11-13: `just verify` passed with 130 host tests, target check/build, BIOS/OVMF boot, active mapping/TLB, IRQ-save lock state, non-yielding timer-preemption/FPU-preservation, cooperative wait, and UART/PS/2 input smokes. The kernel scheduler is single-vCPU and preemptive; SMP, persistent filesystem, and physical-hardware validation remain pending.
- Milestone 4 remains in progress. `process::prepare_user_program` now provides reusable static-ELF/root/guard/stack preparation, bounded to 16 initial stack pages, with retryable ownership cleanup; both bundled init and child use it. Host tests verify multi-page zeroing and rollback after injected page-table preparation, cache-policy, and bounded frame-exhaustion failures. The latest `cargo test -p rustix-kernel` passed with 191 tests, and `just process-smoke` passed with both bundled ELFs using the reusable preparation path. The parent wait still synchronously enters a kernel-prepared child on distinct PID-indexed TSS entry and continuation stacks; per-entry records now isolate continuation RSP, exit state, callback context, and kernel FXSAVE state, but this IF-disabled runner is not scheduler-backed. Host tests exhaust every remaining-frame budget below successful preparation and assert root/frame rollback. Userspace spawn/exec, general child scheduling and stack reclamation, page-table metadata exhaustion, mid-PTE-write injection (not supported by the current infallible backend write contract), normal-boot userspace, hosted CI for current changes, and physical-hardware validation remain pending.

Never advance status or check off a roadmap item merely because source code or an interface exists. Update `docs/roadmap/README.md` only to reflect implementation and validation actually achieved.

## Source-of-truth documents

Consult the relevant documentation before modifying a subsystem:

- [`docs/index.md`](docs/index.md) — documentation entry point and current status.
- [`docs/roadmap/README.md`](docs/roadmap/README.md) — milestone sequencing and exit criteria.
- [`docs/architecture/overview.md`](docs/architecture/overview.md) — current architecture and intended layers.
- [`docs/architecture/boot.md`](docs/architecture/boot.md) — Limine requests, boot snapshot, and trust boundary.
- [`docs/architecture/memory.md`](docs/architecture/memory.md) — memory ownership, frame allocator, and paging direction.
- [`docs/architecture/crabshell.md`](docs/architecture/crabshell.md) — parser/kernel boundary and shell/VFS contract.
- [`docs/architecture/drivers.md`](docs/architecture/drivers.md) — current driver scope and limitations.
- [`docs/security.md`](docs/security.md) — unsafe boundaries and security policy.
- [`docs/development/building.md`](docs/development/building.md) and [`docs/development/testing.md`](docs/development/testing.md) — supported commands and validation expectations.

When code and documentation disagree, inspect the implementation, resolve the discrepancy deliberately, and update the relevant documentation in the same change.

## Repository map

- `src/main.rs` — freestanding entry, boot snapshot acquisition, panic path, and shell handoff.
- `src/boot.rs` — mutable Limine requests, structural response/range validation, owned `BootInfo`, and boot diagnostics.
- `src/memory.rs` — allocation-free memory-map, address-width, canonical-address, Limine HHDM-range, and linker-defined kernel segment validation.
- `src/frame.rs` — bounded physical-frame allocator core; it only uses validated `Usable` ranges, reserves the first MiB, and has fixed range metadata.
- `src/paging.rs` — checked mapping/cache policy, inherited page-table walking, and a bounded candidate-root builder. The default boot path activates a cloned hierarchy and retains its owned table tokens; the HHDM backend accesses only complete allocator-owned `Usable` frames after checked address derivation.
- `src/shell.rs` — kernel-side Crabshell executor using UART IRQ input and cooperative event waits when the runtime is available; polling remains fallback.
- `src/vfs.rs` — fixed-capacity volatile RAM filesystem and host-side tests.
- `crates/crabshell/` — separate `no_std` parser crate. It has no terminal, filesystem, or kernel dependencies.
- `crates/rustix-user/` — separate `no_std` v1 syscall-wrapper crate for x86_64; it does not depend on kernel internals and is not yet a complete application runtime.
- `src/arch/x86_64/serial.rs` — COM1 output/polling plus bounded IRQ RX queue.
- `src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` — bootstrap GDT/TSS/IDT, exception and device IRQ stubs/dispatch, fatal kernel diagnostics, and the opt-in CPL3 process-exit path.
- `src/arch/x86_64/cpu.rs` — CPUID identification and selected feature reporting.
- `src/arch/x86_64/keyboard.rs` — bounded IRQ and polling access to raw PS/2 scancodes.
- `src/arch/x86_64/apic.rs` — validated single-vCPU xAPIC/I/O APIC setup and PIT timer routing.
- `src/input.rs` — bounded SPSC UART/keyboard queues and IRQ-to-scheduler pending-event state.
- `src/kernel_threads.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`, and `src/time.rs` — single-vCPU context runtime with PIT preemption, host-testable scheduling policy, and monotonic tick arithmetic.
- `src/sync.rs` — IRQ-save spin locks that restore the prior local interrupt state; SMP policy remains separate.
- `src/arch/x86_64/io.rs` — narrow port-I/O wrappers.
- `linker.ld`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml` — target, linker, and toolchain configuration.
- `limine.conf`, `scripts/boot.py` — boot configuration and pinned image/emulator workflow.
- `justfile` — supported development commands.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — CI validation workflow.

## Engineering rules

### Keep changes incremental and coherent

1. Inspect the relevant source, tests, docs, and call sites before editing.
2. State assumptions, invariants, and failure behavior for new kernel interfaces.
3. Prefer small vertical slices that compile and can be tested over broad scaffolding or placeholder APIs.
4. Update tests and documentation alongside behavior changes.
5. Do not change unrelated code, rename files gratuitously, add speculative features, or rewrite project history.
6. Do not commit or create branches unless the user explicitly asks.

### Rust and dependency policy

- Preserve the kernel's `no_std`/freestanding constraints. Do not introduce `std` into kernel code.
- Prefer `core` and existing in-tree abstractions. Do not add third-party Rust dependencies without a concrete need and compatibility/security review.
- Keep the Crabshell parser independent of kernel I/O and VFS implementation. Kernel execution belongs in `src/shell.rs` or an appropriate kernel service.
- Do not add allocation-dependent APIs before a real heap exists. Fixed-capacity structures must document their limits and exhaustion behavior.
- Respect the workspace structure and the host-testable `rustix-kernel` library versus freestanding `rustix` binary boundary.

### Unsafe and hardware code

Unsafe code is expected only at explicit hardware, boot-protocol, assembly, or raw-memory boundaries. Keep each unsafe block narrow and document the invariant that makes it sound. Do not add broad `unsafe impl`, mutable global references, unchecked pointer arithmetic, or unreviewed inline/global assembly.

Before changing boot or memory code, account for these facts:

- Limine fills response pointers before `_start`; the request records must remain writable in the ELF image.
- Rustix validates nullness, alignment, counts, arithmetic, and physical ranges, but cannot prove that a non-null bootloader pointer is readable.
- Physical ranges are half-open `[start, end)` and must use checked arithmetic.
- Only regions classified `Usable` may enter the frame allocator. ACPI, bootloader-reclaimable, framebuffer, reserved, unknown, and other types are not free frames.
- A `Frame` is a physical address, not a dereferenceable pointer. HHDM access is allowed only through checked full-frame token-based paths that rely on the documented Limine contract; never access arbitrary physical addresses. Do not change CR3 until a complete, reviewed transition mapping policy and ownership proof exist.
- The kernel currently inherits Limine's page tables. Do not casually replace or mutate them: preserve the executing kernel, boot stack, `BootInfo`, request/response data, exception stacks, and mappings needed to continue execution.
- Kernel-origin exceptions, NMI, double fault, and machine check remain fatal. Only the opt-in synchronous process probe routes other CPL3 exceptions through process teardown; do not treat this diagnostic handler as general recovery. The single-vCPU APIC path enables only configured, registered routes after IRQ dispatch/EOI setup and tests. Do not broaden IRQ use or add preemption without a reviewed ownership, synchronization, and validation plan.
- The shell and VFS run in ring 0 and are not isolated or secure.

For hardware changes, document assumptions about CPU mode, selectors, stacks, page permissions, interrupt state, and failure handling. Avoid new architecture mechanisms that cannot be statically reviewed or validated.

### Shell and filesystem contract

- Crabshell is presently a kernel-mode serial shell, not a userspace program or a POSIX shell.
- Its parser is a separate `no_std`, allocation-free crate; retain that boundary.
- The RAM filesystem is volatile and bounded. Preserve explicit errors and test capacity, path, and mutation edge cases.
- Do not imply persistence, permissions, links, process launching, or shell features that do not exist.
- Update the parser tests and `docs/architecture/crabshell.md` when adding or changing commands.

## Validation workflow

Run the narrowest relevant checks first, then broaden them. From the repository root, the supported commands are:

```sh
just fmt
just test
just check
just build
just image
just smoke
just input-smoke
just process-smoke
just user-fault-smoke
just verify
```

`just test` runs host-side library tests, including ACPI, scheduler, input-queue, paging, frame allocator, heap, VFS, and Crabshell coverage. `just check` checks `x86_64-unknown-none`; `just build` links the optimized ELF. `just verify` includes formatting, host tests, target check, pinned Limine image creation, BIOS/OVMF boot, active-map, cooperative-thread, UART/PS/2 input, fatal kernel #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE, Ring 3 process, and CPL3 #PF/#GP/#UD/#DE QEMU smokes. `just process-smoke` checks syscall write/EFAULT/ready-child wait, running-child `ENOTSUP`, exit, kernel wait/reap, and teardown; `just user-fault-smoke` checks CPL3 exception termination and teardown. Image/boot checks need Python, `xorriso`, QEMU, OVMF, the Rust target, and network access for the first pinned Limine download; Linux/WSL also needs `cc` to build Limine's host utility.

For changes to `src/main.rs`, `src/boot.rs`, linker/request configuration, `src/arch/x86_64/`, `src/frame.rs`, or paging/heap code, the intended full validation is `just verify`. If the environment does not permit a check, report the exact blocker and leave the corresponding roadmap criterion pending.

Do not claim a check passed unless it was run and its successful result was observed. Editor diagnostics are useful but are not a substitute for `cargo test`, a target build, or QEMU. A target check is not a final link; a linked ELF is not proof of boot; a prompt smoke test is not proof of interactive shell behavior or physical-hardware correctness.

## Completion criteria for agent changes

Before reporting work complete:

- Ensure source, tests, docs, and call sites agree.
- Review unsafe and hardware assumptions, including error paths and capacity limits.
- Run appropriate formatting/tests/build/boot checks, or clearly state why they could not run.
- Report files changed, behavior delivered, validation actually observed, and remaining risks.
- Keep milestone status accurate. A subsystem is not complete just because it has code.

# Interrupts and IRQ vector allocation

## Current implementation

`src/arch/x86_64/interrupts.rs` installs the bootstrap GDT, TSS, exception gates for vectors 0–31, device IRQ stubs, and the APIC spurious-vector gate. Kernel-origin exceptions remain fatal. In the opt-in synchronous Ring 3 process probe, noncritical CPL3 exceptions are reported and handed to the installed process callback, which records status `128 + vector`, restores the kernel CR3, and exits through the user-entry trampoline. NMI (#2), double fault (#8), and machine check (#18) remain fatal regardless of saved CPL. QEMU exercises CPL3 #PF, #GP, #UD, and #DE termination in the diagnostic runtime; this is not a general exception or signal mechanism. Maskable interrupts start disabled and are enabled only after the validated APIC route, registered handler, and acknowledgement path are ready.

`src/irq.rs` provides a host-tested, allocation-free token allocator for device vectors `0x20..=0xef` except reserved syscall vector `0x80`; exception vectors and the reserved upper range are also excluded. The IDT overrides `0x80` with a dedicated DPL-3 interrupt gate and assembly stub. The stub rejects CPL0 invocation, saves the full GPR set and x87/SSE state on the TSS entry stack, and dispatches a normalized syscall context with IF clear. Each entered user context owns its continuation RSP, exit status/pending flag, callback context, and kernel FXSAVE image; nested child entry restores the suspended parent's state rather than sharing global entry-depth slots. This state separation is groundwork only: the diagnostic still keeps IF clear and is not scheduler-backed. In the opt-in process probe, the dispatcher implements ABI-version discovery, bounded write and wait-status copyout through allocator-owned user-frame copies, exit, and wait on one kernel-prepared child. If that child is running, the diagnostic enters it synchronously on a distinct continuation stack and resumes the parent after exit; the kernel harness later waits/reaps init. This is not general scheduler-managed process execution or a userspace spawn operation. The normal build only exposes ABI-version discovery. `rustix_irq_dispatch` invokes the registered handler, returns for the APIC spurious vector without EOI, and halts on unregistered/unexpected vectors. Device handlers own their EOI. Vector registration is performed with IF clear before the corresponding I/O APIC source is unmasked.

The initial hardware target is single-vCPU QEMU `q35`: validated ACPI/MADT topology, local APIC and I/O APIC, masked legacy PIC routing, MADT-resolved ISA routes, and a periodic 8254 PIT tick near 100 Hz. OVMF smokes validate PIT delivery/EOI, non-yielding timer preemption, x87/SSE state preservation, and UART/keyboard IRQ delivery. Host tests cover vector ownership and PIT/time arithmetic; they do not replace privileged QEMU coverage.

The scheduler is single-vCPU and supports cooperative waits/yields plus PIT-driven timer preemption. The timer handler advances ticks and sends APIC EOI before any scheduling switch. The common IRQ stub saves the interrupted x87/SSE state before Rust dispatch and restores the selected context before `IRETQ`; the context switch keeps aligned per-context FXSAVE areas. IRQ-safe spin locks save and restore the prior IF state, and the global heap uses one; scheduler mutations are separately serialized by masking local interrupts. IRQ/exception handlers remain bounded and allocation-free, and no current IRQ handler acquires the heap lock. SMP, per-CPU state, and physical-hardware validation remain future work.
